The creditor has reported inaccurate information on my credit report, including multiple addresses that I have never lived at. These inaccuracies have affected my credit score, and have made it difficult for me to obtain credit and loans at reasonable rates. The creditor has violated several federal laws including : Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) - 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) - This section requires credit reporting agencies to follow reasonable procedures to ensure the accuracy of the information in a consumer 's credit report. The inaccurate reporting of multiple addresses may be a violation of this section. 
Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) - 15 U.S.C. 1692e - This section prohibits debt collectors from using false, deceptive, or misleading representations in the collection of a debt. Reporting inaccurate addresses may be a violation of this section if the debt collector knew or should have known that the information was false or misleading. 
Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act ( FACTA ) - 15 U.S.C. 6821 - This section requires businesses to implement reasonable policies and procedures to protect sensitive consumer information from unauthorized access or disclosure. The failure to protect sensitive consumer information resulting in inaccurate reporting of multiple addresses may be a violation of this section. 
Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) - 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. - This law requires lenders to provide borrowers with certain disclosures about credit terms and costs. While the reporting of multiple addresses is not a direct violation of TILA, it may be a violation if the incorrect reporting is tied to an inaccurate disclosure of credit terms or costs. 
Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) - 12 U.S.C. 2601 et seq. - This law requires mortgage lenders to provide certain disclosures to borrowers and prohibits certain practices, such as kickbacks for referrals. Reporting incorrect addresses could be a violation of RESPA if it is tied to a failure to provide required disclosures or if it is tied to a kickback scheme. 
Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) - 15 U.S.C. 1691 et seq. - This law prohibits lenders from discriminating against borrowers on the basis of certain protected characteristics, such as race, gender, or age. Reporting incorrect addresses could be a violation of ECOA if it results in a lender using inaccurate information to make a discriminatory decision. 
Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) - 15 U.S.C. 1666 et seq. - This law requires credit card issuers to provide certain billing error resolution procedures to cardholders. While the reporting of multiple addresses is not a direct violation of the FCBA, it could be a violation if it is tied to a failure to properly handle a billing error dispute. 
These violations have caused me significant financial harm and emotional distress. I have been denied credit and loans, and have been forced to pay higher interest rates due to the inaccurate reporting. It has also caused me significant stress and anxiety, as I feel like my financial security and future opportunities have been compromised. 

I request that you enforce the legal provisions that have been violated, and that the creditor be required to remove the unverified accounts from my credit report. I also request that the creditor be held accountable for the financial and emotional harm they have caused me. 

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter. 

Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted]

I received a response later but was informed that the response they sent me will expire and that I wont be able to access it after a certain date. I do know if I screen shot the response. metadata.full_snippet:
Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am writing to file a formal complaint against Westlake Financial regarding their failure to delete delinquency from my credit report, as well as their involvement in dealer fraud that has had a negative impact on my credit and financial situation. 

In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2022, I reached an agreement with Westlake Financial to pay off an account in return for the deletion of a delinquency from my credit report. This delinquency was preventing me from obtaining a student loan, and I agreed to pay the account in full based on their assurance that the delinquency would be removed from my credit report. 

However, despite fulfilling my end of the agreement and paying off the account as agreed, Westlake Financial has failed to delete the delinquency from my credit report. This has caused significant harm to my credit profile and has continued to impact my ability to obtain a student loan, which has had a detrimental effect on my educational pursuits. 

Furthermore, I recently discovered that the vehicle associated with the delinquency was sold to me with dealer fraud involved. At the time of purchase, the dealer misrepresented the mileage of the vehicle, reducing it from [Redacted] miles to [Redacted] miles, and failed to disclose that the title was a rebuild title. Westlake Financial was aware of this fraud, but failed to disclose this critical information to me, resulting in financial loss and potential legal implications. 

I have attempted to resolve this issue with Westlake Financial directly, but they have been unresponsive and have failed to take appropriate action to rectify the situation. Therefore, I am requesting the assistance of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to investigate this matter and take appropriate action to hold Westlake Financial accountable for their failure to delete the delinquency as promised, as well as their involvement in dealer fraud. 

I have enclosed relevant documentation, including evidence of the agreement to delete the delinquency and information regarding the dealer fraud, for your review. I appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to your prompt action in resolving this issue and ensuring that Westlake Financial complies with relevant laws and regulations. 

Thank you for your assistance

NFCU - Credit card Subject : Explanation of Inability to Open an Account due to Confinement Dear NFCU, I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to address a recent matter concerning an account application that appears to have been initiated under my name. I would like to clarify that I did not open an account with NFCU during the specified time frame due to extenuating circumstances that rendered me unable to do so. 

The application in question seems to have been submitted on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2016. I must emphasize that during the period surrounding that date, I was in confinement and faced significant limitations in my ability to engage in any activities outside of my immediate living space. 

The nature of my confinement was such that I did not have access to the necessary resources, including internet access and physical documentation, required to open a new account. Moreover, my location was not conducive to such activities, making it logistically impossible for me to initiate any account-related procedures. 

I understand the importance of accurate record-keeping and the need for thorough investigations in matters like these. I kindly request that you conduct a comprehensive review of the application details and consider the circumstances I have outlined. It is my hope that this clarification will allow you to confirm my assertion that I did not open the account mentioned in your records. 

If there are any additional steps or documentation required from my end to support this claim, please do not hesitate to inform me. I am more than willing to cooperate fully to resolve this matter promptly. 

I appreciate your understanding and cooperation in this regard. It is my earnest hope that we can swiftly resolve any discrepancies and rectify the situation. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response. 

Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet:
This Is my Third written request for Method of Verification. You company has failed to provide me with this information and continue to violate my consumer and civil rights. I have been maintaining accurate logs of my letters and will file a complaint with the CFPB.

These Unverified accounts continue to hinder my ability to obtain credit. Please provide me with the information below : I demand the following Unverified Accounts be provided Physical Verification or Deleted Immediately. Please Provide Method Of Verification.

The unverified items listed below remain on my credit report in violation of Federal Law. You are required under the FCRA to have a copy of the original creditors documentation on file to verify that this information is mine and is correct. In the results of your first investigation, you stated in writing that you verified that these items are being reported correctly?

Who verified these accounts? Describe the procedure used and method to determine the accuracy and completeness of the disputed information, including the business name, address and furnisher of information connected to any in accurate information.

You need to do a reasonable investigation in compliance with FCRA section 611 part ( b ) sub sections below.

As per the FCRA : ( iii ) a notice that, if requested by the consumer, a description of the procedure used to determine the accuracy and completeness of the information shall be provided to the consumer by the agency, including the business name and address of any furnisher of information contacted in connection with such information and the telephone number of such furnisher, if reasonably available You have NOT provided me a copy of ANY original documentation required under Section 609 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) & Section 611 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ( a consumer contract with my signature on it ) and under Section 611 ( 5 ) ( A ) of the FCRA you are required to promptly DELETE all information which can not be verified.

The law is very clear as to the Civil liability and the remedy available to me for negligent noncompliance ( Section 617 ) if you fail to comply. I am a litigious consumer and fully intend on pursuing litigation in this matter to enforce my rights under the FCRA. I have been keeping detailed records of each letter with certified US Mail tracking in case needed to pursue further legal action.

metadata.full_snippet:
NFCU Subject : Explanation of Inability to Open an Account due to Confinement Dear Ally, I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to address a recent matter concerning an account application that appears to have been initiated under my name. I would like to clarify that I did not open an account with NFCU during the specified time frame due to extenuating circumstances that rendered me unable to do so. 

The application in question seems to have been submitted on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/. I must emphasize that during the period surrounding that date, I was in confinement and faced significant limitations in my ability to engage in any activities outside of my immediate living space. 

The nature of my confinement was such that I did not have access to the necessary resources, including internet access and physical documentation, required to open a new account. Moreover, my location was not conducive to such activities, making it logistically impossible for me to initiate any account-related procedures. 

I understand the importance of accurate record-keeping and the need for thorough investigations in matters like these. I kindly request that you conduct a comprehensive review of the application details and consider the circumstances I have outlined. It is my hope that this clarification will allow you to confirm my assertion that I did not open the account mentioned in your records. 

If there are any additional steps or documentation required from my end to support this claim, please do not hesitate to inform me. I am more than willing to cooperate fully to resolve this matter promptly.

I appreciate your understanding and cooperation in this regard. It is my earnest hope that we can swiftly resolve any discrepancies and rectify the situation. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response. 

Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted]

On or approximately [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I loaned the vehicle to a friend to use for a...
metadata.full_snippet:
BACKGROUND [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I purchased a [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ( hereinafter the vehicle ), which was financed through Santander Consumer USA. On or approximately [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I loaned the vehicle to a friend to use for a few hours. The vehicle was never returned and in accordance with NJ [Redacted] law I reported it stolen to the local Police and my insurance company, [Redacted]. [Redacted] opened a claim and investigated, also contacting Santander advising that I opened a stolen vehicle claim. Despite overwhelming evidence, the local police refused to list the vehicle stolen or report the in the national alert system for stolen vehicles. [Redacted] was unable to continue and pay the claim without this. 

In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I contacted Santander to find out if the vehicle had been located and was informed that the vehicle was recovered and in [Redacted]. I was ecstatic and asked the address where it was being stored as I wanted the vehicle back and catch up the back payments. I was put on hold and when the Santander representative came back on the line, they refused to give me any information and ended the call. Another call to Santander had the same results. 

In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I received a call from my insurance company, [Redacted], regarding my damage claim for the [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. I had not filed a damage claim and after the adjuster looked further into the claim, she advised me that Santander had filed the claim. I was never contacted by Santander or informed that the vehicle was damaged and that they filed a claim with my insurance company. Only until [Redacted] contacted me did I learn of the fate of the vehicle or received any information regarding the vehicle whatsoever. Regardless, after investigation [Redacted] deemed the vehicle a total loss and Santander received a check in the amount of {$26000.00} dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted].

metadata.full_snippet:
This account with Synchrony Bank was opened when I bought a mattress at Mattress Firm and they offered me no interest financing. I have had a myriad of issues with Synchrony. Their operations and systems are chaotic. The latest problem I had was when they randomly decided to cancel my autopay causing me to miss a payment. Their method of informing me was to send an uninformative email on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 to me to click a link to read a message for me. The link did not work when I attempted to click and read the message. I attempted various times. 

Today, I logged into my sychrony account and discovered that my payment was overdue. I went back to the uninformative email of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and was able to click through and open the message. The message stated that my autopayment amount was being changed to {$0.00}. My balance is still {$1800.00}. There is no reason listed for this change and it was not a change that I authorized or attempted to perform. Now my account is overdue. 

Earlier problems with Synchrony include that they did not send me information in the mail when my account was setup and the first payment ( or perhaps multiple payments ) were missed because I didn't know the account had been opened yet. I learned about it after receiving a past due statement. Resolving this was difficult and I spent hours on the phone with off shore customer service agents that could not help and were not trained to address the issue and did not know English sufficiently well to comprehend the problem. I was finally able getting it fixed after one helpful customer service agent finally escalated and I spoke to an American agent who got it resolved. 

Synchrony appears to either act in bad faith intentionally hoping to cause customers to miss payments so that they can charge exorbitant interest rates citing breaches of contract OR their systems and operations are poorly setup to actually manage their accounts.

The FCRA, a federal statute governing the accuracy and fairness of credit reporting, provides specific guidelines that must be followed by furnishers of information like [Redacted] [Redacted] : [Redacted]. **Accuracy of Information ( Section 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ) ** : The FCRA mandates that furnishers provide accurate and complete information to credit reporting agencies. I assert that the late payment reporting on my credit reports is inaccurate and does not reflect my payment history accurately. 

2. **Duty to Correct and Update Information ( Section 623 ( a ) ( 2 ) ) ** : The FCRA places an obligation on furnishers to promptly correct and update any information found to be inaccurate. 3. **Investigation of Disputes ( Section 611 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ) ** : Upon receiving notice of a dispute from a consumer, the FCRA requires furnishers to conduct a reasonable investigation into the disputed information. I hereby formally dispute the late payment reporting on my [Redacted] account, and I expect you to initiate a thorough investigation into the accuracy of these entries. 

4. **Time Limits for Investigations ( Section 611 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ) ** : The FCRA mandates that furnishers must complete their investigations within 30 days of receiving notice of a dispute. I insist that you adhere to this time frame when conducting your investigation.

She then " puts '' notes in the system saying that on Tuesday the [Redacted] when the hold is lifted that I would make the transfers and everything would be okay. I am writing to you due to my concerns with Bank of America 's financial practices. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2022 I purchased a trip for {$1700.00} through a third party travel company called [Redacted] [Redacted] using my Bank of America Credit Card. However, [Redacted] [Redacted] filed for bankruptcy sometime in [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. My travel partner and I did not find this out right away. After attempting to contact the [Redacted], we were told to also contact our credit card companies. She had purchased through [Redacted] and got her money back almost instantly. I contacted BOA who stated they would send me directions via mail ( snail mail ) to send supporting documents back to them proving the matter. They said it must be sent via mail, even though I travel for work. By the time I returned home, and received the communication, it was significantly later. I was outside the window of time they allotted me to get supporting evidence back to them. In addition, they stated that since it was over 6 months from date of purchase it was outside the transaction window/time frame when they can return funds. I was beyond frustrated. They said there wasn't much they could do. I followed up numerous times and never received any follow-up emails or instructions, despite being told they were sending them to me. However, I get confirmation emails and transaction alerts and statements from them regarding my credit cards all the time - there is no way these emails should not have made it to me. 

I have called BOA and wasted hours and hours on the phone with them, not getting anywhere. I believe they purposefully drew out the process, falsely stated they were sending me documents/emails etc, and had no intention of ever following through or returning my money for a purchase where no services were ever rendered. I have never received any written correspondence from the company except for that first letter that was sent while I was away from home. I have never received any type of compensation or refund from the company. 

Sadly, I eventually gave up/did n't have the bandwidth to continue fighting them until I read recent reports about the BOA 's other financial misconduct. I believe their misconduct is deeply ingrained into their entire system.

metadata.title: Mortgage Dispute
metadata.snippet:
Our home was flooded by Hurricane Ian in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], and again by Hurricane Nicole only 42 days later in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. 
I contacted Truist after our first flood ( in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) and we were offered a disaster forbea...
metadata.full_snippet:
Our home was flooded by Hurricane Ian in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], and again by Hurricane Nicole only 42 days later in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. 
I contacted Truist after our first flood ( in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) and we were offered a disaster forbearance on our Mortgage for a 3-month period ( [Redacted] [Redacted] ). I was told this could be extended for a total of 12 months in 3-month increments and that I simply needed to call Truist prior to the end of the 3-month period in order to extend the forbearance each time. 
I did just that and we were granted an extension for [Redacted] [Redacted] and again for [Redacted] [Redacted]. 
In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I contacted Truist in order to extend our forbearance for the last 3 months available to us. Our extension was confirmed for [Redacted]  [Redacted] and I was informed that our first payment would be due on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. 
In mid [Redacted] I began receiving phone calls from Truist Collections requesting that I make a payment as our account was past due. I called Truist to inquire and was told that our account was no longer in forbearance status and was past due. I was given various reasons for this including the 12-month period had been reached ( which was incorrect ), that documentation was missing ( but was not told which documentation specifically ) and was ultimately told the issue could not be resolved and had to be escalated to a supervisor who I should be expecting a call from. 
I did not receive a phone call from a supervisor. But I did receive a letter from an Attorneys office notifying me that they were attempting to collect a debt owed to Truist and that our loan became delinquent on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. 
I still had not received a call back from Truist so I called them again on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and was told our account had been placed under foreclosure since [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], and had been sent to an Attorneys office for collections. I was provided with the Attorneys name and number ( [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ), the same Attorney i had received the letter from, and I was told our account would be reviewed to correct this and that I would receive a call back. 
In the meantime, my husband and I both received very disruptive daily phone calls, text messages and letters from various companies and attorneys regarding our foreclosure. 
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I became aware that a Lis Pendens had been filed against us on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. 
I called the Attorneys office that same day and informed them our account was not under a foreclosure, that we were not delinquent on payments as we were under a forbearance agreement, and that we were attempting to work with Truist to correct this issue. 
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I was called by Truist to inquire on the status of our home repairs. I was not given any more information regarding the correction of the foreclosure or our forbearance and was told I would be contacted by another representative regarding those matters. 
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I called Truist as I yet again had not received a call back. After nearly 20min of reviewing the documentation in our account I was told that our forbearance was re-instated and no longer in foreclosure with our first payment now being [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. I was also informed that paperwork had been mailed out to me the day prior ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ), however as of today ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) I have not yet received anything. 
I am filing a complaint because despite having done what was asked of us, a Lis Pendens was filed in error which is now a part of public records. 
I am a [Redacted]  and my husband is a [Redacted] [Redacted] who owns his own [Redacted] [Redacted] business. This misinformation could be very harmful to us as professionals or as consumers and is not an accurate representation of our characters. 
Neither my husband nor I were notified by Truist at any time that our account was delinquent until I received a call from their Collections Department. Prior to [Redacted] we had not been contacted by any agency regarding an apparent foreclosure, and this luckily has not been reported to the credit bureaus. Based on this it is apparent that we should never have been turned over to an attorney and a Lis Pendens should never have been filed. 
I also received 3rd party notification from a contact of my mother in laws that Truist admitted foreclosure proceedings should not have been initiated since we should have been under a forbearance. This was communicated in an email from Truist Loss Mitigation Dept. 
We are looking to you for guidance on how to proceed in order to make sure this error does not jeopardize us in any way, and to hopefully have some kind of reversal for the Lis Pendens filed. 
In addition, based on our last statement from Truist, there is an amount of {$4700.00} for total fees and charges that has been added to our account which also needs to be corrected. 
My husband and I are still dealing with the stress from the loss of our home due to the hurricanes. We have been living in an RV with our [Redacted] little girls since [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], and we are still waiting for the insurance company to provide us with an estimate that will allow us to make the necessary repairs to our home as it remains unlivable. To throw this situation on top of all of that has honestly added to the frustration and helplessness that we feel on a daily basis. Weve done everything we were supposed to do, kept our accounts up to date and had the appropriate flood coverage for our home, yet we are still battling to get our lives back to normal so that our girls can have a home again. 
Thank you for your time!

metadata.full_snippet:
I received a letter from my mortgage company, PennyMac, with this text on the outside : " IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT YOUR HOME LOAN ''.

Of course I had to open the letter. ( After I realized it was an advertisement, I realized that looking for the presorted-standard postage was the clue that the text was a lie ) The letter offers me up to {$50000.00} with a cash-out refinance. 
Reading the fine print, they're offering me a {$340000.00} loan at an interest rate of 7.624 % after paying for [Redacted] discount points and with a [Redacted] score of [Redacted]. This will have a mortgage payment of $ [Redacted] ( without escrow ). 

My current interest rate is 2.75 % on about {$290000.00} balance ( [Redacted] years remaining ). My non-escrow mortgage payment is currently $ [Redacted]. They're looking to raise my monthly payment by $ [Redacted]. 

I guess I have several problems here. 

1 ) I think it is wildly dishonest to require my attention for an advertisement. Given the important financial relationship I have with PennyMac, I have to pay attention to communications from them ... so sending advertisements under the guise of " IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT YOUR HOME LOAN '' is extremely misleading. 

2 ) PennyMac has all the information to know that this is a terrible deal for me. It is an absolutely usurious offer. There are very few situations where this offer would be anything other than a terrible deal designed to entrap a financially stressed person.

3 ) I had already requested to be opted out of marketing, but apparently that may have only applied to email marketing, not snail-mail too?

I have included images of the envelope, front/back of the letter, and insert. Please feel free to reach out to me with any questions.

metadata.snippet: Background details : I am currently selling a 1.6 acre parcel, which is part of 5 separate and non-contiguous parcels that are outlined on the legal description on my mortgage. The total acreage described on the legal deed exceeds 150 acres, which includes a house that sits on on...
metadata.full_snippet:
Background details : I am currently selling a 1.6 acre parcel, which is part of 5 separate and non-contiguous parcels that are outlined on the legal description on my mortgage. The total acreage described on the legal deed exceeds 150 acres, which includes a house that sits on one of the five parcels. We are selling one small plot in order to raise funds to renovate the house, including adding over 400 square feet of additional living space, renovating the kitchen, and updating the electrical service, heating, cooling and plumbing. The renovation has been approved and permitted by the municipal Health Department. 

We have reached out to the servicer to request a partial release in order to sell the smallest plot of land, which is separate from the main house plot ( not connected ), and represents ~1 % of the total acreage of the property. We provided the servicer with a free and clear title report, a plot map of the 1.6 acre parcel as well as the other nearby parcels, a copy of the municipal permit for the renovation, and architectural drawings for the planned renovation. We have agreed to a desktop appraisal of the property to ensure that the value of the property still exceeds the mortgaged amount.

Issue : The servicer has stated that they can not approve a partial release until a full survey is completed for all 150 acres of land. A survey of this magnitude would include surveying 5 separate parcels. The cost of the survey will be {$46000.00} ( see attached quote from the surveyor ). The only relevant part of the survey is what is related to Parcel 3 ( see attached document ), and even that is not relevant once the value of the home is established by the desktop appraisal. Note, the total value of the land sale for the 1.6 acres is {$25000.00}. The cost of the survey, which is being required by the servicer, exceeds the full proceeds we would earn from the sale of the land.

We have tried to resolve this issue with the servicer, but currently have not had success. I have asked them to provide justification for the survey, including outlining where in their guidelines a survey is required. I will provide this information if they respond.

There is no reason for a survey to be completed on 150 acres of land for a sale of 1.6 acres ( 1 % of the land ). The request from the servicer is egregious and unreasonable, and presents an insurmountable financial burden, which threatens to prohibit the land sale and thus prohibit us, the property owner, from accumulating wealth and improving our property. We have provided clear plot maps to show the location of the parcel in relation to the house as well as a clear title report. We have agreed to a desktop appraisal, which will validate the property value. We have done everything we can do to follow their guidelines, but the servicer has imposed an unreasonable request.

Documents attached : - Plot map of parcels - Estimate from the surveyor - Permit from municipality for approved renovation - Architectural drawings showing planned improvements to the property - Servicer 's partial release of collateral request form - Current title search prepared for this sale - Signed purchase agreement

metadata.full_snippet:
In reviewing my credit reports, I came across a debt item that was listed incorrectly. I disputed this account to the credit bureaus, and they confirmed it was verified as accurate by you. 
I am aware of the rights I have and am requesting that you immediately remove the debt from my credit reports, or you may face damages by reporting inaccurate data to a credit reporting agency. 
( See the FCRA ) This debt is listed as a charge off, with a last date of activity of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2016. You are reporting the charge off date as the date you purchased the debt instead of the actual charge off date. This is a clear violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, as it is clearly stated that " no debt may be reported to a consumers ' credit file for any longer than 7 years from the date of first serious delinquency or charge off. '' Because you have altered the charge off date as the date you purchased it, you are committing fraud. I have informed the credit bureaus of this and have asked for a second verification. When that verification comes to you, I suggest you follow the law and report the true facts. In addition to this debt being over the allowed time to report ( 7 years ) it has also passed the statute of limitations to collect. I have no intention of paying this old expired debt and I am informing you of this now. 
Should you attempt to report or collect this expired debt, I will contact my Attorney General and fill out a complaint to the Federal Trade Commission, and I will take steps to collect damages from you of up to {$1000.00}. I believe I have a case against you for violating sections of the FDCPA and FCRA should you continue.

metadata.full_snippet:
During the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I had issues with my former insurance provider [Redacted] resulting in a missed payment for one month. I obtained new insurance the following month with [Redacted] [Redacted]. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I was sent a letter from Bank of America indicating they would be force placing homeowners insurance due to a lack of coverage. I contacted Bank of America to inform them that I had obtained insurance and there was no need to force place it. The representative indicated they were notified of the insurance obtained but because I missed one month they would be charging it to me and force placing insurance for that month. This is not within the spirit of the regulation. The regulation requiring homeowners to retain homeowners insurance on their property is closely related to safety and soundness of the bank. This spirit of this regulation is to ensure homes do not have lapses in insurance that would result in a loss to the customer or Bank. It does not fit in the spectrum of having [Redacted] claims or losses and charging a customer for insurance 2 months later. Regardless, I said ok and understood that the force placement of insurance for a month would be charged to me. In [Redacted] of [Redacted], I received the escrow analysis for my mortgage. I was unable to determine why it was increased so much. I contacted Bank of America and the associate said it was for the force placement of insurance. I filed a complaint to have the review the escrow analysis given I was only supposed to be charged for the [Redacted] month and they already knew I had insurance. I was told I should hear back within [Redacted] business days. I followed up twice for resolution and the second time ( weeks later in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) was told that although they knew my insurance was current they were still going force place the insurance ( also not consumer friendly or within the spirit of the regulations ). If they were going to still proceed to force place insurance that they need to make sure to inform [Redacted] because I had current auto deductions from my account that would need to be stopped. Best practices for financial institutions is to keep the same insurance and continue to pay the premium out of the escrow as to avoid gross costs to the customer by force placing insurance through an outside source. I advised I would not pay Bank of America AND [Redacted] for insurance. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], my new payment took affect and my auto draft for the insurance continued cause my mortgage to fall behind of which it is currently still behind. I feel this is totally against the purpose of the regulation and is actually a case of disparaging impact as indicated in the [Redacted] regulation. I am asking that this issue be corrected as soon as possible. 

Thanks.

metadata.issue: Charged fees or interest you didn't expect
metadata.snippet:

I applied for one on line, and then I received a barrage of texts and emails from other lenders, which confused me. 
One company in particular represented that I had already applied and been approved for a l...
metadata.full_snippet:
On [Redacted], I was trying to obtain a payday loan or short term loan. 
I applied for one on line, and then I received a barrage of texts and emails from other lenders, which confused me. 
One company in particular represented that I had already applied and been approved for a loan, but I didn't think that I had actually applied at first. I must have, because they had my credit union account information. 
I looked at the terms and knew that it was a usary rate, so I went looked at reviews of on-line loan companies and ultilmately chose a different one. 
A few days later, {$800.00} was depostied into my checking account by Explore credit, which is the company that I desribed above as having represented that I had been approved for a load that I did not remember applying for. 
When automatic payments to pay off the {$800.00} dollars started coming out of my account, I firgured I should repay the money that they deposited into my account. 
I didn't notice at that time, but the company was taking automatic payments ever two weeks of {$210.00} for an [Redacted] dollar loan. I noticed two payments, and thought it was coming out monthly. 
In mid-[Redacted]  of this year, I started receiving texts from Explore Credit about a missed payment. I had been overdrawn, as I am separated and struggling to make ends meet at the moment. 
So I went onto their webiste, and created a login, and went to the portal to schedule a payment. 
The amount that it stated I currently owed was around {$1300.00}. I would state the exact amount, but it changed literally as I watched it, the amount jumped /changed to over {$4000.00}. I think approx {$4800.00}. I was certain this was just a mistake, but then I went into my credit union records, and they had been extracting {$210.00} every two weeks. The total amount that has been paid to date is {$1000.00}. 
I tried texting back one of the representatives that had been texting me, and they urged me to get on the phone to renegoaiate. So then I went to the [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] website, and read many, many complaints against them. They have a rating of an F. 
So then I tried reaching out to the company ( Explore Credit ) on their website, the Contact Us feature. I tried to submit my complaint to them three times, each time I received an error and a message to try again later. 

I am certain that there is some degree of fraudulent activity, and the company does not seem to be in jurisdiction, as it appears to be [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] owned. 

Is there anything I can do legally to settle this without repaying {$4800.00}?

metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/3023 I've rwcieved an email regarding a change to my [Redacted] consumer report. Upon checking I noticed that the company by the name of [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] had unlawfully place a collection account on to my report. Per law I'm requesting that this company provides me with notice of validation of debt pursuant to 12 CFR 1006.34a ( 1 ) In general. Except as provided in paragraph ( a ) ( 2 ) of this section, a debt collector must provide a consumer with the validation information required by paragraph ( c ) of this section either : ( i ) By sending the consumer a validation notice in the manner required by 1006.42 : ( A ) In the initial communication, as defined in paragraph ( b ) ( 2 ) of this section; or ( B ) Within five days of that initial communication ; which this company didn't do. Pursuant to 12 CFR 1006.34c ( 1 ) DEBT COLLECTOR COMMUNICATION DISCLOSURE.1. Statement required by 1006.18 ( e ). The statement required by 1006.18 ( e ) .Section 1006.34 ( c ) ( 1 ) provides that validation information includes the statement required by 1006.18 ( e ). Section 1006.18 ( e ) ( 1 ) requires a debt collector to disclose in its initial communication that the debt collector is attempting to collect a debt and that any information obtained will be used for that purpose. Section 1006.18 ( e ) ( 2 ) requires a debt collector to disclose in each subsequent communication that the communication is from a debt collector. A debt collector who provides a validation notice as described in 1006.34 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( i ) ( A ) complies with 1006.34 ( c ) ( 1 ) by providing on the validation notice the disclosure required by 1006.18 ( e ) ( 1 ). A debt collector who provides a validation notice as described in 1006.34 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( i ) ( B ) complies with 1006.34 ( c ) ( 1 ) by providing either the disclosure required by 1006.18 ( e ) ( 1 ) or the disclosure required by 1006.18 ( e ) ( 2 ). The following example illustrates the rule : i. ABC debt collector has an initial communication with the consumer by telephone. Within five days of that initial communication, ABC debt collector sends the consumer a validation notice using Model Form B1 in appendix B to this part. ABC debt collector has complied with 1006.34 ( c ) ( 1 ) even though Model Form B1 includes the disclosure described in 1006.18 ( e ) ( 1 ) rather than the disclosure described in 1006.18 ( e ) ( 2 ).

metadata.snippet:

metadata.full_snippet:
On or around [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] of [Redacted] I obtained a loan modification from this lender ( Freedom Mortgage ), but the loan modification did not consider my [Redacted] tax exemption and the fact that I was paying my own insurance. 

The servicer acknowledged the problem and promised to correct it by providing a new loan modification package. I proactively reached out to this servicer at least once per month and was told that they were working on it and will send the new loan modification soon. 

Around the end of [Redacted], I received a call from a realtor asking me if I was ready to sell the house. I asked him why and he stated because I noticed that your house is up for foreclosure. I reached out to this servicer, and I was then informed that the house was indeed sent to foreclosure. I requested to talk to a supervisor and a lady named [Redacted] [Redacted] confirmed that the house was in foreclosure and that I was never going to receive such corrected new loan modification package. 

Around [Redacted] of this year, I was told to complete a loss mitigation package, which I did. After a full review, the bank provided a new loan modification with an outrageous number. My APR went from 3.125 % to 6.125 % and my payment went up by one hundred percent. The Bank eventually dismissed the foreclosure after I signed this new loan modification under duress to keep my home, but with no assurance that a new one would not be filed. I asked this servicer to honor the VA COVID-19 guideline and grant me this from the VA [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] 
I tried to make this new loan modification work, but due to the missing payments and foreclosure status placed on my credit report I lost my job and was unable to make those payments. I have a Department of Defense security clearance, which is required to perform my job. I informed this servicer about this issue, and I was told to resubmit a new application to the loss mitigation team. 

As instructed, around [Redacted] of this year, I resubmitted a completely new loss mitigation package. The servicer acknowledged that they have received the completed documents. They confirmed this by email and during phone conversations, but every time I called to confirm they asked for more documents. 

On Monday [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I called this servicer to find out about the loss mitigation status. I talked to [Redacted] [Redacted], he confirmed to me that everything they needed was received, that it can take a few days to be in the system and that he will give me a call on Thursday [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], he never call. On Friday [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I received a call from this servicer telling me that my mortgage was due. I requested to speak with [Redacted] [Redacted] ( Supervisor ), and she told me that I needed to provide new bank statements because the ones that I had initially sent expired. In addition to the bank statement, she said I need to provide my spouse paystubs again. 

On Monday [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I provided those items again via email [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  and via their website portal. In both instances I received confirmation that the items were received. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I reached out to find out about the status of my modification and I was told by [Redacted] [Redacted] that my account is overdue and that it has been sent to foreclosure on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. I asked why and to confirm that information and she stated, it was sent to the attorneys as a " Soft Foreclosure '' on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and the reason was because I failed to provide requested documents, which I clearly did send. 

I have proactively sent every document requested, but every time they asked for new ones and often the very same ones. Please assist me to get to the bottom of this. Thank you.

metadata.full_snippet: Complaint : Regardless of the amount of times Wells Fargo is fined and sued, they continue to deceive their account holders without even attempting to hide it. During this year, I have paid more than {$300.00} in erroneous overdraft fees that are charged to my account the next day, during the grace period that they continuously and falsely advertise. In the evidence that I am submitting, you can clearly see various examples of this, i.e. account is overdrawn on Day [Redacted], the account balance is then made positive via deposit on Day [Redacted], but on Day [Redacted], an overdraft fee appears to have been posted on Day [Redacted]. I have gone to my local Wells Fargo a couple of times where the Manager lectured me on how to understand the way they structured their transactions to make it beneficial for them. The reality is that the manager told me that the Wells Fargo app was only for educational purposes, basically stating that you shouldnt believe what you see because it could not be true and that since this was a reoccurrence in my account it must be my fault. With her attitude, she essentially told me that if I werent poor and stored my money with Wells Fargo more often, I wouldnt have these issues. The worst part of everything is that even when Wells Fargo sees that they are in the wrong, they will tell you We are so sorry but since this is not the first Overdraft Fee we can't waive it despite the fact that the times they have only waived it when they recognize that they are at fault. Wells Fargo will never lose the argument ; they will tell you that X transaction was mysteriously started before I ( the customer ) could even see it, and that's the reason I accrued Overdraft Fees. Basically, if a bill is paid on the [Redacted] of each month and appears on my account on the [Redacted] WF will charge an overdraft fee if I dont pay it on the [Redacted], despite that date being within their imaginary grace period because the transaction started on the [Redacted], despite the fact that it was not reflected on my educational app on the [Redacted]. Wells Fargo offers bill pay services and autopay services but expects its customers to remember the exact day that the transaction is initiated. Wells Fargo hides information from its customers and they will always argue to favor them, leaving the customer with nothing to do. Wells Fargo is stealing from its customers and if you are a minority, you will be treated as if the only money you have is whatever they see in your account. I pay $ 10 monthly to Wells Fargo so I can store my money at their place and I expect Wells Fargo to honor their services and promises. The purpose of my complaint is to show that the billion-dollar settlements that Wells Fargo has recently incurred apparently do not surmount the amount of money that they steal from their account holders while being monitored by the Federal Government . I hope that my complaint is thoroughly reviewed and I do not become another of the millions of customers encountering this same situation.

Re : Alleged Fraud, Violation of Consumer Rights, and Inaccurate Information on Credit Report Thorough Investigation into the Acquisition of Fraudulent and Inaccurate Information from Third-Party Creditors I write and address serious concerns regarding the credit reporting practices of your consumer reporting agency. As an esteemed well-versed in the intricacies of consumer rights and protection, it is incumbent upon me to protect the interests and well-being of my integrity to the fullest extent permissible under the law.

In light of the allegations regarding the fraudulent inclusion of information from third-party creditors on their credit report, it is of paramount importance that a thorough examination be undertaken to ascertain the precise steps taken by your institution to validate the accuracy and veracity of the information in question. To this end, I kindly request that you provide a comprehensive and detailed account of the procedures, protocols, and mechanisms employed to acquire and verify the information attributed to these third-party creditors.

Pursuant to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Section 611 ( 5 ) ( A ), I have the unequivocal right to request that any information on their credit report which is inaccurate,
incomplete, or unverifiable be promptly deleted in order to ensure the accuracy and integrity of their credit profile. It is of paramount importance that you fulfill this legal obligation as delineated in the aforementioned provision.

Drawing reference from FCRA 15 USC Section 1681i, it is evident that any information contained within the credit report must be accurate. In this instance, I have identified discrepancies and inaccuracies within the report, thereby necessitating the immediate rectification of these deficiencies.

Moreover, FCRA 1681a ( 2 ) A ( i ) posits that credit reports must solely encompass information regarding transactions or experiences between the consumer and the entity responsible for reporting such activities. Therefore, any extraneous or irrelevant information must be expunged from my credit report promptly. 

With the utmost regard for personal privacy and consent, as assured by 15 USC 1681 Section 602, I affirm right to privacy and non-consensual dissemination of personal information to third parties. It is therefore imperative that you conform to these statutory provisions and refrain from disclosing my information without their explicit written authorization.

In alignment with 15 USC 1681 Section 604 subsection 2, it is unequivocally stated that no consumer reporting agen
cy, such as yourself, may furnish an account without prior written instructions from the consumer. I emphasize that I HAVE NOT provided written instructions to Experian and [Redacted] in any form, rendering any disclosure by your institution a clear violation of their statutory rights under the FCRA. 
Furthermore, in reference to 15 USC 1666B, it is explicitly outlined that a creditor may not classify a payment on a credit card account as late within an open end consumer plan for any purpose. ANY attempts to do so would constitute a serious breach of the law and a detrimental infringement upon my rights as a consumer. 

I also kindly request that you provide me with any pertinent information regarding past lawsuits or legal actions initiated against your AGENY due to fraudulent practices on consumer credit reports. Such documentation will prove invaluable in assessing the extent of your legal liabilities. 

It is incumbent upon your agency to meticulously outline the specific actions taken to authenticate the reliability and credibility of the information procured from these third-party creditors. I demand an exhaustive, step-by-step account of the measures implemented to ensure the accuracy and integrity of the information before its inclusion in their credit report. Furthermore, please clarify the nature of the relationship between you company and these third-party creditors, including any contractual agreements, financial arrangements, or affiliations that facilitate the exchange of consumer data.

In the interest of transparency and clarity, it is essential that you disclose the details of any individuals, companies, or entities directly involved in the alleged fraudulent scheme. I intend to build a compelling case based on irrefutable evidence, incorporating the relevant provisions of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) other pertinent consumer protection laws. Therefore, any information pertaining to the identity of those responsible for perpetrating or facilitating this wrongdoing will greatly contribute to the efficacy and strength of our legal proceedings. Please understand that I am fully aware of my rights as a consumer and are determined to protect MY rights vigilantly. 

I also write to formally requesting a comprehensive and meticulous investigation into the origin, acquisition, and dissemination of fraudulent and inaccurate information attributed to third-party creditors on my credit report. I strive to ensure that I protect my rights and they are upheld with the utmost rigor and dedication. 

In your response, I implore you to employ precise and articulate language, adhering to the highest standards expected from a reputable financial institution. The provision of concise and unambiguous explanations, utilizing industry-specific terminology, will facilitate my understanding of the intricacies involved in this alleged fraudulent scheme. 

Thank you Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), for keeping track of all the reports that I have sent out to you, as the credit reporting agency has ignored my request, SEVERAL TIMES. They have indeed broken the laws and this letter will be public on social outlets. Therefore, with this information, fines will be granted due to their fraudulent acts.

metadata.full_snippet:
Subject : Dispute of Debt Collection ( Account Number : [Redacted] ) and Urgent Request for Investigation and Rectification Dear Sir/Madam : I am writing to express my serious concern and dispute regarding a specific, inaccurate collection entry on my consumer report. 

Account Name : [Redacted] [Redacted]Account Number : [Redacted]Amount Owed : {$540.00} as of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 I assertively challenge the validity of this debt. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I returned the specified items to a [Redacted] store in New York. Despite being assured of the proper return process, this debt erroneously appeared on my credit profile. 

This unmerited mark not only jeopardizes my financial reputation but has caused significant emotional distress. I've spent countless hours on the phone, mailed evidence, and painstakingly attempted to rectify this situation, only to face continuous roadblocks and a lack of clarity. 

The stress stemming from this matter has been exacerbated by the looming implications it carries. I've found myself questioning future financial decisions, concerned about potential higher interest rates, and apprehensive about the prospect of being declined for financial products or services due to this unwarranted blemish on my credit profile. Furthermore, this experience has left me feeling violated that despite my genuine efforts and rightful actions, my financial narrative can be inaccurately portrayed. This is not just an errant number or a misreported transaction ; it's a reflection of me that is being inaccurately and unfairly tarnished. 

In accordance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), I draw your attention to the following sections : 1681i : Mandates credit reporting agencies, like [Redacted], to conduct a comprehensive and timely reinvestigation when a consumer disputes information.

1681g : Highlights my right to know every piece of information you have about me, including the sources of that information.

1681j : Ensures that no unwarranted charges are levied against me during this dispute process.

1681s-2 ( a ) : Clearly outlines the duties of furnishers of information to provide accurate data. In this context, [Redacted] [Redacted] may have violated this provision. 

My objective is straightforward : I seek an immediate and thorough investigation into this matter. The enclosed receipt unequivocally confirms the return of the [Redacted] equipment. It is my belief that with this evidence, coupled with the responsibilities of both credit bureaus and information furnishers under the FCRA, this unjustified debt collection entry should be removed expeditiously. 

Any failure or undue delay in addressing my concerns and rectifying this error will not only infringe upon my rights under the FCRA but may also compel me to take legal action to safeguard my interests. 

Please treat this letter with the urgency and seriousness it warrants. 

Enclosed : Receipt of returned [Redacted] [Redacted] Internet 5G router and receiver dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023.

This is an email I sent to Kohl 's Manager, who responded via letter that she wouldn't change the mistake. 

I'm reaching out today with great disappointment as I've had to close my [Redacted]year-long Kohl 's account due to an unfortunate misunderstanding that I received no assi...
metadata.full_snippet:
This is an email I sent to Kohl 's Manager, who responded via letter that she wouldn't change the mistake. 

I'm reaching out today with great disappointment as I've had to close my [Redacted]year-long Kohl 's account due to an unfortunate misunderstanding that I received no assistance with. In [Redacted], I set up autopay for my recurring bills through my bank, which was successful. Encouraged by this, I added my credit cards in [Redacted], given my father 's illness and my frequent hospital visits to care for him, making bill payments a challenge. 

However, in [Redacted], my bank account experienced a bounce, prompting me to investigate unauthorized transactions. My bank promptly closed the account, requiring a two-week wait to reinstate everything. Consequently, my Kohl 's payment scheduled for autopay via [Redacted] didn't go through. While I typically trust this system and didn't manually verify the payment, I've had no previous issues and other bill payments went through without a hitch. I never anticipated this glitch with Kohl 's. 

Surprisingly, Kohl 's didn't reach out until my payment was 30 days overdue. I immediately settled the payment and attempted to dispute the credit reporting. Despite my longstanding positive history with Kohl 's, the representatives and managers stated that the bank fraud incident wasn't their concern and that the credit report would stand as is. 

My diligent efforts to maintain good credit have been tarnished by a situation beyond my control. I was vigilant in making the payment as soon as I realized it hadn't been processed by the bank. Since then, I've been proactive in making timely payments. Given my consistent record of timely payments, it's disheartening to think that this isolated incident could impact my credit report for the next decade. I'm kindly requesting a thorough review of this matter. Please advise on any further steps necessary.

metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing to express my deep concern regarding your practices in validating debts that are not associated with my credit report. It has come to my attention that several collections accounts have been added to my credit report without proper validation, despite my repeated attempts to rectify this issue. 

I have made numerous requests to have these debts reviewed and validated, providing supporting documentation that clearly demonstrates that these accounts are not mine. However, I have consistently faced refusal from your organization to conduct a thorough investigation into these discrepancies. 

Furthermore, I am deeply troubled by the fact that the same unverified information continues to be included in my credit report, negatively impacting my creditworthiness and reputation. This not only violates my rights as a consumer but also undermines the integrity of the credit reporting system. 

I demand that you immediately cease reporting these unverified debts on my credit report and take immediate action to rectify this situation. It is crucial that you conduct a comprehensive review of the information provided and remove any inaccuracies without delay. 

I also insist that you provide me with a detailed explanation of the steps you will be taking to address this issue and prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future. Additionally, I request a written confirmation of the actions taken to correct my credit report. 

Please be aware that I am prepared to pursue all available legal remedies, including filing a complaint with the appropriate regulatory authorities if necessary, to ensure that my rights as a consumer are protected and that my credit report reflects accurate and verified information. 

I expect a prompt response to this complaint, including a timeline for resolving this matter satisfactorily. Failure to address this issue adequately will leave me with no choice but to escalate my concerns further. 

Thank you for your immediate attention to this matter.

metadata.full_snippet:
Hi CFPB staff, My student loans are being serviced by EdFinancial. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I received an email from them informing me that on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, they would begin moving my loan to a new student loan servicing system for the purposes of better serving me, and that two weeks after the transfer begins, I will need to register for a new account online to access my loans. Then, as of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, they sent an updated email stating that there was a slight change in the original transfer date of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, and that my loans would be transferred at a later date. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I received an updated email from them stating that effective [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, they would begin moving my loan to a new student loan servicing system to, once again, better serve me, and, once again, that [Redacted] weeks after the transfer begins, I will need to register for a new account online to access my loans. Finally, on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I received an email stating that there has been a slight delay in the original estimated transfer date of my loans to the new servicing system, and that Edfinancial is working to ensure my information is transferred over as quickly as possible. 

It is now [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, over two weeks after EdFinancial 's last correspondence regarding the status of my account, and almost 3 months to the date of their first email. As you know, student loan interest begins accruing again on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], now a week away, and I have not heard any updates from EdFinancial regarding the status of my account. When I access my old account on EdFinancial, the records are not accurate as it shows I have no loan balance and does not include any history of my prior payments. I have tried calling EdFinancial during working business hours, but am met with long hold times of over [Redacted] minutes. There are numerous threads on websites such as Reddit.com of other student loan borrowers in the same position due to EdFinancial 's lack of communication and transparency. 

I am writing this complaint because I am worried that, given student loan interest begins accruing in one week, and given EdFinancial 's previous statements that I would need to wait two weeks after the account transfer to make a new account, that when I receive a new account with EdFinancial, I will be unable to access my loan accounts and submit payments to my loans before the interest begins accruing. I am worried that due to EdFinancial 's lack of adequate communication, myself and other student loan borrowers will be adversely affected when the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] deadline arrives. It is absolutely unacceptable for a company that holds our student loans to have done this migration to a new system, technical difficulties abound, right before student loan payments were to resume- they've had three years! 

If needed, I am happy to provide copies of all correspondence as well. 

Any help would be greatly appreciated. Thank You.

The first issue is SPS failed to reconcile my escrow account before the sale and overcharged by roughly {$2300.00}. 

After the closing, I contacted SPS to request an escrow reconciliation, which they provided dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, and mailed to [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted], and I received via USPS. 

Since the property sale, I have continuously called SPS to get my escrow account refund. Each time I called, I was informed that a check had been mailed, and they would proceed with re-issuing a new check and a stop payment on the old check. Note that the USPS had been notified to forward all my mail to my new mailing address, and no check was ever received. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, an account representative informed me that the check had been cashed on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, and no new check would be reissued. I have two issues : ( 1 ) I had called several times before [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, and this is the first time I've heard of an issue, and ( 2 ) I never received or cashed this check. During this call, I requested a copy of the cashed check to move forward and file a fraud complaint, and I have yet to receive it via USPS. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I called SPS, letting them know I had not received any correspondence regarding my request for a copy of the cash check. I was told it would be re-requested to be mailed out again, AND I am assuming to be mailed out again means via USPS, not paperless on their platform, which I can not access anymore. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and [Redacted] [Redacted] I received two emails to review my SPS account for new correspondence. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I tried logging in several times and seemed locked out of the account. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I called SPS twice to have a representative help me reset my account password to access their platform to review my documents. I was informed that I no longer have access to their platform since my loan has been paid off ; however, they're sending paperless communication through that platform and not using USPS. 

For the last six months, I have been trying to get back my overpayment of approximately {$2.00} from SPS Loan Servicing. metadata.full_snippet:
In accordance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S. Code 1681 ), it is vital to emphasize the findings of Congress, which highlight the significance of accurate credit reporting for the efficiency of the banking system. Marketed as consumer reporting agencies ( CRAs ), these entities play a crucial role in assembling and evaluating consumer credit information. However, the Big 3 CRAs rely on data from smaller CRAs, such as [Redacted], to compile consumer reports. This practice prompts us to be proactive in safeguarding our privacy rights, which is the foundation of this process. 

Identity theft is a paramount concern, and its implications extend beyond the immediate transaction. Consent is essential, and its absence constitutes a breach of privacy. The reporting of unauthorized accounts, without my express written consent, reflects identity theft. CRAs are liable under the law for their negligent and willful noncompliance, as stipulated in 15 U.S. Code 1681n, entailing possible penalties of {$1000.00} per violation. 

Moreover, the practice of buying and selling personal information without consent poses a significant privacy issue. The compilation of a comprehensive report without permission constitutes identity theft. The protection of privacy is a right, not a privilege, and I demand that the agency promptly remove and block the identified information. 

I have meticulously followed the requirements outlined in 15 U.S. Code 1681c-2, as provided by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau . Clear and conspicuous information was not provided to me regarding the reporting of these accounts, as mandated by the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act.

By exercising my rights under 15 U.S. Code 1681c-2 and 15 U.S. Code 1681b ( 2 ), I am seeking a resolution to the violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act. You are now in liability as I have insisted on the immediate removal of the identified items in the past, in line with their legal obligations within four days.

Furthermore, under 15 U.S. Code 1681d, the requirement for proper notification during the creation and furnishing of investigative consumer reports has been overlooked, contravening the law. 

Given the comprehensive evidence I have provided, I am pursuing a resolution to address the FCRA violations and the infringement of my privacy rights.

metadata.title: Money transfer Dispute
metadata.snippet: I am writing to file a formal complaint against Bank of America regarding a series of wire transfers that transpired in [Redacted], [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, which I believe have exposed significant lapses in their security and customer protection protocols. These events have h...
metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing to file a formal complaint against Bank of America regarding a series of wire transfers that transpired in [Redacted], [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, which I believe have exposed significant lapses in their security and customer protection protocols. These events have had a profoundly negative impact on my financial well-being and emotional state. 

In late May, I received a scam call from [Redacted] informing me about a phone number under my name that had been sending fraudulent messages. To address this issue, I was connected to an individual who claimed to be a [Redacted] police officer. This individual manipulated me into believing that I was involved in a secret international money laundering case and that my personal information had been compromised. I was fraud which I totally have no idea and sent totally [Redacted] international wire transfers to [Redacted] and totally around $ [Redacted]. 

The events that followed are deeply troubling : [Redacted]. Failure to Protect Customer : Bank of America facilitated multiple wire transfers totaling a substantial amount to a [Redacted] [Redacted] bank without any substantial safeguards. It was my first time attempting wire transfers of such magnitude, and I was left vulnerable to financial exploitation without any protective measures in place. 
This is the first time I use my account to do wire transfer, and this is huge amount of money. And this is international wire transfer. 
No one from the bank has been texting me to confirm or remind, No one from the bank has been calling me to confirm or remind, No one from the bank has ask me to go in person to confirm or remind to do wire transfers, all leave me online. 

2. Lack of Fraud Notification : Despite the unusual and suspicious nature of these transactions, Bank of America did not exercise due diligence in notifying me of the potential fraudulent activity. No alerts were issued to caution me against the transfers or to verify their legitimacy. 

3. Inadequate Verification Procedures : Bank of America allowed these transactions to occur solely through online channels without requesting in-person verification, which could have served as an additional layer of security. 

[Redacted]. Failure to Detect Suspicious Activity : Bank of America 's systems should have detected and flagged these transactions as unusual and potentially fraudulent, given the circumstances and the magnitude of funds involved. 

In this case, I believe Bank of America shares a significant portion of the responsibility for these events. I urge the CFPB to consider the bank 's accountability in this matter and request that Bank of America return 50 % of the fraudulently transferred funds to my account as a demonstration of their acknowledgment of their role in this situation. While I understand that I should have been more vigilant, I also believe that the bank could have taken measures to prevent this incident. 

I AM NOT SAYING THAT THE BANK SHOULD 100 % RETURN MY MONEY BACK. I ONLY WANT THE BANK TO TAKE THEIR PART OF RESPONSIBILITY, WHICH IS 50 % OF THE FRAUD PROTECTION. AND RETURN 50 % OF MY MONEY BACK. 

I kindly request the CFPB 's intervention in this matter to ensure that Bank of America thoroughly investigates and addresses these grave lapses in security and customer protection. Additionally, I request your assistance in any potential efforts to recover 50 % of the funds that were fraudulently transferred from my account. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. I look forward to your response and assistance in resolving this distressing situation.

metadata.title: Money transfer Dispute
metadata.snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/23 I joined Chipper Cash ( hereafter referred to as " *CC '' ). It took a couple tries to get my acct verified, then I sent {$670.00} to my loved one in [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted], who I've been supporting for over 12 years. He received it immediat...
metadata.full_snippet:
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/23 I joined Chipper Cash ( hereafter referred to as " *CC '' ). It took a couple tries to get my acct verified, then I sent {$670.00} to my loved one in [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted], who I've been supporting for over 12 years. He received it immediately & used it. It hadn't been deducted from my bank acct a week later, so I emailed *CC. 
I've emailed them at least 25x ( with responses from 8-12 different names all on the same thread - some auto-generated & some actually written ). I've also called them 8-10x. The first time, a lady answered & got rather snippy w/me, but every other time a guy named 'Kano ' answers . ( He calls this 'an edge case '. ) I've also contacted my local bank branch 2-4x & the bank headquarters at least 3x. They tell me that *CC tried to access my SAVINGS acct ( vs CHECKING ), so I informed *CC of this - TWICE. The 2nd time, they emailed me right away & said it was fixed, so I tried again to 'load ' {$670.00} on the app, & it seemed to process. That was weeks ago, & it still hasn't been deducted from my bank acct altho it SHOWS that I added {$670.00} both times. 
I tried to 'stop payment ' thru my bank, but they CAN'T bc there's no record of *CC trying to take the money! I'm wondering, if *CC DOES become able to withdraw the payment, will they take it TWICE ( since the app shows that I added it two different times 2 months apart )?

It seems that, since I owe THEM money, THEY'D be anxious to GET IT, but they've treated me as if I'M trying to get money FROM them. 
So crazy!

metadata.snippet: In [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] my card used to edd benefits was personally cut up by my self. I thought the pandemic relief was ending. I learned after that there was an extension but I was put in a process that required me to complete a IDMe verification before any payments...
metadata.full_snippet: In [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] my card used to edd benefits was personally cut up by my self. I thought the pandemic relief was ending. I learned after that there was an extension but I was put in a process that required me to complete a IDMe verification before any payments were made. However I was to certify for benefits as normal while waiting for a email letting me know it was my turn to go through IDMe. I did certify like I was suppose to but never did receive a email.for IDMe. It took many months just to get ahold of the car edd. Once I did I was told that i did not need the IDMe process and that my benefits had already been paid. So I called bank of America to have a replacement card sent to me. I asked the balance and was told there was less than {$1.00} remaining. Completely taken back by this I asked how is it when eds has been paying me and I didn't even know. I never spent any of it. They told me I could not file a claim until I go into my online account to see transactions. I no longer had access to that account nor the email used for it. So that took even more time. Then they wanted a I'd taken into the branch and since mine was not valid I had to wait on a new one to come in the mail. I took it to the branch to verify who I was. Finally a claim was started and since there were over $ [Redacted] transactions it had to be filed in 2 claims. However the representative sent one part of the claim to the claims dept and one part to a different department. The part sent to the claims dept was approved for a little over {$5000.00}. The second part had to be located and repossessed to the claims dept l. This took over a month and that claim for a little over [Redacted] is repeatedly denied. I've ask for investigation to contact me personally but never do they. Many different Supervisors and representatives have placed noted on the account of the error of the two being separated. Showing the approval of the first part and asurring me that it would be taken care of and approved each time. I've asked.for information about the denials. All I get is a list of transcription and told I approved them. It's been nearly 2 years of reconciliation that are promised to end in my favor that don't. The fact that they allowed over {$16000.00} to be taken from my account is one thing. However the fact there was never a physical card to be used and not one red flag was put on my account for exsessive online transactions. Just seeing the transaction history prior should have put an alert for suspicious activity. Not once was the account locked up while these transactions where made. But once they granted the first part of the claim my card was locked every day almost for suspicious activity and I have to call and verify my identity to unlock it. Again not once during the deration of spending {$16000.00} online did they ever seen that necessary.. I'm overly frustrated being as I've lost a lot ..my place to live my car, my storage and it does not seem to be any fair resolution comming
