metadata.snippet: They duped me when I asked about their services. I had explained to them I had previously done my own credit repair and disputed everything myself with success. I hired [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] to see if they could help me out further. They gave me my money back and said ...
metadata.full_snippet: They duped me when I asked about their services. I had explained to them I had previously done my own credit repair and disputed everything myself with success. I hired [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] to see if they could help me out further. They gave me my money back and said you've done everything already theres really nothing else to do, good job. Now I explained this to Lexington Law, that I was willing to do all the paperwork, disputes, pay for deletes on my own and felt capable. My concern was regarding about 4-6 negative accounts showing up as charged-off on my account while i was severely incapacitated and moving from place to place in the middle of corona with poor income, lost my job due to health problems. I said, do you have ways of getting charged-off items removed and how effective are you at doing so? They assured me they should be able to get all the charged off items removed with a combination of a few different letters. I spent hundreds of dollars paying lexington law while they did everything I would've done but slower and less efficiently. I wasted {$370.00} ( maybe more I think I paid one of the monthly fees from a different account ) and the only dispute they resolved for me was deleting a collection account from [Redacted] which took them 2 days and probably wouldve taken me the same. They didn't get this collection account removed from all 3 bureaus, they somehow managed to get it off of one while finding it too difficult to remove from the other two bureaus. This was the only thing they accomplished for me. They did literally two days of easy work resulting in the first removal, which gave me hope that they knew what they were doing. From the months of [Redacted] through [Redacted] I was paying for them to get most if not all of the collections accounts in good standing like their recruiter promised me. Out of the 12 items between 3 bureaus i needed help fixing due to medical emergencies in a pandemic and losing my job, they succeeded in removing only one item and they couldn't even get that item deleted from [Redacted] and [Redacted] so they did not help me save myself from unnecessary debt for an account I didn't believe I owed a cent to. I wouldve fought the validity of it over and over again knowing there was false info on it and worst case scenario if I didnt pay lexington law, I'd be able to pay off debts which would boost my credit score much more than 4 months of lexington law services could accomplish. They charged illegal advance fees making me pay for the credit report up front even though I can obtain them for free and already had. They misled me about their services by convincing me they had tactics beyond just debt validation, goodwill deletion, and pay-for-delete strategies. They made it seem like even though I was incapacitated for a year and missed payments on 4 major accounts for a year without access to a working phone or safe shelter, they could get those charged off accounts removed. I specifically asked the recruiter on the phone if theres a large chance that they can be removed EVEN if every single charge off is validated. They said they had many tactics that were very successful. Accomplishing 1 out of 12 assured goals for a hefty sum of money that could've been used to simply pay back lenders is completely unacceptable to me. They didn't even send out letters or take over communication with the creditors so I wasn't burdened by all the work. They would send me templates that took 10 minutes to draft up and are offered for free downloads on their own website for non paying members. And I was expected to send most of the letters in and try to send lexington law all the letters id receive back from these companies. They assured me they would exceed expectations and accomplish more than I could do on my own for free, and that was a complete lie. Either they blatantly lied about the effectiveness of their services or they are purposefully dragging out this project working at an extremely slow speed to get paid more. Without results.

metadata.full_snippet: I run an mobile clothing business and I used square as my merchant. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/23 I had an customer place multiple orders totaling out to {$800.00}. The money was not available in my account but Ive processed multiple payments so I thought nothing of it. Hours later I get an email stating my account is under review and I need to provide documentation. Ok no big deal, provide the docs and then I waited for an response. Didnt receive one by the next day, so I called customer support and was told that all my documents and answers except one had been verified. The customer service representative told me call back at [Redacted] and it should be cleared. A couple hours later I received an email stating that my account is being closed. I immediately called customer support back and was told that they decided to close my account, but couldnt disclose the reasoning because its an program who runs the information and decides. I believe it was done in error because I havent broken the terms and conditions and there is nothing fraudulent going on. I talked to the customer to make sure it wasnt a chargeback or anything and the customer sent me screenshot of the money leaving his account. So square definitely has the money and are telling me they cant release it until [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. As a [Redacted]  [Redacted]  and a [Redacted]  [Redacted]  [Redacted]  this wait time is unbelievable. My square account has never had a chargeback, a fraudulent payment, has had transfers in and out multiple times. I dont understand how or why it was closed, and how they can hold legitimate money for three months. I also was told by a representative that I could refund the money back to customer and accept a different method, but the customer already has the items. That isnt financially safe for me.

metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing to bring to your attention a concerning situation involving my application for an American Express [Redacted] Card. Despite successfully applying for the card, I never received confirmation of approval or the actual card itself. Subsequently, unauthorized usage occurred on the card, resulting in fraudulent charges and an account that was sent to collections. 

Here is a concise summary of the events : Application : I applied for the American Express [Redacted] Card through the designated application process. While I received an acknowledgment of my application submission, I never received any further communication confirming approval or the mailing of the card. 

Unauthorized Usage : To my surprise, I discovered that unauthorized transactions were being made on the American Express [Redacted] Card, indicating that the card had been issued and was being used without my knowledge or consent. This raised serious concerns about the security of my personal information.

Card Theft : It became evident that the card had been mailed out to an incorrect address. Unfortunately, the card fell into the wrong hands, and an unknown individual stole the card to initiate unauthorized transactions.

Account Closure : Once I became aware of the unauthorized activity, I immediately contacted American Express to report the fraudulent charges and the unauthorized usage of the card. The account was subsequently closed to prevent any further misuse. 

Collections and Damage : Despite taking swift action to report the unauthorized usage and close the account, I was informed that the account had been sent to collections due to outstanding charges that had accumulated as a result of the fraudulent transactions. The total amount sent to collections is {$1400.00}. 

Ineffective [Redacted] [Redacted] : The card 's issuance to the wrong address, coupled with the subsequent unauthorized usage, underscores a severe breakdown in the card delivery and security processes. 

This situation has caused significant distress, financial burden, and damage to my credit. I am seeking your assistance in resolving this matter promptly. I believe that the circumstances surrounding the unauthorized usage of the American Express [Redacted] Card are a result of systemic vulnerabilities in the card issuance and delivery processes, which require a thorough investigation to prevent similar incidents from happening to other consumers. 

I kindly request that you investigate this matter and work with American Express to rectify the situation, including the removal of the erroneous charges from collections, restoring my credit standing, and addressing the security gaps that allowed this situation to occur. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to a swift resolution and appreciate your efforts in safeguarding consumers ' financial well-being.

metadata.full_snippet: According to the Fair Credit Reporting Act 15 USC 1681 section 602 states, " There is a need to ensure that consumer reporting agencies exercise their responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and a respect for the consumer 's right to privacy. '' [Redacted], [Redacted], and [Redacted] are Consumer reporting agencies, and I am the Consumer. I have the right to make sure my private information isn't shared, as noted in 15 USC 6801, which states, " It is the policy of the Congress that each financial institution has an affirmative and continuing obligation to respect the privacy of its customers and to protect the security and confidentiality of those customers ' nonpublic personal information. '' American Express is a financial institution by definition under that title. 15 USC 1681 section 604 a section 2 states, " In general, Subject to subsection ( c ), any consumer reporting agency may furnish a consumer report under the following circumstances and no other : following the written instructions of the consumer to whom it relates. '' American Express, the financial institution, and the Consumer reporting agencies [Redacted], [Redacted], and [Redacted] do not have my consent to furnish this information, and they do not have my written permission. All acquiescence to [Redacted], [Redacted], and [Redacted], American Express, whether verbal, non-verbal, written, implied, or otherwise, is revoked. 15 USC 6802 ( b ) ( c ) declares that " A financial institution may not disclose nonpublic personal information to a nonaffiliated third party unless the consumer is elucidated how the consumer can exercise that nondisclosure option. '' They never informed me of my right to exercise my nondisclosure option. Not only that, 15 USC 1681C ( a ) ( 5 ) discloses, '' Except as authorized under subsection ( b ), no consumer reporting agency may make any consumer report containing any of the following items of information Any other adverse item of information, other than records of convictions of crimes which antedates the report by more than seven years. '' [Redacted] and [Redacted] are not maintaining reasonable procedures. Furthermore, 12 CFR 1016.7 states, " A consumer may exercise the right to opt out at any time. '' I am opting out of reporting services. ''

metadata.issue: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage
metadata.snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], as part of a mortgage refinancing condition from AmeriSave Mortgage Corp., I received a grossly negligent appraisal on my intown [Redacted] house from [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] in Georgia. The [Redacted] sq. ft. home was sorely underval...
metadata.full_snippet:
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], as part of a mortgage refinancing condition from AmeriSave Mortgage Corp., I received a grossly negligent appraisal on my intown [Redacted] house from [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] in Georgia. The [Redacted] sq. ft. home was sorely undervalued at {$390000.00}, and the appraisal was filled with inaccuracies and omissions. The appraisal omitted or disregard the attached two-story [Redacted] sq. ft. deck, the attached carport, the [Redacted] storage room, and several appliances. The appraisal also falsely asserted that the house was not in an appreciating neighborhood, when values in the area has been and still are increasing, and it did not upwardly adjusted the value of the comparables accordingly. 

I immediately appealed to both the lender AmeriSave and the appraiser [Redacted]. The lender said that I can only use their assigned third-party company [Redacted] for any appraisals or reconsiderations. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I filed an appeal for reconsideration and a supplemental appeal, detailing every negligence or error made by the appraiser. The appraiser responded on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] with a denial of my appeal, and not changing the appraisal at all, keeping the appraised value at {$390000.00} meanwhile, not addressing any of the several points of error that I brought up in my reconsideration request. 

In the meanwhile, I sought a second appraisal opinion from an independent, highly reputable appraiser, [Redacted] [Redacted]. [Redacted] [Redacted]  appraisal was more detailed and carefully prepared. The appraisal, dated using the same facts of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], was {$430000.00} an almost 9 % difference in valuation. I also provided [Redacted] [Redacted] with the original appraisal from [Redacted] as well as my reconsideration request and the companys response. He noted the various errors made by the previous appraiser [Redacted]. 

Unfortunately, this negligent, erroneous appraisal by [Redacted], the company that AmeriSave insisted that I use for appraisal, was {$5000.00} less than the minimum {$400000.00} required to receive the rate-locked refinance loan at 3.125 %, and as rates had just begun to skyrocket, I was forced to accept the loan at 4.275 % which although lower than todays current rates, is quite a significant difference in monthly and longterm payments. In addition, I as the homeowner suffered other major financial and market losses due to the unfair and negligently prepared appraisal of the home.

metadata.full_snippet:
I was using the SELF app today [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 because I have a credit card and a credit builder account with them. On their app, there is something called Rent and Bills, it states Get a credit boost by adding your rent payments and bills. It then continues to ask for your bank information using plaid so you can sign in and pick the bills you want to use for an additional credit score boost. After, and only after they take all your information and sign in to your bank account seeing all your payments and charges, they then ask you to pay a monthly subscription to get the boost. This is very deceptive and it is not right! I have pictures from the app. I proceeded to chat with SELF customer service in the app chat section, got a live agent and asked them to remove my information immediately. SELFs own agent responded with you will have to contact a different company! Called [Redacted]. I went to [Redacted] and their agent [Redacted] [Redacted] replied with Please know, your rent+bills account and self account was a separate account however, rent+bill is another feature that self offers. I see and I understand where you're coming from. For your rent+bills ( [Redacted] ) account I see that you don't have a subscription yet but I see that you already linked your bank account. I can delete your bank if you're not ready to use your rent+bills account. 

The add was on the app itself that listed my account details for my credit card, overview, options to make a credit card payment, and then the same type of list stated boost your credit with your rent and bills. This wasnt a little add with an [Redacted]. This was just listed nonchalantly as if it were apart of my credit building service. 


I didnt get to screenshot the last photo after adding my bank info and selecting the bills for the rent boost but take my word for it. They asked me now that they had my info, to please pay a monthly subscription premium of $ [Redacted]But all the other photos are ones that lead up to that page and nowhere does it disclose that payment or purchase is necessary! Im sorry but im not going to add my bank details again just to get the screenshot of the company asking for money. Unless someone explicitly asks me from the consumer affairs.

metadata.sub_issue: Reporting company used your report improperly
metadata.snippet: The Fair Credit Reporting Act 15 USC 1681 section 602 a states " There is a need to insure that consumer reporting agencies exercise their grave responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and a respect for the consumers right to privacy. '' [Redacted] and Experian are consumer...
metadata.full_snippet:
The Fair Credit Reporting Act 15 USC 1681 section 602 a states " There is a need to insure that consumer reporting agencies exercise their grave responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and a respect for the consumers right to privacy. '' [Redacted] and Experian are consumer reporting agencies and I am the Consumer. I have the right to make sure my private information isn't shared which is backed by 15 USC 6801 which states " It is the policy of the Congress that each financial institution has an affirmative and continuing obligation to respect the privacy of its customers and to protect the security and confidentiality of those customers nonpublic personal information. '' [Redacted] [Redacted] is a financial institution by definition under that title. 

15 USC 1681 section 604 a section 2 states that " In general Subject to subsection ( c ), any consumer reporting agency may furnish a consumer report under the following circumstances and no other : in accordance with the written instructions of the consumer to whom it relates. '' [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted] and Experian do not have my consent to furnish this information and they surely do not have my written consent. Any and all consent to [Redacted], Experian, and [Redacted] [Redacted] whether it be verbal, non-verbal, written, implied or otherwise is revoked. 

15 USC 6802 ( b ) ( c ) states that " A financial institution may not disclose nonpublic personal information to a nonaffiliated third party unless the consumer is given an explanation of how the consumer can exercise that nondisclosure option. '' [Redacted] [Redacted] never informed me of my right to exercise my nondisclosure option. 

Not only that 15 USC 1681C ( a ) ( 5 ) states '' Except as authorized under subsection ( b ), no consumer reporting agency may make any consumer report containing any of the following items of information Any other adverse item of information, other than records of convictions of crimes which antedates the report by more than seven years. '' This account is an adverse item they are reporting again without my permission which is against the law.

15 U.S. Code 1681s2 ( A ) ( 1 ) A states " A person shall not furnish any information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if the person knows or has reasonable cause to believe that the information is inaccurate. 15 U.S. Code 1681e states '' Every consumer reporting agency shall maintain reasonable procedures designed to avoid violations of section 1681c of this title and to limit the furnishing of consumer reports to the purposes listed under section 1681b of this title. [Redacted] and Experian are not maintaining reasonable procedures. Also 12 CFR 1016.7 states that " A consumer may exercise the right to opt out at any time. '' I am opting out of your reporting services. 

[Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  [Redacted]

I have in my possession an inaccurate copy of my consumer credit report from the Corporation and your financial agency. This report was lawfully obtained by me, through the declaration of the rights granted to consumers under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. 


The Fair Credit Reporting Act has specific requirement for the accurate reporting of an item when it appears on a consumers credit report. 



[Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  ) FURNISHING reports in connection with credit or insurance transaction That are not initiated by consumer.

The Fair Credit Reporting Act specifically details that all items within a consumers credit report must be reported with 100 % accurate information ( not 99.9 % or less ), must be 100 % verifiable ( not 99.9 % or less ), must be 100 % complete information ( not 99.9 % or less ), and must only be reported during the allowable reporting periods as detailed in the Act for the specific item as it appears. metadata.full_snippet: I filed a Bankruptcy in [Redacted]  with the federal court in Georgia in [Redacted]. The bankruptcy was transferred onto my private consumer report immediately after from the three major credit bureaus that are private entities and not of government agencies : [Redacted], [Redacted], and Experian. The federal court has a system PACER ( Public Access to Court Records ) That anyone that pays a fee and established a username and password can access to see any public records of that of consumers. No entity has the legal right to transfer the information onto consumers report without the permission of the consumer and federal court. These bureaus have continuously violated my federal consumer right by adding this public record to my private consumer report. Furthermore, I have provided the proof that the federal court does not report bankruptcies on consumers report and the bureaus have failed to provide proof r that the reporting is legal. The CFPB has done nothing to support me as the consumer. They have only reached out to the reporting agencies and when the agencies have only validated that I have a bankruptcy but failed to validate the reporting of the bankruptcy is legally reported, the CFPB has then closed the case without proof. There has been no true justice served. The reporting of the bankruptcy has ruined my reputation and has hindered me from getting lines of credit and jobs in the past. If any creditor would like to know if I have a bankruptcy they can access the PACER system like the credit bureaus have done to view that Public report, this should not be viewed on my private consumer credit report and I am requesting all of the reporting bureaus to remove this bankruptcy immediately.

We terminated our service with [Redacted] and anticipated a final itemized bill. [Redacted] never provided an itemized bill, only a total amount that we owed. I spent countless hours on the phone with [Redacted] in an attempt to get them to provide us with an itemized final bill. They refused and threatened to turn us over to collections. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I was contacted via telephone by a representative of Sequium Asset Solutions , LLC ( A debt collection company owned by [Redacted] ). Her name was [Redacted] [Redacted] and that phone call took place at approximately [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] I politely informed [Redacted] that I was aware of my rights under the Fair Debt collection Practices Act. I then requested that any and all future communications take place in the form of letter mail exclusively. 

Shortly thereafter, we received an official letter from Sequium Asset Solutions , LLC informing us that they were now responsible for collecting the debt. In response to this letter I crafted a letter requesting debt validation and mailed it promptly. 

In our letter we requested all the pertinent information needed for us to adequately determine whether the debt they said we owed is valid. We informed them that If their offices fail to respond to this validation request within 30 days from the date of receipt, all references to this account must be deleted and completely removed from my credit file and a copy of such deletion request shall be sent to me immediately. 

We never received a response to this letter. 

[Redacted] [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] - [Redacted] sent a pair of Senior Business Account Executives to our business to try to discuss this debt with us. I politely informed them that their method of contacting us could be a violation of federal law and that any and all communication should be done via letter mail as originally requested. 

This improper action by [Redacted] and their Senior Business Account Executives is the reason for my report today. Based on my understanding of the Law this action on their part may have violated my rights.

metadata.snippet: Subject : Urgent Complaint : SCRA Violation, Signature Forgery, Unlawful Debt Collection, Unreported Rent Assistance, and Violation of Legal Procedures by Rent Recovery Solutions Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am writing to urgently bring to your attention an egregi...
metadata.full_snippet:
Subject : Urgent Complaint : SCRA Violation, Signature Forgery, Unlawful Debt Collection, Unreported Rent Assistance, and Violation of Legal Procedures by Rent Recovery Solutions Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am writing to urgently bring to your attention an egregious situation involving Rent Recovery Solutions, a debt collection agency. It is my firm belief that my rights as a consumer and my legal protections as a servicemember have been severely infringed upon, necessitating your immediate intervention and investigation. 

To offer necessary context, I cosigned for an apartment with my mother, aiming to assist her, before my lease was set to expire. My decision was predicated on the understanding that my mother intended to vacate the apartment within 30 days. Upon enlisting in the United States military, I responsibly informed the apartment complex office of my impending departure, supported by documentary evidence of my military orders. 

However, it has now come to my attention that my mother potentially forged my signature, extending the lease without my consent or knowledge. Despite my complete unawareness, this extended lease was executed. Approximately six months into my military service, Rent Recovery Solutions, seemingly in possession of my income and employment documentation, initiated a debt collection process predicated on a debt traced back to a previous lease. It is my conviction that this debt is intrinsically tied to the extended lease, an extension which I had no knowledge of signing. 

As a servicemember, my rights under the Service Member Civil Relief Act ( SCRA ) hold profound significance. Not only does this Act offer protections from unjust legal actions during military service, but it also necessitates adherence to proper legal procedures. Evidently, my mother 's potential signature forgery and unilateral lease extension may have transgressed these procedures, bypassing my explicit consent and awareness.

Furthermore, I have recently discovered that my mother received a substantial rent assistance stipend amounting to {$15000.00} from an unfamiliar entity. Disturbingly, she neglected to communicate this significant development to me. This undisclosed rent assistance introduces further complexity to the situation and casts doubt on the legitimacy of the debt claim asserted by Rent Recovery Solutions.

Of equal concern is the potential violation of SCRA provisions. The SCRA stipulates that if a landlord or property manager seeks a court order through a default judgment, they are mandated to file an affidavit apprising the court of the tenant 's military status. Should the tenant be in military service, the court must appoint a guardian ad litem to represent the servicemember 's interests. Additionally, the court retains the prerogative to postpone judgment by 90 days if the servicemember is uncontactable or their appearance is required for defense. 

The multifaceted nature of these violations alarms me profoundly. I am urgently requesting your thorough investigation into the practices of Rent Recovery Solutions, with a specific focus on potential SCRA breaches, potential signature forgery, debt collection without legal grounds, nondisclosure of rent assistance, and deviation from legal procedures. 

Moreover, I am in great need of your expert guidance on the steps I must take to address this intricate matter and protect my rights as both a consumer and a servicemember. Your timely assistance and support are of paramount importance as I endeavor to rectify this deeply unsettling situation. 

Thank you for dedicating your time to this matter of utmost urgency. I am eagerly awaiting your response and assistance in rectifying this distressing situation.

metadata.full_snippet:
Consumer Financial Protection Bureau [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  [Redacted], Iowa [Redacted] Subject : Appeal Regarding Unsatisfactory Veterinary Service Dispute with Chase Freedom Card I am writing to appeal to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau for assistance with a recent transaction dispute on my Chase Freedom card. The transaction in question pertains to a service provided by a veterinarian for the treatment of my dog and cat. The transaction took place on [Redacted] of [Redacted] with [Redacted] [Redacted] for amount of [Redacted] dollars. 

Briefly summarized, my pets were administered steroid injections by this new veterinarian with the expectation that it would alleviate their symptoms, including itching, swelling, hotspots, biting, and licking paws. Sadly, three days post-treatment, not only have their symptoms persisted, but they have also significantly worsened. 

Given the lack of improvement and the deteriorating health of my pets, I contacted Chase Freedom 's customer service to dispute the charge, hoping for an understanding and resolution. However, their approach towards the situation was unyielding. They suggested I consult another veterinarian and produce a statement that confirms the ineffectiveness of the previous treatment. While I understand the need for verification, I found this requirement burdensome and potentially inconclusive. A secondary veterinarian, without prior knowledge of my pets ' condition pre-treatment, would be ill-equipped to provide a definitive comparative statement. 

Furthermore, I inquired if Chase would bear the costs for this secondary consultation since it was a condition they imposed, but this was declined. It feels unjust that, in seeking redress for a service that was ineffective, I am compelled to incur further expenses, with no guarantee that they would be recouped. 

It is important to understand that my dispute is not based on mere dissatisfaction but the tangible worsening of my pets ' conditions post-treatment. It is disheartening that the resolution offered involves additional financial and emotional stress for me. 

I kindly request the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to intervene and guide this matter to a fair resolution. I genuinely believe that I should not be held accountable for charges related to services that not only failed to deliver their promised results but also led to further complications for my pets. 

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter. I trust in the CFPB 's mission to ensure consumers like myself are treated justly in financial dealings and look forward to your guidance. 

Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
metadata.snippet: Notice for Proof of Claim Account : PENN CREDIT CORPORATION [Redacted] [Redacted]oWhom it may Concern : This is a this complaint is submitted Under OHIO LAW U.C.C1319.12 Taking assignment of debts States ( C ) No collection agency shall commence litigation for the collection of a...
metadata.full_snippet: Notice for Proof of Claim Account : PENN CREDIT CORPORATION [Redacted] [Redacted]oWhom it may Concern : This is a this complaint is submitted Under OHIO LAW U.C.C1319.12 Taking assignment of debts States ( C ) No collection agency shall commence litigation for the collection of an assigned account, bill , or other evidence of indebtedness unless it has taken the assignment in accordance with all of the following requirements : Credit contracts are non-assignable even if the contract has a clause for assign ability because it violates contract Law. Where there is no fair valuable consideration given, the contract or agreement is void ab inito. The debt is non-transferable. If it is a contract for credit or goes to the character of the parties, it can not be transferred or assigned. No state can make a law impairing contracts, Under OHIO LAW U.C.C 1319.12 Taking assignment of debts ( 3 ) The assignment was manifested by a written agreement separate from and in addition to any document intended for the purpose of listing the account, bill, or other evidence of indebtedness with the collection agency. The written agreement shall state the effective date of the assignment and the consideration paid or given, if any, for the assignment and shall expressly authorize the collection agency to refer the assigned account, bill, or other evidence of indebtedness to an attorney admitted to the practice of law in this state for the commencement of litigation. The written agreement also shall disclose that the collection agency may consolidate, for purposes of filing an action, the assigned account, bill, or other evidence of indebtedness with those of other creditors against an individual debtor or co-debtors. Dartmouth College v. Woodward 4 Wheat 518 : White v. Hart, 13 Id 646. Once the Creditor writes off a debt, it can not be assigned or collected. Since this is an error I demand that you send me the following proofs. As you are obligated to do in accordance with the Fair Debt Collection Practice Act. Section 1692 ( g ) : Under the Law, FDCPA, Section 1692 ( g ), you have 30 days to supply these proofs, if more time is needed please contact me by certified mail and I will extend you 15 extra days. I also request to see a certified copy of any contract or agreement between you and the original creditor that gave you the right to collect this debt.

metadata.snippet: I applied for an Employment Development Department card and received a benefits card in [Redacted] through Bank of America. I made transactions from [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I checked the balance of...
metadata.full_snippet: I applied for an Employment Development Department card and received a benefits card in [Redacted] through Bank of America. I made transactions from [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I checked the balance of my card of {$4700.00}. After this day, I decided to stop making transactions and let my benefits accumulate for the purpose of using the money for another payment in the future. I did not check on any statements, because I entrusted that Bank of America would have secured my benefits and notify me of any suspicious activity or fraudulent charges. My card expired on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and I renewed the card. I received the new card on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Upon activating my card with my credentials, I discovered I had a balance of less than [Redacted] dollars. I filed a claim with Bank of America on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] to dispute any unauthorized transactions and requested a copy of all transactions. During speaking with a Bank of America representative, I was asked if I had received the renewed card. I was frustrated in the moment and forgot that I had the new card in my possession and said I never received the card because I was attempting to dispute the fraudulent transactions, not whether I received the card or not. I was frustrated, because my identity was stolen, and my benefits were stolen and wanted to just dispute the transactions. When receiving the document via email, I saw 43 fraudulent transactions totaling up to {$5400.00}. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I received through the mail, a letter from Bank of America stating that my claim was denied because I renewed my card using my credentials and that the card was mailed to my address. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I called Bank of America again requesting to reopen the claim and filed a complaint with Bank of America. I stated that the issue was not whether or not I received the card but that there were fraudulent charges on my EDD card. I was asked to verify my identity via fax. On the same day, I faxed a photo of my government issued identification card and on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I filed a police report documenting the unauthorized transactions and faxed it to Bank of America, along with my government issued ID and photos of the new/expired EDD cards in my possession. Therefore, I am making a complaint about Bank of America. I believe they were negligent and culpably indifferent towards my claim. I entrusted them with the security of my money/benefits and entrusted them to notify me of any fraudulent transactions and or suspicious activity, which they failed to do. I also entrusted them to reimburse the money/benefits that is stolen from me. If only they had made a thorough investigation of my claim by comparing my transactions from [Redacted] to [Redacted] to the unauthorized transactions I am disputing, they would have discovered that all of the fraudulent charges I am disputing were made outside of my area of residence, out of state, and internationally.

To whom it may concern, I am writing to dispute the following issues with my Bank of America credit cards : * The Bank of America Cash Rewards Credit Card has charged me excessive junk fees, which is illegal. 
* The Bank of America Travel Rewards Credit Card is reporting a missed payment on my credit report, even though I never missed a payment and the account is closed. 
I have never missed a payment on either of these credit cards. I have always paid my bills on time and in full. I have also never received any notice from Bank of America about any late payments. 
I believe that Bank of America is violating my consumer rights by charging me excessive junk fees and by reporting a missed payment on my credit report when I never missed a payment. 
The following consumer laws and codes protect me from these practices : * The Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) prohibits creditors from charging excessive fees on credit cards. 
* The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) prohibits creditors from reporting inaccurate or incomplete information on your credit report. 
* The Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ) prohibits unfair, deceptive, or abusive financial practices.

metadata.full_snippet: I submitted a credit card payment of {$180.00} to be paid to [Redacted] [Redacted] on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 from my Wells Fargo checking account. My ending daily balance was {$720.00} on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. There were sufficient funds to make the payment. When I checked my account on the morning Friday, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 I saw the payment was pending out of my account. I checked my account later in the day, and the payment had posted to my account. It was not in pending status anymore. I checked my account several times over the weekend because I was waiting for another deposit to become available. Every time I checked my account, that payment was recorded as posted. Today, I received notification from [Redacted] that my payment had been reversed. I logged into my online account, and there was no record of the transaction anymore. I contacted Wells Fargo to find out where the payment went, and they reversed posted payment overnight on Monday, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], claiming I had insufficient funds for a payment that had already cleared. They also failed to notify me of this. There were SEVERAL transactions made and bills paid after that one transaction. It took longer for the deposit I was waiting on to show up than expected, so I did have to use my overdraft protection from my savings account and my account balance got down to {$22.00}. I monitored the account ALL WEEKEND and all day Monday to make sure there were no issues. On Tuesday [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 is when [Redacted] received notification that the payment had been reversed and they notified me today, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Wells Fargo intentionally changed the order of my transactions and reversed a posted payment. I asked if I could have a printout of the transactions in the order they were processed from my local branch. I was informed by the customer service representative that they have a different view from what he has and no records of how these transactions were processed could be provided to me. I opened a formal complaint with Wells Fargo and was told it could take 12 business days to hear anything. Customers, local branches, and customer service should all have the SAME VIEW. This is MY MONEY. The payment should never have been returned because I had sufficient funds. Additionally, per Wells Fargos own policy, I have access to direct deposits immediately. The additional deposit was available in my account on Monday night, but what my online banking shows now is that it wasnt available until Tuesday morning. Regardless, the funds were there. Because Wells Fargo chose to change the order in which my transactions were processed and delay crediting a deposit, they claim I had insufficient funds and returned a payment that cleared on Friday, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and have now cost me additional fees. metadata.full_snippet:
I have received numerous American Express gift cards from my employers over the past few years. I could use them almost anywhere - [Redacted], [Redacted], other online vendors, grocery stores, sports stadiums. Sometime between [Redacted], all stores stopped accepting my digital cards. 

The cards would be declined by American Express, even though I had sufficient balances on the cards. When I called in to ask about it, American Express representatives assured me that this was to prevent fraud. They explained that they were no longer allowing most online payments for my type of virtual gift card. They assured me I would be able to add the cards to my [Redacted] [Redacted] and use it at brick-and-mortar stores. Contrary to those assurances, the cards were also declined at those stores. 

I can not use these cards anywhere - I have been trying for months. 

I called American Express and asked to have my balances transferred to physical cards. I was told the type of gift card I was given can not be transferred. 

In my discussions with several American Express representatives, they told me that these prepaid gift cards can not be charged too close to their current balance, nor can they be used for partial payments. This policy appears to be designed to skim money from every single gift card. 

I currently have a balance of {$150.00} across four gift cards that I can not use. This was money given to me by my employers. At the time of purchase, these cards were usable - I have used each of them for at least one transaction. Sometime after their purchase, American Express stopped allowing me to use these cards. 

My employers ( the purchasers of these cards ) have been similarly unable to get American Express to release my money. 

American Express Prepaid Card Management Corporation is holding my money hostage and refuses to offer me any viable solutions to release my funds. I have spent hours on the phone talking to multiple company representatives and all they can tell me is that I should try again at another store. They tell me they are working on a resolution but it's been nearly a year with no change. 

Moreover, American Express continues to advertise their gift cards as " Widely Accepted. Use this Gift Card at merchants that accept American Express Cards in the U.S. '' And : " You can use your American Express eGift Card with any United States-based online, phone, or mail-order merchants wherever American Express Cards are accepted . '' This is no longer the case and the company knows this. 

I have found numerous accounts complaining about this issue. Physical cards are more likely to be accepted but digital cards are increasingly hard to use. I am finding it impossible. 

I have also filed a complaint with my state 's AG about this issue.

metadata.full_snippet: In Regards to AMEX ACCT # [Redacted] I am writing to file a formal complaint against AMERICAN EXPRESS for major violations of consumer reporting laws as outlined in the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C . 1681 et seq. ) and other relevant statutes. I have found numerous inaccuracies and unauthorized reporting on my consumer report, which have had a significant impact on my financial well-being. Upon reviewing my consumer report, I have identified several instances where American Express has reported late payments, amounts, balances, dates, and other personal information without obtaining my explicit consent. These actions are in clear violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681c, which mandates that consumer reporting agencies must ensure the accuracy and relevance of the information they report. Furthermore, American Expresss unauthorized disclosure of my personal information to third parties raises concerns under 15 U.S.C. 1681b, which requires that consumer reporting agencies obtain permissible purposes before disclosing consumer information to any third party. Moreover, my rights to privacy are protected under 15 U.S.C. 1681a ( q ), which acknowledges the significance of safeguarding consumer information and ensuring that it is used only for legitimate purposes. The unauthorized dissemination of my personal data by American Express violates these privacy rights and undermines the principles of data protection enshrined in the law. Additionally, American Expresss reporting of my consumer account as late for reasons not justified by a delay in payment violates the provisions of 15 U.S.C. 1666b. This statute prohibits treating a consumer account as late on an open-end consumer credit plan without reasonable cause. The unauthorized designation of my account as late without valid reasons further compounds the violations committed by American Express. I kindly request that the following actions be taken : 1. Immediate removal of all inaccurate and unauthorized items from my consumer report, as mandated by 15 U.S.C. 1681i. 2. Cease and desist selling or disclosing any debts, personal information, or other relevant data pertaining to me to any third parties, both in the present and future, in accordance with 15 U.S.C. 1681c. Furthermore, I am aware of the consumer law provisions regarding willful noncompliance ( 15 U.S.C. 1681n ) and civil liability for willful noncompliance ( 15 U.S.C. 1681o ). Given the egregious nature of the violations committed by American Express, I am prepared to pursue legal action to seek damages for the harm inflicted upon me due to their deliberate noncompliance with consumer reporting laws. I appreciate your attention to this matter and kindly request a prompt investigation into my complaint. If necessary, I am prepared to provide additional documentation and information to support my case. Let this serve as notice to American Express that I am prepared to fully exercise my rights and will pursue damages to the full extent of the law. Thank you for your time and consideration.

metadata.full_snippet:
My Charles Schwab account was frozen on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] or [Redacted] 2023. It is now [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and I still do not have access to my account. I contacted Charles Schwab and they said I simply have to visit a physical branch and verify my identity. I went to the branch on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and provided requested documents. They told me my account will be unlocked in 3 business days. 

After 3 business days my account was still frozen. I contacted Charles Schwab again and was told that their fraud team was still investigating. The agent told me they would email the fraud team for a follow and they should be contacting me in another 3-5 business days. But I received no contact within that time. 

So, I called again. Another agent said they will email the fraud team and they will contact me in 3-5 business days. Again, no contact. 

I then talked to another agent who got ahold of the fraud team. They now said my in-person identity verification wasn't enough. They told me that a Medical Insurance check that I cashed was flagged. And that they need to verify that I was the person that deposited it. The agent told me to back to a physical branch again and verify. I brought the original check to the branch. 

The clerk didn't know what to do with it, so she called someone. Soon to tell me that that the original check was unhelpful. Wasting my time once again. She said she will email the fraud team for an update. Again, I received no such update. 

I was then told my an agent to try and get a letter from my insurance company to verify that the check is mine. My insurance said that don't do that but they can do a group call with the fraud team to verify. Problem is, even Charles Schwab agents struggle to get a hold of the fraud department. 

Also, my insurance said it shows in their system that Charles Schwab have successfully cashed the check. Proving that it is a real check. 

I have prepared my Explanation of Benefits that details and includes the check in question. If they would even accept that document, no agent in the subsequent weeks have been able to contact the fraud department to ask. 

Through the weeks, I have contacted several agents that will " email the fraud team '' and have gotten nowhere. They have held my money for almost 2 months under the guise of " protecting me. '' I have once again called for and update today, just to receive another " email and 3-5 business days '' response. I'm tired of running in circles with this company.

metadata.issue: Problem with the payoff process at the end of the loan
metadata.snippet: I paid off my entire loan on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, which was before the first payment date due date ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 ). I based my payments on the information available to me on the account portal and the statements issued to me. However, today ( [Redacted]/[Red...
metadata.full_snippet: I paid off my entire loan on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, which was before the first payment date due date ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 ). I based my payments on the information available to me on the account portal and the statements issued to me. However, today ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 ) I received a statement that said I had not paid off my principle and that my loan was still accruing interest. After reviewing the documentation available to me, I couldn't figure out why I was being told I owed this amount. I called GoodLeap. Multiple of their representatives admitted that GoodLeap 's portal does not clearly provide information about the outstanding principle or interest, which is why I didn't see accurate information. Given GoodLeap 's acknowledgement that they did not provide clear information or documentation of what I owed, and that lack of information prevented me from making informed payment decisions, I requested that they waive the remaining balance ( {$57.00} ). The workers I spoke with explained they did not have that power but would elevate the challenges I ran into. I ended up paying the remainder off to avoid accruing further interest because I did not know my other options. I'm filing a complaint in the hopes that 1 ) this will spur prompt reforms at GoodLeap so others don't have this situation, or worse, and 2 ) in hopes I can get a refund for the {$57.00} since it was GoodLeap 's fault that I did not have access to accurate information to base my payment decisions ( had I had access to better information I would have avoided paying additional interest ).

I would like to file a complaint against Comenity Capital Bank, which serves as the credit card account company for the [Redacted] stores. They have engaged in a deceitful practice with me, related to compounding late charges and interest charges, while investigating an erroneous past-due charge, even after admitting that the past due charges were in error. I have now closed my account with them. Here is the history. 

I received a bill for [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 stating that I my account was overdue for the amount of {$36.00} ( total amount due for merchandise purchased ) plus a late fee of {$28.00}. The due date had been [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023. However, I had paid the total amount due electronically through my bank [Redacted] [Redacted]  [Redacted] [Redacted] ). I checked my [Redacted]  [Redacted] [Redacted] account online and found that Comenity Bank had withdrawn my funds for on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023. Following the instructions on my bill regarding what to do if I found a mistake on my statement, I wrote a letter to Comenity describing the above with a copy of the confirmation from my bank. 
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I received a letter from Comenity stating that they had received my claim, and although my statements may display additional finance charges and fees, I was not responsible for them during the investigation, and that my account would be adjusted appropriately if the investigation indicated that an error had occurred.

Subsequent statements from Comenity continued to rack up late fees and interest charges while I waited for a conclusion to the investigation. 
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I received a letter from Comenity Bank saying, Good news, your account has been credited! However, they only credited it for the original late fee of {$28.00}. But the letter stated my balance was {$96.00}, which was for merchandise I had purchased. So, I believed they had erased the other late fees and interest charges as well. 
But then I received a phone call from Comenity saying I was late on another payment for [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023. Again, I looked at my [Redacted]  [Redacted] [Redacted] records and the payment of {$98.00} ( which had been my understanding of the merchandise purchase on the bill ) had been withdrawn well before the deadline on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. I was confused and asked to speak with a supervisor, who told me that I owed numerous late and interest charges. I said that I needed to see an itemized bill before I would pay anything more, and she said she would mail it to me. So, I waited to receive it. 
Then again on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I received a phone call from [Redacted] at [Redacted] stating that I had a balance of {$34.00} remaining on my account. At this point I was tired of dealing with them and just wanted it all to stop. [Redacted] said this was the final amount on my statement, so I decided to just pay it. I did so with my debt card, after being reassured that this would result in a [Redacted] balance with Comenity. It was reconciled with my bank on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023. 
Then on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, after thinking everything was done, I received another [Redacted] bill stating I owed {$100.00} in more late fees and interest fees. I had not purchased anything from [Redacted] since [Redacted] and I never will anymore. I called customer service to try and straighten it out, without success. The woman I spoke with insisted that I still owed late fees from several months ago, despite the call from [Redacted] and my payment the prior month. It was futile to argue with her. I went ahead and paid the amount only because I discovered that they had ruined my credit rating. I have had a credit rating of approximately [Redacted] for many years. Because of Comenity Bank it is now [Redacted] points. 
At this point, I thought I was done with Comenity, but I received a phone message from Comenity on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], instructing me to call an [Redacted] number for an important message. When I called this number I found out that I now owed {$130.00}. [Redacted]. So I called a customer representative, who told me my payment of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] had been refunded because it had an incorrect routing number or account number, so Comenity had added another late fee. 
Again because of my fear of further damage to my credit score, I paid this fee through their site. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I looked at my J.Jill/Comenity site and my account stated that my current balance was {$0.00}. And that payment of {$130.00} had been received on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023. 

I am so upset and frustrated by my attempts to correct this situation. I have always paid my bills on time. I believe they have been dishonest with me from the very start, and unresponsive to my pleas to correct these situations. Basically I gave up and paid them money, I did not owe, because the consequences of not doing so, have caused me harm in terms of ruining my credit rating. I would like to have my credit rating restored, and my money for the late fees and interest refunded to me. 

Thank you.

I am writing to address a matter of utmost urgency regarding the payment processing system on the AppFolio portal.

I have observed a concerning discrepancy in the fees applied to transactions conducted through the AppFolio platform. Specifically, the portal advertises a fee of 3.49 % for credit card transactions, while significantly lower flat fees apply to check or debit card payments through the same channel.

However, when I attempted to utilize my debit card on the AppFolio portal, I was unjustly charged the incorrect amount of 3.49 %, resulting in a total charge of {$94.00}. This irregularity has been a source of significant inconvenience and financial strain.

I have taken proactive steps to resolve this matter, initially engaging with AppFolio through the Better Business Bureau ( BBB ) as it became apparent that direct consumer contact channels were not available. Regrettably, my attempts to find a resolution through this avenue have proven fruitless. 

Furthermore, I diligently communicated this issue to my property management company, Personal Property Management ( contact information : [Redacted], located at [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ). They have consistently assured me that this fee discrepancy is beyond their control, as it pertains to a third-party charge facilitated by AppFolio.

Conversely, AppFolio, in their responses via the BBB complaint system, has repeatedly directed me to contact my property manager. This continuous cycle of redirection has created significant frustration, as my property manager lacks the authority to influence or rectify these fees.

As a concerned consumer who values fair and transparent financial transactions, I am earnestly requesting that AppFolio promptly assess fees in accordance with the rates advertised on their portal, thereby ensuring compliance with consumer protection acts.

My primary objective remains the resolution of this situation, and I implore AppFolio to take immediate corrective action to restore fairness and transparency to their payment portal. 

I trust that this matter will receive the attention it warrants and will be addressed with the urgency it demands. Your swift response and resolution are eagerly anticipated.

metadata.full_snippet:
Equifax has egregiously violated my consumer privacy rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

Specifically, Equifax continues to maintain inaccurate and unauthorized information in my credit file, despite previous notification. This includes extensive transaction details that are solely between me, as the consumer, and the companies I do business with. The magnitude of irrelevant transaction data demonstrates Equifax 's willful violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681a ( 2 ) ( A ) ( i ), which strictly prohibits such information.

This ongoing issue was initially raised in CFPB complaint # [Redacted], yet Equifax has failed to adequately address it. I have not provided permission for Equifax to access or use my detailed transaction history, which is a clear violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( 2 ).

In response to the CFPB complaint, Equifax stated that the account SELF/LEAD BANK was verified as accurate pursuant to 15 USC 1681i ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ) ( iii ). I am requesting a description of the specific procedures used by Equifax to determine the accuracy and completeness of this account information during the investigation.

Pursuant to 15 USC 1681i ( a ) ( 7 ), Equifax has 15 days to provide me with the requested investigation information detailing the verification procedures used.

As a trusted custodian of sensitive consumer financial data, Equifax has breached its fiduciary duties by intentionally misusing my information. The unauthorized inclusion of my transaction details exemplifies Equifax 's bad faith and negligent handling of my data.

If prompt action is not taken to permanently delete the inaccurate transaction information and comply with FCRA consumer protections, I will pursue legal action to enforce my consumer rights, including seeking maximum statutory damages under 15 U.S.C. 1681n ( a ) for Equifax 's willful FCRA violations.

Equifax must immediately implement stronger data privacy policies and internal controls to prevent further harm. Please confirm receipt of this notice and provide the requested information within 15 days, as required by the FCRA. I look forward to your timely response.

metadata.full_snippet:
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I sent a list of disputes via certified mail to transunion. I received nothing in regards to my letter and was given no information on any investigation. I called and was told my letter was received but would not be processed, even tho it was mailed certified, along with my state issued Drivers License as well as a copy of my bank statement for address verification. They failed to even process my letter and even stated on the phone that they received a fax copy that was blurry. This was impossible as I personally mailed and signed my letter with blue ink and printed in color. I have the delivery verification. The letter disputed a long list of negative accounts and I made clear to the agent that I was holding them accountable for the letter and all the disputes it listed as there was no valid reason it was not processed. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I sent another dispute letter with additional requests to validate and send me proof of their investigation. Most I requested the proof along with proof of payment status since the account was open. I have delivery verification on this letter as well. 

This time, I did receive a response letter. HOWEVER, I did NOT receive any proof of their investigations at all. Simply their statement on my report that the items were " verified as accurate ''. I received nothing in regards to paperwork proving the accuracy, just their word that the investigation was complete and verified. I asked for proof and they're failed to supply me with any proof from these companies that verified these accounts and their balances or payment history. 

Transunion has been given more than enough time to collect this information, especially if they have " verified '' the accounts as accurate. They certainly failed to send me the proof of the investigation/paperwork of accounts and payment history from the opening of each account proving that there were any late payments or payments made on time or statements showing any kind of accuracy of the transactions made to obtain these totals. 
They failed BIG TIME with my first dispute letter and they should be held accountable for that. No one should have their letter disregarded when it was personally signed, sent via certified mail and sent with adequate verification for identification ( state issued license and copy of my bank statement ). So for them to again mishandle my next letter by not sending me the proof I requested in the time frame they are legally given... .transition should do what they are legally bound to and delete any and all accounts they did not supply me with proof from these companies showing any payment history, monthly statements proving the amount from the opening of the account to prove the totals due and how they got that amount or any proof that verified these accounts to other than their word they did the investigation. Their word is not proof and they did not supply me with any proof. 
We trust these breaus to do the investigations accurately and when proof is requested they should do that. I'm left to wonder how they got these totals, proof of any payments or missed payments. Or if these companies legally own the accounts at all! 
Two+ months they have had for these investigations so not to send me the requested proof is unacceptable.

metadata.full_snippet:
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I unfortunately fell victim to a scam. I thought it an old friend from high school, but apparently their [Redacted] account had been hacked and the malicious actor was posting fake items for sell. I put a deposit down for the item, when they kept asking for more that's when the red flags popped up. I realized I had been scammed so called Venmo to see if they could prevent these transactions from going through since they were still pending, I let them know these were fraudulent payments and that I had been scammed. They seemed to accept my report and opened up an investigation they told me could take up to 30 days. The spokesperson actually recommended I call my bank and try to stop the transaction there. So that's exactly what I did, I put a block on all transactions going to Venmo. No money was transferred out of my account. All is well or so I thought. 

About 3 weeks later on 8-14, I get a call from Venmo stating I have a negative balance on my account for {$500.00} ( Two payments of [Redacted] $ ). Venmo apparently didn't cancel the reported fraudulent charges and ate the transaction value since my bank had blocked all transactions with Venmo. When I spoke with the Venmo representee on the phone he told me that Venmo denied my investigation, so I was responsible for the [Redacted] . 

I informed Venmo the day of, if not minutes after the transaction happened ( it was still pending on Venmo ) that this was fraud. They should have canceled the pending transaction on their end, nor should I be held responsible for the debt. I own up to falling to a scam, but I reported this in a very timely manner to which it could have been prevented. I have read horror stories about Venmo customer service sending folks to debt collection, and therefor affecting their credit score for this same type of thing and do not wish to be part of this statistic. 

I requested the case details/information

metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing to formally dispute the validity of a debt reported by [Redacted] [Redacted] for {$16000.00} on my credit report. I am requesting your immediate intervention in this matter to investigate and remove the debt from my credit report as it is not mine. I have recently obtained a copy of my credit report from [Redacted], [Redacted], and Equifax, and I was surprised to find an entry for a debt from [Redacted] [Redacted] listed as outstanding. I have thoroughly reviewed my financial records and can affirm, without a doubt, that I have never had any business transactions or contractual obligations with [Redacted] [Redacted]. I understand that under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), it is the responsibility of the credit reporting agency to ensure the accuracy and verifiability of the information they report. 

Furthermore, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) has been established to enforce the provisions of the FCRA and protect consumers ' rights. In light of the above, I kindly request that you initiate an investigation into the following matters : Provide a detailed verification of the debt, including the original creditor, date of inception, and any supporting documentation that substantiates the legitimacy of the debt. Verify that [Redacted] [Redacted] has followed all required legal procedures in attempting to collect this alleged debt. Confirm that [Redacted] [Redacted] has complied with all relevant statutes of limitations pertaining to the collection of this debt. Provide evidence of any contractual agreement or documentation with my valid signature, binding me to this alleged debt. I would also like to inform you that the inclusion of this erroneous debt on my credit report has had a significantly negative impact on my creditworthiness and financial well-being. It has affected my ability to obtain credit, secure favorable interest rates, and may have implications for future employment opportunities. I believe it is paramount to rectify this issue promptly to mitigate any further harm caused by this false reporting. Should this dispute not be resolved in a timely manner or if the debt is not conclusively proven to be valid, I will be compelled to pursue legal action to protect my rights under the FCRA, including but not limited to filing a complaint with the CFPB, engaging legal counsel, and seeking appropriate remedies available under the law. 

I appreciate your immediate attention to this matter and request that you provide me with written or emailed confirmation of the receipt of this dispute within 7 days from the date of this complaint. Additionally, I kindly request that you keep me informed of the progress of your investigation and provide me with a detailed response within 15 business days. Thank you for your prompt assistance in this matter. I trust that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau will act diligently and impartially to resolve this dispute and protect my consumer rights. I look forward to a favorable resolution and the removal of this incorrect debt from my credit report.

metadata.full_snippet:
I am a Navy Federal Credit Union Customer. I have been for many years. 

I have been in the market to purchase a used vehicle for the last month. My last vehicle was totaled. Someone rear ended my vehicle, while I was idling at a red light. The journey to find another vehicle has been overwhelming and very tiresome. 

I applied for two pre approved car loans. One through [Redacted] [Redacted] and the other one through Navy Federal Credit Union. I was pre-approved to begin vehicle searches for both [Redacted] [Redacted] and Navy Federal Credit Union. 

I selected to continue the auto process through Navy Federal Credit Union. I searched the Navy Federal Credit Union Used Car Auto site and found a truck. I went to the Federal Credit Union Site to complete my entire car loan application. With no problems, I was approved. The online car loan site gave me several options to choose from for a car loan, but I selected the one with the VIN number option because I had a VIN number. I was not aware that this was a " set in stone option ''. There was no note or " be aware '' notification to say that the promissory note could not be transferred if I did not go with the original Car Dealership. As a consumer, I would not have known this stipulation because it was not explained on the Online Car loan site. 

After several attempts to work with the original Dealership ; the truck failed two pre-inspections. I had no choice to not do business with this dealership. We did not finalize the original paperwork and I did not hand over the check. The check is {$17000.00} ( I was approved for this amount around [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ). It was still at the branch waiting for me to pick up the cashier check. 

I found another truck from a different dealership. The dealership was also located on the exact Navy Federal Credit Union Used Car Auto site. Both dealerships were certified to be honest dealers. The first one did not work out, but the second dealership was honest. The second truck I selected to purchase passed the first pre-inspection. The truck was a good purchase. I made my way to the Navy Federal Credit Union in [Redacted] Texas to pick up the check. 

I waited for 30 minutes to see a bank branch representative. I was able to meet with a bank branch representative and she provided me with the Auto Loan Check with the new Dealership 's name on it. As I proceeded to leave the bank, I noticed the amount of the check was not the same as on the new contract from the new Dealership. I proceeded back into the bank to bring this to the bank branch representative attention. 

She stated she could not alter the amount on the new contract and that I should have the new Dealership to add on new items to equal the check amount of {$17000.00}. This did not make sense so I asked for a branch manager. 

I want to simply ask if the promissory note can be changed to reflect the new dealership. I have research and the Promissory note does not say it can not be altered or transferred by Navy Federal Credit Union. I have already been approved for the {$17000.00} car loan. The new amount is lessor and I have a truck waiting for me at the dealership to purchase. 

I have made several attempts to rectify this matter and no success. I was told to apply for a second car loan and of course I was denied. I would be denied because my Debt to income Ratio has decreased because I have been approved for a {$17000.00} car loan, which is now on my credit. My credit score dropped by [Redacted] points because of the Navy Federal Credit Car loan. I did try to go back to [Redacted] [Redacted]. I was denied. I have a promissory note for a car loan already pending with Navy Federal Credit and my credit has changed within the last two weeks. If I try to go through other third party lenders, my interest rate will be higher than the 9 % I once had with [Redacted]  [Redacted] and the 10 % I was approved already with Navy Federal Credit Union. They will determine this because of the other inquiries and the outstanding loan amount with Navy Federal Credit Union. 

The auto loan amount is active with Navy Federal Credit Union and I have already made a car loan payment toward that loan amount. IT IS AN ACTIVE LOAN!!! 

I am asking for this matter to be resolved within 24 hours. I have a car waiting for me at a local [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. A [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] for only {$15000.00} ( does not include the tax, title and fees ). It only has [Redacted] miles. The truck is in excellent shape. PLEASE HELP ME. 

Thanks God Bless [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.snippet: [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 To Whom It May Concern, I hope this letter finds you well. metadata.full_snippet:
[Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 To Whom It May Concern, I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to address certain legal provisions that pertain to the sharing of my private information by consumer reporting agencies. While the initial letter was directed at Equifax and [Redacted], the content is equally applicable to any Furnisher of information to credit agencies. 

As a consumer, I am vigilant about my rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), specifically 15 USC 1681 section 602 a. This section emphasizes the need for consumer reporting agencies to operate with fairness, impartiality, and respect for the consumer 's right to privacy. Whether it be Equifax, [Redacted], or any Furnisher of information to credit agencies, it is essential that they abide by these principles. 

Under 15 USC 6801, financial institutions, which include Furnishers of information to credit agencies, are mandated to respect customer privacy and protect the confidentiality of nonpublic personal information. This obligation is critical in safeguarding consumer privacy. 

According to 15 USC 1681 section 604 a section 2, consumer reporting agencies may furnish consumer reports only in accordance with the written instructions of the consumer. Neither Equifax, [Redacted], nor any Furnisher of information to credit agencies has obtained my written consent to furnish this information, nor do they possess my consent in any form, be it verbal, non-verbal, implied, or otherwise. 
Furthermore, 15 USC 6802 ( b ) ( c ) requires financial institutions to inform consumers of their right to exercise their nondisclosure option, which Equifax, [Redacted], and Furnishers of information to credit agencies have not done. This lack of transparency is a cause for concern. 

As per 15 USC 1681C ( a ) ( 5 ), consumer reporting agencies are prohibited from including adverse items of information in a consumer report without authorization. The account in question is being reported as an adverse item without my permission, a clear violation of this statute. 


[Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ( [Redacted] ) ( [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ) [Redacted] [Redacted] Equifax Account number : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] Account type : Credit Credit Credit Account Type : Revolving Revolving Revolving 15 U.S. Code 1681s2 ( A ) ( 1 ) A further stipulates that information should not be furnished if it is known or reasonably believed to be inaccurate. I assert that the information being furnished is inaccurate, and it is the responsibility of Equifax, [Redacted], and all Furnishers of information to credit agencies to ensure the accuracy of the data they provide. 

Lastly, 15 U.S. Code 1681e requires consumer reporting agencies to maintain reasonable procedures to avoid violations of the FCRA. It is evident that these reasonable procedures are not being maintained by Equifax, [Redacted], or any Furnisher of information to credit agencies. 

Additionally, 12 CFR 1016.7 reaffirms my right to opt out of reporting services at any time. I am hereby exercising this right to opt out of the reporting services provided by Equifax, [Redacted], and all Furnishers of information to credit agencies. 

In light of these legal provisions and concerns, I expect immediate compliance with the FCRA and a cessation of the reporting of my private information to any consumer reporting agency. I kindly request written confirmation of your acknowledgment of this letter and your commitment to rectify these issues promptly. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I trust that you will take the necessary steps to ensure compliance with the law and protect consumer rights. 

Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted]
