metadata.snippet: I was transferred to Mohela... they asked me to set up a new account so I attempted and got an error message. On the error message page it says " contact us '' with this reference ID. When you click to contact them and go through the hoops .... they will not let you contact them ...
metadata.full_snippet:
I was transferred to Mohela... they asked me to set up a new account so I attempted and got an error message. On the error message page it says " contact us '' with this reference ID. When you click to contact them and go through the hoops .... they will not let you contact them via web without logging in, which I can not do in the first place, that is the error. So I call the number... the number after waiting 10 minutes to hear the spheel about how you can access all these things online I finally get the option to choose a number to get help. They say it's a 71 minute wait. But! I can get a call back, so I choose that option. Before I can say " yes '' to confirm my phone number the auto voice immediately says " im sorry I didn't catch that '' and puts me into the que without any other chances to get a callback. It feels like they are intentionally limiting their contact options and putting folks through an outrageously long wait time in hopes that they will just give up and not have to be contacted. It's really not accessible to have that broken feedback loop on the website in terms of contacting. 

I also went to get feedback on studentloan.gov and the feedback page for that site is also down .... it just seems so suspicious to me that there is no way to flag these very apparent contact issues.

metadata.sub_issue: Trying to communicate with the company to fix an issue related to modification, forbearance, short sale, deed-in-lieu, bankruptcy, or foreclosure
metadata.snippet: Roundpoint Mortgage purchased my loan while it was in a delinquent status. I was unable to make payments while the transfer process proceeded, resulting in me falling further behind in my mortgage. I finally contacted them and began a loan modification process. I made my payments...
metadata.full_snippet:
Roundpoint Mortgage purchased my loan while it was in a delinquent status. I was unable to make payments while the transfer process proceeded, resulting in me falling further behind in my mortgage. I finally contacted them and began a loan modification process. I made my payments as requested throughout the trial period and after while I was waiting for my modification papers to arrive. 

My modification papers arrived, requiring I have them notarized. Since I work [Redacted]  during business hours, I was having trouble getting them notarized. I contacted Roundpoint and made a payment that was to be debited [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 from my account. At the time, I did mention that I was working on getting the papers notarized. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 I called Roundpoint to make another payment, and was told they were not able to take the payment because my loan modification was rejected because it was not received in a timely manner. They were only able to accept all of the amounts in arrears. 

I received a Notice of Default and Intent to Accelerate dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023. 

Throughout this process, I have been frustrated by the lack of information and inability of Roundpoint Mortgage to give me exact amounts owed. The website shows I owe roughly $ [Redacted], but they cite $ [Redacted] in the mortgage modification. They have credited payments in excess of payments I actually made, and the last time I checked my account online, they have reversed those payments without crediting accurate payments. 

Today, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I received a completed loan modification packet. According to the loan modification dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I should be considered current, but there is no mention of the payment they refused to take on the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. 

My online account still reflects that my loan is in default, and states that my loan balance is approximately $ [Redacted]. 

By refusing to take my payment on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I was not allowed to continue making payments. I understood at that time I was no longer in compliance with the loan modification agreement, and I was not surprised when I received the letter stating their intent to foreclose. Now that they have sent the papers back executing the loan modification, I am more confused than ever. 

I have decided the only way to protect my home is to declare [Redacted]  [Redacted] bankruptcy because I don't trust Roundpoint at all. It should not be this difficult to understand my account. I should be able to see an accurate accounting of the amounts owed, the payments made, as well as understanding whether I am current or in default. I do not want to lose my home, and it feels as if Roundpoint is being purposefully confusing and vague. 

I would like this lender to be examined, and if they are placing obstacles in the way of customers paying their debts and keeping their homes, please require them to act fairly and responsibly.

metadata.title: Mortgage Dispute
metadata.issue: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage
metadata.snippet: I am writing to file a formal complaint against Chase Mortgage regarding their refusal to provide manual underwriting for FHA mortgage loans, specifically under the bankruptcy rule of less than 2 years but greater than 1 year. Despite my eligibility under the Federal Housing Admi...
metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing to file a formal complaint against Chase Mortgage regarding their refusal to provide manual underwriting for FHA mortgage loans, specifically under the bankruptcy rule of less than 2 years but greater than 1 year. Despite my eligibility under the Federal Housing Administration ( FHA ) guidelines, Chase Mortgage has stated that they do not offer manual underwriting for such cases. 

As a responsible borrower who has taken necessary steps to recover financially after a bankruptcy, I have relied on the FHA 's favorable guidelines to secure a mortgage loan. According to FHA guidelines, borrowers who have experienced a bankruptcy but have demonstrated financial responsibility for at least one year after the bankruptcy discharge should be eligible for manual underwriting. This provision allows borrowers to present their case for loan approval based on their current financial standing, rather than solely relying on their credit score or traditional underwriting. 

However, despite meeting the required criteria, Chase Mortgage has refused to consider my application for manual underwriting under this rule. Their refusal indicates a departure from FHA guidelines and shows a lack of commitment to providing fair and inclusive access to mortgage financing. 

I believe that Chase Mortgage 's failure to offer manual underwriting for FHA mortgage loans under this specific bankruptcy provision is discriminatory and may potentially infringe upon the principles of equal opportunity and fair lending. By denying qualified applicants an opportunity to present their case through manual underwriting, Chase Mortgage is hindering their access to homeownership and contributing to further financial exclusion. 

I kindly request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate this matter thoroughly and take appropriate action against Chase Mortgage if found in violation of FHA guidelines or engaging in unfair lending practices. Furthermore, I urge you to ensure that Chase Mortgage reviews its policies and procedures to align with FHA guidelines, guaranteeing fair treatment and equal opportunity for borrowers recovering from bankruptcy. 

If there is any additional information needed to assist with the investigation, I am more than willing to provide any necessary documentation or details to support my case. I trust the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau 's commitment to consumer protection and fair lending and request your prompt attention to this matter. 

Thank you for your attention to this complaint, and I look forward to a resolution that promotes fair lending practices within the mortgage industry.

I was repaying my student loans and did not request to be put into deferment when I began my [Redacted] studies. Unbeknownst to me, I was put into deferment witho...
metadata.full_snippet:
In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I enrolled at [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  to begin my [Redacted]  studies. I was repaying my student loans and did not request to be put into deferment when I began my [Redacted] studies. Unbeknownst to me, I was put into deferment without my consent. As soon as I realized my student loan payments were not being drafted from my bank account, I reached out to [Redacted], the loan servicer at that time. However, [Redacted] was also shifting to [Redacted] so there was much confusion. When I contacted [Redacted] to request that I NOT be put into deferment, I was told I would have to contact the school. I did and have documentation to show that I asked the school ( [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  ) to remove my deferment. I stated that I did not want to be in deferment and wanted to keep my payments because I was working toward PSLF. At that point, I had been repaying my student loans for several years. 
Despite my repeated attempts, it took 24+ months for my payments to begin again. I believe, in part, this was because [Redacted] was shifting to [Redacted] and possibly information was lost, requests were lost, etc. The loan providers would tell me to ask my school and my school was not responsive and/or would tell me to contact the loan providers. I could never get anyone to help me resolve the problem. 
Now, the loan provider is MOHELA. MOHELA has significantly better systems than [Redacted] and [Redacted]. With new improvements to PSLF, I have read on the fact sheet shared by the U.S. Department of Education that previous problems can be corrected, including with deferment and forbearance. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I uploaded documents within my MOHELA account to request this problem I have with my student loans be corrected. In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I called MOHELA because I received a response I did not understand. The response did not seem relevant to the request I submitted. I have spoken with staff at MOHELA four different times. I have the dates and names of each person I spoke with but because the directions here state not to include names, I can submit them separately if needed. 
Because I have not been able to get the situation resolved, I have submitted PSLF reconsideration requests. 

My request, in my opinion, is simple. I was put into deferment without my permission. I have documentation to show I repeatedly asked to be taken out of deferment and allowed to continue making payments. That was not done for 24+ months, despite my attempts. I want to be able to repay the amount of payments I would have made during those 24+ months ( approximately 26 or 27 months ) and have those months count toward my PSLF payment count. I am currently at 89 or 90 payments ( waiting for documents to be processed with MOHELA ). I should be at approximately 116 or 117 out of 120 payments.

Whether it is MOHELA, studentaid.gov/the Department of Education , I only want to be allowed to repay those months I was trying diligently to be taken out of the deferment I never requested, never consented to, and have documentation that I was repeatedly asking to have the deferment stopped and be allowed to return to payments. No one should be allowed to make financial decisions for me that affect me negatively without my consent and that is exactly what was done. I only request to fix it. I am not asking to be given those months spent in deferment. I am asking to be allowed to repay those months and have them count toward my PSLF payment count. Thank you.

I kindly request your intervention to help expedite the closure of my online savings account with Citizens Bank and to address the issue of excessively long wait times and disconnected calls experienced during this process. 
I have documented my attempts to resolve this issue, including dates and times of phone calls and any interactions I had with Citizens Bank 's customer service. 
Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I hope for a prompt resolution to my concerns. 

Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet:
This notice is my, required by law, demand to cease and desist collection activities prior to validation of purported debt and you must validate the enclosed claim of an alleged debt. You must provide verification that an actual debt really exists by producing the following :. ( 1 ) The name and address of the organization or other governmental unit alleging a debt ;. ( 2 ) The name and address of the person or persons in that organization or other governmental unit alleging a claim of a debt ;. ( 3 ) The name of the actual creditor even if that is myself ;. ( 4 ) The origin of the funds used to create this alleged claim of a debt. ( 5 ) The actual records of the organization or other government unit showing the time and place of the deposit and distribution of the funds used to create this alleged claim of debt.

. ( 6 ) The actual records of the organization or other governmental unit showing that an actual loan was made from the organization or other governmental units own funds that resulted in the enclosed alleged claim of a debt.

. ( 7 ) The actual records of the organization or other governmental unit with a live signature on any and all document/instrument ( s ) used to allege the existence of a real loan of funds or debt from the organization or other governmental unit to myself or anyone else by a similar name.

. ( 8 ) Be advised that verification is defined ( Blacks Law Dictionary, 6th Edition ) as follows : Confirmation of correctness, truth, or authenticity, by affidavit, oath or deposition. Affidavit of truth of matter stated and object of verification is to assure good faith in averments or statements of party.

. ( 9 ) The actual records of the organization or other governmental unit showing that an honest disclosure of facts relating to the alleged loan was made by the organization or other governmental unit in compliance with the truth in lending laws of the United States Code, Title 15 1601 et. seq. and Regulation Z.

metadata.full_snippet:
Dear [Redacted], I am writing to formally register a complaint in connection with my American Express [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] Credit Card [Redacted] which I opened under the terms of your prominently advertised welcome offer. This correspondence seeks resolution for an issue pertaining to the promised {$200.00} promotional credit, which has not been credited to my account despite my adherence to the stipulated conditions. 

As an eligible applicant, I was preapproved for the Blue Cash Every Day Credit Card and subsequently submitted my application directly through the designated welcome offer portal. At the time of application, I perused the offer terms in a cursory manner, noting a clause that explicitly stated, " if you are not eligible for the welcome offer, intro APRs, and intro plan fees, we will notify you prior to processing your application so that you have the option to withdraw your application. '' To fulfill the terms of the welcome offer, I diligently made eligible purchases totaling {$2000.00} within the first six months of card activation. Furthermore, I ensured that all outstanding balances were paid in full well in advance of the closing cycle, as evidenced by the attached documentation. 

It is deeply disconcerting that, despite my adherence to the terms and conditions, American Express failed to honor the commitment of providing the promised {$200.00} promotional credit. When I contacted one of your agents via telephone, I was informed that American Express does not possess real-time information on an applicant 's eligibility for the welcome offer. This response contradicts the very terms of agreement that your company has put forth, which explicitly state that applicants should be informed of their eligibility status before their application is processed, thereby affording them the opportunity to withdraw their application if necessary. 

Regrettably, I received no indication of ineligibility until I proactively reached out, six months after the requisite spending and payments were completed, to inquire about the conspicuous absence of the {$200.00} statement credit. It is important to note that American Express records all phone calls, and despite this fact, the company has yet to acknowledge its own deviation from its stated obligations. 

I am deeply disappointed by this lack of transparency and failure to uphold the terms of the welcome offer, which was a significant factor in my decision to open an American Express credit card. I kindly request that this matter be addressed promptly and that the {$200.00} promotional credit be applied to my account in accordance with the terms initially presented to me. 

I anticipate a timely resolution to this matter and kindly request written confirmation of the actions taken to rectify this situation. Failure to address this issue satisfactorily may necessitate further action on my part to ensure that my rights as a consumer are upheld. 

Thank you for your immediate attention to this formal complaint. I look forward to a prompt resolution. 

Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet:
I currently have {$92000.00} in outstanding student loans, of which the oldest loan goes back to [Redacted] timeframe. They have been consolidated several times, most recently on [Redacted] [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], so that I have one consolidation loan. This was done after a recommendation due to the one time IDR account adjustment, for which I received the Department of Education letter indicating some or all of my loans qualified for forgiveness, and that action would be completed starting mid-[Redacted]. 

My loans have changed hands numerous times and in [Redacted] were transferred from [Redacted] to MOHELA. I submitted applications for PSLF and TEPSLF prior to the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] deadline, and prior to consolidation, was at a [Redacted] PSLF payment count. It took several calls to MOHELA to get this count, as they initially missed 30+ payments for which they had credited surrounding payments for the same employers. I am now left to wonder if I have even more qualified payments that I am unaware of. 

I understood that when I consolidated, my count would temporarily reset to zero. What has happened since consolidation has been a source of tremendous stress and frustration. Any calls to MOHELA, provided one can get through, have been answered by someone " in training ''. I get different answers each time to my inquiries. 

The final straw is that I had applied for and been approved for the SAVE plan, and was under the impression that my loans would remain in forbearance until the one-time account adjustment occurred. This is apparently not the case. Furthermore, after my consolidated loan initially showed the repayment plan as SAVE with a [Redacted] [Redacted] monthly payment, it has in recent days switched, without my action, to a level repayment plan and a payment of around {$560.00}, which I can not afford as I recently took a massive pay cut and have other financial obligations. 

I understand that there is a tremendous volume of actions occurring, but what I do not understand is why a company that was a proxy in a lawsuit to stop forgiveness is the same company handling my student loan forgiveness actions. I also find it unacceptable that any action on my part results in the effective " wiping out '' of any progress that I can see, and at this point, I am not confident that MOHELA will accurately adjust my account for the one time IDR account adjustment, or that it will happen in a timely fashion. 

It should not be too much to ask for a company to provide it's customers with ACCURATE, up to date information, and if the system is so antiquated that making account adjustments requires an actual person to do the counting, I am not confident that MOHELA has enough trained and competent individuals to process these actions. I should be able to see my actual account standing prior to the resumed payment date of [Redacted] [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], which until the last few days, was not even showing on my account -- it showed no upcoming payments due. 

What is our recourse as consumers, when a company we did not choose is mishandling our student loans and failing to provide us with accurate, up to date information? I can not even reapply for SAVE at this time, because the MOHELA portal for repayment plan applications is " undergoing maintenance '' and unavailable, and I am directed to StudentAid.gov. The problem there is studentaid shows my account balanace at {$0.00}, because the last update they received from the NSLDS is from [Redacted] [Redacted]. 

Thank you, [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: I recently sold a wheelchair that I purchased with my own money on [Redacted]. A buyer agreed to the purchase price and sent me a check for the cost of the chair plus an additional amount to cover the cost of someone he had who was to pick the large chair up and handle shipping it. The buyer said it would be easier to do it this way because he knew the picker and it would be easier for me because I would not have to arrange shipping. Im a quadriplegic, so this sounded good. I deposited the {$3500.00} check and waited for citizens bank to clear the check and make the money available in my account. AFTER CITIZENS cleared the check, I paid the picker a person named [Redacted] [Redacted] {$2500.00} to schedule a pickup and handle the shipping of the [Redacted]. After I sent {$2500.00} via [Redacted], conversation with the buyer got weird and I got very suspicious ( I have records of all conversations ). Out of an abundance of caution I called citizens around [Redacted]. Citizens said the situation sounded off, but said that the check cleared and my account appeared safe. This was a recorded conversation. Despite this, I still felt uneasy, so I looked at the original {$3500.00} check that I had remotely deposited on Thursday [Redacted]/[Redacted]/31. I looked up the routing number and called the bank associated with the check account, [Redacted] [Redacted]. They couldnt tell me much, but they did say that it sounded like fraud and told me that there was a good chance the {$3500.00} would be returned, thereby stripping it from my checking account! In this scenario I would lose the {$2500.00} I [Redacted]. Concerned, I looked up the [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], a [Redacted] [Redacted]  company which was the name listed as the payer I spoke with the CFO [Redacted]. She knew right away, I had been scammed. She said for the last month someone had been using their company to defraud people. [Redacted] said that the money was not coming from their account, instead it was just their company name being used. So I dont know where the money was coming from specifically, accept that it was associated with [Redacted] [Redacted] . Obviously I was extremely concerned. I cant afford to lose {$2500.00}. As a quadriplegic, my resources are limited. So I again continue with my due diligence. I called Citizens Bank again in attempt to proactively resolve the issue. I spoke with Fraud and Claims and explained the situation. They basically told me that there was nothing they could do!!!! I explained that I had done the due diligence that I believe was Citizens fiduciary responsibility! How can I be punished after Citizens failed to verify the source and status of the check? And even more infuriating, now that I had uncovered a fraudulent scheme that has been ripping people off for the past month, citizens says there is nothing they can do! ( [Redacted] from [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] said that it has been going on for a month ). So Citizens told me that there is nothing I can do. I asked if I could file a claim proactively, I told them I would not have money for mortgage payments, I begged them to help me. Citizens told me there was nothing they could do. I had to wait till the {$3500.00} check was returned, meaning I would lose the {$2500.00} I sent via [Redacted], then I could file a claim, but that Citizens probably would not reimburse me!!! I explained that Citizens was at fault, they should not have cleared the check. Finally, I asked what would happen if I moved the money in my account to another bank to protect my money. Citizens told me that I would be charged an overdraft fee!!!! This is completely ridiculous. A billion dollar bank, at fault for clearing a fraudulent check, is going to punish me?! Over {$2500.00}? I have records and documents to prove the validity of all these statements. I am desperately in need of the money, I can not afford to lose {$2500.00}. I hope you can help me.

A scammer, who identified himself as [Redacted] [Redacted], responded to my [Redacted] [Redacted] ad in which I listed 2 tickets to a [Redacted]  concert for sale. I believe that Capital One 's handling of my situation demonstrates a reckless, unfair, and possibly illegal position that fails to meet its responsibilities under federal consumer protection laws, including the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) and the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), as well as its obligations to me as a consumer. 

-- Timeline of Events -- -- Incident with [Redacted] On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I received a package from [Redacted] containing items that I did not order. 
After contacting [Redacted], I was informed that another customer had placed an order using my credit card information, but that due to privacy regulations, they could not disclose further details about the account in question. 
[Redacted] instructed me to report the matter to my credit card company. 

-- Interaction with Capital One Immediately after my conversation with [Redacted], I contacted Capital One to report fraudulent activity and to cancel my current card for reissue. 
Despite providing all the relevant facts, Capital One concluded a cursory investigation, stating that the charges were legitimate because they were shipped to my address and were from a retailer with whom I had previously conducted business. 
I participated in a three-way call with [Redacted] and Capital One, where [Redacted] again confirmed that the order came from an account unrelated to me. However, Capital One continued to dismiss my claim. 

-- Key Issues : Failure to Conduct a Comprehensive Investigation : Capital One failed to adequately investigate the situation, taking into account only the shipping address while ignoring other relevant facts. 
Ignoring Documentation and Third-Party Confirmation : Even after a three-way call with [Redacted], who confirmed the fraudulent activity, Capital One dismissed the evidence provided. 
Violation of Consumer Rights : Capital One 's actions seem to be in direct violation of the [Redacted] and [Redacted], which require credit card companies to properly investigate disputes related to " unauthorized charges. '' -- Request for Action I am seeking immediate reimbursement of the fraudulent charges : {$140.00} from [Redacted] dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 {$100.00} from [Redacted] dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 I hope that the FTC will take prompt action to investigate this matter. I am more than willing to provide any additional information or documentation that may be necessary for your investigation. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt response. 

Sincerely, Complainant

metadata.full_snippet:
Subject : Discrepancies in Credit Report and Transaction History - Request for Rescission, Compensation, and Credit Report Update I am writing to bring to your attention significant discrepancies that have been identified in my recently obtained credit report and transaction history through Credit Acceptance. Upon careful review, it has become evident that both my name and address are incorrect in the report, rendering the entire agreement null and void due to the inaccurate representation of my personal information. 

Additionally, I believe Credit Acceptance has engaged in fraudulent practices as defined under 15 U.S.C. 1662 ( b ). During the loan application process, I was explicitly informed by Credit Acceptance that a down payment was mandatory. Consequently, I made the required down payment in good faith. However, it has come to my attention that the down payment made by me was not applied to my loan amount as initially stated. This discrepancy has caused significant harm to my creditworthiness over a period of seven years, which is a substantial violation of my rights as a consumer. 

In light of these findings, I hereby exercise my right to rescind the transaction under 15 U.S.C. 1635. I request that the transaction be immediately rescinded, and I be provided with a full refund of the down payment amount. Furthermore, I would like to draw your attention to 15 U.S.C. 1681n ( a ) ( 1 ), which outlines the legal provision for compensation due to inaccuracies in credit reporting.

According to 15 U.S.C. 1681n ( a ) ( 1 ), I am entitled to compensation for each inaccuracy in my credit report. I request compensation of {$1000.00} per inaccuracy, as outlined by the aforementioned statute. Given the multiple inaccuracies in my credit report and the resulting harm caused to my creditworthiness, I expect an appropriate compensation amount to be awarded to me. 

Furthermore, I kindly request that all accounts pertaining to Credit Acceptance be removed from my credit report. These accounts are based on erroneous information and have contributed to the inaccurate representation of my creditworthiness. Therefore, their removal is necessary to rectify the harm caused by these discrepancies. I also request an updated credit report reflecting these changes to be provided to me. 

I expect Credit Acceptance to promptly investigate these matters, take the necessary actions to rectify the inaccuracies in my credit report and transaction history, and provide me with a written confirmation of the rescission of the transaction, along with a detailed breakdown of the refund amount. 

Please be aware that failure to address these concerns within a reasonable timeframe may leave me with no choice but to pursue legal remedies available to me under applicable consumer protection laws. 

I look forward to your immediate attention to this matter and a satisfactory resolution. Please respond to this letter within 30 days from the date of receipt. 

Thank you for your immediate attention to this matter. 

Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]

The total amount paid totaled about {$78000.00}, leaving me with a balance of {$84000.00}. Due to rec...
metadata.full_snippet:
Greetings. Prior to the pandemic, I was owing {$160000.00} ( [Redacted] principal and {$15000.00} interest ) in my student loan. I made payment towards my loan during [Redacted]. The total amount paid totaled about {$78000.00}, leaving me with a balance of {$84000.00}. Due to recent financial difficulties I requested the money be refunded to me as prescribed by the cares act. This occurred sometime around [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 when I was still with Ed financial. The agent I spoke to confirmed my request and said she processed it. She informed me that it will take about 60 days to receive my check in the mail. Shortly after this, I noticed my loan amount had increased back to the previous amount of {$160000.00}, which makes sense as I had requested the payment originally made be refunded to me. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] my loan servicer was then switched to [Redacted]. After the 60 days had elapsed and I had not received my check in the mail as expected, I reached out to [Redacted] who could not see that I made payments during COVID and that I had requested a refund either. All they could see on their end was that I owe {$160000.00} ( No mention of the {$78000.00} paid prior or refund request that was supposedly submitted ). Because they have no history of my previous payment, they are unable to make any refund request on my behalf. I called Ed financial, and they said they requested the refund, but they are unable to tell me the status of my refund request or what was delaying the check. I even logged into studentaid.gov website which show my previous payment of {$78000.00}, but make no mention of the refund request and reports a balance of {$160000.00} ( Which inaccurately insinuates that my pre pandemic total loan is [Redacted] + [Redacted] ). 

It seems like the money I paid towards my student loan has been erased because I have not received my check as requested and my loan balance has returned to the pre-payment amount and no one is able or willing to tell me where my money/ refund is. I keep getting the run around. [Redacted] is unable to help me because they do not have the full record and Ed financial is giving me the run around. I tried calling the department of Finance, but unable to get a hold of a human on the phone in order to discuss my situation. Can you please assist me by figuring out if my refund was actually and accurately submitted to the department of education. If it was, I need to figure out where and when my refund will be sent to me. If it was not, I need the application resubmitted or have my loan amount updated to {$84000.00} instead of {$160000.00} to reflect payment already made since they are not refunding my payment.

metadata.full_snippet:
Dear CFPB, I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to bring to your attention a concerning matter regarding a series of attempted money transfers from the United States to [Redacted], which have led to significant complications and remain unresolved. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I initiated [Redacted] separate transactions with MoneyGram, each with the following transaction numbers : [Redacted], [Redacted], [Redacted], and [Redacted]. Unfortunately, MoneyGram was unable to successfully deliver or deposit the funds, and these transactions were canceled without any prior notification to me. 

In my pursuit of a resolution, I engaged in a conversation with MoneyGram 's customer service on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, and requested a refund for the undelivered funds. They assured me that a refund would be processed within [Redacted] hours. Regrettably, this promise was not fulfilled. 

Recognizing the ongoing delay and lack of communication, I reached out to MoneyGram once again on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, as I had not received any updates or my promised refund. During this interaction, I was informed that a technical issue had been encountered, but the funds would be refunded within [Redacted] business days. It is important to note that this ordeal has persisted for more than [Redacted] months, causing immense frustration and inconvenience. 

Unfortunately, my efforts to resolve this matter amicably were met with rudeness and refusal from MoneyGram 's agents. Subsequently, in an attempt to retrieve my funds, I reported the situation to my bank, initiating a dispute process. In response to my action, MoneyGram has taken the drastic step of closing my account and has conveyed that, due to my dispute, they are unable to complete the refund. Furthermore, they advised me to contact my bank for any further information. 

To date, MoneyGram has not issued the promised refund, and my inquiries for information have yielded no results. Given the circumstances, I kindly request that an investigation be initiated to ascertain the status of these transactions and to facilitate the return of my funds. This situation has caused undue financial strain and distress, and I believe a thorough examination is warranted. 

I appreciate your prompt attention to this matter and look forward to a resolution as soon as possible. Please do not hesitate to contact me should you require any additional information or documentation regarding these transactions. 

Thank you for your assistance in addressing this issue. 
Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted]

Name : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] : [Redacted] Address : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] # [Redacted] [Redacted], FL [Redacted] [Redacted] Date : [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]  To : TransUnion [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], PA [Redacted] Subject : Dispute of unauthorized Credit Reporting under 15 USC 1681b ( a ) ( 2 ) Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to dispute the accuracy and authorization of information contained in my credit report maintained by your agency, [Redacted]. Under the provisions of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), & as outlined in 15 USC 1681b ( a ) ( 2 ), any consumer reporting agency may furnish a consumer report, but only under specific circumstances, subject to subsection ( c ). This includes ONLY furnishing a consumer report in accordance with the written instructions of the consumer to whom it relates. I have reviewed my consumer report, and I have discovered accounts that were and are currently being furnished WITHOUT my written instructions, authorization, or consent, which violates my rights under this provision of the FCRA. 

The following accounts on my credit report ARE BEING furnished WITHOUT my written instructions. And I now give my written instructions to remove these accounts immediately from my consumer report : Account Name : [Redacted] [Redacted] Account Number : [Redacted] Account Name : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] Account Number [Redacted] [Redacted] Account Name : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  Account Number : [Redacted] Account Name : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  SS Account Number : [Redacted] Account Name : [Redacted] [Redacted]l Account Number : [Redacted] To my knowledge and awareness, I have not provided any written instructions, authorization or consent to have these accounts reported on my consumer report. As such, the inclusion of these accounts is a violation of my rights under the FCRA, specifically 15 USC 1681b ( a ) ( 2 ), which requires a permissible purpose for credit reporting, including written instructions from the consumer.

I kindly request that you investigate this matter promptly & I am requesting that you take the following necessary actions : [Redacted]. Conduct a thorough investigation to obtain & provide proof that written permission exists for the inclusion of the aforementioned accounts on my credit report. 

[Redacted]. If you can not provide conclusive evidence of my written authorization, immediately delete the aforementioned accounts from being furnished on my credit report. 

[Redacted]. If you are able to find conclusive & written consent, due to the negligence of this reporting agency, which has failed to alert me of my option to opt-out of certain disclosures, and have failed to comply with the requirements outlined in 15 USC 6802b ( 1 ) ( a ) - ( c ), I now indefinitely and permanently revoke said written consent, and now give my written instructions for this reporting agency to delete the aforementioned accounts and cease to furnish said accounts on my consumer report, effective immediately. ( Furthermore, I have not received the necessary and federally mandated notice detailing my right to prevent the disclosure of certain personal information, and how I can invoke that right. That is a direct violation of my consumer rights. ) [Redacted]. Also, provide me with written confirmation of the actions taken to resolve this dispute, including the removal of the disputed accounts from my consumer report. 

[Redacted]. Provide a written and clear explanation of my rights to prevent the disclosure of certain personal information. 

[Redacted]. Provide furnishing instructions on how I can exercise this right of non-disclosure, including the necessary forms or contact information. 

[Redacted]. Provide clear and fully detailed written instructions ( and the related law ) that clearly specify the types of personal information that I have the right to prevent from being disclosed, and how I can prevent that information from being disclosed moving forward. 

I do understand that the FCRA allows for a 30-day period for the investigation and resolution of such disputes. Therefore, I expect to receive a written response from your agency, and for the aforementioned accounts to be deleted within 30 days of receipt of this dispute letter, according to 15 USC 1681i ( 5 ). 

Please be aware that I am also entitled to a free copy of my credit report following the resolution of this dispute. I request that you send me an updated consumer report reflecting the removal of the disputed accounts. Send it to the address on the heading of this letter. 

Failure to comply with the FCRA by not promptly investigating and correcting this matter will result in legal action on my behalf. 

I trust that you will handle this dispute with the utmost urgency and professionalism. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. 

Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing to file a formal complaint concerning a flagrant violation of my federally protected rights delineated in the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), specifically under 15 USC 1681. The presented list of accounts starkly demonstrates a blatant disregard for my fundamental rights to privacy and confidentiality. 

Despite explicit requests for reinvestigation directed at Equifax regarding the following accounts : [Redacted] : [Redacted], [Redacted] : [Redacted],, their responses have consistently asserted the completeness and accuracy of all information. However, these assertions directly conflict with the undeniable inaccuracies in critical details such as open dates, dates of last activity, and other pivotal elements. 

Under 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( 5 ), these agencies are unequivocally mandated to rectify inaccurately reported accounts. Moreover, under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( A ) ( 1 ), any entity is explicitly prohibited from furnishing inaccurate information to consumer reporting agencies when knowledge or reasonable cause exists of such inaccuracies. 

The ramifications of these inaccuracies extend beyond mere data errors. They significantly impact crucial credit ratios, such as the length of credit history, debt-to-credit utilization, and misrepresented balances, consequently impeding my ability to secure credit. 

These inaccuracies are an infringement of my rights and impair my capability to obtain fair access to credit opportunities due to misrepresented and flawed data. 

Additionally, it is crucial to note that while other bureaus could not verify these accounts, they inexplicably remain on the reports of these agencies. This incongruity is perplexing, as all bureaus are expected to follow similar verification processes. The persistence of these inaccuracies across multiple reporting agencies underscores a systemic issue that requires urgent attention. 

I implore the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) to investigate this matter promptly and take decisive action against the entities responsible for their failure to adhere to federal regulations to safeguard consumer rights. Rectifying these inaccuracies is essential to restore the integrity of the consumer reporting system and ensure fair access to credit for individuals. 

Thank you for your immediate attention to this pressing issue.

metadata.full_snippet: I was in the final week of closing on a property in Texas. The house was supposed to close on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] in Texas. On Monday, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I was emailed ( along with my lender ) at [Redacted] and asked for contact info for the buyer. The display name of the email was the same person who I have been working with at [Redacted] [Redacted] based in [Redacted]. The actual email was " [Redacted] '' which is different from the real email of [Redacted] [Redacted] contact. The loan [Redacted] for my lender responded with my name, email and phone number. About [Redacted] minutes later, I received an email asking me to wire the funds to close on the property, without anyone else on copy. This email came from the loan [Redacted] as the display name, but it was actually the same gmail noted above. I responded to their email multiple times and they provided the wire instructions. I wired {$100000.00} to Fifth Third bank, however, did not list the beneficiary as the scammer requested. Instead I put [Redacted] [Redacted] on the recipient 's as the receiver account name. I used the account number provided on the scammer 's wiring instructions PDF. When at closing to sign documents, I told the closer that I wired the closing funds. The closer called the title company, and title said they didn't receive it. Then I contacted my loan [Redacted], and he said he didn't provide the wiring info. That's when I looked back at the emails and realized it was a fraud. I contacted [Redacted] [Redacted] that day ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) to recall and reverse the wire. I also submitted an [Redacted] case to the FBI the same night and have been in contact with an agent. He said the resolution needs to come from the banks, but that the scammer 's account was frozen, and the money is held by Fifth Third Bank. A few of the [Redacted] address in the different scam email headers are [Redacted], [Redacted], [Redacted] Since this happened, I have visited [Redacted] [Redacted] ( multiple branches on [Redacted], [Redacted], [Redacted], [Redacted] ) and called the recipient bank ( Fifth Third ) multiple times. I called [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] wire department every day for the first [Redacted] weeks, and called the consumer complaint department many times. I have called [Redacted] Fifth Third branches ( including the one where the account holder is ) as well as the general customer support. [Redacted] has tried numerous times to contact Fifth Third Bank. According to [Redacted], Fifth Third Bank has not responded or even acknowledged receipt. [Redacted] then closed the recall due to Fifth Third not responding. During a visit and a follow up call to [Redacted], I successfully reopened the recall case and asked to escalate. I also filed a complaint with [Redacted] [Redacted] for closing the case after about [Redacted] weeks of it being opened. When I contact Fifth Third, they will not give much information since I do not have an account with them. They said they do respond to messages and are unsure why [Redacted] would claim Fifth Third hasn't responded. I am also filing a police report and will be emailing the [Redacted] teams at both banks today.

metadata.title: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports Dispute
metadata.sub_issue: Reporting company used your report improperly
metadata.snippet: I am writing again in response to a letter that was constructed on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. In the response letter it said you may not opt out of this sharing. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I received a welcome letter from [Redacted] and in that welcome letter afte...
metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing again in response to a letter that was constructed on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. In the response letter it said you may not opt out of this sharing. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I received a welcome letter from [Redacted] and in that welcome letter after [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] transferred my account it said Within 90 days of the transfer, these changes will be reflected on your credit report and [Redacted] will continue to report on your federal student loan ( s ). Under 12 CFR 1016.7 ( a ) ( 1 ) states you are required to provide a clear and conspicuous notice to each of your consumers that accurately explains the right to opt out. The notice must state- ( ii ) That the consumer has the right to opt out of that disclosure; and ( iii ) A reasonable means by which the consumer may exercise the opt out right. I was not provided a clear and conspicuous notice that accurately explained my right to opt out. All I received in writing was that you notified me that you are reporting my account to the CRAs which excludes reasonable opt out means. Under 12 CFR 1016.7 ( 2 ) Examples it lists what are considered reasonable opt out means for consumers which none were provided to me. Since you have given me unreasonable opt out means in 12 CFR 1016.7 ( 2 ) ( iii ) the only means of opting out I have is writing my own letter which is attached to this complaint to exercise my right to opt out.

By Law under 15 U.S. Code 6802 ( B ) states that the consumer is given the opportunity, before the time that such information is initially disclosed, to direct that such information not be disclosed to such third party ; and 15 U.S. Code 6802 ( C ) states that the consumer is given an explanation of how the consumer can exercise that non-disclosure option. Before you reported my account to third parties such as Equifax, [Redacted] and [Redacted] I was not given an explanation of how I the consumer could exercise the non-disclosure option. 

Not only have you disclosed my nonpublic personal information to third parties without consent and given me unreasonable means to opt out, you also havent protected my privacy as a student. In the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act ( FERPA ) it states in ( 20 U.S.C. 1232g ; 34 CFR Part 99 ) that FERPA is a Federal law that protects the privacy of student education records. The law applies to all schools that receive funds under an applicable program of the U.S. Department of Education. You are violating that federal law by disclosing my account data to the CRAs. In FERPA it also states that the only information that may be disclosed is directory information which includes such as a student 's name, address, telephone number, date and place of birth, honors and awards, and dates of attendance. However, schools must tell parents and eligible students about directory information and allow parents and eligible students a reasonable amount of time to request that the school not disclose directory information about them. I have not received a letter about the reporting of my directory information or was allowed time to have an option not to disclose that information nor have I given written or verbal consent to disclose that information to consumer reporting agencies like [Redacted], [Redacted] and Equifax who are credit bureaus that have my directory information. 

On top of that on [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] there was an update reported by [Redacted] to [Redacted] of a transaction ( attached is a copy ) which means there was transaction history reported to the CRAs. Reporting transaction history is illegal as it states in 15 U.S. Code 1681a ( 2 ) ( A ) ( i ) that a consumer report does not include report containing information solely as to transactions or experiences between the consumer and the person making the report. Directory information as well as transaction history were reported to [Redacted] and Equifax and I have copies attached to this complaint as well. 

In the Privacy Act of 1974 ( 5 U.S. Code 552a ( b ) under Conditions of Disclosure it states- No agency shall disclose any record which is contained in a system of records by any means of communication to any person, or to another agency, except pursuant to a written request by, or with the prior written consent of, the individual to whom the record pertains, unless disclosure of the record would be. I have not given a written request or written consent to disclose my records to any agency. My records have not been kept between me and [Redacted] and have been disclosed to other third party agencies without my consent. Although under ( 12 ) of Conditions of Disclosure it says a record may be disclosed to a consumer reporting agency in accordance with 3711 ( e ) of title 31. It needs to be in accordance with 3711 ( e ) of title 31. I have not received any notice of disclosing my nonpublic information to credit bureaus. Prior to the credit bureaus receiving my information you gave them, my written instruction of consent was not given to disclose that information therefore not only have you violated the Fair credit reporting act but also the Privacy Act of 1974. For all of these valid reasons it is my right to exercise opting out of your reporting services.

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 [Redacted] Bank Subject [Redacted] [Redacted] of Authorizations and Notification of Violations Under Relevant Federal Laws I, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], am writing to inform you of my decision to opt-out of any and all autho...
metadata.full_snippet:
Requested opt out... 
[Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 [Redacted] Bank Subject [Redacted] [Redacted] of Authorizations and Notification of Violations Under Relevant Federal Laws I, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], am writing to inform you of my decision to opt-out of any and all authorizations I may have given you, whether written, unwritten, verbal, or nonverbal as is my right per FCRA Section 15 USC 1681 ( b ) and 16 CFR 313.7 ( e ), ( f ), ( g ) ( 1 ).

You have repeatedly provided inaccurate information as well as my non public personal information to all credit reporting agencies which has caused substantial harm to my life by these actions.

I have proof of multiple violations of the protection provided to me as a consumer under several federal laws, including but not limited to : 15 USC 6801 ( a ) states It is the policy of the Congress that each financial institution has an affirmative and continuing obligation to respect the privacy of its customers and to protect the security and confidentiality of those customers nonpublic personal information.

According to 15 USC 6809 ( 4 ) ( A ) The term nonpublic personal information means personally identifiable financial information ( I ) provided by a consumer to a financial institution ; ( ii ) resulting from any transaction with the consumer or any service performed for the consumer ; or ( iii ) otherwise obtained by the financial institution.

15 USC 1681 ( b ) requires every financial institutionshall establish appropriate standards for the financial institutions administrative, technical, and physical safeguards ( 1 ) to insure the security and confidentiality of customer records and information ; ( 2 ) to protect against any anticipated threats or hazards to the security or integrity of such records ; and ( 3 ) to protect against unauthorized access to or use of such records or information which could result in substantial harm or inconvenience to any customer.

16 CFR 313.7 ( e ) Time to comply with opt out. You must comply with a consumers opt out direction as soon as reasonably practicable after you receive it. ( f ) Continuing right to opt out. A consumer may exercise the right to opt out at any time. ( g ) Duration of consumers opt out direction. ( 1 ) A consumers direction to opt out under this section is effective until the consumer revokes it in writing or, if the consumer agrees, electronically.

I exercise these rights under the aforementioned federal laws with the aim of protecting my personal information from unauthorized access, use, and sharing.

I kindly request that you review all your past and current practices relating to the collection, storage, use, and sharing of my personal information to ensure compliance with the relevant statutory provisions.

Failure to do so may result in the violation of federal law, which could lead to serious consequences.

I expect you to promptly address any violations, including inaccuracies, and take necessary steps to rectify the situation. Furthermore, I request that you provide me with a detailed written response that outlines the actions taken to comply with the applicable laws within thirty ( 30 ) days of receiving this letter. 
I would like to continue receiving periodic statements by mail and any legally mandated communications regarding my account. However, any other uses or sharing of my personal financial information should cease unless explicitly authorized by me. I appreciate your immediate attention to this request and compliance with the relevant federal laws. 
[Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet:
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], two equal payments of {$260.00} were sent by ACH by my bank to GreenSky, a Goldman Sachs Company ( see receipts from [Redacted]  [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] indicating that two payments were electronically made to GrenSky, with two different ACH trace numbers-Exhibits [Redacted] and [Redacted] respectively ). 
Due to concerns about the payments being applied as intended, I phoned GreenSky on at least two occasions to be sure that one payment was applied to the [Redacted] payment for the account and the other payment was applied to principle only, without interest being deducted from that payment, and was told on all occasions that the payments were applied correctly. I did not record the representatives names because I did not think it would come down to me having to file a formal complaint with the CFPB just to get the payments applied correctly and obtain proof positive that the payments had been applied correctly. 
Based on the assurance by GreenSky personnel, I did not think much more about it until, on or about [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I received notification that my electronic statement was ready for download. I downloaded my [Redacted] statement which is payable [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. ( See Exhibit [Redacted] ). That statement alerted me that GreenSky had, in fact, received the double payment, totaling {$530.00} ( [Redacted] ) but did not give me a clear, concise indication as to how those payments were applied. 
I have had other telephone conversations about how the payments were applied and got the same answer as I received during my first conversations with GreenSky personnel-that the payments had been applied correctly. Again, on at least one occasion, I was told that the payments were applied correctly and again I did not record the representatives names because, giving GreenSky the benefit of the doubt, I assumed that GreenSky would be professional and apply the payments as I indicated they should be applied during our multiple telephone conversations, and did not think it would have to come down to me having to file a formal complaint with the CFPB just to get the payments applied correctly and obtain proof positive that the payments had been applied correctly. 
I began checking GreenSkys website regularly to be assured that the payments were applied as intended, although I did not download or take screen shots of what I was seeing online at the onset. I began communicating with GreenSky about the payments via secure messaging via their online portal ( See [Redacted] email chain regarding my communications with GreenSky, Exhibit [Redacted]. ) Finally, because I was not getting satisfaction and was not receiving the positive proof of how the payments were applied, I began downloading and taking screenshots of what I was seeing on the GreenSky website and even that was not a simple task inasmuch as the information was not readable/understandable because it had been scrambled despite me having logged in using my credentials. I lieu of printing out what I was seeing online due to printing issues, I took screen shots ( see Exhibits [Redacted] ). 
I have given GreenSky every opportunity to resolve the issue regarding the double payments and provide positive proof that the payments were applied as they should have been. Absolutely nothing lets me know how the payments were applied or that they were applied correctly and as of this writing, I still have not received the written proof that the payments were applied as they should have been. 
I regret that I have been pushed into filing a formal complaint, but it seems as though this is the only way to resolve the issue with [Redacted]. There are no clear, viable reasons not to be able to obtain a complete accounting of my account, letting me know exactly what they do with my money. Simply stating " applied '' is not sufficient proof of exactly how the money is applied to the account and is not acceptable. 
It was/is my intent to begin paying down the principle and paying the loan off early and that has not and will not change. I'm either going to do it monthly by sending double payments to GreenSky and if they can not /will not provide me with an full accounting of how the money I send them is allocated, that is acceptable to me, then I will put the money aside to pay the loan off early and will collect the interest from that money until I do make a final payment, paying off the account. Either way, the loan is going to be paid off early. I have a double payment set up for [Redacted] but if I do not get the proof as to how the money I sent them in [Redacted] was allocated, that is acceptable to me, I will cancel the second payment intended for principle only, and send only the monthly payment and begin putting the money aside and collecting the interest until I make a lump sum payment to pay the loan off in its entirety, which will be before the loan 's maturity date. 
Until now, GreenSky and I have had a good relationship and it saddens me that something so simple, that they should be doing anyway, has tarnished that relationship.

metadata.full_snippet:
I am filing a complaint against Sallie Mae for what I believe to be an unjust termination of a reduced payment plan agreement and for not providing full disclosure regarding the limitations on the number of reduced payment plans available to a borrower over the lifetime of their loan. 

Details of the Complaint : Agreement Breach : I entered into a reduced payment plan with Sallie Mae, which was supposed to last for [Redacted] years after making [Redacted] qualifying monthly payments. 
I made the first qualifying payment as verified by my bank statements. 
Despite this, I received a notice from Sallie Mae the following day stating that I was removed from the payment plan for failing to make the first payment, which is factually incorrect. The payment was authorized on the day of the agreement was signed ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) and the payment was cleared within [Redacted] hours. 

Misrepresentation and Lack of Disclosure : Upon contacting Sallie Mae, I was informed for the first time that a borrower is only entitled to two reduced payment plans over the lifetime of their loan.

This limitation was never disclosed to me at any point during my loan agreement or while setting up this recent payment plan. 
The lack of disclosure and subsequent use of this undisclosed policy to terminate my payment plan constitutes misrepresentation. 

Impact : This unexpected cancellation of the payment plan has caused financial distress and uncertainty regarding my loan repayment strategy. 
The misinformation and sudden policy enforcement have also led to a lack of trust in the loan servicing processes of Sallie Mae.

metadata.full_snippet:
I am filing this complaint because I am concerned about the unethical servicing practices of First Hawaiian Bank and their obstruction of any path towards resolving delinquent payments related to my grandmothers passing. My name is [Redacted] [Redacted] and I am the legal and rightful owner of the subject property located at [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted]. This loan is held in the [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ( trust ) and upon my grandmothers passing I am listed as the successor. My family has the ability and desire to make the mortgage payments on this property which has been placed into foreclosure after my grandmothers death because the bank has refused to accept payments, engage or communicate with my family to resolve the situation. 

My family built this home back in the [Redacted]. My grandmother [Redacted] [Redacted] created a trust in [Redacted] and I am the beneficiary and successor for the property. We refinanced the referenced loan in [Redacted]. In [Redacted] [Redacted]  my grandmother passed away. The mortgage payments had been set on auto-pay from her First Hawaiian bank account. Once they found out that she had passed away they froze her bank account, which automatically led to missed mortgage payments. Even though I provided the bank with the will and trust documents, their agents refused to engage with me or discuss the mortgage. The letters that were sent regarding the delinquent payments were sent certified and since my grandmother was not available to sign for the letters since she was deceased we could not access them. As the mortgage fell further behind we attempted to resume making payments on the property but the bank would not accept them. 

I contacted the Attorney who was sending the notifications and he said that we needed to provide the death certificate in order to engage with First Hawaiian. This does not make sense, because the bank froze my grandmothers account when they found out she had passed away, not when they received her death certificate. If they were to equitably apply this standard they would have continued drafting mortgage payments out of her bank account until the money ran out or they received her death certificate. 

The reason we were not able to get the death certificate in a timely fashion is because my grandmother was a state of Hawaii employee and she was a victim of identity theft. Someone had stolen her credentials for the state and logged in and then they sold her information on the dark web. As a result it took us almost one year to receive her death certificate. During that time the bank refused to engage with us, refused to speak with us, froze my grandmothers bank account and blocked access to her safe deposit box. Then they filed foreclosure against my familys home. 

This is wrong and we have provided them with the will, the trust paperwork and the death certificate and the bank needs to work with my family. My son [Redacted] currently resides in the subject property and he will make the mortgage payments with help from me and my mother so that we can get back into good standing.

My former mortgage company, PennyMac, currently holds approximately {$17000.00} of funds that were issued from my former insurance company, [Redacted], for an insurance payout after flood damage to the property on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. 

I sold the property yesterday, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Since then I've received multiple emails from PennyMac congratulating me on paying off loan [Redacted], PennyMac insurance tracking number [Redacted], and confirming that the same loan was paid off. 

I've contacted PennyMac 's Insurance Department multiple times to confirm that the loan is satisfied and to request they issue the remaining insurance funds to me expediently. 

PennyMac can not confirm that the loan has been paid off, despite multiple confirmations to me attesting that it has been via email. They will not release the remaining insurance funds and have advised it could take up to a combined span of 31 days to release the funds. This includes 10 days to verify that the loan has been closed and a 21 day period to process and send the funds. 

It is unacceptable and unethical for PennyMac to delay this payout for an event that happened in [Redacted], especially after multiple confirmations that the loan has been paid off. This delaying tactic allows PennyMac to accrue additional interest on the funds that they simply will not release. 

" Canned responses '' with PennyMac 's typical verbiage of " sorry we missed the mark '' or " we apologize that you feel this delay doesn't meet your expectations '' are not acceptable. The expedient, if not immediate, release of my funds from their impoundment at PennyMac is the only agreeable solution to the situation PennyMac has created. When released, these funds should be sent via check in a trackable, overnight mailer.

metadata.full_snippet:
My federal student loans were being serviced by [Redacted] at the start of [Redacted]. I am on the Income-Based Repayment plan ( IBR ) which is a type of Income-Driven Payment plan that requires yearly income recertification or the payment increases to the what the borrower would have paid had they been on a standard payment plan when first entering IBR. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]  I received notification that my IBR payment would soon increase and that I needed to recertify my income by [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] or my current payment rate ( {$590.00} ) would expire on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and subsequent payments and would increase to {$2800.00}. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]  I submitted my IBR recertification to [Redacted] dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]  the COVID-19 Emergency Relief and Federal Student Aid ( COVID forbearance ) went into effect. All federal student loan borrowers, including myself, were notified by FSA that payments were automatically paused, interest was set at % 0, and income recertifications were not required while the forbearance was in effect. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I received the following email from [Redacted] It could take up to 15 business days for us to review and process this request for you. We understand that you want a response as quickly as possible and appreciate your patience. 

However, the COVID forbearance went into effect on this date. Thus, on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] my certification had NOT been officially processed and therefore my IBR from [Redacted]  was still active and in effect on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]  when COVID forbearance began. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] sent me a correspondence date [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] that I no longer met partial financial hardship and that my payment would increase to {$2800.00}. metadata.snippet: I received a voicemail on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, from a man named [Redacted] [Redacted], informing me that there was a " pre-litigate complaint '' forwarded to his office that morning. He said I had [Redacted] hours to reply with a verbal statement about my intention regardi...
metadata.full_snippet:
I received a voicemail on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, from a man named [Redacted] [Redacted], informing me that there was a " pre-litigate complaint '' forwarded to his office that morning. He said I had [Redacted] hours to reply with a verbal statement about my intention regarding the debt. 

I knew throwing around hints of a lawsuit was an empty threat, as I had received no written communication regarding one, but I made sure to call back to see what this is about. 

I called [Redacted] back on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023. He informed me that an old payday loan I defaulted on with a company called [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] had escalated to the point where they were pursuing legal action against me. He said notices had been sent to an old address of mine. I informed him I no longer live there and have received no notices. Rather than ask me for the correct address to send notices to, he went straight for payment. 

I was given the option to either pay {$2700.00} now to settle the debt or be sued for over {$6000.00}. According to him, the ability to pay in installments was no longer an option. 

I informed him I intended to pay the debt and had always intended to pay the debt, but that I don't have {$2700.00} right now and it would be at least a [Redacted]  before I do. He said I have until Monday before they send my file to the attorneys. 

Once again, an empty threat -- Monday is [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. I'm pretty sure neither he nor any attorneys will be working. 

Nonetheless, I told [Redacted] [Redacted] I would attempt to come up with the money by Monday. My plan was to look into loan options or put off paying some other bills in favor of settling this debt. 

However, on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I received another voicemail from [Redacted] [Redacted]. This one accused me of blocking his number, which I did not, and that they're now going to forward the complaint to the attorneys as a " direct refusal to comply '' even though I made a verbal promise to pay just the day before.

At no point in any of my communications with [Redacted] [Redacted] was I given a " Mini-Miranda Warning '' in accordance with the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act. Even though [Redacted] [Redacted] works for a pre-litigation firm and not a collection agency, my understanding of the FDCPA is they are still bound by the same debt collection regulations.

metadata.title: Vehicle loan or lease Dispute
metadata.snippet: This is a kind of long story so to make it short, I had a truck loan through PNC. Years I had this loan setup through autopay and back in [Redacted] I tried to take it off autopay due to some unexpected issues with money and for the first time since opening the loan I did not hav...
metadata.full_snippet: This is a kind of long story so to make it short, I had a truck loan through PNC. Years I had this loan setup through autopay and back in [Redacted] I tried to take it off autopay due to some unexpected issues with money and for the first time since opening the loan I did not have the money in the account it was going to have to be late and they were understanding and said no problem we'll take you off autopay and you'll just have to make a one time payment when you can. Well the date of my usual autopay always came out it did. Not once but tried twice. Causing hundreds of dollars of overdraft and return payment fees that I was forced to just pay cause my bank said not there problem and PNC said oops sorry it was a mess up in our system but your fees are not our problem. Cool, fast forward to now the next month. Already now having made the payment I owed from [Redacted] after catching back up from the overdraft and return item fees, on top of paying [Redacted] 's payment 4 days early on the [Redacted] of [Redacted] ( due date is [Redacted] and that's what the autopay was setup to ) being all caught up for the month and expecting to be back on track for my next payment for [Redacted], to my surprise I check my bank statement and yet again they're autopay system took out another payment. So again I call. They overdrafts my account again costing me more money in overdraft fees and return item fees and the real problem was from last month I assumed it would proceed to try again the next day like it did the month before and my direct deposit was going in that night so if it did try again I would be out the money. Again they understood but said they don't understand why they're system was doing this and the most they could do is send it to they're " escalations '' and we have to wait for them to investigate the problem and they'll be back to me within 48 hours. We'll sure as rain the system did try again, the money was in there and it did take it draining my bank account less then a month before [Redacted]. So I call and they say they're looking into the problem they'll be back in touch in another 24 hours. Now to make this even a worse story the truck I had on the loan actually blew the motor during this whole problem and I ended up trading it in because they said it was going to be months to repair through warranty because of backorder parts. Neither here nor there but it adds a little more confusion cause the account is now closed. So I waited another couple days for a call back from they're supposed escalations department and they never called. Countless calls and almost 3 weeks later cause they said they're escalations expert was out of office they finally said they don't know what happened they don't know why but the account is paid off and we'll mail you a check 7 to 10 days which is a little aggravating as it was being days before [Redacted] and they took {$660.00} dollars out of my account that I was now trying to make up for. So thinking it was over I waited and waited and it is now 20 days later from when they said they mailed the check and no check. I've left voicemails to the so called escalations expert 4 or 5 times since the [Redacted] no call back and if I call a normal representative they said they can't pull up anything cause my account is closed and only the escalations can. I'm at witts end with this and not sure what else to do. It's absolutely insane to me that not only am I out of this money cause of they're faulty system but I have now paid close to {$200.00} overdraft, return item and late fees on other bills that that {$660.00} dollars was supposed to be going to. If the shoe was on the other foot you can be sure I'd have to pay there fees but since they're a financial institution, I have to pay for they're negligence? I really apologize for the length of this complaint but I feel as if all info was necessary and I know for a fact somewhere in they're system it is recorded because between waiting for them just to tell me they'll finally give me my money back ever representative said the account was well noted. To the point of I would just call and say read the notes it's to long of a story. Please help. Thank you
