metadata.full_snippet:
*Mortgage Assistance Paperwork sent to Carrington on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 [Redacted]On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, a Reinstatement Letter was emailed to our email with the amount needed to reinstate the loan. The amount was {$8000.00} to be received by Carrington on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] [Redacted]  Pacific Standard Time. 

*Received a voicemail from [Redacted] [Redacted] on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] [Redacted]  *requesting a return call. 
*Returned phone call to Carrington at [Redacted] [Redacted]  and spoke to a female representative. 
Confirmed with representative that there would be no issues wiring the money on Saturday [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 from [Redacted] [Redacted]. Representative assured us that there would be no problems as long as the wire had an origination date on or before [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and the wire would be processed on Tuesday, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023. I confirmed again that there would be no issues due to the [Redacted] [Redacted] holiday, she reiterated what she had previously told me. 

[Redacted]On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 a wire transfer was sent from [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] MI at exactly [Redacted] [Redacted]  in the amount of {$8000.00} from an account belonging to [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] 

*The transfer was initiated by [Redacted] [Redacted] and approved by [Redacted] [Redacted] who was shown the instructions detailed in the Reinstatement Letter sent by Carrington Mortgage .

*On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] [Redacted]  we contacted [Redacted]  and spoke to [Redacted] [Redacted]o make sure the payment was received. [Redacted] said it had not yet been processed and to call back later in the afternoon as there can be a delay after a holiday. 

[Redacted]On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 called Carrington at [Redacted] [Redacted]  to check on the status of the payment. Carrington was still unable to locate the payment, we were asked to call back. 

[Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted]  called Carrington at [Redacted] [Redacted]  to inquire about the status of the payment. Call was escalated to a supervisor who still could not locate payment. Was told if the payment was bounced back to the account, the sale of the house would stand. 

[Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted] at [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted] received a text from [Redacted] who informed us he had purchased our property at auction. 

[Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  at [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] called Carrington again to locate the funds. [Redacted] was instructed to email [Redacted] [Redacted] with the wire transfer paperwork, which included the exact amount ( {$8.00}, [Redacted] ) and the transaction number ( [Redacted] ) and was told the cashier department would be able to locate the payment using both the amount and transaction number. 

*Called Carrington again on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] [Redacted]  to see if the payment had been located. Was told that the cashier department was closed for the evening and to call back in the morning. 

*Several calls were made on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. Each time we spoke to a different representative. Each time we were asked to give more time and call back and that the situation was escalated to a supervisor. 

*The money was pushed back to [Redacted] [Redacted] account [Redacted] [Redacted]  from Carrington Mortgage company. This was after spending the entire day on the phone with Carrington and being told they did not have the money, yet Carrington pushed the money back to the account. It was not returned for insufficient funds.

We never received a notice from the sheriff that our house was foreclosed. There was no notice of sale posted. We never received a certified letter saying the house was foreclosed. We have paperwork showing we made the payment prior to the date stated in the Reinstatement Letter. That paperwork is date and time stamped. We provided a very unique payment amount, as well as a transaction number that were both searchable according to Carringtons own representatives. Carrington contends they never had the money yet Carrington returned the money to [Redacted] [Redacted] account. I am surprised that they can return money that was not in their possession. The home was sold Tuesday morning before Carrington would have the appropriate time to process the payments made over the weekend, which was confirmed by Carringtons own representatives when they continued to tell us to call back that the payment takes time to process.

We believe that Carrington intentionally did not apply the payment. Carrington stood to make more money with the sale of our property than to apply the payment to our loan so we could resume payments. Carrington failed to properly notify us of the foreclosure and impending sale as required by law. At the very least, this is a terribly unethical practice which is par for the course for Carrington. It seems that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has taken action against Carrington for previous deceptive practices.

metadata.sub_issue: Reporting company used your report improperly
metadata.snippet: *** Attached is a PDF version of this complaint should formatting be an issue *** Concerned Parties : Missouri Higher Educ Loan Auth ( MOHELA/[Redacted] ) Re : Request for Correction Account # : [Redacted] Complaint Details : I, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redact...
metadata.full_snippet:
*** Attached is a PDF version of this complaint should formatting be an issue *** Concerned Parties : Missouri Higher Educ Loan Auth ( MOHELA/[Redacted] ) Re : Request for Correction Account # : [Redacted] Complaint Details : I, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], am contacting you regarding the below items on the above account. The reporting of these items evidence violations of federal law. I have enumerated these violations in further detail in sections ( A ) through ( C ) below. Each item is numbered in the attached marked copy of my recent credit report for reference. 


Payment History/Rating : ** ( see attachment 1 ) ** ( [Redacted] ) [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : [Redacted] ( [Redacted] ) [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : [Redacted] ( [Redacted] ) [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : [Redacted] Background : In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], facing the culmination of a prolonged two-year period of unemployment exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, and having exhausted my unemployment benefits, I engaged in a conversation with Mohela in efforts to explore viable options under the prevailing circumstances. This dialogue resulted in my enrollment in Mohela 's Unemployment Reduced Repayment Option, a program tailored to provide temporary relief through reduced monthly payments.

The accommodation, a direct response to my financial hardship enabled me to adhere to a modified payment schedule during this challenging phase. By [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I had successfully navigated back to my regular payment schedule. 

However, in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], upon meticulous review of my credit report, I encountered an unexpected revelation - the report reflected delinquencies for the months of [Redacted] through [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. This discovery was particularly disconcerting as it contradicted my understanding of the provisions under the [Redacted]ARES Act, which, to my knowledge, should have precluded the reporting of such adverse information. Compounding this issue was the absence of any form of written notice from Mohela regarding the reporting of this negative information, a lapse that raises significant concerns about compliance with mandatory disclosure requirements and the overall integrity of the credit reporting process.

( A ) : Violation of FCRA Provisions During COVID-19 Pandemic Accommodation Under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( F ), the law is unequivocal : if a furnisher, like Mohela in my case, extends an accommodation to a consumer, and the consumer adheres to the terms of this accommodation, the obligations or account must be reported as current. The failure of Mohela to adhere to this mandate, in my situation, is not only a glaring oversight but a direct contravention of the FCRA.

The agreement between Mohela and I enacting their Unemployment Reduced Repayment Option ( **See Attachment 2** ) constituted an accommodation*** given that, per the CARES Act definition, the coverage period extended through [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted]. Despite adhering to the new payment terms, Mohela 's subsequent reporting of my monthly credit obligation failed to reflect the mandated " current '' or PAANL status. This misreporting occurred despite my account being brought to a current status during the accommodation period*****, which should have triggered a reporting adjustment reported as stipulated under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( F ) ( ii ) ( bb ).

In light of these violations, I demand that you take immediate corrective action by 1. Modifying items ( 1-3 ) to PAANL or Paid on Time ( B ) : Failure to Provide Required Notice of Negative Information Contrary to the obligations outlined in 15 USC 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 7 ) ( A ) ( i ), Mohela neglected its duty to provide written notice to me prior to, or within 30 days after, reporting negative information to credit bureaus. Upon discovering adverse entries on my credit report, I conducted a meticulous review of all my billing statements, separate correspondences, and electronic records. This thorough examination revealed a complete absence of the legally required notification from Mohela concerning the reporting of this negative information.

This omission not only represents a significant lapse in compliance with the FCRA but also deprived me of the opportunity to address or rectify the issues preemptively. Such an oversight is particularly consequential, given the substantial impact of negative credit reporting on a consumer 's financial health. This breach necessitates immediate attention and corrective action to rectify the resulting inaccuracies in my credit report and to ensure compliance with the FCRAs stringent consumer protection standards.

NOTE : Distinctiveness and Independence of Legal Arguments and Requests It is important to note that arguments and codes presented in both section ( A ) and section ( B ) are distinct and separate from each other. While each section advocates for the removal of certain items from my credit report, the reasons and legal bases provided in each section are independent and should be considered on their own merits.

Therefore, the requests for the removal of items and their supporting codes within each section should in no way be construed as diminishing or negating the validity of the requests made from other codes in other sections. Each code within each section provides separate and equally compelling legal grounds for the removal of different items from my credit report. I trust that these requests will be evaluated individually.

***15 USC 1681s2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( F ) ( i ) ( I ) ****15 USC 1681s2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( F ) ( i ) ( II ) defines the end of the covered period as 120 days after the termination of the National Emergencies Act declared on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. The act was terminated on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ( see Termination of National Emergency Concerning COVID19, Pub. L. 1183, Apr. 10, 2023, 137 Stat. 6 ), thus the coverage period extends to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] *****See Attachment [Redacted] ( Billing statement for [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) - The accommodation period ended [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.title: Credit card Dispute
metadata.snippet: Reference # [Redacted] Dear Chase Card Services, I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to express my deep frustration and dissatisfaction with the challenges I have encountered while attempting to open business credit cards with Chase. As a longstanding customer, I have...
metadata.full_snippet:
Reference # [Redacted] Dear Chase Card Services, I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to express my deep frustration and dissatisfaction with the challenges I have encountered while attempting to open business credit cards with Chase. As a longstanding customer, I have recently experienced a series of perplexing and time-consuming issues that have significantly impacted my confidence in the application process. 

In early [Redacted], I applied for the Chase Ink Business card, and to my relief, the application was swiftly approved. However, my satisfaction was short-lived when I faced difficulties creating an online account for the card. Upon contacting Chase, I was directed to the fraud department, where I was asked a question about a loan from decades ago. Unfortunately, I couldn't recall the answer, leading to a requirement to visit a Chase branch to verify my identity and confirm that I was indeed the applicant and not a victim of identity theft. Although the in-person visit resolved the issue, the inconvenience and uncertainty surrounding this process were disheartening. 

Fast forward to early [Redacted], when I applied for another Chase Ink Business card under a different business entity ( the first being a sole proprietorship and the second with a valid business EIN ). Despite having recently and physically verified my identity at a Chase branch with [Redacted] forms of identification for a similar application just [Redacted] months prior, I am once again being asked to submit additional documents to verify my identity. This repeated demand for verification is perplexing and frustrating, given that I am not a victim of identity theft, have never been one, and have never placed a credit freeze on my account. My loyalty to Chase over the years adds to my confusion as to why my business applications consistently undergo a secondary verification process, citing reasons such as " Name verification - name provided is unable to be verified. '' I am reaching out to seek resolution and clarity on this matter. I am requesting a thorough review of my account and the application process to identify the root cause of these persistent issues. It is crucial to understand why my applications are subject to additional scrutiny, especially when others do not face such hurdles.

I value my relationship with Chase and believe in the importance of security measures. However, the repeated and seemingly unnecessary verification process is eroding the trust I have placed in the bank 's systems. I trust that you will investigate this matter promptly and provide a resolution that ensures a smoother and more efficient experience for loyal customers like myself.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to a prompt and satisfactory resolution.

metadata.full_snippet: Our loan originated on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2017 with OneMain Financial. When we first applied for this loan, the company did not explain that we were taking out a title loan. We just assumed that we were putting our car up for collateral, but were young and naive and didn't understand what that meant. The company did nothing to explain it to us, and therefore, we ended up owing {$17000.00} on a car that was worth less than {$5000.00}. Since that original loan, we have had to " extend '' our loan several times, especially through covid. There was even an additional life insurance premium added to our contract that we were told we were required to purchase. So, we have been paying 18 % interest on a {$1300.00} now for [Redacted] years. Currently, when you login to our account, it shows that they total owed is around {$9400.00} but when we call to get a pay off amount, they tell us we owe upwards of {$11000.00} due to the extensions on our account. Again, no one told us about this. Most recently, I found out that a family member of mine went to a local branch of OneMain, the employee ( s ) there gave them ALL of our account information including the interest, amount owed, original amount financed. This seems like a major breach of contract. There are so many issues here that I don't even know where to begin.

metadata.full_snippet: I have contacted Freedom Mortage several times in an attempt for a repayment plan from a Covid forbearance, when I lost my job due to the closures. They offered this forbearance plan so easily with only a few clicks and no real application. I since have started work again and have more than enough to do a repayment plan for 6 or 12 months, which they say the offer. I have applied several times and they never call back and just keep sending new packets. When I ask for a call back from a manager they say the notes said they did call me back. I have no missed calls from them and no messages on my online account or on my phone. It seems like they are purposely not trying to work with me because I can afford to pay it back. The application is ridiculously long and difficult and they keep saying to do it all again. I even had a manger tell me I was approved and then never would call me back and no one can find that anywhere now. They only want to talk about foreclosure options or refinancing with them. They also blame the VA and their rules that are the issue. When I called the VA representative he stated that is not true that they do not even have a time frame for a repayment plan that according to their loan rules I could take as long as I needed as long as once I started the repayment plan it was forward progress. That there would not be a reason for refinancing unless I defaulted, after the agreed on repayment plan. I am at a loss and do not know what to do I am a [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] veteran and dont want to lose my house or my 2.25 % APR. Please help!

metadata.full_snippet:
I trust this message finds you well. My purpose in writing to you today is to bring attention to a matter of significant concern regarding the contractual agreement associated with my recent vehicle purchase from [Redacted] [Redacted], an affiliate dealership of Credit Acceptance. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I entered into a financing arrangement for a [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], with [Redacted] miles on the odometer. While I understand that financing comes with associated costs, it has come to my attention that I may have fallen victim to what is commonly referred to as " payment packing. '' The disclosed cash price for the vehicle, an exorbitant {$11000.00}, raises serious questions about the transparency and fairness of the transaction. My independent research indicates that the market value of the [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], with similar mileage, is considerably lower than the amount I was charged. 

Upon inquiring about purchasing the vehicle outright with cash, I was informed that the cash price would be higher but not to the extent reflected in the contract. This lack of clarity and transparency is deeply troubling. 

The itemization in the amount financed on the contract further reveals inconsistencies. It shows that [Redacted] [Redacted] sold me the vehicle through Credit Acceptance for {$10000.00}, while the service contract or warranty indicates that the car was sold for {$10000.00}. This discrepancy in the recorded sale price contributes to a sense of confusion and reinforces concerns about the accuracy of the information provided.

These discrepancies, coupled with the apparent inflation of the vehicle 's cash price, align with concerns raised in the case filed by the New York Attorney General and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) against Credit Acceptance. As a consumer, I believe these actions may be in violation of the Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ). 

According to 12 U.S.C. 5536 ( a ) of the CFPA, it is considered a violation for any covered person or service provider to engage in any unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice. I am reaching out with the hope that we can address and rectify these concerns promptly and amicably.

I kindly request a thorough review of the discrepancies mentioned and a transparent explanation of the pricing structure associated with my purchase. Additionally, I am open to discussions aimed at reaching a fair resolution that aligns with consumer protection laws.

Your prompt attention to this matter is highly appreciated, and I look forward to your timely response.

metadata.full_snippet:
In [Redacted] of [Redacted], I applied to consolidate approximately all of my undergraduate and graduate student debt via Studentaid.gov. I used the Studentaid.gov calculator to estimate the total sum of my forthcoming consolidation loan to verify the expected sum after consolidation. The debt was being consolidated from [Redacted], who held all of my loans, and was to be transferred to EdFinancial. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted], I received notice of my repayment schedule and consolidated loan from EdFinancial. The total balance appeared accurate per the consolidation terms I had agreed to. However, on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I received an updated statement, showing an additional, erroneous amount of {$290000.00} that had been added to my total student loan debt with no explanation. 

Upon reviewing my [Redacted] and EdFinancial accounts, I can see this same erroneous amount, {$290000.00}, added as a Disbursement to my [Redacted] account on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted]. However, this amount was deducted as a - {$290000.00} " Write-off '' that same day. My EdFinancial online account shows a Disbursement of my student loan balance on [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] This Disbursed amount is accurate. However, it is followed by an Adjustment that same day, adding the erroneous {$290000.00} to that balance. There is no explanation of what this adjustment relates to. 

I have contacted EdFinancial numerous times by phone and in writing since [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ( over four months ) in effort to resolve this error. EdFinancial has failed to respond to my request or even acknowledge that an error was made. 

Ive also opened a case with the Federal Student Aid Ombudsman via the U.S. Department of Education 's Dispute and Resolution office. EdFinancial responded to the Ombudsman once asking for more time and then, in the Ombudsmans words, went silent. The Ombudsman escalated the case but has not provided me with any updates. 

It has been several months since my consolidation was completed, and interest is now accrueing on the inaccurate balance claimed by EdFinancial. I am not comfortable paying my student loan until the balance and interest are retroactively adjusted to be accurate. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I asked EdFinancial to apply an administrative forbearance to my account, but their representative declined. Instead, they informed me that there is a student loan onramp for the coming months, and that my account will not be affected if I miss payments, so I am declining to make payments until this situation is resolved. 

A record of my communication with EdFinancial and the Federal Ombudsman is included below. I have not received a response to any of this communication. Please help me to resolve this situation. 

Communication Record : [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : Phone call to inform EdFinancial of the inaccurate balance and request for an investigation into my account. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I wrote to EdFinancial using the contact form on their website explaining the situation and requesting that it be addressed immediately. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I wrote to a Federal Student Aid Ombudsman to inform them of the situation with EdFInancial and asked whether I should report this to Studentaid.gov. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I called EdFinancial to follow up ; they were closed. I received a callback until [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. I missed the call ; EdFinancial did not leave a voicemail. My account had not been updated. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I followed up with a Federal Student Aid Ombudsman in writing. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I called the Federal Student Aid Ombudsman and left a voicemail. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I called EdFinancial and requested a callback. EdFinancial returned my call that day at [Redacted] [Redacted]. I explained again that my balance was incorrect ; the representative did not see any notes on my account from my [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] call. The representative said that they would leave a note on my account and look into it. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : The Federal Student Aid Ombudsman returned my call, reviewed my case, and confirmed that an additional balance of {$290000.00} ( which has since grown due to interest ) had been applied to my account. The Ombudsman opened a new case number and said that it was not necessary for me to file a report on Studentaid.gov, as the case had already been escalated to the U.S. Department of Education 's Dispute and Resolution office. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I received a canned email from an EdFinancial Representative in response to my written request on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. My original message about the balance error was embedded below the Edfinancial Representatives email, but the Representative did not address it at all. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I replied to the email from the EdFinancial Representative at [Redacted], restating the issue, shared the Federal Case #, and recopied my original note in full. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I called the Ombudsman to follow up but did not get through. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : The Federal Student Aid Ombudsman returned my call and left me a voicemail stating that EdFinancial had gone radio silent on them. They stated that they had followed up three times on my case ; the first time EdFinancial requested more time they have not responded to the Ombudsmans other inquiries. The Ombudsman shared that they had escalated the case, and didnt have more information yet. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I called EdFinancial and was able to get through to a representative. The call lasted 49 minutes. Unfortunately, the EdFinancial Representative did not see any notes on my account from the previous calls, could not access the written communication Id sent, and had no information on the Federal Ombudsmans case. The EdFinancial Representative repeatedly suggested that the additional {$290000.00} dollars that was applied to my balance could be due to interest capitalization or fees. However, this is not mathematically possible given my interest rates, previous loan balance, and the length of time I've held the loans for. The representative did not seem to be listening and during the call. Instead, they sent me four canned emails about unrelated topics, including : Public Loan Forgiveness, Auto Pay, how to visit StudentAid.gov, and how to set up an online account. Eventually, the EdFinancial Representative agreed to have my case investigated, '' but they were unable to tell me what this meant. The representative would not commit to contacting [Redacted], who their company received my loans from. The representative also declined my requests to speak with a supervisor. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I missed a call from EdFinancial. No voicemail was left, my account had not been updated, and no one had responded to my previous inquiries. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I received an email from [Redacted] that reads " We see that we were able to speak to you since your e-mail inquiry on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and your inquiry is resolved. If you still have outstanding questions, please reach back out and we will be able to assist. '' However, as described above, my call on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] did not resolve my inquiry in any way, and no action had been taken to address the errors on my account. 

[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] : I wrote to EdFinanical at [Redacted], copying the Federal Student Aid Ombudsman. I shared that I had a time-sensitive request, and included my account #, the Federal Case #, and a summary of the inaccurate balance and interest that have been applied to my account. I asked EdFinancial to confirm that they had received the email, complete their investigation, remove the inaccurate balance and any associated inaccurate interest from my account, and respond to the federal inquiry. 

As of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], the only communications I have received from EdFinancial are automated account reminders. Even when I have spoken and written directly to EdFinancial Customer Service Representatives, I have only received automated responses that do not relate in any way to my request to address the {$290000.00} that was erroneously applied to my account during the consolidation process.

Prior to endorsing the bill, I contacted in writing, the CFO of Capital One, [Redacted] [Redacted], as agent of behalf of the principal, accepting all rights, all titles, all interest and all guaranteed equity owed to the principal of the account and instructing [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] to apply the principal 's balance of {$6300.00} to the principal 's account and to accept the tender of payment. In this letter, I also stated that if there were any discrepancies, that he should respond in writing within 5 business days of receipt and if there was no communication, I could assume that the aforesaid instructions had been completed. Many days later, I sent a second letter to [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] as an opportunity to cure, expressing the same acceptance of all titles, all rights, all interest and all guaranteed equity to the principal and to apply the principal 's balance to the principal 's account and that he should respond within 5 business days or receipt if there were any discrepancies and again, that if there was no communication, that I could assume he had completed the instructions given. I had received confirmation by certified mail that the letters sent to CFO [Redacted] [Redacted] had been received. I did not receive anything in return from CFO of Capital One [Redacted] [Redacted], so as stated in the letters sent to him, I assumed that the instructions given had been completed. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, days after sending my first endorsed bill, I tried to make a purchase using my Capital One card, which still had an available credit balance from the precious debit payment that was made on the account from the previous month and my card was declined. When I called Capital One to inquire why my card had been declined, the representative that I spoke to, told me that my account was closed on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 because of the instructions that were written on the remittance coupon. Days later I received a letter in the mail from Capital One stating that my account had been closed because " activity on this or another account is not consistent with our expectations for account usage and violates the Capital One Customer Agreement '' and that I would still have to make payments on said closed account. I also received a letter from Capital One saying that they had removed my name and address from future Capital One credit offers. I asked Capital One for full disclosure of the account including a copy of the original contract for the account and the sent me a copy of their Customer Agreement which reads under subsection " Making Payments '', " Your payments must be made in U.S dollars from a U.S account in a form acceptable to us. We do not accept cash payments through the mail. You may not make payments with funds from your account or any other credit account with us or any other company in the Capital One organization. You must send mailed payments to us as instructed on your statement unless we tell you otherwise ''. I believe that Capital One is discriminating against me by not allowing me to endorse my bill using a bill of exchange, which is applicable by law under the Bill of Exchange Act as well as by removing my information prohibiting me from being able to obtain any credit through Capital One, which if a violation of the Equal Credit Opportunity Act.

metadata.full_snippet: For several months my tenant paid for a portion of her rent with money orders that were issued by Walmart in [Redacted], PA. Walmart now refuses to cash these money orders despite the fact that they were made out to me and I presented identification. I attempted to cash them at my financial institutions on several occasions within the last 12 months. They would not honor them. It is now one year and several months past the one year mark from when two of these money orders were issued, and though there is no mention of additional fees to cash them in Pennsylvania on their website, nor on the money order, [Redacted] [Redacted] claims that the money orders have depreciated significantly in value, and can not be cashed any longer at face value, though it does not mention this anywhere on the money order nor on their website either. Walmart refuses to cash even the money orders that it issued within the past month. When I called to find out why, the representative stated that it somehow violated Walmart policy to cash my money orders that were made out to me to cash, but she would not say why. I feel that this is discriminatory because I am a divorced woman who owns a home.

metadata.full_snippet: This is a follow-up complaint from the initial complaint I filed on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] # [Redacted]. Please refer to this initial complaint for additional history on my account. This follow-up is warranted because the correction made to my account in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] still does not comply with the CARES Act for student loan income driven repayment income recertification. My account was updated in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] following my initial complaint with an IDR Recertification date adjustment from [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Due to the CARES Act, and according to information provided by the U.S. Department of Education on the fsa.gov website, income recertification for income-based repayment is not required and can not be required by loan servicers any date before 6 months after the end of the student loan payment pause. The earliest recertification for any direct federal loans based on this information would be on or after [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Since my initial IBR income recertification date was scheduled for [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], this date should have been pushed by 12 months automatically and then based on the current scheduled end of the student loan pause, by another 12 months to reflect a date of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. This would entail the same monthly payment requirement as was determined by my IDR application in the amount of {$170.00} starting with payments on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] to be certified through [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. I have called MOHELA customer service an additional two times to get the IDR income recertification date updated to be in compliance with the CARES Act twice since the last correction was made to my account with calls on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. The first call on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], the customer service representative assured me that my account would be corrected and an additional call would not be warranted. Without any change occurring on my account in the subsequent 30 days, and the date in question coming up rapidly, I called again on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] to check the status and notify MOHELA that I would pursue an additional consumer protection complaint if the issue was not fixed within 30 days. I am requesting that MOHELA adjust my income driven repayment plan income recertification date to be in compliance with the CARES Act and therefore, the date currently reflected on my account of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] be updated to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted].

metadata.full_snippet:
On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] I checked my MoneyLion account and noticed an unauthorized transaction on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 for {$500.00} that was pending. I immediately locked my debit card and looked for my debit card but I was unable to find it. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] I called MoneyLion customer service to report my card lost and dispute the unauthorized transaction. The MoneyLion representative canceled my debit and ordered a new debit card for me. He then told me that since the unauthorized transaction was still pending he was not able to start the dispute claim until it posted to my account. I asked when it would post and he told me it could take 1 to 5 days to post but he would be monitoring my account and when it does post he would start my dispute claim for the unauthorized transaction and contact me to confirm. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] I had still not received a confirmation from the MoneyLion representative so I called to check the status of my dispute claim. The MoneyLion representative told me that there was a note on my account showing I reported the unauthorized transaction but the previous representative failed to start the dispute claim process. The representative opened the dispute claim for the unauthorized transaction then asked if I needed to order a new debit card and I explained that the previous representative already ordered a new debit card for me. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] I received an email from MoneyLion requesting that I complete the attached statement of fraud form which I immediately completed and submitted by email. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] I received an email from MoneyLion stating they have thoroughly investigated my claim and determined that no error had occurred and they have come to this conclusion because it is a card present transaction initiated by me and I have indicated that I have possession of the card. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] I responded to MoneyLions email informing them once again that my debit card was lost and I did not have it in my possession which is exactly what I told them during both phone calls as well as what I stated on the statement of fraud form which I completed and previously returned. I also attached another copy of the form to this email for them to reference. After emailing my response I called MoneyLion to request a copy of the documents used in the investigation and requested they reopen my dispute claim since they wrongfully denied then closed my claim based on incorrect information. The MoneyLion representative [Redacted] [Redacted] told me she would put in my request for the documents and a request to reopen claim based on the additional information I provided. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] I received an email stating that in order to reopen my dispute claim they would need me to provide additional information or relevant documentation to support my claim. At [Redacted] I emailed my response informing them that I had already provided additional information by email and again over the phone to [Redacted] [Redacted] when I requested the claim be reopened. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] I received an email from a MoneyLions dispute representative named [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] the documents I requested. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] I replied to the email from [Redacted] [Redacted] and requested once again for my dispute claim to be reopened because they wrongfully closed my claim based on incorrect information stating the debit card was in my possession when in fact the debit card was lost and no longer in my possession. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 at [Redacted] I received a response email from [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] that in order to reopen my dispute claim I would need to provide additional information or relevant documentation to support my claim. 

I have already provided the required information and relevant documentation to support my claim several times and I will not continue to keep repeating myself to MoneyLions incompetent representatives.

metadata.full_snippet:
The mortgage company is claiming that they have denied my request to close the escrow account that the only reason they opened was to pay for the hazard insurance. Now they are claiming that they have to keep it open because I supposedly have paid my loan over 30 days for a few months which is false information. This company keeps lying over and over and keeps bringing up the hazard insurance they obtained which I am not disputing. Yes they got the hazard insurance and opened the escrow account for that purpose. The hazard insurance was for {$3900.00} so why are they asking me to pay {$840.00} every month to cover that amount for the next 12 months when that only equals to [Redacted] [Redacted] monthly. They are trying to rip me off and continue to charge me for an escrow account that has now been paid in full and has a positive balance. This escrow account should no longer be open because the reason it was opened for has been resolved. The mortgage lender opened this escrow account for the sole purpose of paying the insurance and that has been covered so why would you keep it open now when I am not supposed to have an escrow account? I have attached my payment history showing that the months they are claiming I paid over 30 days late, I actually paid on time and by the end of the month which they advised me is the latest I could before being considered deliqnuent. This mortgage company is a huge fraud and a huge red flag because now they are making up lies to try to continue to charge fraudulently for an escrow account that should be closed. Please find attached the payments made for [Redacted], [Redacted], [Redacted] and [Redacted] all within the month and never once 30 days past due. 

[Redacted] was paid on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] was paid on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] was paid on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] was paid [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] was paid [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] was paid [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] All within the month the payment was due each month and I was told by them that as long as I pay within that month the payment is due, it is not 30 days late and neither of these payments are 30 days late. Now they are lying to say I'm delinquent several times to keep this fraudulent escrow account open and for what? I don't owe you anything anymore. The money that was disbursed on my behalf for the insurance has been paid in full so why would I continue to pay into an escrow account that I am not supposed to have. If I need to obtain a homeowners insurance policy now to cancel this escrow then I need to be told that but no one ever gives me accurate information when I call. They don't know what lies to make up. I was holding off on getting insurance because this insurance is good until [Redacted] and has been paid off in full so why would I get another insurance policy until then. If I do get an insurance policy effective in [Redacted], are they going to refund me for the amount that they were overpaid for and close out the escrow and pay the funds that are sitting in escrow as that were overpaid? This company needs to be reported to the Federal Trade Commission for fraudulent activities and for lying to keep illegal escrow accounts open after the reason they opened it for has been paid in full. I will not pay for any escrow fees when I am not supposed to have one anymore. I pay my taxes directly and I will obtain a homeowners insurance policy in [Redacted]. As soon as I send proof, I want a refund for everything that they have been overpaid for and the escrow account shut down and my monthly payment back to normal. I also want this company heavily investigated for their fraudulent activities that have been done to my account. 

I'm also attaching the payment confirmation emails for the months they are claiming that I was over 30 days late. I don't have [Redacted] because I made the payment over the phone since they didn't allow to pay online anymore due to it being grayed out.

metadata.full_snippet:
15 U.S. Code 1681n - Civil liability for willful noncompliance U.S. Code Notes prev | next ( a ) In general Any person who willfully fails to comply with any requirement imposed under this subchapter with respect to any consumer is liable to that consumer in an amount equal to the sum of ( 1 ) ( A ) any actual damages sustained by the consumer as a result of the failure or damages of not less than {$100.00} and not more than {$1000.00} ; or ( B ) in the case of liability of a natural person for obtaining a consumer report under false pretenses or knowingly without a permissible purpose, actual damages sustained by the consumer as a result of the failure or {$1000.00}, whichever is greater ; ( 2 ) such amount of punitive damages as the court may allow ; and ( 3 ) in the case of any successful action to enforce any liability under this section, the costs of the action together with reasonable attorneys fees as determined by the court. 
( b ) Civil liability for knowing noncompliance Any person who obtains a consumer report from a consumer reporting agency under false pretenses or knowingly without a permissible purpose shall be liable to the consumer reporting agency for actual damages sustained by the consumer reporting agency or {$1000.00}, whichever is greater. 

( c ) Attorneys fees Upon a finding by the court that an unsuccessful pleading, motion, or other paper filed in connection with an action under this section was filed in bad faith or for purposes of harassment, the court shall award to the prevailing party attorneys fees reasonable in relation to the work expended in responding to the pleading, motion, or other paper. 

( d ) Clarification of willful noncompliance For the purposes of this section, any person who printed an expiration date on any receipt provided to a consumer cardholder at a point of sale or transaction between [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], and [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], but otherwise complied with the requirements of section 1681c ( g ) of this title for such receipt shall not be in willful noncompliance with section 1681c ( g ) of this title by reason of printing such expiration date on the receipt.

metadata.full_snippet:
Subject : Complaint Regarding Unjustified Account Freeze and Delayed Resolution by Coinbase Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), I am writing to file a formal complaint against Coinbase , Inc., regarding the ongoing freeze on my account and the unreasonable delays in its resolution. 

Account Freeze and Financial Hardship : Since [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], my Coinbase account has been frozen, restricting access to {$14000.00} of my funds. The alleged reason for the freeze is " suspicious activity, '' but I have received no specific details about this activity despite repeated attempts to clarify the situation. 

I have contacted Coinbase customer service via phone on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and attempted to provide any necessary information to expedite the investigation. However, each call resulted in a further delay in accessing my funds. The latest estimated resolution date, originally [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], and has been pushed back several times to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], a delay of 60+ days, with no clear explanation or update on progress. 

This ongoing freeze has caused significant financial hardship. I have missed out on time-sensitive investment opportunities, resulting in a loss of several [Redacted] dollars. The constant uncertainty and shifting timelines exacerbate my stress and disrupt my financial stability. 

Transparency and Fair Treatment : I vehemently assert that my account does not exhibit any genuine " suspicious activity. '' On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], a customer service representative confirmed that their system did not detect any frozen activity on my account. I am a legitimate user of the platform and have always complied with Coinbase 's Terms of Service. In addition, one the first call ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) the service representative said my account would be escalated and reviewed in 3-5 business days. When I made the second call after not hearing back in this time frame, I was told it had been rejected with no explanation or notification. I have called 3 more times after this each opening a new ticket to be escalated each call and have not heard and feed back about these tickets. On the last call on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] the date at which my account was supposed to be available the representative told me they had pushed it back an additional 60 days. I was not informed of this. through this time I had re-verified my ID and sent emails responding to coinbase about myself and intent of using there platform ( which they requested ). I have asked to speak tho a manager each time on the phone and they will nnot give me anyone to talk to.They have completely left me in the dark after taking my money costing me {$1000.00} 's in investment opportunity cost. 

Therefore, I demand immediate action to rectify this situation. Specifically, I request : A full and transparent explanation for the account freeze, including the precise details of the alleged suspicious activity. 
An expedited review of my case and a guaranteed timeline for regaining access to my funds. 
Direct communication with a dedicated representative who can provide regular updates on the investigation 's progress. 
While I understand the importance of Coinbase 's security protocols, the current handling of my situation is unreasonable and inflicts undue hardship. I expect a prompt and fair resolution to this matter. 

Attached to this complaint are copies of my communication history with Coinbase, including call logs and email transcripts. I urge you to investigate this matter and hold Coinbase accountable for their unfair and detrimental practices. 

Thank you for your time and consideration. 

Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.snippet: Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 USC 1681, Section 602a ), it is emphasized that consumer reporting agencies, such as [Redacted], Experian, and [Redacted] must carry out their responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and res...
metadata.full_snippet:
Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 USC 1681, Section 602a ), it is emphasized that consumer reporting agencies, such as [Redacted], Experian, and [Redacted] must carry out their responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and respect for the consumer 's right to privacy. As a consumer, I am entitled to ensure the protection of my private information, as supported by 15 USC 6801, which states It is the policy of the Congress that each financial institution has an affirmative and continuing obligation to respect the privacy of its customers and to protect the security and confidentiality of those customers nonpublic personal information. '' The entity providing information to credit agencies, commonly known as the 'Furnisher of information, ' qualifies as a financial institution under this title. According to 15 USC 1681, Section 604 a ( 2 ), a consumer reporting agency may only furnish a consumer report in accordance with the written instructions of the relevant consumer. In this case, both the financial institution ( Furnisher of information ) and the consumer reporting agencies, [Redacted], Experian, and [Redacted] lack my consent and, specifically, my written consent to furnish this information. 

Referring to 15 USC 6802 ( b ) ( c ), which states that A financial institution may not disclose nonpublic personal information to a nonaffiliated third party unless the consumer is given an explanation of how the consumer can exercise that nondisclosure option. Unfortunately, the furnisher of information did not inform me of my right to exercise this option. 

Furthermore, 15 USC 1681C ( a ) ( 5 ) explicitly states Except as authorized under subsection ( b ), no consumer reporting agency may make any consumer report containing any of the following items of information : Any other adverse item of information, other than records of convictions of crimes which antedates the report by more than seven years. Therefore, reporting this adverse item without my permission is a violation of the law. 

According to 15 U.S. Code 1681s2 ( A ) ( 1 ) A, A person shall not furnish any information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if the person knows or has reasonable cause to believe that the information is inaccurate. Additionally, 15 U.S. Code 1681e mandates that every consumer reporting agency must maintain reasonable procedures to avoid violations of section 1681c and limit the furnishing of consumer reports to the purposes listed under section 1681b. 

[Redacted], Experian, and [Redacted] appear to be failing in maintaining these reasonable procedures. Furthermore, as per 12 CFR 1016.7, [Redacted], Experian and [Redacted] have failed to comply with all the laws mentioned above.

metadata.full_snippet:
To Whom It May Concern, This letter is a formal complaint that you are reporting inaccurate and incomplete credit information. 
I am distressed that you have included the information below in my credit profile and that you have failed to maintain reasonable procedures in your operations to assure maximum possible accuracy in the credit reports you publish. Credit reporting laws ensure that bureaus report only 100 % accurate credit information. Every step must be taken to assure the information reported is completely accurate and correct. The following information therefore needs to be re-investigated. 
According to the Fair Credit Reporting Act, Section 609 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), you are required by federal law to verify, through the physical verification of the original signed consumer contract, any and all accounts that you post on a credit report. Otherwise anyone paying for your reporting services could fax, mail or email in a fraudulent account. 
I demand to see verifiable proof ( i.e. : an original consumer contract with my signature on it ) that you have on file for the account listed below. 

Your failure to positively verify these accounts has hurt my ability to obtain credit. Under the FCRA, unverifiable accounts must be removed and if you are unable to provide me a copy of verifiable proof, you must remove the account listed below. 
I demand that the following account be verified or removed immediately : The following account is not mine : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], Account Number : [Redacted] Please remove it from my credit report. 

I respectfully request to be provided proof of this alleged item, specifically the contract, note or other instrument bearing my signature. 
Failing that, the item must be deleted from the report as soon as possible. This information is entirely inaccurate and incomplete, and as such represents a very serious error in your reporting. Please delete this misleading information and supply a corrected credit profile to all creditors who have received a copy within the last six months, or the last two years for employment purposes.

Additionally, please provide the name, address, and telephone number of each credit grantor or other subscriber.

Under federal law, you have thirty ( 30 ) days to complete your investigation. Be advised that the description of the procedure used to determine the accuracy and completeness of the information is hereby requested as well, to be provided within fifteen ( 15 ) days of the completion of your investigation.

Thank you,

metadata.title: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports Dispute
metadata.sub_issue: Reporting company used your report improperly
metadata.snippet: Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 USC 1681, Section 602a ), it is emphasized that consumer reporting agencies, such as [Redacted], [Redacted], and TransUnion must carry out their responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and r...
metadata.full_snippet:
Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 USC 1681, Section 602a ), it is emphasized that consumer reporting agencies, such as [Redacted], [Redacted], and TransUnion must carry out their responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and respect for the consumer 's right to privacy. As a consumer, I am entitled to ensure the protection of my private information, as supported by 15 USC 6801, which states It is the policy of the Congress that each financial institution has an affirmative and continuing obligation to respect the privacy of its customers and to protect the security and confidentiality of those customers nonpublic personal information. '' The entity providing information to credit agencies, commonly known as the 'Furnisher of information, ' qualifies as a financial institution under this title. According to 15 USC 1681, Section 604 a ( 2 ), a consumer reporting agency may only furnish a consumer report in accordance with the written instructions of the relevant consumer. In this case, both the financial institution ( Furnisher of information ) and the consumer reporting agencies, [Redacted], [Redacted], and TransUnion lack my consent and, specifically, my written consent to furnish this information. 

Referring to 15 USC 6802 ( b ) ( c ), which states that A financial institution may not disclose nonpublic personal information to a nonaffiliated third party unless the consumer is given an explanation of how the consumer can exercise that nondisclosure option. Unfortunately, the furnisher of information did not inform me of my right to exercise this option.

Furthermore, 15 USC 1681C ( a ) ( 5 ) explicitly states Except as authorized under subsection ( b ), no consumer reporting agency may make any consumer report containing any of the following items of information : Any other adverse item of information, other than records of convictions of crimes which antedates the report by more than seven years. Therefore, reporting this adverse item without my permission is a violation of the law.

According to 15 U.S. Code 1681s2 ( A ) ( 1 ) A, A person shall not furnish any information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if the person knows or has reasonable cause to believe that the information is inaccurate. Additionally, 15 U.S. Code 1681e mandates that every consumer reporting agency must maintain reasonable procedures to avoid violations of section 1681c and limit the furnishing of consumer reports to the purposes listed under section 1681b. 

[Redacted], [Redacted], and TransUnion appear to be failing in maintaining these reasonable procedures. Furthermore, as per 12 CFR 1016.7, [Redacted], [Redacted] and TransUnion have failed to comply with all the laws mentioned above. 

I, the consumer, am rescinding any previous authorization given to [Redacted] [Redacted], whether it was written, unwritten, verbal, or nonverbal, to report ANY of my transaction history to ANY credit bureau. Not only am I opting out of all or any authorization, but I am also requesting that [Redacted] [Redacted] cease and desist immediately from all illegal activities. 

Finally, the CFPB is required to contact the consumer reporting agencies to update my consumer credit profile accordingly, specially for any transactions that [Redacted] [Redacted] has reported or any other transaction history or experiences I have with [Redacted] [Redacted] please have them fix these violations by deleting these transactions from my consumer report. 

Best regards,

As a responsible credit union member, I expect institutions like Navy Federal ...
metadata.full_snippet:
I am submitting a formal complaint against Navy Federal Credit Union, expressing significant concerns about potential privacy law violations, particularly the insufficient disclosure of opt-out rights. As a responsible credit union member, I expect institutions like Navy Federal Credit Union to uphold transparency, fairness, and compliance with regulations. Recent observations raise serious concerns, warranting a thorough investigation into Navy Federal Credit Union 's practices.

My primary concern is the apparent lack of disclosure regarding consumers ' right to opt out of information sharing, a crucial aspect of privacy. Section 15 USC 6802 ( b ) ( c ) mandates clear explanations, but Navy Federal Credit Union may not effectively communicate this information. The absence of opt-out information, a right under 12 CFR 1016.7, is troubling, hindering informed decisions and raising compliance questions. 

Beyond opt-out disclosures, concerns extend to potential Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 USC 1681 ) violations. Section 602a emphasizes fairness, impartiality, and respect for consumer privacy, areas where Navy Federal Credit Union may lack full compliance.

The apparent lack of information on opt-out options may signal broader insufficient privacy disclosures. Section 15 USC 1681C ( a ) ( 5 ) prohibits certain adverse information disclosure without proper authorization, necessitating clear privacy disclosures under The Privacy Act of 1974.

Notably, under 15 USC 6805, the privacy notice reveals involvement with third-party companies, implying potential Privacy Act and terms and conditions violations. 16 CFR Part 313 and 16 CFR 433.2 outline requirements for privacy practice information.

Emphasizing 5 USC 522a in relation to identity theft, protecting personal information is vital, and any false use of identity, as suspected with Navy Federal Credit Union, contravenes the law.

Additional concerns involve potential FCRA Sec 603 ( d ) ( 2 ) ( a ) ( I ) violations, as it prohibits having a consumer report containing solely transactional information. Such violations breach consumer trust and ignore fundamental principles of consumer protection.

Lastly, 15 U.S. Code 1681s2 ( A ) ( 1 ) A underscores the importance of furnishing accurate information to consumer reporting agencies, a responsibility that must be upheld.

In light of these concerns, I urgently request a thorough Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigation into Navy Federal Credit Union 's practices. I implore the Bureau to address opt-out and privacy disclosures, considering relevant laws, and ensure compliance with privacy laws and consumer protection statutes.

I appreciate your attention to this matter and trust the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau will take necessary steps to safeguard consumer rights.

metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing to bring to your attention certain concerns regarding the information contained in my consumer credit report, as provided by Experian, [Redacted] and [Redacted]. As a consumer, I am keenly aware of my rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and the importance of ensuring the accuracy, fairness, and privacy of my credit-related information. 

Under 15 USC 1681, Section 602a, there is a fundamental need to ensure that consumer reporting agencies exercise their responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and a respect for the consumer 's right to privacy. Furthermore, 15 USC 6801 underscores Congress 's policy that each financial institution has an ongoing obligation to respect the privacy of its consumers. 

I have recently become aware that [ [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ], a financial institution by definition, has reported certain information to your agency without obtaining my explicit consent as required by 15 USC 1681, Section 604a, Section 2. Additionally, I must assert my right to revoke any and all authorizations, whether verbal, nonverbal, written, implied, or otherwise, in accordance with 15 USC 6802 ( b ) ( c ). 

Moreover, it has come to my attention that the reported information includes adverse items, violating the statutory provision of 15 USC 1681 ( c ) ( a ) ( 5 ), which prohibits consumer reporting agencies from including certain items of information without proper authorization.

I wish to emphasize that, as per 15 USC 1681s-2 ( A ) ( 1 ) ( a ), any information furnished to a consumer reporting agency must be accurate. Given the discrepancies I have identified, it is evident that there may be inaccuracies in the reported information, constituting a potential violation of the law.

Furthermore, 15 USC 1681E mandates that consumer reporting agencies maintain reasonable procedures to avoid violations of section 1681C and limit the furnishing of consumer reports to the purposes listed under section 1681B. I am concerned that the procedures in place may not be sufficient to meet these statutory requirements.

In light of the aforementioned issues, I am formally disputing the accuracy of the information reported by [ [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ] and kindly request a thorough investigation into the matter. I have enclosed relevant documentation supporting my claim for your review. 

Please be advised that, under 12 CFR 1016.7, I am exercising my right to opt out of any adverse reporting services provided by [ [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ]. I trust that you will promptly investigate this matter and take the necessary steps to correct any inaccuracies in my credit report. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. I anticipate your cooperation and a swift resolution.

metadata.title: Credit card Dispute
metadata.snippet: I signed up for a best buy CitiBank card around [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. The terms were not explained to me by the employee that had signed me up or an information packet and the employee unbeknownst to me at the time did not put in my address details completely correct....
metadata.full_snippet:
I signed up for a best buy CitiBank card around [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. The terms were not explained to me by the employee that had signed me up or an information packet and the employee unbeknownst to me at the time did not put in my address details completely correct. 

I was told my card would arrive in 7-10 days per an email directly from Citibank. I waited longer than this to contact them due to slow postal service times however I never received my card in the mail. 

I received a voicemail from Citi that my card had been returned because of an address issue ; when I contacted customer service I was told I would not be able to update my address to receive the card unless I was able to verify my account, however, to verify the account I would need the full account number, which I did not have since I did not have the physical card. I was told to wait a period of time ( a few hours ) and I would be called back, but never was. 

Next time I called I am unsure about ( a few times in [Redacted] ) but I was similarly told the same except I would receive a letter instead, but I would not get the letter since my address on the account was still not updated. After talking to another customer service agent, I was told my account would be placed on review/hold for [Redacted] days and to wait for notification from Citibank to be able to verify my account. I had never received text, email or voicemail regarding this after [Redacted] days. Last call [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I was told I would be contacted and would need to call back once that happened most likely within [Redacted] hours. This has still not happened. 

Similarly throughout this process, I am told I am unable to close the account according to customer service reps because I can not verify it. This means I can not even pay the account fee on the card itself, let alone use it. I also can not use the online portal due to not having the physical card ; I can not make an account without the full card number. I have been asked for exceedingly personal information about my account ( e.g my SSN ) so there is no reason I should need to further verify anything to simply change address or close the account outright that to this day has not been used and is unusable.

metadata.title: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports Dispute
metadata.snippet: I am writing to request the deletion of specific entries in my file, which are listed in the attached report. As a victim of identity theft, I did not authorize these changes. In compliance with the Federal Trade Commission, I have reported this identity theft and have included c...
metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing to request the deletion of specific entries in my file, which are listed in the attached report. As a victim of identity theft, I did not authorize these changes. In compliance with the Federal Trade Commission, I have reported this identity theft and have included copies of the FTC 's Identity Theft Affidavit. 

It appears that certain activities about my account contravene multiple sections of the U.S. Code Law, including : 15 U.S. Code 1681 a ( 4 ) - Consumer Right to Privacy. You are reporting fraudulent accounts that aren't mine, infringing upon my privacy rights.

15 U.S. Code 1681a - Definitions ; rules of construction. This law states that transactions are not included in a consumer report. Thus, I demand the removal of all late payments from my report.

FDCPA 807 - Misleading false reporting. The information you are reporting suggests I applied for these inquiries & accounts, which is inaccurate and misleading.

15 USC 1681 n - Civil liability for willful noncompliance. You accepted credit information about me without verifying its accuracy, leading to willful noncompliance.

18 U.S. Code 1028A - Aggravated identity theft. You shared my information with creditors without my consent, which constitutes aggravated identity theft.

15 U.S. Code 6802 ( b ) 1 ( ) ( a ) ( A ) ( B ) ( C ) - Obligations with respect to disclosures of personal information. You didn't disclose to me that I had the right to opt-out of this information being shared.

And several other violations, which I have detailed in the attached document.

I kindly request that you adhere to 15 U.S. Code 1681c-2, which requires you to complete this reinvestigation and block or update all information resulting from identity theft within four days of receipt of this letter. Failure to comply will lead to criminal and civil liabilities as outlined in my attached invoice. 

I am the original creditor, and I did not authorize, benefit from, or consent to the accounts and inquiries listed in the attached report. I filed FTC report [Redacted] [Redacted] regarding this matter. 

Please remove all fraudulent accounts from my credit report immediately. According to FCRA 605B, this information must be blocked until the investigation is concluded.

Furthermore, as per 15 U.S.C. 1681g, I demand that you disclose all documents recorded and retained in your file at the time of the request concerning the accounts that you are reporting on my credit report.

metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing this complaint to bring to your attention the violations committed by United Auto Credit and [Redacted] [Redacted] in regards to my retail installment contract. The issue at hand is related to the determination of finance charge, which was not included in my contract as required by 15 U.S. Code 1605. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I signed a retail installment contract with [Redacted] [Redacted] for the purchase of a vehicle. The contract stated that the amount financed was {$6000.00}, but the finance charge was not included in the contract. According to 15 U.S. Code 1605, the finance charge should have been disclosed to me before entering into the contract. However, neither United Auto Credit nor [Redacted] [Redacted] informed me of this crucial information. 

Furthermore, I was charged an illegal down payment of {$4000.00}, which is also in violation of 15 U.S. Code 1662 - Advertising of down payments and installments. As the creditor, I was never informed of my rights or the terms of the contract, which were both illegally charged to me without my knowledge or consent.

I urge you to take appropriate action against United Auto Credit and [Redacted] [Redacted] for their blatant disregard of consumer protection laws. These actions are unacceptable and can lead to serious financial consequences for innocent consumers like myself. I request a thorough investigation into these matters and demand that the necessary steps be taken to rectify this situation immediately.

What you will find is that according to 15 U.S Code 1681 ( a ) ( 4 ) ( b ) and 15 U.S. Code 1681s2 ( a ) ( b ) ( d ) [Redacted]  [Redacted] has not used reasonable procedures to protect ME, the consumer. This practice is in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act of 1970 aka FCRA. If you also take a look at the listed attachments you will see [Redacted] [Redacted] is currently being sued for my exact claim from other consumers due to predatorial lending practices, charging high fees, Deceptive marketing, AND abusive collection practices. This is probably the reason why [Redacted] [Redacted] all of a sudden chose to retire from her position as Chief Operations Officer and Executive Vice President on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ( refer to form [Redacted] filed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ). 
Now, let me draw your attention to something even more infuriating. [Redacted] [Redacted] not only is conducting predatorial lending practices, amongst many other things, but they have THE NERVE to be selling our securities on the secondary market. How did I receive a benefit of generating credit using my social security number ( card ) to lend myself money then you tell me I owe you + interest, then turn around and sell /trade my application ( aka my security )? Please refer below, as well, form 10k, pg.85, section labeled investments in the attachments ).

Investments Investment securities Debt securities that management has the positive intent and ability to hold to maturity are classified as held-to-maturity and recorded at amortized cost. Securities not classified as held-to-maturity are classified as available for sale and recorded at fair value, with unrealized gains and losses excluded from earnings and reported in other comprehensive income. The Company did not hold any available for sale securities at [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] or [Redacted]. 

When the estimated fair value of a security is lower than the book value, a security is considered temporarily impaired. On a quarterly basis, the Company evaluates any securities in a loss position to determine whether the impairment is other-than-temporary. If there is intent to sell the security, or if the Company will be required to sell the security, or if the Company believes it will not recover the entire cost basis of the security, the security is other-than-temporarily impaired ( OTTI ) and impairment is recognized. The amount of impairment resulting from credit loss is recognized in earnings and impairment related to all other factors, such as general market conditions, is recognized in AOCI in the case of securities classified as available for sale.

Management considers a number of factors in its analysis of whether a decline in a securitys estimated fair value is OTTI. Certain factors considered include, but are not limited to : ( a ) the length of time and the extent to which the security has been in an unrealized loss position, ( b ) changes in the financial condition of the issuer, ( c ) the payment structure of debt securities, ( d ) adverse changes in ratings issued by rating agencies, ( e ) and the intent and ability of the Company to hold the security for a period of time sufficient to allow for any anticipated recovery in fair value. 

Purchased premiums and discounts on debt securities are amortized or accreted over the terms of the securities using the effective-yield method. Gains and losses on the sale of securities are recorded on the trade date and are determined using the specific identification method.

I am writing to request the deletion of specific entries in my file, which are listed in the attached report. As a victim of identity theft, I did not authorize these changes. In compliance with the Federal Trade Commission, I have reported this identity theft and have included copies of the FTC 's Identity Theft Affidavit. 

It appears that certain activities about my account contravene multiple sections of the U.S. Code Law, including : 15 U.S. Code 1681 a ( 4 ) - Consumer Right to Privacy. You are reporting fraudulent accounts that aren't mine, infringing upon my privacy rights.

15 U.S. Code 1681a - Definitions ; rules of construction. This law states that transactions are not included in a consumer report. Thus, I demand the removal of all late payments from my report.

FDCPA 807 - Misleading false reporting. The information you are reporting suggests I applied for these inquiries & accounts, which is inaccurate and misleading.

15 USC 1681 n - Civil liability for willful noncompliance. You accepted credit information about me without verifying its accuracy, leading to willful noncompliance.

18 U.S. Code 1028A - Aggravated identity theft. You shared my information with creditors without my consent, which constitutes aggravated identity theft.

15 U.S. Code 6802 ( b ) 1 ( ) ( a ) ( A ) ( B ) ( C ) - Obligations with respect to disclosures of personal information. You didn't disclose to me that I had the right to opt-out of this information being shared.

And several other violations, which I have detailed in the attached document.

I kindly request that you adhere to 15 U.S. Code 1681c-2, which requires you to complete this reinvestigation and block or update all information resulting from identity theft within four days of receipt of this letter. Failure to comply will lead to criminal and civil liabilities as outlined in my attached invoice.

I am the original creditor, and I did not authorize, benefit from, or consent to the accounts and inquiries listed in the attached report. I filed FTC report # [Redacted] regarding this matter. 

Please remove all fraudulent accounts from my credit report immediately. According to FCRA 605B, this information must be blocked until the investigation is concluded.

Furthermore, as per 15 U.S.C. 1681g, I demand that you disclose all documents recorded and retained in your file at the time of the request concerning the accounts that you are reporting on my credit report.

metadata.snippet: In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], my husband [Redacted] [Redacted] and I ( [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] received a letter from Loan Depot informing us that we had a shortage in our escrow account connected to loan number [Redacted], for a total of {$10000.00}.
