metadata.full_snippet: I had a one year CD account with Citi Bank, that matured on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] After it matured, Citibank said that I have a seven day grace period to make any changes to the account. This is now two pieces of crucial, misinformation that I was given by that representative it is not fair for me to pay a penalty when I was assured I would not be and also misinformed that my external transfer would be an option to close my account.

metadata.full_snippet: I opened a checking and savings account with Chase Bank in [Redacted] of 2023. They were advertising a promotion to receive an account-opening bonus if you met their qualifications within 90 days of account opening. The total bonus promised was {$900.00}, after meeting direct deposit and balance requirements ( maintain $ [Redacted] in savings through the 90 day period ). After the qualification period ended, I noticed that I had not received the first part of the advertised bonus. I went into the [Redacted], GA [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] and spoke with a representative who was able to research and find that Chase had an internal issue with the code that was applied when opening the accounts. They admitted that they'd experienced this issue/glitch with multiple customers and that the issue continued to impact others that opened accounts through their online channel. I was told that the code was applied ( in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 ) and that the bonus would be paid as initially promised. After more time went by, there was still no bonus paid. I went into the branch and spoke with a representative about my concerns, who had their manager call me later ( with no progress made ). I also spoke with several people through their [Redacted] number who told me that I would have to wait 90 days from when *Chase* manually applied the coupon code on their system. This is not what I agreed to when I opened the accounts and I am unable to move my funds until their 90 period ends. My money has been tied up there for months and they have failed to follow through on their promise. They should make this right, immediately, and pay interest that I could have been earning in a better account with a bank who does right by the customer!!!

metadata.full_snippet:
There is information that on my consumer report that is a result of identity theft. I did not provide written permission of instructions for the identified transactions to be reported on my consumer report. I am requesting that the reporting of this information be blocked and deleted. As a federally protected consumer I'm seeking proof of the alleged debt, under the doctrine of estoppel by silence, Engelhardt v Gravens ( Mo ) 281 SW 715, 719, I may presume that no proof of the alleged debt, nor therefore any such debt, in fact exists. In a good faith effort to resolve this matter amicably, I demand for proof of the debt, specifically the alleged contract or other instrument bearing my signature in wet ink, as well as proof of your authority in this matter. Absent such proof, you must terminate this collection action and correct any erroneous reports of this debt as mine. For the record, I state again that as I have no account with you, nor am I your customer, nor have I entered into a contract with you, I must ask for the following information : 1 ) Please evidence your authorization under 15 USC 1692 ( e ) 15 USC 1692 ( f ) and USC 1692 ( g ) in this alleged matter. 2 ) What is your authorization of law for your collection of information? 3 ) What is your authorization of law for your collection of this alleged debt? 4 ) Please evidence your authorization to do business or operate in the state. 5 ) Please provide proof of the alleged debt, including specifically the alleged contract or other instrument bearing my wet signature. You have 7 days of this notice to respond. Your failure to respond, on point, in writing, hand signed, and in a timely manner, will work as a waiver to any and all of your claims in this matter, and will entitle me to presume that you sent your letter ( [Redacted] ) in error, and that this matter is permanently closed. Your continued silence is unacceptable. Either provide the proof or correct the record to remove the invalid debt from my credit files with the three-primary credit-reporting agencies. You are currently in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act and the Fair Debt Collection Act. I can't obtain housing or employment due to the violations on my credit file. Failure to respond within 7 days of this letter will begin my small claims action against your company. I will be seeking { {$5000.00} } in damages for the following : 1 ) Defamation 2 ) Negligent Enablement of Identity Fraud 3 ) Violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act After obtaining the judgment against your company, I will obtain a Writ of Execution from the Sheriffs office in your county and I will begin the process of attaching property or funds to satisfy the judgment. For the purposes of 15 USC 1692 et seq., this Notice has the same effect as a dispute to the validity of the alleged debt and a dispute to the validity of your claims. I am requesting that the reporting of this information be blocked and deleted. My request to block is not being made in error ; nor is my request to block being made on the basis of a material misrepresentation of fact by me relevant to the request to block the identified transactions. You are in violation under 15 U.S.Code 1681i ( 5 ) removal of Inaccurate/Invalidated Credit Information and 15 U.S.Code 1681 ( e ) ( b ) Compliance procedures maximum possible accuracy & section 604 15 us code 1681 B.

The identified transactions are not information related to any transaction by me as the consumer ( see attached )

metadata.full_snippet:
I am writing to further escalate my unresolved dispute with TransUnion, as it has been two years since I first reported the issue and it remains unresolved, causing financial damage and hardship. I had high hopes of purchasing a home, but due to this ongoing matter, my plans have been delayed and my financial stability has been severely affected. 

I initially filed a complaint with the Department of Consumer Protection DFPI against TransUnion, but the issue has not been resolved and I feel my concerns have been neglected. Every time I have followed up on the dispute, either through phone calls or mail, I have been informed that my file could not be located and they have no record of my dispute history. This has left me frustrated and concerned about the lack of attention given to my case. 

I believe that my consumer rights have been violated and I request your assistance in resolving this matter promptly. Enclosed with this letter, you will find a copy of the previous letter I submitted to TransUnion for your reference. I kindly request that you review the details of my case and take appropriate action to ensure a fair and satisfactory resolution. 

I respectfully ask for the following actions to be taken : 1. Conduct a thorough investigation into my dispute with TransUnion and ensure that my file is located and reviewed in a timely manner. 
2. Hold TransUnion accountable for their negligence in addressing my concerns and ensuring that appropriate measures are taken to rectify any inaccuracies. 
3. Provide clear and transparent communication regarding the progress of my case, ensuring that I am informed of any updates or findings. 
4. Offer me necessary assistance, guidance, and resources to resolve this matter and help mitigate any financial damage caused by this prolonged dispute. 

I sincerely hope that my complaint will receive your immediate attention and that you will take the necessary steps to bring about a fair and swift resolution. I look forward to your prompt response and your assistance in achieving a satisfactory outcome. 

1. Violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) : The FCRA governs the use and reporting of consumer credit information. Inaccurate or misleading information can be grounds for violations of the FCRA. I urge you to review Section 1681s-2 ( a ) of the FCRA, which sets forth the obligations of credit reporting agencies to conduct investigations and remove inaccurate information upon notification by a consumer. 

2. Damages for Defamation and Negligence : The inclusion of false and damaging information on my credit reports can be considered defamation and negligence on the part of the credit reporting agencies. I want to emphasize that I am prepared to take legal action to seek compensation for any harm caused by this inaccurately reported collection account. 

3. Potential Regulatory Actions : Credit reporting agencies are subject to oversight by regulatory bodies such as the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) and the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ). The failure to comply with their guidelines and regulations may result in investigations, fines, and other enforcement actions.

metadata.full_snippet:
Previously on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023, I requested an investigation regarding inaccurate/erroneous items on my TransUnion credit [Redacted] that were being reported erroneously. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 the agency sent a letter stating that they had completed your investigation and these items were not deleted, as requested. 

I requested specific information as proof of ownership of debt, and did not receive that information, merely a copy of my credit report showing the items verified, no change or updated. There was NO PROOF of validation as requested for the items listed below. 

I contend that these accounts are inaccurate, as [Redacted] has provided no proof of their initial investigation as requested previously, and I requested on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] a thorough investigation into its validity and immediate removal from my credit report in accordance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and its relevant provisions. 

Under the FCRA, it is the credit agency 's responsibility, as a credit reporting agency, to ensure the accuracy of the information they report. 

I am writing to file a formal complaint against TransUnion, as they have failed to respond to my re-investigation dispute request for them to provide me with proof of validation and methods used to come to their conclusions within the mandated [Redacted] RE-Investigation time period, as per the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I submitted a re-investigation dispute request to TransUnion, challenging several incorrect and erroneous items on my TransUnion credit report that I did not receive documentation for the first time I disputed. 

As outlined in the FCRA, I understand that TransUnion is obligated to conduct a timely and thorough re-investigation into the disputed items and provide me with the results, including any supporting documentation that I specifically asked for, as noted on the attached letter. including original contracts with my signature. 

As of today 's date, more than 15 days have passed since my re-investigation dispute request, and I have not received any response from TransUnion. This lack of communication is not only a violation of the FCRA but also an impediment to my right to accurate and fair credit reporting. 

Furthermore, I explicitly requested documentation showing proof of TransUnion 's initial validation of the disputed accounts. This documentation is essential for me to assess the validity of the reported information and ensure that TransUnion complies with the FCRA 's requirement for a reasonable investigation. metadata.full_snippet:
Subject : Formal Complaint [Redacted] and BNY Dispute Resolution Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to file a formal complaint against [Redacted] and the Bank of New York ( BNY ) regarding a dispute related to a short-term apartment rental. My efforts to resolve this matter have been met with unresponsiveness, and I seek your intervention to ensure a fair resolution. 

In [Redacted] ], I rented an apartment through [Redacted], located at [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted], NY [Redacted] [Redacted] Subsequently, it came to light that neither the host nor [Redacted] had obtained a Certificate of Occupancy for safe habitation, leading to citations from the [Redacted] and DOB ( Dept of Buildings ) and a full vacancy order issued for the residence. 

Prior to filing a dispute with my bank, I attempted to address the issue directly with [Redacted]. Unfortunately, my attempts proved futile as I encountered a constant runaround. The emails I sent were consistently redirected to [Redacted] staff in [Redacted], and with each new representative, I had to reexplain the matter repeatedly. Moreover, I received a single message in their website portal, but due to a website glitch, the messages do not open, redirecting instead to a server error. 

In response to these circumstances, I filed a chargeback with my bank, based on the grounds that [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] law prohibits the collection of rent for illegal apartments. This action was taken due to [Redacted] 's lack of due diligence on safety and the host 's intention to deceive, both of which I believe violate the Visa Merchant Agreement. 

My concern arises from the lack of cooperation received from the Bank of New York ( BNY ). It is my understanding that BNY is [Redacted] 's merchant provider. [Redacted] [Redacted], a [Redacted] Dispute Analyst at BNY , offered no assistance, stating that her department would not process the dispute. However, as the dispute is rooted in violations of terms set forth by Visa, I am uncertain whether BNY has the jurisdiction to deny reporting this matter to Visa and ignore the complaint. 

I am seeking further clarification from all involved parties and relevant regulators. Additionally, I would appreciate your assistance in obtaining a statement from Visa to clarify whether utilizing their network to collect payments for services that are against the law is prohibited. 

I believe that both [Redacted] and BNY must be held accountable for the profits obtained through an illegal service. Moreover, I was informed that the [Redacted] Mayor 's office has a dedicated team to protect tenants in such matters and will prosecute those involved. 

I have attached relevant documents, including the email correspondence with [Redacted] [Redacted] from BNY. Your prompt attention to this matter is crucial, and I appreciate your time, understanding, and support in resolving this issue. 

Thank you for your consideration. 

P.S. 
As quoted on [Redacted] own website : https : [Redacted] New short-term rental regulations Starting [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], the city began enforcing its rules which require all eligible short-term rental Hosts to be registered with the city, or have Class B status, to continue hosting short-term rental stays. 

Therefore, this reservation for this booking should have been canceled due to the enactment of new laws in [Redacted], preceding the [Redacted] rent period. The host neglected to secure proper registration with the city, presumably due to a lack of a Certificate of Occupancy ( COO ) permit, possibly linked to illegal construction. [Redacted] violated the law by permitting the listing and transaction despite being aware that the transaction contradicted the newly implemented laws.

metadata.full_snippet:
This complaint is in reference to inaccurate reporting on my credit report from MACYS/CBNA. Violation of FCRA 1681s- ( 2 ) ( 5 ). The last four of account is[Redacted]. 
This account was originally opened on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. However, on my current credit report there is no payment history from [Redacted] at all. I have repeatedly told Macy 's and all three credit reporting bureaus that this account and trade line is inaccurate. 

I have since requested statements and bills from Macy 's for all payments in [Redacted] and for the entire account history. Macy 's and Citibank are unable to furnish any information to me on this account because of the " age of this account ''. There are NO RECORDS that exist to date for this account. This account should not be on my credit report if the creditor can not verify/validate or provide copies of account information when asked. 

I was also informed by Macy 's that legally they can not collect any money on this account " due to the statue of limitations ''. Therefore, it is a violation of the law for this account to be reported on my credit report. Macy 's specifically told me that their credit/collections department is " in house only, therefore the account will not be reported on my credit report ''. 

1681s2. Responsibilities of furnishers of information to consumer reporting agencies ( a ) Duty of furnishers of information to provide " accurate information '' ( 1 ) Prohibition ( A ) Reporting information with actual knowledge of errors A person shall not furnish any information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if the person knows or consciously avoids knowing that the information is inaccurate. 

( B ) Reporting information after notice and confirmation of errors A person shall not furnish information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if- ( i ) the person has been notified by the consumer, at the address specified by the person for such notices, that specific information is inaccurate; and ( ii ) the information is, in fact, inaccurate. 

Macy 's intentionally " failed '' to report any credit activity from [Redacted], to illegally extend the negative reporting on my credit report. I have asked for statements to validate the last payment made on this account and Macy 's could not furnish this information. This is a violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act. Due to Macy 's unlawful actions, I have been denied for credit for the past 7 years. I most recently received a denial to refinance my auto loan in [Redacted]. 

I tried to rectify this account with Macy 's, CBNA, and all three credit reporting bureaus since [Redacted]. Unfortunately, my attempts have been unsuccessful. Since [Redacted], Macy 's has never sent any account information to me after several repeated requests. I have disputed this account several times and the credit bureaus have done " nothing '' to remedy this issue. 

1681s2 ( 5 ) Duty to provide notice of delinquency of accounts A person who furnishes information to a consumer reporting agency regarding a delinquent account being placed for collection, charged to profit or loss, or subjected to any similar action shall, not later than 90 days after furnishing the information, notify the agency of the month and year of the commencement of the delinquency that immediately preceded the action. Macy 's is in violation of statue 1681s-2 ( 5 ) as well. I did not receive any copies of information furnished to the credit bureaus. 

On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I contacted Citibank 's Profit Loss Department ( instructed by a Macy 's customer service representative ) at [Redacted] and to date Citibank does not have any record of my name, SSN, or DOB. Macy 's explained to me that Citibank is " their bank '', why is this account on my credit report when Citibank has no record of my account, payment history, or personal information? 

Further, I contacted the phone number listed on my credit report for this account and I was directed to another department. I spoke to a customer service representative named [Redacted] who advised me to call [Redacted]. 

I asked to speak to a supervisor several times. I was told that there was not a supervisor available and Macy 's does not have a legal department. I was not being told the truth. 
I have been dealing with inflexible people from Macy 's and Citibank who will not and can not assist me in this matter. The information Macy 's is reporting to the credit bureau with account number ending in [Redacted] is not accurate this trade line is a violation of the law for the past 7 years. 
This has caused emotional and financial damage to my credit history, credit score, and creditworthiness. I have been receiving some of the worst credit card offers and astronomically high interest rates on credit cards and loans. Macy 's has offered NO recourse of action to rectify this problem within the past 7 years. 

Error # 2, on my credit report this account is written as a " charge off '', further activity on this account should have ceased when the account status changed to charge off, but it did not. 

Error # 3, this account shows {$150.00} past due as of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Statement in error # 2 and error # 3 contradict each other. Why is this account showing " past due '' activity as if it is an active open account when it is a " charge off account ''?

Error # 4, this account also states that it is " closed '' why is charge off activity still being reported as recently as [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], when it was charged of in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]? 
[Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] is when the collection activity was legally supposed to cease. 

Error # 5, shows a credit limit of {$500.00}, then reports that I am over the limit by {$8.00}. Yet, in the credit history there is no factual data SHOWING ON MY CREDIT REPORT when I was actually over my credit limit. Where is the data?

Error # 6, if the credit limit was {$500.00} and the amount remaining is {$150.00}, why did you illegally withhold payment history data from this account? Where is the record of payments being made if money was received on this account? 

This is egregious and tortious act committed by Macy 's, Citibank, [Redacted], [Redacted], and [Redacted]. I currently have a Macy 's account that is in good standing, in addition to this negative account that is being reported. 

To add insult to injury, Macy 's decreased my credit line by {$600.00} when my account was in good standing ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) for no reason. Macy 's and Citibank are intentionally violating the FCRA without any regard for it's consumers or their accounts. Therefore, I ask that the CFPB please investigate this matter as soon as possible to bring a fair resolution to this egregious credit situation.

metadata.full_snippet:
This is a formal complaint against Toyota Motor Credit Corporation ( TMCC ), pursuant to Consumer Financial Protection Bureau judgement against TMCC ( Case No. [Redacted] ) and in relation to the difficulties I experienced during the COVID-19 pandemic which have had a significant impact on my financial situation and credit standing. 

During this challenging period, I held a lease agreement with TMCC. As an employee of a non-profit in the education sector facing financial hardship, I sought to explore options for mitigating my financial burden, including the possibility of amending my lease terms by removing services or paying off the lease prematurely. Regrettably, my attempts to communicate with TMCC were met with insurmountable challenges. The customer service infrastructure, notably the phone tree system, proved to be ineffective and unresponsive, often leading to disconnections or cyclical routing without resolution. Despite repeated attempts over an extended period, my efforts to engage with TMCC to address this matter were unsuccessful. 

Ultimately, resigned to the situation, I prepared for the inevitable repossession of the vehicle. The repossession process was conducted without any prior communication or attempt by TMCC to resolve the issue. This incident, which was avoidable, remains the sole blemish on my otherwise unblemished credit record, and is indicative of an anomaly in TMCC 's business practices at the time. 

Furthermore, I have taken steps to rectify the impact of this incident on my credit reports. This includes submitting requests for the removal of this record to [Redacted] and [Redacted], specifically citing the CFPB 's [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2023 judgement against TMCC for related lending misconduct. Despite these bureaus acknowledgment of my requests, no changes have been made to my credit history or scores, and I have not received any substantive explanation for this inaction. 

This unresolved matter has adversely affected my ability to secure a car loan, despite maintaining a credit score in the mid-700s. It is my contention that the conduct of TMCC, in this case, is not only inconsistent with the expected standards of customer service but also reflective of the practices for which they were recently sanctioned by the CFPB, and should, therefore, be removed.

[Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  NAVY FEDERAL INVESTMENT SERVICES, LLC [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]  Subject : Opt-Out Request Regarding Consumer Reporting Dear, Navy Federal Credit Union I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to request an opt-out from the sharing of my personal information by Navy Federal Credit Union with consumer reporting agencies, in accordance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and related statutes. 

Under the provisions of the FCRA, specifically highlighted in sections 15 USC 1681 and 15 USC 6801, there exists a fundamental requirement for financial institutions to uphold the privacy and security of customers nonpublic personal information. My concern stems from the obligation stipulated in 15 USC 1681 section 604 ( a ) ( 2 ), which states that consumer reporting agencies may only furnish a consumer report with the explicit written instructions of the consumer. To date, I have not provided such written consent for the disclosure of my personal information. 

Moreover, the FCRA mandates that financial institutions like Navy Federal Credit Union must inform consumers about their rights to exercise nondisclosure options regarding their nonpublic personal information, as indicated in 15 USC 6802 ( b ) ( c ). I have not been adequately informed about or provided with the means to exercise this right. 

Additionally, the FCRA prohibits the inclusion of certain adverse items in a consumer report after a specific timeframe, as outlined in 15 USC 1681C ( a ) ( 5 ). Yet, I have observed adverse information being reported without my consent, which contravenes the statutory provisions. 

Furthermore, it is my understanding that every consumer reporting agency is required by 15 U.S. Code 1681e to maintain reasonable procedures to prevent violations of the FCRA and to limit the furnishing of consumer reports to specific purposes listed in section 1681b of the Act. I am concerned that Navy Federal Credit Union may not be adhering to these statutory requirements. 

Finally, under 12 CFR 1016.7, consumers hold the right to opt out at any time from the reporting services provided by financial institutions. Therefore, I am formally exercising my right to opt out of Navy Federal Credit Union 's Consumer reporting services. 

I kindly request that Navy Federal Credit Union cease sharing my personal information with consumer reporting agencies and confirm in writing that this opt-out request has been actioned accordingly. 

Please provide written acknowledgment of receipt of this opt-out request at your earliest convenience. If any additional information is required to process this request, please do not hesitate to contact me at the provided contact information. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. 

Sincerely, [ [Redacted] [Redacted] ]

I, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], am a natural living person. I am writing to dispute certain information present on my credit report, which I believe is inaccurate. This dispute is based on the provisions outlined in the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including 15 U.S. Code 1681a, 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2, and 15 USC 1681a 2 ( A ) ( i ).

According to 15 U.S. Code 1681a, the definition of a consumer report excludes reports containing information solely as to transactions or experiences between the consumer and the reporting entity. It is evident that the information in dispute falls under this exclusion.

Furthermore, 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2 emphasizes the responsibility of furnishers of information to consumer reporting agencies. The law stipulates that furnishers must provide accurate information and prohibits reporting with actual knowledge of errors.

In addition, 15 USC 1681a 2 ( A ) ( i ) supports my claim by specifying exclusions from the definition of a consumer report, highlighting the relevance of the disputed information to this exclusion.

I am also placing a FTC reference number- # [Redacted] so that you can verify the inaccuracy of fraud that is placed on my credit report. 

Now based on the provisions mentioned above, I kindly request an investigation into these discrepancies and urge prompt action to rectify the inaccuracies. As per my rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, I also request that you provide me with a written explanation of the results of your investigation. 

Enclosed are copies of documents supporting my claim for your review. 

I appreciate your prompt attention to this matter and request that the inaccurate information be corrected or removed from my credit report at the earliest.

The company is [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], website [Redacted]. I purchased these on my American Express card, account ending in [Redacted]. The charge was {$250.00}. Transaction reference number [Redacted]. The purchase was 2 seats for a performance of [Redacted], the musical. 

Once purchased I wanted to access the tickets to give as a gift - have something to print out. I was given no way to do this and tried to contact the company to ask. There was no way to get anyone on the phone, chat, email, etc. - zero customer service with this company. I even googled how to contact someone there. I feel this on purpose, they don't want anyone to be able to reach them. 

I opened a dispute with American Express immediately, on that very same day. I did so on the AMEX app and then feeling I wasn't able to fully describe the situation I called Amex customer service. The dispute as opened under 2 dispute numbers : [Redacted] and [Redacted]. 

I purchased other tickets for the event and felt confident AMEX would resolve the matter, given the lack methods to communicate with this sham merchant. 

Today, I found out Amex closed both disputes saying they were unable to investigate the charge, for me to contact the merchant directly. There is no one you can simply just contact at this " merchant. '' That was the issue from the get-go. 

I never received the dispute resolution letter from AMEX. It is not in my account when I look in the message folder, where it is suppose to be, if sent. 

I will pay disputed amount and not withhold funds to AMEX for this. Frankly, it's not about the amount of money, it's the principle of this merchant being disreputable and having no way to contact them, and in my view an unscrupulous merchant. I want to do what I can to stop this company from duping other. 

I've been a AMEX account holder since [Redacted]  and always paid on time and carry no balance. It is my go-to credit card as their customer service is typically top-notch and they are known to back you up if and purchases need to be disputed. The only other dispute I had, in [Redacted], was easily resolved. I felt confident this one would be easily resolved as well, and was shocked when it wasn't.

metadata.full_snippet:
I'm filing this complaint because of an unsatisfactory or fair resolution with Capital One Venture X credit card. 
Details : I booked airfare on [Redacted] through Capital One Travel on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] for a trip on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] leaving at [Redacted] [Redacted]  and arriving at [Redacted] [Redacted]  ( [Redacted] hour layover ). I paid for this airfare with my yearly {[Redacted]} travel credit which I'm given as a benefit with the rest being covered with credit card points. I was notified by [Redacted] on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] that they canceled my original flight and rebooked me on an alternative flight leaving at [Redacted] [Redacted]  and arriving at [Redacted] [Redacted]  ( [Redacted] hour layover ). Unfortunately, [Redacted] 's alternative travel times did not meet my needs so I needed to change them. I contacted [Redacted] for additional flight time alternatives, but they couldn't provide me with any acceptable options therefore I had to find another airline that could meet my needs. Once I found a replacement flight using the Capital One Travel portal, I canceled my [Redacted] flight. When this was being completed, I noticed a credit for the {[Redacted] travel credit and the points I used back in my account. I then rebooked a new flight with [Redacted] [Redacted] on the same date and destination as the original travel using the Capital One Travel portal. As I was completing the purchase for this trip, I noticed that the [Redacted] travel credit was not available for me to use and when I looked at the account, I could see that it was put back in my account when I canceled the [Redacted] trip, but then it was listed as expired as of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. I contacted Capital One Venture X and they said that the {$300.00} travel credit expired and they couldn't backdate it so I could use it again for this replacement travel. They offered to escalate the issue for resolution and would get back to me within 7-14 days. I told them that if they couldn't backdate the {$300.00} travel credit, then I would also accept an alternative of issuing me the {$300.00} in credit card points which would be [Redacted] points. I rebooked the replacement airfare with Capital One Travel on [Redacted] [Redacted] and paid for the purchase with all credit card points since the {$300.00} travel credit wasn't available to use. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I called Capital One Venture X customer service, they called me on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and asked me to call them back, to discuss the resolution of my escalation. The result of my escalation to Capital One was that they were telling me that they couldn't give me the ability to use the {[Redacted]} travel credit because it had expired and that they couldn't issue me the same amount in credit card points as a replacement either. They didn't offer any other alternatives or support and just told me that they were sorry but my {[Redacted]} travel credit expired and they couldn't offer me anything to resolve the situation. I explained the situation again and asked to escalate this and I was put in contact with a supervisor. I again explained the situation and she told me the same answer. I asked her to escalate the complaint and she put me on hold to talk to another person but then came back with the same response that they couldn't do anything for me and there wasn't a way to escalate any futher. This is why I'm creating this complaint with the CFPB. 
I understand this wasn't Capital One 's fault, nor was it my fault, but rather it is [Redacted] 's fault which is why I canceled my trip with [Redacted]. I was really expecting that Capital One would have allowed for a 24-48 hour window to reallocate the usage of the [Redacted] travel credit before it would have expired for situations like this where it's a cancellation and rebooking, or issue credit card points as a replacement. I am very disappointed with how Capital One handled my situation especially how they didn't offer any type of a resolution at all that could have been seen as good will or good customer service. 
I feel that I'm the one that has been taken advantage of to the tune of [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: According to the Fair Credit Reporting ACT15 USC 1681 section 602 states, " There is a need to ensure that consumer reporting agencies exercise their grave responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and a respect for the consumers right to privacy ''. Equifax and [Redacted] are consumer reporting agencies and I am the consumer. I have the right to make sure my private information isn't shared which is backed by 15 USC 6801 which states " It is the policy of the congress that each financial institution has an affirmative and continuing obligation to respect the privacy of its customers and to protect the security and confidentiality of those customers nonpublic personal information. A financial institution by definition under that title. 15 USC 1681 section 604 in section 2 states that " In general subject to subsection ( c ), any consumer reporting agency may furnish a consumer report under the following circumstances and no other. By the written instructions of the consumer to whom it relates. Today ( [Redacted] of [Redacted] ) I was able to pay all fees and bring my accounts to full in order to return my truck. Once given the opportunity I was told I was not able to pick up my truck until the following [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ) because the company is in [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] over an hour away and they do not work in [Redacted] [Redacted] This is clearly Vystar breaking the law and is working against the [Redacted] statute [Redacted] to not only not allow me to retrieve my personal items from my truck, they are impeding the return of my vehicle after bringing the accounts to date. I'd like to pursue a civil lawsuit for wrongful repossession, damages, and attorney fees. REGULATION OF TRADE, COMMERCE, INVESTMENTS, AND SOLICITATIONS Chapter 537 TITLE LOANS View Entire Chapter 537.012Repossession, disposal of pledged property ; excess proceeds. ( [Redacted] ) If a borrower fails to repay all amounts legally due under the title loan agreement on or before the end of the title loans maturity date or any extension of such date and fails to make a payment on the loan within 30 days after the end of the loans maturity date or any extension of such date, whichever is later, the title loan lender may take possession of the titled personal property. A lender may take possession of the titled personal property only through an agent who is licensed by the state to repossess motor vehicles. ( [Redacted] ) Prior to engaging a repossession agent, the lender shall afford the debtor an opportunity to make the titled personal property available to the lender at a place, date, and time reasonably convenient to the lender and the borrower. Prior to taking possession of titled personal property, the lender shall afford the borrower a reasonable opportunity to remove from the titled personal property any personal belongings without charge or additional cost to the borrower. After the lender takes possession of the titled personal property, the lender, at the lenders sole expense and risk, may authorize a third party to retain physical possession of the titled personal property.

According to Cavalrys prior written response, the underlying Capital One account was charged off on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and allegedly acquired by a Cavalry affiliate on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Cavalry further stated that a judgment was entered on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] in the amount of {$10000.00} plus costs and post-judgment interest. However, the consumer reporting agencies are currently reporting a balance of {$11000.00}. Cavalry has not provided : A certified copy of the judgment An itemized calculation showing how {$10000.00} became {$11000.00} A complete chain of title from the original creditor A bill of sale identifying this specific account The original signed agreement Documentation confirming the Date of First Delinquency Proof of lawful authority to report the account post-judgment If a judgment exists, the reporting must accurately reflect the legal status and balance of that judgment. Absent proper documentation, continued reporting appears inaccurate and misleading under the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

metadata.full_snippet: Summary of the issue : CreditFresh mishandled my payments, attempted to collect money that was not owed, provided false and contradictory explanations, and escalated to threats and harassment after I blocked an unjustified ACH withdrawal. Their conduct appears to violate fair billing, fair lending, and [Redacted] standards. -- - Chronological Narrative [Redacted]. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> {$4600.00} payment made I made a {$4600.00} payment on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. When I asked why the minimum due still showed {$270.00}, CreditFresh repeatedly claimed the payment was outside the billing cycle and therefore did not affect the cycle fee or minimum due. 2. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> {$50.00} payment made I made a {$50.00} payment on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. CreditFresh claimed this payment was inside the cycle, even though it was made 13 days after the {$4600.00} payment. Their own posted cycle dates show both payments were inside the same billing cycle. 3. Their system proves no fees were due CreditFresh attempted to debit {$220.00} from my bank account based on the false claim that the {$4600.00} payment did not count. I have screenshots showing : - When their system believed the {$220.00} ACH succeeded, my balance dropped from {$560.00} to {$340.00}. - The entire {$220.00} was applied to principal only. - No cycle fee, interest, or other charges were applied. This proves no fees or interest were due and the account was current. When the ACH failed, the balance immediately jumped back to {$560.00}. This reversal happened only because the ACH failed, not because any fee was owed. 4. Selective and improper handling of payments CreditFresh mishandled the {$4600.00} payment by applying it entirely to principal, not recalculating the minimum due, and not sending a confirmation. The {$50.00} payment was handled correctly. This shows selective and inconsistent application of payments. 5. I initiated an ACH block due to unjustified collection attempts CreditFresh continued insisting that {$270.00} ( later {$220.00} ) was still owed despite the payments fully satisfying the cycle obligations. Because their claim was unjustified and contradicted by their own system data, I initiated an ACH block through my bank to prevent an improper withdrawal. 6. Retaliatory threats began only after the failed debit Before the failed ACH attempt, there were no threats or arrears language. Immediately after the failed debit, CreditFresh began sending : - Missed payment messages- Arrears language - Periodic creditreporting threats - Daily paymentdue messages These communications were retaliatory and occurred despite the account being current. 7. Repeated false information despite correction I repeatedly explained the issue and provided screenshots showing the correct balance. CreditFresh continued responding with the same inaccurate statements, insisting the {$4600.00} payment was outside the cycle and that {$220.00} was still owed. Their explanations contradicted their own system data. 8. The account was current, but they continued demanding payment Their own system showed : - Both payments were inside the same billing cycle - No fees or interest were due - The only remaining balance was principal Despite this, they continued demanding payment for a balance that had already been satisfied. 9. I will not remove the ACH block and will pay manually Due to their attempt to collect a satisfied balance and their retaliatory conduct, I will not remove the ACH block. I will make payments manually to prevent further improper withdrawal attempts. 10. I am requesting a switch to monthly billing CreditFreshs biweekly billing cycle has been used to misapply payments, generate false fees, and pressure me into paying amounts not owed. I am requesting that my account be switched to monthly billing going forward.

The date of first delinquency and proof of the statute of limitations applicable to this account. If you are unable to provide the above documentation, you must immediately : Cease all collection activity ; and Delete this account from all consumer reporting agencies to which you have furnished information. If you continue to report this account without providing proper validation, I will file additional complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ), and the Tennessee Attorney Generals Office for investigation of unlawful collection practices. metadata.full_snippet: I took out a private student loan through Climb Credit for a [Redacted] [Redacted]. The program was marketed with a job guarantee and career outcomes that were misleading. Degree requirements to qualify for refunds and realistic job placement were not clearly disclosed before enrollment. I BELIEVED I withdrew after several months when I realized the representations did not match reality, but I am still being held liable for the full loan. I am requesting investigation, correction, and relief. Since then I tried resolving this issue here and I respectfully disagree with the companys response and believe it does not fully address the substance of my complaint. First, their response relies almost entirely on the existence of a signed loan and enrollment documents, while failing to address my central concern : that the [Redacted] program was marketed with misleading job guarantee and career outcome representations that were not clearly or adequately disclosed before enrollment. The existence of Truth in Lending disclosures does not negate potential deceptive or misleading marketing tactics tied to the underlying educational product being financed. Second, the claim that I did not attempt to withdraw from the course is inaccurate. I attempted to cancel the course on three separate occasions using the cancel button given to us by [Redacted]. To cancel there is a prompt pop up that states that a student may cancel by submitting a written request ( I want to cancel course ). It does not say that booking a call is required in order for cancellation to be processed. It fact says the exact opposite, in that to avoid booking a call I may submit that written request. Only after 3 attempts and failing to cancel did [Redacted] inform me through email that I was required to schedule a call on THEIR time in order to cancel. This requirement was not clearly disclosed at the time I attempted to cancel and was not presented when I used the cancellation button. As a result, my attempts to withdraw were effectively blocked by undisclosed procedural barriers. Third, continued access to the platform should not be interpreted as consent to remain enrolled or acceptance of the programs terms after discovering that material representations did not align with reality. Access alone does not negate attempted withdrawal or concerns regarding deceptive marketing. Finally, while Climb states it is solely a loan originator, the loan is directly tied to the financing of an educational program that was marketed with allegedly misleading claims. Financing a product that is later found to involve deceptive tactics remains a relevant consumer protection issue. For these reasons, I believe the response is incomplete and does not adequately address the misleading marketing, undisclosed cancellation requirements, or the substance of my complaint. I respectfully request that this feedback be included in the record for further review. Thank you for your consideration.

metadata.full_snippet: To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding an improperly reported collection account furnished by Southwest Recovery Services, which is reporting a collection tradeline without providing legally sufficient proof that it has the authority to collect or furnish information for this account. This conduct violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ) and applicable federal standards governing third-party debt collectors. Account Information Collection Agency : Southwest Recovery Services Account Number : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] Original Creditor : [Redacted] [Redacted] Amount Allegedly Owed : {$480.00} Date Opened ( as reported ) : [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] Date Reported : [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] Account Status : Collection / Charge-Off Reporting Bureau [Redacted] [Redacted] Failure to Provide Proof of Legal Assignment Southwest Recovery Services is reporting this account as a collection obligation without producing any valid proof of assignment or ownership. Under federal law, a third-party debt collector must be able to demonstrate a lawful chain of assignment from the original creditor to itself before it may lawfully collect or report a debt. Legally sufficient proof requires, at minimum : A bill of sale or assignment agreement Documentation that specifically identifies this account as part of the transfer Proof that Southwest Recovery Services has authority to collect and furnish data to consumer reporting agencies A copy of a billing statement, invoice, account summary, or payment ledger from the original creditor is NOT legally sufficient. Such documents do not establish ownership or assignment, and any party can create or reproduce them. Courts and regulators require actual assignment contracts, not generic account documents. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Violations By continuing to report this collection account without proof of assignment, Southwest Recovery Services is violating, but not limited to : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) Furnishing information that is inaccurate, incomplete, or materially misleading. 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation and verify legal authority after dispute. 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy. Without proof of lawful assignment, Southwest Recovery Services has no permissible purpose to report this tradeline. Demand for Relief I hereby demand that Southwest Recovery Services : Immediately delete this tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies, including [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] Absent production of valid assignment documentation, continued reporting constitutes willful noncompliance with federal law. This complaint is being submitted to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) for regulatory review and enforcement. Please provide a written response within the CFPB-mandated response timeframe.

metadata.full_snippet: Summary SST Card Services is reporting a [Redacted] late payment on my Experian credit report for an account ( # [Redacted] ) that I never applied for, never agreed to, and never received any card, statement, bill, or correspondence for. You can not be late on a payment you never agreed to make. SST does not have my mailing address and has never sent me a single statement or bill. Despite this, SST reported me 30 days past due, damaging my credit score and my ability to operate my small business. I previously disputed this account through [Redacted] [Redacted] investigation sided with SST, and my report now states Completed investigation of FCRA dispute consumer disagrees. I do disagree. SST must remove this late payment immediately. The Late Payment Is Fraudulent My [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] credit report shows the SST/Tally account with the following details : Account # [Redacted], opened [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] Original balance : {$9700.00} Current balance : {$8600.00} ( updated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) Monthly payment : {$280.00} Type : [Redacted] unsecured installment loan Late payments reported : 1 ( 30 days past due ) [Redacted] comment : Completed investigation of FCRA dispute consumer disagrees A late payment can only be valid if the consumer has a legitimate payment obligation. I have no payment obligation to SST Card Services because : 1. I never signed a credit application or agreement with SST Card Services 2. I was never issued a credit card by SST Card Services 3. I have never received a single piece of mail from SST no welcome letter, no card, no statement, no bill, no correspondence of any kind 4. I have never received any electronic communication from SST 5. I have never spoken with anyone at SST Card Services SST does not have my mailing address. If SST had a legitimate account in my name, they would have my address and would have been sending monthly statements for over four years. The complete absence of any communication from SST proves they do not have a legitimate account with me. A company that has never sent me a bill can not report me as late for not paying that bill. Prior Dispute Failed I previously disputed this account through [Redacted] [Redacted] investigation did not result in removal of the tradeline or the late payment. My [Redacted] report now carries the notation Completed investigation of FCRA dispute consumer disagrees. This means SST was contacted during the investigation and verified the account - but SST can not legitimately verify an account that was never opened with my knowledge or consent. SSTs verification was false, and [Redacted] investigation was not reasonable under FCRA 1681i. The Coercion SSTs reporting creates a coercive trap : either I make $ 286 monthly payments on a debt I never agreed to, or SST reports me as late and damages my credit. This is not a legitimate creditor-debtor relationship- it is extortion through the credit reporting system. The 30-day late payment currently on my report is the direct result of this coercion. I refused to pay a debt I do not owe, and SST punished me with a derogatory mark. Impact I am a [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] who launched [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] My [Redacted] score has dropped from [Redacted] in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] to [Redacted] in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] - a [Redacted] decline- despite never missing a single payment on any credit card account I actually agreed to. Late payment marks are one of the most damaging items on a credit report. This single fraudulent late payment from SST is actively harming my ability to obtain business financing, maintain vendor relationships, and sustain my practice. I am also the mother of a five-year-old son. I launched my practice to have a better work-life balance and be more present for him. Instead, I am spending my time fighting a company that is reporting me as late on a debt I never agreed to, for an account I never opened, from a company that has never once contacted me. Legal Basis FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) - Furnishers must provide accurate information to credit bureaus. Reporting a late payment on an account the consumer never agreed to is inherently inaccurate. FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) - Upon notice of a dispute, furnishers must conduct a reasonable investigation. SST falsely verified this account during [Redacted] prior investigation despite having no signed agreement and no mailing address for me. FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. 1692e - Using false or deceptive representations in connection with debt collection, including reporting a debt - and late payments on that debt - that the consumer does not owe. FCBA, 15 U.S.C. 1666 - SST has never provided a single billing statement, yet reports late payment history. You can not be late on a bill you were never sent. N.J. Consumer Fraud Act, N.J.S.A. 56:8-1 et seq. - Treble damages for unconscionable commercial practices, including coercive credit reporting to force payment on debts the consumer never agreed to.

metadata.full_snippet: Subject : CFPB Complaint Request for Investigation of Potential Unauthorized Charges and Documentation Deficiency I am submitting this complaint to request regulatory review of an auto finance account serviced by Bridgecrest Acceptance Corporation. I am seeking assistance because I have reason to believe additional products or charges may have been included in my loan without proper authorization or disclosure, and the company has failed to provide complete documentation verifying these charges. I formally requested a complete copy of the contract file, including all addenda, ancillary product agreements, authorization forms, and electronic signature records. In response, I was provided only partial documentation that does not contain any records demonstrating that I knowingly agreed to any additional products that may be included in the financed balance. Specifically, the documents provided do not include : Add-on product authorization forms Itemized product agreements Electronic signature authentication logs Audit trail records Complete contract file Without these materials, there is no documentation confirming that any ancillary or add-on products were properly disclosed, explained, or knowingly authorized. The documents provided do not establish whether such products were required or optional, nor do they contain records demonstrating that I affirmatively accepted them. To date, I have paid approximately {$28000.00} toward this account, which exceeds the original amount of the loan, yet a remaining balance is still being asserted. Additionally, I recently paid {$1300.00} out of pocket for vehicle repairs despite being informed that a service or warranty product may be associated with my account. This raises concerns regarding whether such products were properly disclosed, validly authorized, or actually in effect. My concern is not simply the balance amount but whether the account includes charges that were never knowingly accepted. Creditors are required to maintain accurate documentation supporting financed charges and to verify authorization when such charges are questioned. I respectfully request that the CFPB review this matter and require the company to provide : Complete contract file Proof of authorization for any add-on products Full payment application history Electronic signature audit records Documentation supporting the current balance Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I sold my home. My mortgage was serviced by Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, Shellpoint issued an official payoff quote in the amount of {$180000.00}, which was stated to be valid through [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. In reliance on this payoff statement, the title company handling the closing wired {$180000.00} to Shellpoint on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, which was the valid good through date of the payoff quote. After the payoff quote was issued, Shellpoint internally processed a property tax disbursement from the escrow account, which increased the payoff amount. This transaction occurred after the payoff quote was generated and was not communicated to the title company or to me prior to the payoff payment being sent. Because of this internal escrow transaction, Shellpoint rejected the payoff wire even though it exactly matched the payoff quote that was valid for that day. As a result, I was required to obtain a new payoff quote and resend payment at a later date, which caused additional per diem interest to accrue. This sequence of events resulted in {$490.00} in additional per diem interest being charged. Shellpoint refunded {$70.00}, leaving {$420.00} still outstanding. The payoff payment was sent on the valid payoff date and for the exact quoted amount. The discrepancy occurred because Shellpoint processed an escrow disbursement after issuing the payoff quote. This internal transaction was outside of my control and created a payoff mismatch that could not have been reasonably anticipated by the borrower or the title company. I am requesting reimbursement of the remaining {$420.00}, which represents excess interest incurred solely due to this servicing issue.

These fraudulent inquiries and accounts constitute unauthorized use of my personal information. I have taken immediate steps to address this, including : 1.Contacting the lenders and companies involved to report the fraudulent activity and request that the accounts be closed, canceled, or flagged as identity theft. 2.Placing a fraud alert and a credit freeze on my credit reports to prevent further unauthorized applications. 3.Filing a police report with my local law enforcement agency to officially document the identity theft. 4.Reporting the identity theft to the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ). The unauthorized use of my personal information is a direct violation of federal law, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). I demand immediate removal of all fraudulent accounts, inquiries, and applications from my credit reports unless proper, verifiable documentation proving my authorization is provided. Failure to comply will be considered a willful violation of federal law, and I am prepared to pursue all available legal remedies, including regulatory enforcement, civil damages, and reporting to law enforcement authorities. The accounts and inquiries appearing on my credit report are the result of criminal misuse of my identity and must be permanently removed to restore the integrity of my credit file. Under the FCRA, especially Section 605B, I have the right to request the blocking and removal of any information that resulted from identity theft. I am formally invoking this right and demand that all fraudulent accounts and inquiries be investigated and deleted immediately. The fraudulent activity has caused significant stress, inconvenience, and potential harm to my financial standing. However, after contacting [Redacted], I was informed that the payment for this account was not due until [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. Because the account was still within the normal billing period and had not yet reached its due date, the representation that the account was in collection appears to be inaccurate and premature. Reporting or attempting to collect a debt that is not yet delinquent may constitute the furnishing or use of inaccurate information regarding a consumer account. This conduct may violate the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), which requires that companies ensure the accuracy and integrity of information used in connection with consumer credit and debt reporting. Attempting to collect or potentially reporting a debt as delinquent before it is actually due creates inaccurate information about the status of the account. I respectfully request that this matter be investigated and that TSI correct their records to reflect that the account was not delinquent as of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. I also request confirmation that no inaccurate information has been or will be reported to any consumer reporting agencies regarding this account.

Specifically, I requested documentation showing the chain of transfers of the loan from the original lender to the current owner. This included any endorsements of the promissory note, allonges, assignments of the mortgage, purchase or transfer agreements, and other documentation demonstrating how the loan was transferred and who currently owns the loan. I also requested documentation identifying the current owner of the loan, documentation establishing Lakeview Loan Servicings authority to service and enforce the loan, and a complete accounting of the loan balance and payment application history. In response to these requests, the servicer stated in writing that it has no record of any note endorsements or allonges. The servicer also declined to provide purchase agreements or other transfer documentation, stating that such records are proprietary. Without these documents, the servicer has not demonstrated the chain of title or authority required to enforce the mortgage obligation. These requests were made in good faith in order to verify the ownership of the loan, confirm the authority of the servicer, and verify the accuracy of the account. To date, the requested documentation establishing ownership of the loan, the transfer history, and the servicing authority has not been provided.

metadata.full_snippet: My fiance and I applied for a personal loan in [Redacted] of [Redacted]. He has been a SoFi member for 5 years. We both work [Redacted] but have consistent and demonstrable income combined of around $ [Redacted] year. The loan amount of $ [Redacted] was below what was advertised to us as a pre-approval and we were quickly approved through the website. The loan sat in review for 2 weeks ( it was near the new year ). We finally heard from Sofi that they needed additional documentation from my fiance, which we supplied immediately. We even offered to upload our complete tax returns but we were assured that nothing further was needed. Then we heard nothing else until the loan was rejected 2 weeks later. When I called to enquire why it was determined that the loan application had expired due to Sofis own self imposed timeline and negligence. For 2 weeks after that I had to call Sofi every 48-72 hours only to be told that they are still attempting to revive the application at the highest level and I should hear back in 24 hours. Eventually on one of the calls I initiated I was informed the application could not be retrieved, no explanation given. I asked if it would be more beneficial for my partner to apply alone, as he is a Sofi member and has W2 income in excess of [Redacted] a year. I was told that was not necessary or advisable, which proved to be patently false. Meanwhile we both received an adverse action on our credit reports, lower scores, and a higher debt ratio because it had been 6 whole weeks. Had I known it would be this drawn out I wouldve immediately gone to another lender. I then spoke with a resolution specialist who acknowledge SoFis culpability and submitted the adverse action reversal. He also offered us an additional percent off our advertised rate for SoFis negligence. I agreed to reapply with SoFi and was assured there would be a dedicated person following this process to ensure the same issues didnt arise. I was called by a SoFi rep and asked to upload a piece of documentation from [Redacted]. I discussed with the rep since I had her on the phone that it may be more beneficial for me to do my [Redacted] taxes as this process had drawn out so long, or again for my fiance to apply alone. [Redacted] wasnt an incredible year for me freelance wise, but still contributed to an average personal income of $ [Redacted] across 2 years ( 3+ actually, for consistency ), as stated in both loans when they were pre approved ( in addition to my partners roughly $ [Redacted] yearly income ) The rep assured me that rushing to do my [Redacted] taxes wouldnt be necessary and that she would give me a call before any decision was made if it looked like it would be better to do them. That did not happen and the loan was automatically rejected within an hour of me uploading the requested documentation ( documentation that had been part of our loan application since [Redacted], as you can see in the email correspondence ). I have been matched with 3 resolution specialists who all seem to be helpful at the onset and then just ghost / punt it off to another rep. My co borrower and I are now in a significantly worse position to secure a loan owing to the 2x adverse actions and the sheer amount of time that has passed. We had a number of expenses in the last two months that we were intending to use the loan for, that have now had to go on a credit card, affecting our debt ratio. This is entirely SoFis mismanagement. Maybe their personal loan experience isnt meant for freelance film professionals or anyone with less standard income streams, but each representative assured us this was not the case. They are excellent at the upsell and truly horrendous at the execution. One of the credit pulls has been submitted to be suppressed, they have refused to suppress the other. It has now become clear after speaking to multiple representatives that it would've been better for my fiance to apply alone owing to my sole proprietorship and how they calculate net vs gross income for self employment. Had this information been made available to us at the start this journey, there would be no issue. As it stands, Sofi representatives are trained to say whatever necessary to secure the loan application, even if it is blatantly false. This is very evident in our recorded calls, which I of course do not have access to.

PRAs actions also violate FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) for reporting inaccurate information, FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 3 ) for failing to properly mark the account as disputed, and FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 5 ) for failing to provide required date information which raises concerns of illegal re-aging. metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting a new complaint regarding the continued improper servicing of a private student loan serviced by LendKey Technologies , Inc . This complaint follows a previous CFPB complaint in which LendKey acknowledged that incorrect information had been provided to me regarding my forbearance eligibility. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], at approximately [Redacted] a.m., I spoke with a LendKey representative by phone after receiving an email suggesting I may have exhausted my forbearance eligibility. During that call, I was informed that all of my loans were currently in forbearance for the upcoming [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] payment, that the servicer was not showing that I had exhausted my forbearance eligibility, and that if any limitation applied I may only need to make [Redacted] full payments before becoming eligible for forbearance again. I was also told that the prior conflicting email regarding my forbearance status may have been due to a manual system issue. Based on this information, I reasonably believed my loan remained protected under forbearance. Afterward, I was charged the full monthly payment for the loan. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I submitted a formal forbearance request. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], that request was denied with the explanation that the borrower had exhausted the allowed months of forbearance. I contacted the company again to request clarification. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I received a written response stating that the loan had permanently exhausted its lifetime [Redacted] forbearance allowance, that no additional forbearance was available, that in-school deferment was not permitted, and that refinancing was the only option. Because these statements directly contradicted the information I had previously received, I submitted a complaint to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. In response to that complaint, LendKey acknowledged that incorrect information had been provided to me and clarified that, under the loan agreement, the loan is eligible for up to [Redacted] months of forbearance granted in six-month increments. LendKey stated that my forbearance had been extended through [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and that [Redacted] months of forbearance would remain available after that date. Despite this response, the loan servicer still charged me the full monthly payment during months that should have been covered by forbearance. Because payments were collected during this time, the remaining available forbearance months should now reflect those payments and the available balance should be adjusted accordingly. After the prior CFPB complaint was closed, I requested additional forbearance based on the remaining months that LendKey itself stated were available. This request was again denied, with the company stating that the forbearance time had been exhausted. This is now the third instance in which the company has provided conflicting and inaccurate information regarding the forbearance eligibility for this loan. LendKey has stated in writing that the loan has remaining forbearance months available but has continued to deny requests and apply the loan terms inconsistently. As a full-time third-year medical student, the required monthly payment of approximately {$600.00} is not financially sustainable without the forbearance that the company itself confirmed is available under the loan agreement. I am requesting that the CFPB review the servicing of this account and require the servicer to apply the correct forbearance terms as outlined in the loan agreement and acknowledged in the companys prior CFPB response. I am also requesting correction of the loan account to reflect the proper forbearance period and clarification of the remaining months of eligibility. This issue reflects an ongoing pattern of inconsistent and inaccurate information provided by the servicer regarding the terms and protections associated with this loan.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing a complaint regarding a credit denial and the companys refusal to provide a reason for that denial. I have been a customer of American First Finance for several transactions, over several years, including multiple furniture lease-to-own agreements and personal financing accounts. I have never missed a payment and have consistently paid my accounts on time or early, often paying them off ahead of schedule. Recently, I applied for another financing agreement through American First Finance to purchase furniture. The application initially indicated that I was pre-approved, but the application was later denied. When I contacted customer service, I was told that my application had been denied and that I would not be able to apply again for 90 days. I specifically asked multiple representatives for the reason for the denial, but they were unable or unwilling to provide any explanation. I also spoke with a supervisor who was polite and professional. During that conversation, the supervisor indicated that the companys system may sometimes decline customers who pay off accounts early because those accounts generate less revenue for the company. As someone who has consistently paid early and maintained a perfect payment history, it was concerning to hear that responsible payment behavior may negatively affect approval decisions. My concern is not simply that the application was denied, but that no adverse action reason was provided despite multiple requests. My understanding is that lenders are required to provide the principal reason for a credit denial under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B. As a consumer who has maintained a perfect payment history with this company, I believe I am entitled to understand why my application was denied.

metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this complaint regarding my account with Sezzle and its handling of my request for review under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act ( SCRA ), 50 U.S.C. 39014043. I was an active-duty servicemember during the relevant period and experienced documented military pay disruptions during initial training that temporarily affected my ability to make scheduled installment payments on my Sezzle account. These disruptions were related to military administrative pay issues. Once my military pay was restored, I promptly brought all outstanding balances on my account current. I do not dispute the underlying obligations and no principal balance remains unpaid. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I contacted Sezzle through its support system and formally placed the company on notice of my SCRA rights. I explained that my military service had materially affected my ability to make payments during the period of pay disruption and requested written confirmation that my account had been reviewed for compliance with the SCRA. I also requested a complete accounting of any fees or penalties that were assessed during the period of covered military service and clarification as to whether any fees had been reviewed or adjusted pursuant to SCRA compliance procedures. Sezzle later responded by stating that payment installments for Buy Now, Pay Later companies like Sezzle do not fall under SCRA protections because the company does not charge interest. The response also stated that if an installment payment fails, the company may charge failed payment fees or late payment fees, and that once a fee has been charged it can not be reversed. The companys response did not provide the accounting I requested and did not confirm whether my account had been reviewed for SCRA compliance. It also did not indicate that any individualized analysis was conducted regarding whether my military service materially affected my ability to meet the payment obligation during the period of pay disruption. I am requesting that Sezzle provide written confirmation that my account has been reviewed for SCRA compliance, provide a complete accounting of all fees assessed during the period of covered military service, and review whether any fees assessed during the period in which my military pay disruption occurred should be corrected or adjusted under applicable federal law.

metadata.full_snippet: [Redacted] Account [Redacted] This letter serves as a formal demand for documentation and notice of potential statutory violations regarding the repossession and subsequent reporting of the above-referenced account. Under the provisions of the Uniform Commercial Code Article 9 ( 9-601 through 9-628 ) governing secured transactions and repossession procedures, creditors must strictly comply with statutory requirements when repossessing and disposing of collateral. Specifically, pursuant to UCC 9-611 and 9-614, a secured party must provide the debtor with proper written notice of the disposition of collateral prior to sale. Additionally, UCC 9-610 requires that any sale or disposition of collateral be conducted in a commercially reasonable manner. At this time, I have not been provided with sufficient documentation demonstrating compliance with these statutory obligations. Accordingly, you are hereby required to provide the following documentation within 30 days : 1. A copy of the original signed contract and security agreement. 2. Documentation of the alleged default and full payment history. 3. Proof of lawful repossession including date, location, and repossession agent. 4. A copy of the Notice of Right to Cure, if applicable. 5. Copies of any Notice of Intent to Sell and Notice of Sale of Collateral as required by UCC 9-611. 6. Detailed records showing the date, location, and method of the sale or auction. 7. Documentation establishing that the sale was conducted in a commercially reasonable manner as required by UCC 9-610. 8. A complete accounting of the sale proceeds and calculation of any alleged deficiency balance. Failure to provide the above documentation raises substantial concerns that the repossession and subsequent deficiency claim are unlawful. Courts have consistently held that when a creditor fails to comply with Article 9 repossession and notice requirements, the creditor may lose the legal right to pursue a deficiency balance. Furthermore, if your organization continues to furnish derogatory information regarding this account to credit reporting agencies without the ability to verify its accuracy and legal enforceability, such reporting may constitute violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ). If this account has been placed with a third-party debt collector, continued collection activity without proper validation may also violate the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ).
