metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint regarding Navy Federal Credit Unions continued claim of a lien on my vehicle without providing documentation demonstrating their lawful authority to maintain or enforce that security interest. The vehicle is a [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ( VIN : [Redacted] ). Navy Federal Credit Union remains listed as the lienholder on the vehicle title issued through the Minnesota Driver and Vehicle Services. However, the underlying credit account associated with this loan was charged off and reportedly transferred to a third-party debt buyer, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] . Navy Federal Credit Union is no longer furnishing this account to the consumer reporting agencies. Due to the transfer of the account and the unclear status of the security interest, I sent Navy Federal Credit Union a written request for documentation on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] via certified mail requesting verification of their authority to maintain the lien and enforce the security interest. In that written request, I asked Navy Federal Credit Union to provide documentation including : Proof they are the current holder of the promissory note Documentation showing they retained the security interest after any sale or transfer Copies of any assignment or transfer agreements Identification of the entity with legal authority to enforce repossession Confirmation of whether any repossession action has been authorized If they are no longer the secured party, issuance of a lien release These requests were made to determine the party with lawful authority to maintain a secured claim against my vehicle. To date, Navy Federal Credit Union has failed to provide adequate documentation demonstrating that it is the current secured party or that it retains the legal authority to enforce the lien. If the account was sold or assigned to another entity, the security interest must also follow the note and there must be documentation showing the chain of assignment of the promissory note and security agreement. Maintaining a lien without the ability to demonstrate lawful authority creates an improper encumbrance on my vehicle title and raises concerns about misrepresentation of the legal status of the debt and the party authorized to enforce it. This situation prevents me from having clear title to my vehicle and creates ongoing uncertainty regarding potential repossession rights.

metadata.full_snippet: Consumer Reporting Agencies play a crucial role in gathering and assessing consumer credit information. However, they must exercise their responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and respect for the consumers right to privacy. The banking system relies on accurate and fair credit reporting, and when these reporting methods are unfair, it undermines public trust, which is vital for the system 's stability. I never gave my explicit, written consent for these agencies to report my information, which is a violation of 15 U.S. Code 1681b ( 2 ). This violation has led to an alleged case of identity theft, breaching 15 U.S. Code 1681c-2. The accounts in question are not related to any transactions made by me. The Fair Debt Collection Practices Act was created to ensure that laws and procedures are in place to protect consumers from abusive, deceptive, and unfair practices by debt collectors. In this case, the company has violated 15 U.S. Code 1692f, which prohibits debt collectors from using unfair or unconscionable means to collect a debt. Specifically, they can not collect any amounts that arent explicitly authorized by the agreement or allowed by law. Additionally, the company has violated 15 U.S. Code 1692e, which prohibits the use of false, deceptive, or misleading representations in debt collection efforts. This includes using deceptive methods to collect a debt or gather consumer information. Moreover, they are forbidden from contacting consumers at inconvenient times or places, or engaging in behavior that harasses or abuses consumers. In this case, the company has harassed me by claiming I owe a debt that I do not recognize as my responsibility. They have also contacted me at inconvenient times and places, in violation of the law. metadata.full_snippet: Subject : Request for review and correction of TD Bank fraud classification affecting my [Redacted] access On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I received a [Redacted] payment in the amount of {$270.00} from a repeat client for services that I provided. The client had an established relationship with me, booked the appointment directly, appeared for the appointment, received the services, and made the payment knowingly and voluntarily. After the appointment, the client later complained about the result and requested a partial refund. In the message history, the client explicitly requested half a refund and later stated that if I did not respond, she would call the bank to refund the [Redacted] and that it would start an investigation. These statements show that the sender acknowledged making the payment and was seeking a refund after the services had already been rendered. Any same-day complaint would still constitute a dispute following services rendered, not an unauthorized transaction. The timeline also appears inconsistent. Based on information I received from TD Bank, the sender may have initiated the dispute on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], while in the later message history on [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], the sender stated that she would contact the bank and start an investigation if I did not provide a partial refund. I visited a TD Bank branch and submitted supporting information for review, including communications with the client and information showing that this was a legitimate repeat-customer payment. metadata.full_snippet: To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this message as a formal Notice of Error regarding the servicing of my mortgage escrow account and the failure to make a required hazard insurance payment. My homeowners insurance policy with [Redacted] was canceled due to non-payment, despite the fact that my mortgage is escrowed and the payment responsibility lies with SouthState Bank to disburse insurance premiums from the escrow account. As a result of this failure, I was forced to secure a new homeowners insurance policy at a significantly higher cost. For clarity, the relevant facts are as follows : My previous [Redacted] homeowners insurance policy had an annual premium of {$1200.00}. Due to the cancellation caused by non-payment, I was required to obtain a new homeowners policy with [Redacted] [Redacted] with an annual premium of {$3300.00}, requiring an immediate down payment in that same amount. The most recent request for payment from [Redacted] was issued on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], and it was sent to the email address [ EMAIL ADDRESS ] associated with SouthState for insurance billing notifications. I have attached written confirmation from [Redacted] verifying that the billing request was sent and that the policy was ultimately canceled due to non-payment. At the time the premium should have been paid, sufficient funds were available in my escrow account to cover the insurance payment. Additionally, I spoke directly with Senior Vice President [Redacted] [Redacted] regarding this matter. During that conversation, [Redacted] [Redacted] acknowledged that the policy was canceled due to non-payment but refused to provide any compensation or accommodation for the financial harm caused. Instead, I was told that I should have exercised better follow-up with SouthState regarding the payment. This position is particularly troubling given that escrow accounts exist specifically so that lenders manage and disburse required insurance payments. During my discussion with [Redacted] [Redacted], it was also suggested that confusion surrounding the cancellation may have been related to a prior inspection requirement associated with the policy. That inspection issue was fully resolved in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2025 and is entirely unrelated to the subsequent cancellation of the policy. I have documentation confirming that the inspection requirement was satisfied and closed months prior to the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] billing request referenced above. This situation has created unnecessary financial harm and significant frustration. When a mortgage loan is serviced with an escrow account, the lender assumes responsibility for disbursing insurance premiums on time. It is unreasonable to shift that responsibility to the borrower after a servicing failure has already occurred. The consequences of this error have included : Cancellation of my homeowners insurance policy Loss of a lower-cost policy that I had maintained in good standing The need to secure a significantly more expensive replacement policy Extensive time and back-and-forth communication attempting to resolve an issue that should not have occurred in the first place I am therefore requesting that SouthState Bank : 1. Formally acknowledge the servicing error related to the failure to pay the escrowed insurance premium. 2. Reimburse or credit the difference between the [Redacted] annual premium ( {$1200.00} ) and the replacement [Redacted] [Redacted] premium ( {$3300.00} ). 3. Confirm that my escrow account records will be corrected and that appropriate procedures are in place to prevent any future failure to disburse required insurance payments. This situation has involved repeated back-and-forth communication and an unfortunate lack of professionalism in addressing a legitimate servicing concern. As a client, I expect responsible handling of escrow obligations that are contractually assigned to the lender. Please treat this correspondence as a formal request for investigation and resolution. If this matter can not be resolved promptly and fairly, I will proceed with submitting this complaint to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau for further review. I look forward to your written response. Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] Loan no. metadata.full_snippet: Subject : Complaint Regarding Student Loan Servicer Guidance and Missed Forgiveness Opportunity I am submitting this complaint regarding guidance I received from my student loan servicer concerning eligibility for federal student loan forgiveness programs. My loans originated as federal student loans in the [Redacted], and I have been in repayment since approximately [Redacted]. These loans were serviced by [Redacted] for many years and are currently serviced by MOHELA. My loans are listed as [Redacted] loans owned by [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. In [Redacted], I contacted my servicer directly to ask whether I qualified for any federal student loan forgiveness programs. During that conversation I was told that I did not qualify and that there were no forgiveness options available for my account. I relied on that guidance when evaluating my options. At no time during that conversation was I clearly informed that consolidating my [Redacted] loans into a Direct Consolidation Loan could impact my eligibility for federal relief programs tied to repayment history, including the [Redacted] account adjustment that required consolidation before a federal deadline. Because I sought guidance from my servicer and relied on the information provided, I did not pursue consolidation prior to that deadline. Had I been clearly informed of the importance of consolidation for eligibility purposes, I would have taken immediate action. I have located a prior communication from [Redacted] dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] referencing [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] and indicating that [Redacted] loans require consolidation into Direct Loans to qualify for certain federal forgiveness programs. This suggests that the servicer was aware that consolidation could impact eligibility for federal relief programs. Given that I have been in repayment for nearly [Redacted] decades and have already paid significantly more than the original principal borrowed, I believe I may have been disadvantaged by incomplete or misleading information provided by my servicer when I sought guidance regarding forgiveness eligibility. I respectfully request that my account and repayment history be reviewed to determine whether relief or reconsideration may be appropriate due to reliance on servicer guidance regarding federal forgiveness eligibility.

metadata.full_snippet: In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, my husband and I agreed to install solar panels at our home in [Redacted] [Redacted] The system was sold and installed by [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] and financed through Dividend Finance, a division of Fifth Third Bank. During the sales process, we were repeatedly told that installing solar panels would eliminate or replace our electric bill and that the system would cover our homes energy usage. Based on these statements, we agreed to proceed with the installation and financing. After installation, we discovered that the loan amount financed was approximately {$99000.00}. Solar panels were installed on structures on our property, including our pole barn and part of the roof of our home. Despite this large loan amount, we continue to receive high electric bills in addition to our monthly solar loan payment. We were not clearly informed about the true cost of the system, potential dealer fees, or the total amount that would be paid over the life of the loan, which exceeds {$150000.00}. The system also does not appear to provide the level of energy savings that was represented during the sales process. We believe the sales presentation and financing terms may have been misleading and that we entered into this loan based on incomplete or inaccurate information about the cost and expected savings. We are requesting that this loan and the associated sales practices be reviewed and investigated. We would also like a full breakdown of the system cost, dealer fees, and financing structure and assistance resolving this loan due to the misrepresentation of expected savings and system performance.

metadata.full_snippet: In [Redacted] I enrolled in a course with the university but was never provided access to the course platform or instructional materials required to participate in the class. Because I was unable to access the learning management system or course content, I did not receive the educational service being billed. Despite this, the university later reported a balance and placed the account with a third-party collection agency, ConServe, on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. The collector states they sent a validation notice the following day and claims the debt was verified by the creditor. I disputed the debt because the underlying service was never delivered. I requested documentation showing that I actually received the course or had access to the platform required to participate. The collector responded that the debt was verified but did not provide any documentation demonstrating that the service was delivered. Specifically, the collector has not provided documentation such as : proof of course access login records to the learning platform proof of participation or attendance an itemized billing statement a signed enrollment agreement Because the service being billed was never provided, I do not believe I am responsible for this debt. Charging for services that were never delivered constitutes a failure of consideration and makes the collection attempt improper. I am requesting that the company provide proper documentation demonstrating that the service was delivered or remove the account from collection and credit reporting.

metadata.full_snippet: I am disputing this verified account pursuant to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), and I request that this inaccurate and unauthorized account be blocked or removed immediately. I have attached my Identity Theft Report issued by the FTC ( FTC REPORT NUMBER : [Redacted] as evidence. Under the FCRA, specifically 15 U.S.C. 1681i, 1681c-2, and 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 7 ), credit reporting agencies must block or remove inaccurate and unauthorized information within four ( 4 ) business days of receiving an identity theft report. Despite my prior complaint and attempts to resolve this, the following inaccurate and unauthorized account was verified on my credit report : Account Name : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] - [Redacted] This verification is causing significant harm to my credit and financial opportunities. I have requested verification and contract copies from the reporting company, but after 60 days, received no response. This account was previously removed by other agencies due to lack of verification. This simple verification is illegal, as no evidence or written certification of my authorization for this account has been obtained. According to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), the reinsertion or verification of previously deleted information requires written certification from the data furnisher confirming accuracy, and the consumer must be notified. metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint against [Redacted], my federal student loan servicer, for an ongoing autopay processing failure that has resulted in my account being wrongfully designated as delinquent since [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. My loans were transferred from [Redacted] to [Redacted] without my consent, with first payment activity on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Upon transfer, I enrolled all loans in 100 % auto-debit, correctly configured at a [Redacted] ratio with each loan 's monthly payment amount. My account settings requested a total of {$260.00} per month, and I had every reasonable expectation that this amount was being withdrawn, as I was never notified of any discrepancy or incomplete payment at any point during the 18 months prior to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. From [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] through [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], no delinquency notices were issued and no alerts of any kind were received. I have maintained a $ [Redacted] available bank balance throughout, and my separate loans with another servicer have continued auto-paying without issue during the same period. Beginning [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] began issuing delinquency notices on my account for the first time. Upon investigation, it was determined that [Redacted] 's system had been withdrawing {$260.00} per month instead of the {$260.00} my account settings requested specifically, [Redacted] [Redacted] had been withdrawing between $ [Redacted] {$25.00} instead of the correctly configured {$32.00}. I was never notified of this shortfall at any point during the prior 18 months. I had no reason to audit exact withdrawal amounts against my settings, as auto-pay was configured correctly, no alerts were issued, and no delinquency notices appeared until [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. The discrepancy exists entirely within [Redacted] 's system. My account settings have not been modified since initial setup, and screenshots taken hours before my [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] call confirm they remain correctly configured to this day. As a result of this processing failure, [Redacted] generated automated delinquency notices and wrongfully marked my account delinquent. The delinquent balance was initially shown as {$64.00}, which I paid manually on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] in good faith despite the charge later being confirmed as erroneous by [Redacted] representatives. The balance has since been erroneously increased to {$96.00}, meaning [Redacted] has been compounding charges on an error they created and acknowledged. I contacted [Redacted] on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and spoke with Representative [Redacted] [Redacted]. Before reaching [Redacted], I was deliberately disconnected after approximately [Redacted] minutes on hold and routed to a customer satisfaction survey with no representative contact. On my second attempt, [Redacted] acknowledged the following on record : Loan [Redacted] was confirmed as the source of the delinquency The delinquency notices were erroneous payments were satisfied per [Redacted] 's own records The {$64.00} [Redacted] paid on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] was not actually owed the charge was a result of the system error [Redacted] [Redacted] system was at fault for the partial withdrawal on Loan [Redacted] The issue was being referred to [Redacted] 's research department with an expected resolution of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] explicitly instructed me NOT to make the upcoming [Redacted] payment manually and advised me to follow up on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] if unresolved. I followed these instructions. The research department resolution deadline of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] was not met. I contacted [Redacted] again on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] when I received another delinquency notice showing my account now 62 days past due. The following occurred : FIRST CALL First call ( [Redacted] [Redacted] MT ) : I was connected to Representative [Redacted] [Redacted], immediately requested a supervisor, was placed on hold, and was deliberately disconnected after approximately [Redacted] minutes and routed to a satisfaction survey. No supervisor contact was made. SECOND CALL Second call ( [Redacted] [Redacted] MT ) : I reached Representative [Redacted] [Redacted], who initially provided resistance to my supervisor request. At [Redacted] [Redacted] MT, [Redacted] stated on record : " Your payment history is immaculate. It makes no sense why you have any delinquency notices. There is no reason your account should have any delinquent status. This needs to be fixed immediately. '' She further stated : " It's not about sympathy it's about what is right and wrong. '' SUPERVISOR EVASION Despite my repeated requests across both calls, I never spoke directly with a supervisor. A supervisor was reportedly present but communicated only through [Redacted] while I was placed on hold. The supervisor 's name was never provided. FORBEARANCE DENIAL At approximately [Redacted] [Redacted] MT, [Redacted] offered to apply a voluntary forbearance to clear the delinquency. I explicitly declined this offer and requested an administrative forbearance backdated to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] the correct remedy for a servicer caused error. [Redacted] stated this could not be accommodated due to " too much red tape. '' This is not a legitimate justification. Administrative forbearance exists precisely for servicer caused delinquencies. EXPLICIT DECLINATION At [Redacted] [Redacted] MT, I explicitly and finally declined any voluntary forbearance on record. I stated clearly that I do not consent to any forbearance unless it is an administrative forbearance. [Redacted] acknowledged this. TICKET SUBMITTED At [Redacted] [Redacted] MT, [Redacted] confirmed a ticket was submitted to correct the withdrawal amount for Loan [Redacted] from {$260.00} to {$260.00}. Ticket Reference Number : [Redacted]. Correspondence expected within [Redacted] hours. However, it remains unclear how [Redacted] intends to clear the existing delinquency without an administrative forbearance, as no mechanism was specified. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I entered into a financing agreement through EasyPay Finance for {$3600.00} to pay for vehicle repairs recommended by a now terminated [Redacted] shop manager. The agreement required bi-weekly payments of {$180.00} for [Redacted] weeks at 118 % APR, with a 90-day promotional payoff option. The loan was entered into based on representations that the recommended repairs would resolve the mechanical problems and return the vehicle to working condition. This did not occur. The repairs performed under the financed work did not correct the vehicles issues, and the car continued experiencing the same mechanical problems almost immediately after pickup. Timeline of Events [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] had possession of the vehicle performing the financed repairs under the supervision of now terminated employee. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I contacted [Redacted] to report that the vehicle was still experiencing the same problems. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] The vehicle was returned to the shop for evaluation. The now terminated shop manager oversaw the inspection and stated they could not find any additional issues. The vehicle continued experiencing the same mechanical problems after this visit. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I contacted EasyPay Finances dispute department via email to notify them that the financed repairs had failed and that the vehicle remained unreliable. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] new management, the [Redacted] location towed the vehicle back to the shop at their own expense for further inspection. The new manager indicated that the prior manager had been terminated and that repairs performed during his employment had often failed to meet company standards. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] A formal written dispute was submitted to EasyPay Finance explaining that the financed repairs had failed and requesting that the loan be re-aged once the vehicle was properly repaired. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] completed corrective repairs at their own expense after determining that a component originally identified by the technician should have been replaced during the initial repair. The technician also indicated that his original shop notes reflecting this recommendation had been redacted. Once the component was replaced, the vehicle finally returned to proper working condition. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] EasyPay Finance sent written late and past-due notices despite the active dispute and the ongoing repair process. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] A third written notice was sent to EasyPay dispute department requesting supervisory review and a formal response to the dispute. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] After repeated collection calls, I spoke with an EasyPay Finance representative and explained that the account was under formal dispute and that defective repairs had been confirmed. During this call we were informed that EasyPay considers the merchants recommendation when handling disputes. After this conversation, we contacted the [Redacted] manager, who stated he had spoken with EasyPay previously but did not understand that his comments would influence dispute resolution. After reviewing the situation, he contacted EasyPay Finance directly and advised that the loan should be re-aged to the date the corrective repairs were completed due to the defective original work. Collection calls continue every few days despite the account being under formal written dispute. Issue This loan financed repairs that were materially defective and incomplete, leaving the vehicle unreliable until the shop corrected the work at its own expense. The merchant has acknowledged the defective service and supports re-aging the loan to the date the vehicle was properly repaired. Despite this, EasyPay Finance has : Failed to respond to multiple written dispute notices Continued collection activity during an active dispute Refused to re-age the loan despite merchant acknowledgment of defective service Suggested applying for a new loan instead of correcting the disputed account ________________________________________

metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this complaint regarding Truist Banks handling and application of interest rates on two [Redacted] [Redacted] accounts that were opened under the same promotional offer. My partner and I opened a joint [Redacted] [Redacted] account with Truist under a promotional interest rate advertised at approximately 4 % APY. Shortly thereafter, while the same promotion was still active, I opened an individual [Redacted] [Redacted] account under the same promotional offer, with a substantially larger balance. Both accounts were opened within the same promotional timeframe and are structured as the same type of [Redacted] [Redacted] account product. While I understand that interest rates may fluctuate, the issue is that the interest rates applied to these two accounts have diverged significantly, despite being opened under what appears to be the same promotion and product structure. Currently : The joint account with the lower balance is earning approximately 3 % APY The individual account with the significantly larger balance has fluctuated between approximately 0.5 % and 1.7 % APY Truist has not provided any explanation for this discrepancy. I have contacted Truist customer service multiple times seeking clarification regarding the rate structure and the promotional terms applied to these accounts. Specifically, I have requested : The rate tier structure applicable to this [Redacted] [Redacted] product The promotion code and product code associated with each account An explanation as to why accounts opened under the same promotional offer are receiving materially different interest rates Instead of providing this information, Truist customer service has repeatedly directed me back to the branch manager at the Truist branch in [Redacted] [Redacted], West Virginia. This is not an acceptable resolution path. I have previously experienced significant issues with this branch manager regarding the mishandling of a line of credit application, which ultimately resulted in the application being disqualified due to issues involving an appraiser selected by Truist. During that process, I was informed that the matter had been escalated to management when it had not been. I ultimately secured a line of credit through another institution within two weeks. Given this history, I do not have confidence that the branch manager can provide an impartial or competent resolution to this issue. More importantly, this matter should not require resolution at the branch level, as it involves the application of promotional interest rates and product terms that should be governed by Truists corporate policies and disclosures. Despite multiple attempts to resolve this issue through Truists customer service channels, the bank has refused to provide documentation or explanation regarding how the interest rates are determined or why the accounts are receiving materially different rates. The lack of transparency raises concerns regarding whether Truist is properly disclosing and consistently applying the terms of its promotional [Redacted] [Redacted] accounts, particularly when accounts are opened under the same advertised promotion. At this point, I am requesting that Truist provide the following : 1. The official promotional terms and rate structure applicable to the [Redacted] [Redacted] accounts opened during this promotion. 2. The product code and promotional code associated with each of my accounts. 3. A clear explanation of why the two accounts are receiving materially different interest rates despite being opened under the same promotional offer. 4. Confirmation that the interest rates applied to my accounts are consistent with Truists published disclosures and promotional terms. To date, Truist has not provided any meaningful explanation and has instead redirected the issue to a branch manager who has previously mishandled other matters related to my accounts. Given the circumstances, I am requesting a formal review by Truists corporate compliance team to ensure that the promotional terms and interest rate structures are being applied transparently and consistently.

metadata.snippet: I am submitting this complaint regarding Citizens Bank, N.A.s handling of my residential mortgage loan, which involved misrepresentations related to pricing and rate matching, inadequate disclosure of material issues prior to closing, and failures of internal supervision that res...
metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this complaint regarding Citizens Bank, N.A.s handling of my residential mortgage loan, which involved misrepresentations related to pricing and rate matching, inadequate disclosure of material issues prior to closing, and failures of internal supervision that resulted in borrower harm. I selected Citizens Bank after receiving multiple more favorable mortgage offers elsewhere. I proceeded specifically based on representations made by Citizens Mortgage Loan Originator, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], who indicated she would obtain competitive pricing, successfully match rates, and provide compensation for issues that arose during the process. Many of these representations were conveyed via unrecorded cellphone conversations. I learned that certain rate matches were denied based on explanations that were inaccurate, including claims that competing rates could not be matched because they were not offered in [Redacted] % increments, despite evidence that they were. During the end of the loan process, I was encouraged by the MLO to submit a competitive rate match request using language suggesting Citizens could not track the source of the competing quote and that she would get it submitted back to lock desk. I possess written documentation showing that a competitors quote was sent to me by the MLO prior to my submitting the match request. As a result of these issues, my loan terms materially worsened. I ultimately closed in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] with a [Redacted] % [Redacted] ARM, after pursuing a [Redacted] % [Redacted] fixed product. I am now in a position where I will almost certainly be required to refinance in the future, increasing long-term cost and risk. In addition, neither I nor my team of professionals ( attorneys and buyers agent ) were informed of any unresolved underwriting or property eligibility issues until the scheduled closing date of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. We were told the loan was clear to close and were physically present at the closing table when, after hours of waiting, we were informed that the loan could not proceed due to documentation Citizens had not yet obtained. This delay occurred without prior notice and pushed the transaction dangerously close to the expiration of my lease. This sequence of events occurred immediately before [Redacted]. My spouse and I experienced significant emotional distress due to the genuine fear of housing instability. Our belongings were packed, we were unable to celebrate the holiday, and the stress took a substantial mental toll. Despite these issues, the loan officer ultimately received her commission. Citizens later offered {$800.00} in compensation, which I declined as inadequate given the scope of the issues and harm caused. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I initiated a formal complaint with Citizens Bank regarding the handling of my mortgage loan and requested remediation for the issues described above. While there was some initial acknowledgment and limited contact following that complaint, no meaningful remediation was offered, and the substantive issues I raised were not addressed. After providing detailed written information outlining the events, Citizens ceased communication for an extended period. I then received a letter by mail without any prior outreach, discussion, or request for supporting documentation. The letter did not meaningfully engage with the material facts I presented, nor did Citizens request any proof or clarification despite my willingness to provide documentation. This lack of engagement and follow-through further contributed to my concern that Citizens did not adequately review or investigate the issues raised in my formal complaint. During the pendency of my formal complaint and while remediation discussions were ongoing, I received a mailed thank you for choosing me referral postcard from the loan officer involved in this matter. Receiving marketing and referral solicitation from the same individual whose conduct was the subject of an unresolved complaint further underscored the lack of internal coordination, oversight, and sensitivity surrounding Citizens Banks handling of this issue. FOR CRS : This newly created complaint has new material information in the files I have attached.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint against Credit Collection Services regarding two alleged collection accounts that they are attempting to collect and/or reporting to the credit reporting agencies. I previously disputed these accounts and sent a formal debt validation request pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g. In that request, I asked Credit Collection Services to provide competent evidence that I have a legal obligation to pay the alleged debts and that the company has the legal authority to collect and report them. Specifically, I requested proper documentation including : A copy of the original agreement or contract bearing my signature A complete chain of title showing the transfer or assignment of the debt to Credit Collection Services Documentation verifying the amount of the alleged debt, including principal, interest, and fees Proof that Credit Collection Services has the legal authority to collect and report the debt To date, the company has failed to provide adequate validation of these alleged debts. Despite the fact that the debts were formally disputed, Credit Collection Services continues to attempt to collect and/or furnish information about these accounts to the credit reporting agencies. Continuing collection activity and reporting unverified information after a dispute may constitute violations of federal law, including but not limited to : The Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), which requires a debt collector to cease collection activities until proper validation of the debt is provided. The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, which prohibits furnishers from reporting information that is inaccurate, incomplete, or that has not been properly investigated after a consumer dispute. Because Credit Collection Services has failed to provide sufficient validation, the accuracy and legitimacy of these accounts remain in serious doubt. metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this complaint regarding a collection account that is currently being reported on my credit report and appears to be inaccurate and improperly validated. A collection account from Allied interstate LL in the amount of {$1400.00} is currently being reported on my credit report. I dispute the validity and accuracy of this alleged debt and the manner in which it is being reported. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692g of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), a debt collector is required to provide proper validation of an alleged debt upon request. To date, I have not received sufficient documentation verifying the debt, including but not limited to a signed agreement, original account statements, or documentation proving that I am legally responsible for the alleged obligation. Additionally, under 15 U.S.C. 1692c of the FDCPA, debt collectors must follow strict guidelines regarding communication with consumers and may not engage in practices that violate consumer protections established under federal law. Furthermore, under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), any entity furnishing or reporting information to consumer reporting agencies must follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy of the information reported. Reporting a collection account without proper validation and documentation raises serious concerns about the accuracy and compliance of this reporting. The continued reporting of this account without proper verification is causing harm to my credit profile and may constitute a violation of federal consumer protection laws. Therefore, I am requesting the following : 1. A full investigation of this account and the reporting practices related to it. 2. Complete validation of the alleged debt as required under 15 U.S.C. 1692g. 3. Proof of reasonable procedures used to ensure maximum possible accuracy as required under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ). 4. Immediate deletion of the collection account from all consumer reporting agencies if the debt can not be fully verified and validated. If the company can not provide sufficient documentation proving the validity and accuracy of this debt, I request that the account be removed from my credit reports immediately and that all credit bureaus be notified of the correction. Thank you for your attention to this matter and for ensuring that my consumer rights are protected under federal law.

metadata.full_snippet: Subject : Affirm Holding Consumer Liable Without Proof of Delivery and Incomplete Dispute Records I am filing a complaint against Affirm regarding a financed purchase for an item that was never delivered. The order was shipped to my PO Box . For PO Box deliveries, packages must be transferred to and accepted by [Redacted] before delivery to the recipient can occur. Affirm has acknowledged in prior communication that there is no record showing the package was transferred to or accepted by [Redacted]. Without [Redacted] acceptance, delivery to a PO Box can not be completed. Despite this, Affirm upheld the charge based on a delivery photo provided by the merchant. The photo does not show delivery to my PO Box or any identifiable mailbox location. Instead, it shows the package placed in a general lobby or unsecured area within a post office. The carrier did not transfer the package to [Redacted] personnel for acceptance. Leaving a package in an unsecured area without transfer of custody does not constitute completed delivery and does not establish that the item was delivered to me. I have attempted to contact both the merchant and the carrier, but the merchant has not responded. Affirm has advised me to pursue the merchant or file a police report. A police report is not appropriate, as there is no evidence the package was ever delivered to the addressed location. Additionally, I am unable to access prior communications related to my dispute within [Redacted] system, including key statements previously made by Affirm regarding the lack of [Redacted] transfer. This raises concerns about the completeness, transparency, and reliability of their investigation and recordkeeping. Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, creditors are required to conduct a reasonable investigation of disputed charges and may not hold consumers liable for charges where goods were not delivered as agreed. In this case, Affirm has upheld the charge without verifiable proof of delivery and despite acknowledging a missing delivery chain. Affirm continues to hold me financially responsible and has indicated potential credit reporting consequences, despite the lack of evidence that the item was delivered to me. This reflects a failure to properly validate delivery and a reliance on insufficient evidence to support a financial obligation. I am requesting that Affirm : Reverse the charge due to lack of proof of delivery Provide a complete record of all dispute communications and findings Review and correct their dispute investigation process for PO Box deliveries

ZuntaFi accepted that payment. Notwithstanding this agreement and acceptance of funds, your company has continued collection efforts. Out of fear of adverse credit reporting, I made additional payments under duress. Continued collection activity under these circumstances is improper. I request refunds of any payments made since [Redacted] of 2024, totaling {$3300.00}. I was advised by the Minnesota Attorney General 's office that the Federal Trade Commission Holder Rule preserves a borrowers right to assert against a loan holder any claims and defenses that could be asserted against the seller of goods or services when the lender and the seller have a connected or referral relationship. Where a school and a lender have an ongoing business relationshipincluding referral arrangements, coordinated financing programs, or other financial tiesthe lender is subject to the same defenses arising from the schools misconduct. I informed Zuntafil this originally and they told me the Holder Rule does not apply to my loan. [Redacted] [Redacted] from [Redacted] [Redacted] is the school in connection with this loan. They have been found guilty by several courts that they engaged in deceptive and unfair practices related to the extension of credit and representations made at enrollment. Because this loan was made in connection with, and as a direct result of, that schools conduct and lender relationship, ZuntaFias holder and assigneeis legally subject to those claims and defenses. Under the Holder Rule, my recovery and offset rights apply up to the amounts paid under the contract. I have already paid [Redacted] [Redacted]far exceeding the alleged principal of {$28000.00}. At minimum, no further collection is permissible, and cancellation is warranted. I have tried negotiating and talking with them and they do not answer my questions, nor offer any further explanations. metadata.full_snippet: Formal Complaint Deceptive Lending Practices & Bait and Switch OneMain Financial. To the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am submitting this formal complaint against OneMain Financial regarding deceptive lending practices that I experienced recently. COMPLAINT DETAILS : Company Name : OneMain Financial Branch Location : [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted], FL [Redacted] WHAT HAPPENED : I previously borrowed {$8000.00} from OneMain Financial and responsibly paid that loan back in full. This year, I decided to return to OneMain Financial to consolidate my bills in the same amount of {$8000.00}. Through the [Redacted] [Redacted] app, I was shown multiple pre-approved loan offers, all from OneMain Financial. I selected the offer that best matched my needs in terms of loan amount and monthly payment terms. Based on that selection, I received an online approval. Shortly after, a OneMain Financial representative contacted me to confirm my approval and invited me to come into the branch. When I arrived at the [Redacted] [Redacted] location, I was told that I would not be approved for the {$8000.00} I had applied for instead, I was only being offered {$1500.00}. The representative stated that this was because of the assessed value of my vehicle. This is a classic bait and switch practice. I was drawn in with an online approval for the amount I requested, only to have the terms changed entirely once I was in the office. This is deceptive and misleading to consumers. I declined the offer and left. Later that day, I submitted a second application for a lower amount through a different link. That application was denied because OneMain Financials system flagged it as a duplicate application. At [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] the following morning a Sunday I received an automated denial letter that was worded in a way that implied I had poor credit, which is not accurate. The denial was the result of a duplicate application flag, not my creditworthiness. WHAT I AM REQUESTING : [Redacted]. A formal investigation into OneMain Financials use of pre-approval offers through third-party platforms such as [Redacted] [Redacted] that do not reflect actual approval terms. [Redacted]. A review of whether this practice constitutes deceptive advertising under the Consumer Financial Protection Act. [Redacted]. That this complaint be added to the official record against OneMain Financial. I am happy to provide any additional documentation or information needed to support this complaint. Respectfully submitted,

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing a formal complaint against Way2Go Card services regarding ongoing inability to access my account, repeated improper fees, and failure to provide customer support. I activated my Way2Go card over a year ago. However, over the past [Redacted] ( [Redacted] ) months, I have experienced continuous issues accessing my account and reaching customer service. During this time, I have been repeatedly charged {$0.00} per call when attempting to contact customer service. These charges are being applied even though I am not calling to check my balance. The system automatically forces a balance inquiry instead of allowing me to reach a representative. As a result, I have accumulated well over [Redacted] charges in the past [Redacted] months alone, totaling more than {$20.00} in fees for services I did not request. In addition, I have made numerous attempts to reach customer support, often being placed on hold for extended periods with no resolution. Most recently, as of last Friday, I was on hold for approximately [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and was forced to hang up because no representative ever answered the call. There is no direct or accessible way to reach technical support or a dispute department. If I miss a return call, I am required to restart the entire process and incur additional charges again. This creates a cycle where I am continuously charged fees without ever receiving actual assistance. This is unacceptable and appears to be an unfair and deceptive practice. I am being charged repeatedly due to a system that does not function properly and actively prevents me from accessing customer support. Since child support funds are only accessible through this card, I have no alternative way to access my money without dealing with these barriers and fees. This situation has caused financial hardship and unnecessary stress, as these funds are essential for my household. I am requesting the following : * A full refund of all call-related fees charged over the past [Redacted] months * Immediate correction of the system preventing access to customer service * A clear explanation of these charges and why customers are being billed for unsuccessful attempts to reach support * Assurance that these practices will be corrected to prevent further harm If this matter is not resolved promptly, I am prepared to pursue additional action through all available regulatory and legal channels.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint against Wells Fargo Bank , N.A . for multiple violations of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), Regulation Z, as well as for negligence in handling unauthorized transactions, failure to maintain accurate account access, and failure to conduct a lawful and reasonable investigation. case number [Redacted]. Below is a detailed summary of the issues : 1. * * Unauthorized Transactions Ignored by Wells Fargo * * More than [Redacted] [Redacted] transactions were posted to my credit card account over several months. I do not have an [Redacted] account, I do not use [Redacted] services, and I did not authorize any of these charges. The only transaction I personally made was a {$240.00} cash advance. [Redacted]. * * Wells Fargo Removed My Credit Card From My Online Banking Platform * * My credit card disappeared from my Wells Fargo online banking access, leaving only my savings and joint account visible. This prevented me from monitoring activity, viewing statements, or making payments. Wells Fargos representative, [Redacted] [Redacted], admitted that the bank removed the card from my online access but provided no explanation. This system failure directly caused the delayed discovery of fraud and the past due status. [Redacted]. * * I Paid My Legitimate {$240.00} Cash Advance Immediately After Regaining Access * * As soon as Wells Fargo restored my online access and I was finally able to see my account again, I * * immediately paid the {$240.00} cash advance * *, which is the * * only transaction I actually made * *. This demonstrates that I have acted in good faith and that any past due status was caused solely by Wells Fargos removal of my card from my online platformnot by any negligence on my part. [Redacted]. * * Incorrect Contact Information Maintained by Wells Fargo * * Wells Fargo had an outdated mailing address and an incorrect phone number on file. I did not receive statements, alerts, or notifications. I updated my information immediately after discovering the issue. [Redacted]. * * Delayed Discovery Caused by Wells Fargos System Error * * I only became aware of the fraudulent activity after receiving an email regarding my credit card status. When I contacted Wells Fargo, I was informed of a balance of {$580.00} and a past due amount of $ [Redacted] resulting from unauthorized charges and the banks removal of my card from online access. [Redacted]. * * [Redacted] Confirms No Transactions Exist Under My Information * * I contacted [Redacted] multiple times. [Redacted] confirmed that no transactions exist under my name, card number, or personal information. They stated the charges [Redacted] have been made through a virtual wallet or another account, which does not apply to me. This further confirms the transactions were fraudulent. [Redacted]. * * Wells Fargo Unable to Identify the Source of the Charges * * Wells Fargo could not determine where the transactions originated, yet still attempted to hold me responsible. This violates Regulation Z, which requires the bank to prove a transaction was authorizednot the consumer. [Redacted]. * * Credit Score Damage Caused by Wells Fargo * * My credit score has been negatively impacted due to past due amounts caused by fraudulent charges and Wells Fargos removal of my card from online access. This harm is a direct result of the banks negligence. I am requesting the CFPB to require Wells Fargo to : - Remove all unauthorized [Redacted] charges. - Reverse all interest, late fees, penalties, and past due amounts associated with these fraudulent transactions. - Correct all negative credit reporting caused by this issue. - Provide a written explanation for why my credit card was removed from my online banking platform. - Conduct a lawful, complete, and documented reinvestigation as required by Regulation Z. - Provide proofif any existsthat I authorized these transactions. Attached to this complaint, I am providing : - Copies of Wells Fargo letters and notices - Email correspondence with [Redacted] ( multiple agents ) - Screenshot showing only two accounts visible on my online banking platform - FTC Identity Theft Report - For Confirmation that Wells Fargo representatives admitted the card was removed from my access, please refer to the bank compliance recordings- Proof of payment of the {$240.00} cash advance immediately after regaining online access Wells Fargos handling of this matter has been negligent, non compliant with federal law, and harmful to my financial standing. I request immediate CFPB intervention.

The store advised me to dispute the charge with my credit card issuer. I then contacted Discover and filed a dispute. I am disputing that I received a defective or compromised product that was not as described at the time of sale. Despite explaining this, Discover did not investigate the issue as a defective merchandise claim and instead treated it only as a fraud claim, which led to the denial. I have also filed a complaint with the Federal Trade Commission regarding this incident. As a result, I paid for a product that was compromised prior to purchase, and neither the merchant nor the credit card issuer has resolved the issue.

metadata.full_snippet: am formally disputing Charles Schwab Banks response to my complaint ( CFPB Case # [Redacted] ), as it inaccurately characterizes the fraudulent transaction and fails to adequately address the circumstances of this incident. Schwab asserts that the transaction was authorized because I entered my login credentials and shared authentication codes. This characterization is misleading and incomplete. I did not knowingly or willingly authorize a wire transfer to a third party. I was the victim of a sophisticated impersonation scam in which the fraudster posed as a Charles Schwab representative. My actions were taken under false pretenses, based on the belief that I was communicating with my bank. At no point did I intend to grant access to a fraudster or authorize a wire transfer. The access and subsequent transaction were the direct result of deception. This distinction is critical. A transaction induced through impersonation and fraud should not be treated the same as a legitimately authorized transaction. Additionally, Schwabs response does not sufficiently address its own fraud detection and prevention responsibilities. The transaction involved : A new or compromised login session The rapid initiation of a wire transfer following account access Activity that should reasonably be considered high-risk and atypical Given these factors, it is reasonable to expect that Schwabs internal controls and fraud monitoring systems would have flagged or prevented this transaction. Schwab has not provided any explanation of what safeguards were in place, whether any alerts were triggered, or why the transaction was allowed to proceed without additional verification. Furthermore, the fact that the fraudster successfully impersonated a Schwab representative raises serious concerns about customer protection and communication security. As a customer, I relied on the trust and credibility of the Schwab brand. This type of social engineering attack directly exploits that trust. Schwabs reliance on the claim that I shared authentication information ignores the broader context of how that information was obtainedthrough deception and impersonation. Consumers should not bear full liability when they are manipulated by individuals posing as their financial institution. This incident has caused significant financial harm and has had downstream impacts on my ability to meet financial obligations. Given the above, I respectfully request : [Redacted]. A reconsideration of [Redacted] determination that this transaction was authorized [Redacted]. A full reimbursement of the unrecovered funds [Redacted]. A detailed explanation of [Redacted] fraud detection protocols and why they failed in this instance [Redacted]. Clarification on how Schwab protects customers from impersonation-based scams I believe this matter warrants further review, as the current response does not adequately reflect the realities of fraud or the responsibilities of financial institutions to protect their customers. Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint against TransUnion LLC for failing to maintain reasonable procedures to ensure the maximum possible accuracy of information on my consumer credit report, and for failing to conduct a meaningful reinvestigation of a previously disputed account, in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) and 15 U.S.C. 1681i. TransUnion is currently reporting a collection account from [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], allegedly originating from [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], Account No. [Redacted], with a balance of {$4700.00}. This account has already been flagged as disputed by the consumer on my TransUnion report, yet the material inaccuracies identified below remain uncorrected. Specifically, the following inaccuracies and deficiencies exist on my TransUnion report : [Redacted]. COMPLETE ABSENCE OF PAYMENT HISTORY : My TransUnion report reflects absolutely no payment history for this account. Under the FCRA, a consumer reporting agency can not continue reporting information that can not be verified. The total absence of any payment history indicates this account can not be substantiated and should be deleted. [Redacted]. UNRESOLVED PRIOR DISPUTE : This account is currently flagged as disputed by the consumer on my TransUnion report, yet the material inaccuracies have not been corrected or the account deleted. TransUnion 's failure to resolve a previously flagged dispute is a direct violation of its reinvestigation obligations under 15 U.S.C. 1681i. [Redacted]. INCONSISTENT CLOSURE DATE : TransUnion reflects a closure date of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] for this account, while [Redacted] reflects [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] a discrepancy of over one year on the same account. This cross-bureau inconsistency is a strong indicator that the information being furnished has not been properly verified. [Redacted]. INCONSISTENT ORIGINAL BALANCE : TransUnion reports an original balance of {$21000.00}, while [Redacted] and [Redacted] reflect no original balance at all. This fundamental discrepancy across all three bureaus undermines the verifiability of the entire account and the accuracy of the reported balance. TransUnion has an independent obligation under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) to follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy, and under 15 U.S.C. 1681i to conduct a meaningful reinvestigation when a consumer disputes information. The continued reporting of this account despite an active consumer dispute flag and the absence of verifiable payment history constitutes a clear failure to meet these obligations.

metadata.full_snippet: THIS IS A SECOND COMPLAINT FILED BECAUSE GM FINANCIAL 'S RESPONSE TO CASE NUMBER [Redacted] FAILED TO ADDRESS ANY VIOLATION ALLEGED, AND BECAUSE GM FINANCIAL HAS CONTINUED AND ESCALATED ITS UNLAWFUL CONDUCT AFTER THAT COMPLAINT WAS FILED AND CLOSED. This complaint is related to prior CFPB complaint Case Number [Redacted], filed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and [Redacted] filed on or about [Redacted], [Redacted], which all were closed without an inadequate response from GM Financial dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], and [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I filed a formal complaint with the CFPB against GM Financial, assigned Case Number [Redacted]. That complaint alleged fraudulent loan origination, misassignment of buyer and cosigner roles, violation of the FTC Holder Rule, unlawful post-rescission credit reporting, and wrongful repossession of a motor vehicle. GM Financial responded on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] through their Compliance Department, signed by [Redacted] [Redacted] Their response consisted of [Redacted] paragraphs that : ( 1 ) recited the contract terms, ( 2 ) disclaimed responsibility for [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] conduct, ( 3 ) stated that the credit reporting was accurate, and ( 4 ) directed me to contact their customer service line. Their response did not address a single violation alleged in the original complaint. Specifically, GM Financial 's [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] response failed entirely to address : The fraudulent misassignment of buyer and cosigner roles at signing The FTC Holder Rule, 16 C.F.R. 433, which is printed in bold capital letters on page 5 of the very contract GM Financial attached to their response The wrongful repossession of the vehicle on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] days before their response was even written The {$500.00} repossession fee assessed on a rescinded contract The legal invalidity of reporting delinquency on a contract rescinded before the first payment was ever due The [Redacted] formal written rescission notices received by GM Financial on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I submitted consumer feedback to the CFPB disputing GM Financial 's response in its entirety. The complaint was closed without resolution. This second complaint is filed because GM Financial 's conduct has continued and escalated since the prior complaint was filed. NEW AND CONTINUING VIOLATIONS SINCE THE PRIOR COMPLAINT A. The Wrongful Repossession - [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] GM Financial 's own payment history, submitted as part of their CFPB response to Case Number [Redacted], confirms the following critical timeline : [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : Contract signed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : GM Financial received and signed for formal Rescission of Contract via certified mail, [Redacted] days before the first payment was ever due [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : First payment due date under the contract [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : GM Financial received Final Demand for Immediate Rescission via [Redacted] [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : GM Financial received Notice of Fair Debt Collection Practices Act Violations, Notice of Dispute and Demand for Validation Cease and Desist Demand, Notice of Fair Credit Reporting Act Violations [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : GM Financial initiated repossession setup confirmed by their own payment history [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : GM Financial assessed a {$500.00} miscellaneous repossession fee confirmed by their own payment history [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : First CFPB complaint filed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : GM Financial responded to CFPB complaint without addressing the repossession along. The first payment under this contract was not due until [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. My rescission was received by GM Financial on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] days before any payment was ever owed. No valid payment obligation ever legally arose under this contract. GM Financial repossessed the vehicle on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], nearly [Redacted] weeks after receiving the first rescission notice and [Redacted] weeks after receiving the Final Demand. This is a wrongful repossession as a matter of law. The vehicle has not been returned as of the date of this complaint. GM Financial repossessed the vehicle while simultaneously preparing a response to a federal consumer complaint alleging fraud. They did not disclose the repossession in their [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] CFPB response. The CFPB was not informed that GM Financial had taken the vehicle [Redacted] days before filing their response. [Redacted] GM Financial 's Own Contract Prohibits Their Defense GM Financial 's [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] response states they were not present during contract negotiations and bear no responsibility for [Redacted] [Redacted] 's conduct. This position is directly and completely foreclosed by page [Redacted] of the Motor Vehicle Retail Installment Sales Contract that GM Financial itself attached to its CFPB response. That page contains the following in bold capital letters : NOTICE : ANY HOLDER OF THIS CONSUMER CREDIT CONTRACT IS SUBJECT TO ALL CLAIMS AND DEFENSES WHICH THE DEBTOR COULD ASSERT AGAINST THE SELLER OF GOODS OR SERVICES OBTAINED PURSUANT HERETO OR WITH THE PROCEEDS HEREOF. This is the FTC Holder Rule, 16 C.F.R. 433. By purchasing this contract from [Redacted] [Redacted], GM Financial assumed legal responsibility for all claims and defenses arising from its fraudulent origination. GM Financial submitted this language to the CFPB as part of their defense and appears to have either not read it or hoped the CFPB would not. This is itself an unfair and deceptive act in connection with a consumer complaint response. C. Continued Unlawful Credit Reporting As of the date of this complaint, GM Financial continues to report this account as delinquent on all three major consumer reporting agencies, Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. These derogatory entries reflect payment obligations that never legally arose because the contract was rescinded before the first payment was ever due. GM Financial 's [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] response stated the credit reporting is accurate. It is not. Reporting delinquency on a contract rescinded before any payment obligation arose, after receiving [Redacted] written rescission notices, and a debt validation constitutes willful furnishing of inaccurate information in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). Every day these entries remain on my credit report after GM Financial 's receipt of the original rescission notice on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] is a separate violation. These false entries are causing me the following ongoing, documented financial harms : Active impairment of my home mortgage qualification. I am attempting to purchase a home and these entries are directly blocking my ability to qualify Forced cosigner requirement on a separate vehicle purchase due to artificially damaged credit score Ongoing reputational and financial damage from false delinquency reporting visible to any creditor who pulls my credit Unlawful Fees Assessed on a Rescinded Contract GM Financial 's own payment history confirms the following fees assessed after receiving rescission notice on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : {$63.00} late fee assessed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] {$63.00} late fee assessed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] {$500.00} repossession fee assessed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] {$2500.00} in interest accrued on the account Every one of these charges was assessed after GM Financial received written notice that the contract had been rescinded. None of them are legally valid. GM Financial is now asserting a total balance of {$69000.00} on a contract that was rescinded before a single dollar was ever owed. VIOLATIONS ALLEGED The following federal violations have occurred and are documented : 1. Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), Willful furnishing of inaccurate derogatory information to consumer reporting agencies after receiving written notice of rescission on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and Final Demand on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Each derogatory entry reported after [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] constitutes a separate violation. 2. FTC Holder Rule, 16 C.F.R. 433, Refusal to honor all claims and defenses arising from the fraudulent origination of the assigned contract, despite the Holder Rule notice being printed on the face of the contract GM Financial submitted to the CFPB. 3. Consumer Financial Protection Act, 12 U.S.C. 5531, Unfair, deceptive, and abusive acts and practices including : enforcing a fraudulently induced contract, repossessing a vehicle on a rescinded contract, assessing fees on a rescinded contract, and continuing derogatory credit reporting after receiving [Redacted] written rescission demands. 4. Truth in Lending Act, 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. Failure to accurately disclose the identity and legal role of each party on the consumer credit contract. 5. Wrongful repossession constituting conversion under applicable law repossession of a vehicle under color of a void or voidable contract after receiving [Redacted] formal written rescission notices and a debt validation.

metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this Identity Theft Report to formally document that credit inquiries and accounts have been opened in my name without my knowledge, authorization, or consent. I am the victim of identity theft, and this statement details the fraudulent activity, the immediate steps I have taken, and the actions required to rectify my credit file. All information provided herein is accurate to the best of my knowledge. I first became aware of the fraudulent activity upon reviewing my credit report and noticing multiple inquiries and accounts that are completely unfamiliar. I have never applied for or authorized any of these accounts, nor have I shared my personal information with these lenders or companies. This unauthorized activity was discovered despite my diligent efforts to safeguard my personal information. None of the accounts or credit applications reflected on my credit report were initiated, approved, or authorized by me. These fraudulent inquiries and accounts constitute unauthorized use of my personal information. I have taken immediate steps to address this, including : 1. Contacting the lenders and companies involved to report the fraudulent activity and request that the accounts be closed, canceled, or flagged as identity theft. 2. Placing a fraud alert and a credit freeze on my credit reports to prevent further unauthorized applications. 3. Filing a police report with my local law enforcement agency to officially document the identity theft. 4. Reporting the identity theft to the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ). The unauthorized use of my personal information is a direct violation of federal law, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). I demand immediate removal of all fraudulent accounts, inquiries, and applications from my credit reports unless proper, verifiable documentation proving my authorization is provided. Failure to comply will be considered a willful violation of federal law, and I am prepared to pursue all available legal remedies, including regulatory enforcement, civil damages, and reporting to law enforcement authorities. Any continued reporting of fraudulent accounts without proper validation will be considered malicious and legally actionable. To be absolutely clear : I had no involvement whatsoever with these fraudulent applications or accounts. I did not initiate, approve, authorize, or benefit from any of these actions. The accounts and inquiries appearing on my credit report are the result of criminal misuse of my identity and must be permanently removed to restore the integrity of my credit file. Under the FCRA, especially Section 605B, I have the right to request the blocking and removal of any information that resulted from identity theft. I am formally invoking this right and demand that all fraudulent accounts and inquiries be investigated and deleted immediately. The fraudulent activity has caused significant stress, inconvenience, and potential harm to my financial standing. I have taken all appropriate steps to protect myself, including documenting, reporting, and securing my personal information. It is imperative that the credit bureaus and all involved creditors act swiftly to correct these inaccuracies. I declare under penalty of perjury that all statements herein are true and accurate. I demand that the fraudulent entries be permanently removed from my credit file, and I expect immediate corrective action from all responsible parties.

metadata.full_snippet: PenFed Credit Union inaccurately reported my mortgage as 60 and 90 days delinquent during an approved trial modification plan, despite all payments being made on time. This inaccurate reporting caused significant financial harm, including a mortgage denial, multiple credit limit reductions, and a substantial credit score drop. PenFeds Admission of Error : In their written response dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, PenFed explicitly stated : PenFed has determined that an error occurred. This confirms the reporting was inaccurate. Failure to Address Damages : Although PenFed admitted the error, they refused to provide compensation for the documented harm caused while the inaccurate reporting was present on my credit reports. Their position is that correcting the reporting fully resolves the error. This is incorrect. The harm occurred before the correction and remains unaddressed. Failure to Comply with My Request for Information ( RFI ) : My Notice of Error and Request for Information ( delivered [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>[Redacted] ) requested : All [Redacted] [Redacted] codes used during forbearance, hardship review, trial modification, and subsequent months A detailed explanation of how reporting me delinquent during a trial plan complied with FCRA and CFPB guidance PenFeds internal process for evaluating compensation requests The name, title, and department of the individuals who conducted the investigation PenFed did not provide any of this information in their response. This is a violation of 12 C.F.R. 1024.36 ( d ). Failure to Fully Address the Notice of Error : PenFeds response did not address the actual impact of the error, as required under 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( e ). They acknowledged the error but did not address the consequences of the inaccurate reporting. Requested Resolution : I am requesting that the CFPB require PenFed to : 1. Provide a complete and compliant response to all outstanding RFI items 2. Provide a full explanation of how the inaccurate reporting occurred 3. Address the financial harm caused by the inaccurate reporting 4. Reevaluate my request for monetary compensation I have attached PenFeds written response, my original Notice of Error, and supporting documentation.

metadata.full_snippet: Subject : Dispute Claim - Missing Bill Pay [Redacted] [Redacted] In late [Redacted], we were invited to go on a [Redacted] trip with a group of friends. One person in the group made reservations at a [Redacted] and offered to pay for it upfront, with the understanding that we would reimburse him. In [Redacted], he sent a message confirming the lodging was set and that each person 's share was {$1500.00}, along with his mailing address. We all paid him around that time. I have been a Wells Fargo and [Redacted] user for decades ( originally [Redacted] [Redacted] before transitioning to [Redacted] when [Redacted] exited that business ). I entered the payee information as I would for any payment and scheduled a bill pay for [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Shortly after the [Redacted], I noticed the money had left my account and thought nothing more of it. While we were on vacation in [Redacted], [Redacted] ( the person who paid for the lodging ) asked me, " Hey, I never received your payment for the [Redacted]. '' I was surprised. I opened my phone app, searched his name, showed him the payment from [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], and sent him a screenshot. He said he would check with his bank. He called them, and the next day he told me he had provided them with the information but they had not received the payment. I then contacted Wells Fargo. They advised me to provide the recipient with the entry from my bank statement, which I did in the form of a screenshot. Wells Fargo also offered to initiate a claim/dispute, but I asked to wait and see if his bank could locate the payment first. This seemed like a simple matter to resolve. I spoke with [Redacted] a few days later ( after we had all returned home ). He said his bank was unable to locate the payment using the tracker from my statement, or any other means. I asked if he could accept [Redacted] or another payment method. He confirmed he had [Redacted] and provided the necessary information. I then sent him the money via [Redacted].
