metadata.full_snippet: Complaint Against Central Portfolio Control , Inc. I am filing this complaint regarding improper and potentially unlawful debt collection practices by Central Portfolio Control , Inc. On or about [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> I received an unsolicited text message from this company identifying itself as a debt collector. The message stated : " [Redacted] [Redacted], we will try calling you in the next several days. In the meantime, for possible discount or payment options on your account, please visit us online at www.PayCPC.com using AGENCY ID : [Redacted] or call [Redacted]. Text STOP to unsubscribe. '' This communication raises several serious concerns : The message attempts to induce payment or engagement without providing any of the disclosures required under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ), including the amount of the debt, the name of the original creditor, and notice of my right to dispute the debt. The company is attempting to collect on an alleged debt prior to providing any written validation or verification of the obligation. The use of text messaging as an initial contact method, combined with a link and agency ID, creates confusion and raises concerns about the legitimacy and accuracy of the alleged debt. As of the date of this complaint, I have not received any written notice or validation of this debt by mail. The communication appears designed to pressure immediate action ( payment or contact ) before the consumer has an opportunity to verify the debt. I dispute this alleged debt in its entirety. I have not been provided with sufficient information to determine whether this debt is valid, belongs to me, or is legally collectible. I request that Central Portfolio Control, Inc. be required to : Provide full validation of the alleged debt, including the original creditor, account details, and chain of assignment Cease all collection activity until proper validation is provided Refrain from reporting any information to credit reporting agencies until the debt is properly validated Confirm whether this debt has been reported or is intended to be reported to any credit bureau Additionally, I request that all future communications be conducted in writing only.

metadata.full_snippet: Re : FHB Servicing Errors and Violations ( False Balance on Closed and Paid Off HELOC ) This letter constitutes a formal Notice of Errors and Violations by FIRST HAWAIIAN BANK under 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 regarding the servicing, payoff, and subsequent handling of my HELOC Summary Borrower refinanced his home with [Redacted] [Redacted]. The existing HELOC with First Hawaiian Bank was Paid Off and Closed as part of the refinancing. First Hawaiian Bank ( FHB ) issues a Payoff Statement requiring {$200000.00} to pay off and close the HELOC. [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] wires {$200000.00} to FHB, ( matching the amount in FHBs Payoff Statement ) and Closed Escrow on the refinance. FHB provides written confirmation to Borrower that the HELOC was Paid-Off and Closed FHB Re-Opens the Paid-Off and Closed HELOC and applies an Unsupported, False Balance without providing any reason for its actions, without providing documentation, and without Notice to Borrower. Any alleged shortage was never disclosed by FHB. FHB reports inaccurate information to the credit bureaus based on the False Balance that it applied to the improperly Re-Opened HELOC FHB improperly charged interest to the Borrower for months based on the False Balance FHB improperly withdrew funds from Borrowers bank account to pay improper interest charges, without authorization of the account holder and without notice to account holder To date, FHB has failed to provide any documentation supporting its position, has failed to take any corrective action despite multiple requests and notification that its actions constitute a violation of the law and are causing financial harm to the Borrower 1. Payoff Statement and Escrow Closing On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], First Hawaiian Bank ( FHB ) issued a written HELOC Payoff Statement : indicating : TOTAL PAYOFF : {$200000.00}. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ( [Redacted] [Redacted] ) closed escrow on my refinance and wired {$200000.00} to FHB, exactly matching the amount demanded by FHB. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted] issued a written confirmation stating : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] wired {$200000.00} to FHB which was precisely the amount demanded and did so pursuant to and in reliance upon the Payoff Statement. My Borrowers Settlement Statement likewise reflects a Loan Payoff to First Hawaiian Bank in the amount of {$200000.00}. The HELOC Account History shows Principle Payments equaling the amount of the account balance owing prior to HELOC closure. Evidencing the loan was paid in full Any alleged shortage was never disclosed by FHB. To Date, no documentation in support of any alleged shortage has been provided by FHB. 2. FHB Provides Written Confirmation that the HELOC was Paid Off and Closed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] In response to my email requesting : Kindly confirm that the HELOC was Paid Off and Closed, two FHB employees confirmed in writing that the HELOC was Paid Off and Closed, as follows : [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] FHB Confirmation # 1 : From : [Redacted] [Redacted] ( [Redacted] ) I see it is showing as closed in our system. SCREENSHOT ATTACHED SHOWING {$0.00} BALANCE [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] FHB Confirmation # 2 : From : [Redacted] [Redacted] ( [Redacted] ) Your HELOC was paid off and closed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], the HELOC was no longer visible on my FHB online banking dashboard when I signed in to my online FHB account 3. FHB Re-Opened the CLOSED and PAID-OFF HELOC and Applied a False Balance to the Account Despite confirming, in writing, that the HELOC was PAID-OFF and CLOSED : On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], FHB Re-Opened the Closed and Paid-Off HELOC and Applied an Unsupported, False Balance to the Account Subsequent Account Details ( attached ) show : Total Outstanding False Balance : {$9000.00} Total Credit Line Improperly Reported : {$9000.00} Interest YTD : {$7500.00} ( as of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) The outstanding balance is not legitimate and exists solely because FHB, in violation of RESPA and FCRA, wrongfully applied an Undocumented , False Balance to a Closed and Paid Off HELOC 4. Wrongful Interest Charges Applied and Automatic Payments Drafted by FHB FHB improperly charged Interest on the Undocumented, False Balance FHB, without the Approval of or Notice to the Account Holder, initiated automatic withdrawals from my bank account to pay the wrongful interest charges on the False Balance Using FHBs own Account Details and transaction history : A. Wrongful Interest Interest YTD before payoff ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) : {$6500.00} Interest YTD after payoff ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) : {$7500.00} Wrongful Interest charged after payoff : {$1000.00} B. Wrongful Automatic Withdrawals FHB withdrew automatic payments to satisfy interest charges applied to the false balance, without Notice, Documentation, or Borrower Authorization : {$1000.00} in interest {$1100.00} in improperly drafted payments Total wrongful charges through [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : {$2200.00} These charges were taken after the loan was paid off and after FHB confirmed the account was closed. 5. FHB Reported Inaccurate Information to Credit Bureaus FHB Improperly Reported : a {$10000.00} balance on a closed and paid off HELOC Credit Line Suspended an active HELOC account This inaccurate reporting has harmed my credit profile and is currently impeding my ability to refinance. 6. Communications And Failed Resolution 6.1 Emails to FHB Requesting Correction Multiple attempts to resolve the issue by Borrower FHB ignored or failed to respond to Borrower No correction made despite documentation proving HELOC payoff and closure Calls not returned ; questions unanswered by FHB 6.2 Evidence of Non Response by FHB Employees who confirmed closure did not resolve the error No explanation provided for payoff reversal To date, FHB has provided no documentation supporting its actions In three separate emails spanning multiple months ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ; [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ; [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ), FHB claimed to be still investigating the matter. No findings were ever communicated, and no corrective action was taken. Despite repeated outreach and documentation, FHB did not correct the False Balance, stop wrongful charges or take any other corrective action 7. Harm and Potential Additional Damages FHBs errors have caused and are causing ongoing harm, including but not limited to : Wrongful withdrawals and wrongful interest charges Improper charges for interest, fees, and minimum payments on a loan that was paid off and closed ; Wrongful negative credit reporting. The appearance of an outstanding balance and adverse comments on Borrowers credit reports ; Ongoing Harm to Refinancing : I am currently in the process of applying for a refinance loan. FHBs Errors and Violations are causing continual and ongoing financial harm, including, without limitation, delaying underwriting, threatening my interest rate and loan eligibility, jeopardizing closing and interfereing with my ability to obtain a new refinance loan on optimal terms. If FHBs errors and/or its failure to promptly correct such errors results in any adverse impact to my pending refinance, including, but not limited to, rate increases, loan denial, or closing delays I will consider such harm to be a direct result of FHBs servicing errors and violations and its failure to resolve said issues in a timely manner. This shall serve as notice that I reserve all rights and remedies available under federal and state law. 8. Errors Asserted Under 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 I assert the following documented Servicing Errors and Violations by FHB : 1. Failure to Provide Required Written Notice of Significant Account Changes Regulation Z 12 C.F.R. 1026.9 ( c ) ( 1 ) ( i ) Requires written notice before a creditor makes a significant change to a home secured credit account. FHB Violations : Reopened the HELOC Added a {$10000.00} balance Reversed the payoff Resumed interest and withdrawals Reported the account as active No written notice was provided. This is a direct violation. 2. Failure to Provide Adverse Action Notice ECOA / Regulation B 12 C.F.R. 1002.9 Requires written notice when a creditor : Suspends a credit line Changes terms Reports adverse information FHB Violation : FHB reported the HELOC as active with Credit Line Suspended without issuing an adverse action notice. 3. Failure to Provide Notice Before Furnishing Negative Credit Information Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) 15 U.S.C. 1681s 2 ( a ) ( 7 ) Requires notice to the consumer before furnishing negative information to credit bureaus. FHB Violation : Reported the HELOC as active with derogatory status without notifying the borrower. 4. Failure to Provide Documentation Supporting Claimed Indebtedness RESPA 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( e ) Requires servicers to provide documentation supporting their position when a borrower disputes an account. FHB Violation : FHB has not produced any documentation supporting its claim that {$10000.00} is owed. 5. Unfair or Deceptive Acts or Practices ( UDAP ) HRS 480 2 Prohibits unfair or deceptive acts in commerce. FHB Violations : Reopening a paid off HELOC Adding an unsupported balance Failing to notify the borrower Failing to provide documentation Continuing to charge interest Reporting inaccurate information Each of these is independently unfair and deceptive. 6. Failure to Maintain Accurate Account Records RESPA 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( k ) ( 1 ) ( C ) Regulation X 12 C.F.R. 1024.38 ( a ) Servicers must maintain accurate and complete account information. FHB Violation : Created an erroneous balance of {$10000.00} after payoff. 7. Wrongful Assessment of Fees and Interest Regulation X 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( b ) ( 5 ) Prohibits charging fees or interest not permitted by the loan. FHB Violation : Charged {$2200.00} in interest and withdrawals after the loan was paid off. 8. Failure to Apply Payoff Properly Regulation Z 12 C.F.R. 1026.36 ( c ) ( 3 ) Requires lenders to accept a payoff statement amount as full satisfaction of the loan once the borrower tenders that amount. Violation : FHB reversed the payoff after confirming the loan was paid in full. 9. Failure to Correct Servicing Errors Regulation X 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( b ) ( 1 ), ( b ) ( 3 ), ( b ) ( 5 ), ( b ) ( 11 ) Defines servicing errors including : Failure to apply payments correctly Imposing charges not permitted by the loan Providing inaccurate information Failing to respond to borrower inquiries Violation : FHBs payoff reversal and post payoff charges fall squarely within these categories. 10. Failure to Comply with Hawaii Mortgage Servicer Requirements HRS 454F 4 Requires servicers to : Apply payments accurately Maintain truthful records Conduct servicing in a fair and honest manner Violation : FHBs reversal of a valid payoff and creation of an erroneous balance violates these duties. 11. Failure to Provide Notice of HELOC Suspension or Adverse Action Regulation B ( ECOA ) 12 C.F.R. 1002.9 Requires written notice when a creditor takes adverse action on a credit line. Violation : FHB reported Credit Line Suspended without issuing an adverse action notice. 12. Improper Withdrawal of Funds Without Authorization or Notice Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) 15 U.S.C. 1693e ( a ) requires that electronic fund transfers be authorized in writing by the account holder and that the consumer receive notice of such transactions. Regulation X 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( b ) ( 6 ) and ( b ) ( 10 ) defines servicing errors including failure to properly apply payments and imposing charges not permitted by the loan agreement. Consumer Financial Protection Act ( UDAAP ) 12 U.S.C. 5531 & 5536 prohibits unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices in connection with consumer financial products. Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) Regulation Z 1026.9 ( c ) requires written notice of any new charges or changes in account terms. FHB Violations : Initiated unauthorized electronic withdrawals from borrowers account to pay interest on a false balance. Failed to obtain account holder written authorization or provide notice of withdrawals. Assessed interest on a non existent debt after payoff confirmation. Misrepresented the existence of a valid balance and treated it as collectible debt. Failed to correct the error despite borrowers repeated notifications. Each withdrawal constitutes an unauthorized electronic fund transfer and a servicing error under 12C.F.R.1024.35 ( b ) ( 6 ) and ( b ) ( 10 ), as well as violations of EFTA, TILA , and UDAAP. 11. Preservation of Rights, Notice of Non-Waiver This Notice of Errors and Violations is submitted pursuant to 12 C.F.R. 1024.35. Please treat it as such and respond within the timeframes required by law. Nothing in this letter should be construed as a waiver of any rights, claims, or remedies I may have against FHB, and I expressly reserve all rights and remedies under applicable federal and state law. 12. Attachments and Supporting Documentation Attached, please find the following documents : 1.1 FHB Payoff Statement ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) Payoff amount demanded : {$200000.00} Issued by FHB Consumer Credit Service Center. 1.2 Borrowers Settlement Statement ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) Shows {$200000.00} wired to FHB by [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. Confirms payoff was funded exactly as demanded. [Redacted] Old [Redacted] Title Payoff Letter ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) [Redacted] Wire Confirmation ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) Confirms [Redacted] [Redacted] wired the exact payoff amount demanded. [Redacted] Old [Redacted] Title Payoff Confirmation Letter ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) Confirms [Redacted] [Redacted] wired the exact payoff amount demanded. States any alleged shortage was not disclosed by FHB. 1.6 FHB CONFIRMATIONS OF PAYOFF & CLOSURE 1 Email from FHB Loan Officer ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) Your HELOC was paid off and closed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. 2 Email from FHB Personal Banking Officer ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) I do see it is showing as closed in our system. These emails confirm the loan was closed in FHBs system. 1.7 FHB ACCOUNT HISTORY SHOWING PAYOFF REVERSAL Shows Principle Payments demonstating HELOC Paid in Full [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] Payment {$82000.00} [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] Payment {$9000.00} [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] Payment {$200000.00} Shows the following critical entries : [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] Regular Payoff + {$200000.00} [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] Reversal {$200000.00} 1.8 FHB [Redacted] Account Balance Shows an Account Balance equal to the Payoff Statement 1.9 Email from Refinancing Lender ( [Redacted] [Redacted] ) Shows financial harm caused by FHB improper credit reporting, Re-Opening the Closed and Paid HELOC and Application of a False Balance on reopened HELOC

Despite this, foreclosure-related activity appears to be continuing, as reflected by the assessment of approximately {$3600.00} in foreclosure attorney fees, additional title charges, and {$2700.00} in foreclosure/closure attorney fees. We have not received any written confirmation that foreclosure activity has been suspended. The continued advancement of foreclosure-related actions and fees during an active loss mitigation review raises serious concerns regarding improper dual tracking and non-compliance with servicing obligations under RESPA ( Regulation X ). Additionally, AmeriHome failed to disclose that a foreclosure sale date had been set on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. The sale date was subsequently moved forward and advertised after we were advised our file was in underwriting. As a result, we have experienced harm, including unsolicited contact from attorneys and real estate agents, as well as individuals coming onto our property and posting materials without permission. AmeriHome has also failed to produce previously requested call recordings and servicing notes from [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] to present. We formally request : ( 1 ) immediate written confirmation that foreclosure activity has been suspended, ( 2 ) a complete and itemized accounting of all foreclosure-related fees ( including dates incurred and whether actual or estimated ), ( 3 ) reversal and removal of any foreclosure-related fees improperly assessed during the active loss mitigation review period, and ( 4 ) full production of all requested servicing records. Absent timely resolution, we will pursue all available regulatory remedies.

metadata.full_snippet: In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I used Affirm ( [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ) to finance a purchase from [Redacted] ( Order # [Redacted] ). The loan was processed on or around [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. The order was cancelled immediately after placement, and the merchant explicitly acknowledged the cancellation. The merchant confirmed in writing that a refund would be processed within approximately 21 days. The order was never fulfilled or shipped, and remains in an unfulfilled status. Based on the merchants confirmation, I reasonably believed the matter was resolved and that the refund would be processed and the loan would be closed. No goods or services were ever delivered, and I received no benefit from this transaction. However, Affirm continued to treat the loan as valid. Over time, the account became delinquent, was charged off, and was ultimately sent to a collections agency. I contacted Affirm to dispute the loan and provided documentation showing : The order was cancelled The merchant acknowledged cancellation and refund The order was never fulfilled or delivered Affirm declined to reopen the dispute, citing a 120-day dispute window, without addressing the fact that no goods or services were ever delivered. Additionally, the merchant has recently stated that a chargeback has already been filed for this transaction, while Affirm maintains that no refund has been received. This creates a conflicting situation between the merchant and Affirm regarding the financial settlement, which is outside of my control. As a consumer, I should not be held responsible for a loan tied to a transaction that was cancelled and never completed. This is not a delayed refund issue, but a case of non-fulfillment, where the underlying transaction did not occur. Despite this, I am being asked to pay for a product I never received, and this has resulted in collection activity and potential damage to my credit. I am requesting reversal of the loan, withdrawal of the account from collections, and correction of any credit reporting.

metadata.full_snippet: In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I entered into a lease agreement with Acima Credit for furniture purchased at [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], located in [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], CA. The approval amount was {$3400.00}. When the furniture store attempted delivery, the delivery personnel refused to carry the couch up the stairs to my unit. I verbally cancelled the order on the spot, the delivery team left with the couch, and I followed up by calling the store directly to confirm the cancellation. I never received or kept any merchandise. Despite the cancellation, Acima continued to charge my account. I made payments totaling at least {$1200.00} ( a {$50.00} payment on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and a {$1200.00} payment on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) before realizing the store had never reported the cancellation to Acima. I contacted Acima customer service multiple times over the following months. Each time, I was told they would contact the store to verify the cancellation and that I should not worry. I was also told to disregard automated default notices because the account could not be closed until a store representative confirmed the return something Acima was responsible for pursuing, not me. At some point, I discovered that [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] had permanently closed, making it impossible for anyone to obtain store-side verification. I informed Acima of this. Despite this, they continued to send collection notices and failed to resolve or close the account. This cycle continued for approximately a year and a half. To be clear : I purchased the same furniture the following week from a different retailer, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], using my own funds confirming I had no use for or possession of the originally leased item. Now, in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] nearly five years later I am receiving urgent text messages from a third-party collector called [Redacted] ( [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ) referencing a pending case related to this same Acima lease. I also received a settlement offer from Acima in [Redacted] for {$1500.00}, citing {$8300.00} in remaining payments an account that should have been closed years ago. I am requesting that the CFPB investigate Acima 's failure to : [Redacted]. Properly verify and process a merchandise return/cancellation when the retail partner closed. [Redacted]. Close an account for merchandise that was never received. [Redacted]. Cease collection activity on a disputed account. [Redacted]. Refund payments made for merchandise I never received. I am seeking a full account closure, a refund of all payments made, removal of any negative credit reporting related to this account, and confirmation that all collection activity has ceased.

metadata.snippet: Complainant, a cardholder in good standing on the Capital One [Redacted] [Redacted] account, submits this formal complaint concerning Capital Ones unfair, deceptive, and procedurally defective administration of the advertised {$300.00} annual Capital One [Redacted] credit. metadata.full_snippet: Complainant, a cardholder in good standing on the Capital One [Redacted] [Redacted] account, submits this formal complaint concerning Capital Ones unfair, deceptive, and procedurally defective administration of the advertised {$300.00} annual Capital One [Redacted] credit. The credit expired on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] without any notice whatsoever. Complainant first contacted Capital One customer service on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ( only [Redacted] days later ) seeking relief. The banks rigid refusal to provide any remedy, combined with systemic design flaws, has caused direct financial harm and substantial non-economic harm ( mental anguish, frustration, and significant time wasted on multiple calls ). Complainant is not done with this matterthe cumulative impact far exceeds the face value of the forfeited credit. [Redacted]. Deceptive Restriction of the Travel Credit to the Primary Cardholder Only Engineered Denial of Benefit to Authorized Users and [Redacted] [Redacted] Capital Ones policy that the {$300.00} annual travel credit applies only when the primary cardholder books ( and never when an authorized user books ) is a deceptive practice designed to deny the benefit in the very scenarios most consumers would use it. As first-time cardholders, Complainant and his authorized user spouse reasonably believed the credit would apply to family travel booked through the Capital One [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] Complainants spouse booked the qualifying travel for [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] through [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ( total spend approximately {$3000.00} ) using the authorized-user card. The primary cardholder was included on the itinerary and ultimately paid the balance due. Despite actual expenditure through Capital Ones own portal and multiple calls to the travel desk ( including inquiries about miles ), the credit was never applied. This is not a neutral policyit is a deliberate structural barrier. Capital One markets the {$300.00} credit as a core advertised benefit of the [Redacted] [Redacted] card, yet its internal rules render the credit unavailable whenever an authorized user ( or family member ) handles the booking. The portal terms and conditions contain no clear, conspicuous warning at the point of booking that authorized-user transactions are ineligible. This omission is materially deceptive : consumers are induced to choose Capital One [Redacted] expecting the credit, only to have it withheld on technical grounds that Capital One never prominently discloses. [Redacted]. Deliberate and Engineered Failure to Provide Any Notification of Impending Expiration Systemic Forfeiture Mechanism Capital One furnished [Redacted] notificationby email, physical mail, mobile push alert, text, or any other channelthat the {$300.00} credit would expire on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. When this omission was raised on the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] call, the Capital One [Redacted] representative expressly admitted that the bank dont send notifications and that such alerts are not part of the terms and conditions. The official terms require manual monitoring of the My travel credits and offers View activity page. This is not oversight ; it is corporate policy. Capital One possesses ( and routinely uses ) robust notification systems for statements, fraud alerts, payments, and other events, yet deliberately withholds any reminder for the single highest-value, time-sensitive benefit tied to the {$390.00} annual fee. This engineered forfeiture maximizes the number of unused credits, enriching Capital One at consumers expense. This conduct has caused Complainant significant anguish, mental distress, [Redacted], and a substantial expenditure of time across multiple calls to the travel desk and customer service. As first-time users relying on the advertised benefit, the opaque policies forced repeated, unproductive follow-ups that would have been entirely unnecessary had Capital One implemented basic notifications or clearer disclosures. The mental pressure and time wasted are worth materially more than the {$300.00} credit itself. [Redacted]. One-Sided Call-Recording Policy and Unauthorized Access of Authorized-User Records Fundamental Fairness and Privacy Violations Capital One records all customer calls for its own protection yet explicitly prohibits customers from recording the same conversations, citing policy. The representative in this matter insisted the customer could not record while simultaneously accessing and discussing prior call transcripts and booking details tied to the authorized user spouse without ever requesting or obtaining verbal authorization from the primary cardholder. The agent later conceded she pulled the records simply because the primary cardholder had asked to review previous conversations. This creates a profound and unfair imbalance : the bank equips itself with complete documentation while denying the consumer the identical right to document interactions for dispute resolution or regulatory complaints. [Redacted]. Refusal to Provide Any Case ID, Tracking Number, or Formal Record of the Complaint Additional Deceptive Barrier to Escalation During the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] call, the representative explicitly stated that Capital One [Redacted] doesnt work through cases, provides no case ID or tracking number for the conversation, and has no formal process to reference or escalate the complaint. The agent further advised the customer to simply write down the date and time of the call. This is a deliberate policy that leaves consumers without any verifiable record or reference number with which to follow up, escalate, or prove the content of the interaction. [Redacted]. Absolute Prohibition on Supervisory Override or Manual Relief Rigid No Exceptions Policy That Locks in Forfeitures Capital One representatives repeatedly asserted that there is no manual process for any supervisor or higher-level agent to override policy and reinstate or apply the expired {$300.00} travel crediteven when the expiration was discovered and reported within [Redacted] days, the travel had already occurred through Capital Ones own portal, and the cardholders acted in good faith. Agents stated they could not go against policy and had no discretion whatsoever to provide relief. This blanket prohibition on supervisory discretion is itself potentially deceptive and creates an impenetrable procedural wall that prevents any meaningful customer-service resolution. [Redacted]. Misrepresentation Regarding the Absence of a Retention Department Further Barrier to Resolution and Potential Deception When Complainant specifically asked to be transferred to a retention department ( or any department with authority to provide goodwill or escalation ), the representative explicitly stated that Capital One [Redacted] does not have a retention department and that no such department exists for this purpose. The agent offered only a transfer to the general credit card line. This statement is potentially deceptive or materially misleading. By denying the very existence of a retention pathway, Capital One creates yet another artificial barrier that discourages legitimate escalation. Account verification : my [Redacted] [Redacted] account ; authorized user spouse ( on file ). Complainant is prepared to furnish full call recordings/transcripts, booking confirmations for [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], portal screenshots showing the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] expiration, and any other supporting materials. This matter involves clear, quantifiable consumer injury and non-economic harm and systemic practices that have harmed ( and continue to harm ) a significant number of cardholders. Prompt regulatory intervention and remedial action are warranted.

I am very concerned that the hardship review, documentation, and correction of this reporting error will not be transferred properly, which may cause additional issues or further inaccurate reporting. Given the ongoing inconsistencies and misinformation I have received, I am requesting CFPB oversight to ensure the transition does not result in more harm. I am also concerned that the ongoing lack of communication and inconsistent information from Onity Mortgage may lead to additional errors that could place me at risk of foreclosure. As a [Redacted] parent with a [Redacted] child, I do not have alternative housing options, and any further mistakes could cause serious harm to my familys stability. metadata.full_snippet: I am filing a complaint regarding inaccurate and misleading credit reporting by SoFi related to my private student loan ( Loan # [Redacted] ). SoFi is currently reporting my account as delinquent. However, this reporting fails to account for critical facts and is therefore misleading under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). At the end of 2025, my loan was transferred to SoFi for servicing. Following this transfer : My SoFi online account did not display any active student loan or account information I did not have access to statements, billing details, or payment instructions When I contacted SoFi through their support chat, I was explicitly told that I did not have any open student loans with SoFi I relied on this information in good faith. Based on the absence of any visible loan and the confirmation from SoFis own support channel, I reasonably believed that my loan had been transferred to another servicer. I continued making payments to another servicer during this time. At no point did I intend to avoid repayment of my loan. I made consistent, good-faith efforts to pay what I believed was the correct servicer. Only later did I receive notice that SoFi considered the account delinquent and had reported negative information to the credit bureaus. I submitted a formal dispute to SoFi, including evidence of : Their system failing to display my loan A chat transcript where I was told I had no loan with SoFi SoFi responded by stating that all reporting is valid and accurate, but did not address or acknowledge this evidence in their investigation. Under the FCRA, furnishers are required to conduct a reasonable investigation and must not report information that is incomplete or misleading. Reporting this account as delinquentwithout accounting for the fact that SoFis own system and representatives indicated no loan existedcreates a materially misleading impression. SoFi failed to : Provide accurate account visibility after the servicing transfer Provide correct information through its customer support channel Conduct a reasonable investigation that considers the evidence I submitted As a result, negative credit reporting has been applied in a situation that was directly caused by SoFis own system and communication failures. Desired Resolution : Removal of all negative credit reporting associated with this account Correction of my account status to reflect that the delinquency resulted from servicer error and misinformation Confirmation that SoFi has conducted a reasonable investigation that includes review of my submitted evidence I am willing to resolve the outstanding balance ; however, I am disputing the accuracy and fairness of the credit reporting.

metadata.full_snippet: My wife, [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted], and I are residents of [Redacted] [Redacted], Arizona. I am writing to bring a story to your attention that I believe is of significant public interest both as a consumer fraud warning and as an account of a major financial institution refusing to cooperate with law enforcement. On Saturday, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, my wife received a text message appearing to be from Wells Fargo, asking if she had authorized a {$2100.00} transfer from her credit card to her checking account. She had not. She immediately drove to our local Wells Fargo branch on [Redacted] [Redacted] in [Redacted] [Redacted] to report the unauthorized transaction. Before she could speak with anyone inside, she received a phone call from someone claiming to be Wells Fargo 's fraud control department. The caller, speaking with an American accent and with apparent authority, told her not to speak with the branch staff warning that a bank employee was involved in the fraud. He instructed her to withdraw our entire savings of {$16000.00} in cash and redeposit it at a different Wells Fargo ATM on [Redacted] [Redacted] in [Redacted] [Redacted], which was closed that Saturday. Following these instructions, believing she was protecting our money, [Redacted] [Redacted] withdrew {$16000.00} [Redacted] hundred-dollar bills and deposited the cash at that ATM. She received no receipt. The money was diverted to an unknown account and has not been recovered. This is our entire life savings. Here is what makes this story especially troubling : Wells Fargo has an ATM that accepted a {$16000.00} cash deposit and apparently diverted it to a fraudulent account. The bank should have video footage of my wife at that ATM, and a transaction record showing exactly where those funds went. Wells Fargo initially denied the existence of both. However, they finally released the photos, to the [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], of [Redacted] [Redacted] making the deposit but has not released the data showing the account that was credited. We reported the crime immediately to the [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ( [Redacted] [Redacted]. [Redacted] ). Deputies were dispatched and went directly to the bank. Wells Fargo refused to provide transaction information to law enforcement. The Sheriff 's Office obtained a subpoena. As of now, the Sheriff 's Office has informed us that Wells Fargo has still not released the information. Detective [Redacted] [Redacted], ( [Redacted] ) [Redacted], is working the case but so far has only found the photos. He does not answer our calls but eventually returns them but shows no progress after [Redacted] months. We have met with branch officers multiple times. Nothing has been done. We have contacted [Redacted] attorneys, each of whom told us the case was not financially worth pursuing for them despite the severity of our loss. We are seniors. This money represented our security. We are not asking for sympathy we are asking for accountability. I believe this story raises serious questions that deserve public scrutiny : How did a bank ATM accept and redirect {$16000.00} in cash with no traceable record? Why has Wells Fargo denied the existence of ATM transaction records? Why has a major financial institution failed to comply with a law enforcement subpoena? How many other customers have been victimized by this same scam at Wells Fargo ATMs? I am available to speak at any time. Thank you for your time and for the work you do holding powerful institutions accountable. Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted] and [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], Arizona ( [Redacted] ) [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]

This practice increased the total interest paid over the life of the loan. I currently have a foreclosure sale scheduled for [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. metadata.full_snippet: Complaint Against TD Bank Secured Credit Card, Missing Funds, Improper Fees, and Credit Reporting Issues In [Redacted], I opened a secured credit card account with TD Bank and provided a {$500.00} security deposit. The purpose of this account was to build my credit while preparing to purchase a home. In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I contacted TD Bank to close this account. During that conversation, the representative informed me that my account had a balance of approximately {$20.00} and that my original {$500.00} security deposit would be returned to me, minus the balance, in the form of a check for {$480.00} within 1015 business days. I relied on this information. I did not receive the check. Approximately one month later, I contacted TD Bank again. During this call, the representative was unable to locate my account details and escalated the matter to a supervisor. The supervisor informed me that : [Redacted]. My secured credit card had been converted into an unsecured credit card without my knowledge or clear notification. [Redacted]. My {$500.00} security deposit had allegedly been placed into a dormant account and subsequently turned over to the state as unclaimed property. [Redacted]. My account now had an outstanding balance of {$40.00}, consisting of {$20.00} past due and a {$20.00} late fee. This information directly contradicted what I had been told during my prior call. I was never notified that my account had been converted from secured to unsecured, nor was I notified that my funds were at risk of being classified as dormant or turned over to the state. Despite disputing these issues and requesting an investigation, TD Bank continued to assess additional fees. I later received a bill for {$80.00}, which included additional fees on the alleged past-due balance. This compounding of fees appears excessive and unjustified, particularly given that I had previously been told no payment was due. To avoid further damage, I paid the {$80.00} under protest to close the account. However, TD Bank reported late payments to the credit bureaus, which caused my credit score to drop significantly ( from approximately [Redacted] to [Redacted] ). I have never had a history of late payments prior to this incident. Additionally, I independently searched my states unclaimed property database and was unable to locate any record of my {$500.00} deposit, raising further concerns about the accuracy of TD Banks statements regarding the disposition of my funds. I am requesting the following resolution : [Redacted]. A full investigation into the status and location of my original {$500.00} security deposit. [Redacted]. Immediate reimbursement of any improperly assessed fees. [Redacted]. Correction and removal of any inaccurate negative reporting related to this account from all credit reporting agencies. [Redacted]. Written clarification as to why I was provided conflicting and inaccurate information by TD Bank representatives. [Redacted]. Documentation supporting the claim that my funds were transferred to the state, including the date and jurisdiction of such transfer. This situation has caused financial harm, unnecessary stress, and damage to my credit due to inaccurate and inconsistent information provided by TD Bank. I am seeking a fair resolution and accountability. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint regarding the mishandling of my vehicle payoff by Mazda Financial Services [Redacted] Toyota Motor Credit Corporation. I traded in my vehicle on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. As part of the trade-in, the dealership was responsible for paying off the remaining balance on my auto loan. The dealership initially issued the payoff check to Toyota Financial / Toyota Motor Credit Corporation because Toyota Financial was listed as the lienholder on the Texas DMV records, and because Toyota Financial has a servicing/partnership relationship with Mazda Financial Services [Redacted] After that first payoff check was sent, Mazda Financial Services informed me that the check needed to be issued directly to Mazda Financial Services, not Toyota Financial / TMCC. Based on that instruction, the dealership voided the first check and reissued a second payoff check at the end of [Redacted], payable as instructed. However, the situation was then mishandled by Toyota Financial / Mazda Financial Services. Toyota Financial apparently forwarded the first check to Mazda Financial Services, and Mazda Financial Services cashed or attempted to process that check. Because the dealership had already placed a stop payment on that first check based on Mazda Financials own instruction, Mazda Financial could not apply the funds. Instead of contacting the dealership or me to resolve the issue, Mazda Financial Services returned the second valid dealer-sent payoff check without consulting either party. As a result, my account still shows an outstanding balance even though the dealership already sent the payoff and I followed the instructions given by Mazda Financial Services. I did nothing wrong in this process. The delay and confusion were caused by Mazda Financial Services / Toyota Financials inconsistent instructions and improper handling of the payoff checks. I am now receiving repeated debt collection calls regarding a balance that should have been resolved through the dealer payoff. I am also concerned that I may be charged additional interest, fees, late charges, or face negative credit reporting because of Mazda Financial Services error and delay. I am requesting that Mazda Financial Services immediately correct my account, apply the proper payoff as of the original trade-in/payoff date, waive any interest, late fees, collection activity, or other charges caused by this issue, stop all collection calls, and ensure that no negative information is reported to the credit bureaus. If any negative credit reporting has already occurred, I request that it be removed immediately. I also request a written explanation of what happened, why the second valid payoff check was returned without contacting the dealership or me, and written confirmation that my account has been corrected and closed with no remaining balance caused by this mishandling.

metadata.full_snippet: This notice will serve as a Qualified Written Request and complaint of my experience with the loan origination practices of Pulte Mortgage. I am filing this complaint against Pulte Mortgage for repeated failures in communication, underwriting practices, and loan processing practices during my FHA mortgage application that caused substantial financial harm. [Redacted]. Direct Financial Harm and UDAAP Complaint Lack of Communication Resulting in Direct Financial Harm. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026, [Redacted] [Redacted] and [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ( hereafter known as the Buyers ) entered into a purchase agreement contract for a property purchase amount of {$430000.00} with Pulte Mortgage ( hereafter known as Sellers ) for a new construction townhome, subject property located at : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], FL [Redacted] It was determined during the loan application and credit review process that the borrowers would add a third-party to the title only with vested interest, identified as [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] The Seller agreed to the change and submitted a formal Change Order to the purchase contract, including [Redacted] [Redacted] on title but not as a guarantor to the mortgage. During the loan application, pre-approval, and [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], the loan closing date was originally estimated to be on or around [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026, the Seller advanced the closing date to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026 at [Redacted] [Redacted] and this date was confirmed by the title company ( [Redacted] [Redacted] ) by way of email and phone calls to both Buyers. In reliance on that confirmation, [Redacted] [Redacted] arranged international travel from [Redacted], [Redacted], and [Redacted] [Redacted] arranged travel from California, returning to Florida and accommodating the closing date. The Seller failed to correctly submit title vesting information in the Change Order to the purchase contract, now requiring the addition of [Redacted] [Redacted] per Florida law as spouse to [Redacted] [Redacted]. [Redacted] [Redacted] advised that [Redacted] [Redacted] would need to be vested on title and be present for the closing appointment, resulting in last minute additional travel for [Redacted] to Florida, also from [Redacted], [Redacted]. Travel costs incurred : [Redacted] [Redacted] : {$1100.00} ( initial ticket purchased for [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026 ) [Redacted] [Redacted] : {$1100.00} ( changed to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026 for closing ) [Redacted] [Redacted] : {$410.00} ( Purchased [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026, due to closing reschedule ) [Redacted] [Redacted] : {$1200.00} ( purchase ticket for [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026 ) [Redacted] [Redacted] : {$230.00} ( Purchased [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026, due to closing reschedule ) [Redacted] [Redacted] : {$160.00} ( return to Florida from California, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026 ) Total travel : [Redacted] On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026, all parties arrived at [Redacted] [Redacted] by [Redacted] [Redacted] as scheduled and were notified that the loan was not ready to fund and closing had never been scheduled. While at the title company, Pulte Mortgage Loan Processor [Redacted] [Redacted] called [Redacted] [Redacted] to apologize for the miscommunication and, for the first time, to review pending conditions over the phone, to determine how to satisfy each. Simultaneously, Loan Officer [Redacted] [Redacted] was attempting to call [Redacted] [Redacted] and [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], successful in his attempt with [Redacted], having previously left a voice message with [Redacted], also apologizing for the miscommunication of not reaching out regarding the lack of a closing date but offering no resolution to the circumstance. Clearing the pending conditions required no additional documentation from the Borrowers. Within three ( 3 ) days, all conditions were cleared and the closing was rescheduled for [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026. This demonstrates that the Borrowers had submitted all required documents timely during loan application and credit approval review, but the Seller neglected to review, address, or clear the conditions in advance, or to properly communicate with the Buyers of any open issues, or the inability to schedule a proper closing date, thereby causing the entire failure and direct financial harm, for which no remedy was provided or offered. Unnecessary Financial Risk to Borrower In addition, Pulte Mortgage violated the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA, 12 U.S.C. 2601 et seq. ) and Regulation X by requiring the borrowers to pay cash-to-close amounts or related fees directly to [Redacted] [Redacted] prior to final loan approval and before the loan was ready to close. This demand to pay closing costs to [Redacted] [Redacted] was requested despite the loan not being fully underwritten, conditions not yet cleared, and approval letter not received exposing borrowers to unnecessary financial risk and out-of-pocket expenditures on a transaction that Pulte Mortgage itself could not complete. RESPA and its implementing regulations are intended to protect consumers by ensuring transparency, proper timing of settlement cost disclosures, and prevention of abusive or premature collection of settlement-related charges in federally related mortgage loans. Requiring advance payment to a third-party settlement provider ( [Redacted] [Redacted] ) before the Pulte Mortgage had approved the loan and cleared all conditions constitutes an unfair and improper practice that contributed to the overall financial harm, including the wasted travel, living expenses, lost wages, and additional per diem interest detailed elsewhere in this complaint. The cash-to-close was requested by [Redacted] [Redacted] and paid by the Borrowers at [Redacted] [Redacted] on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026. Approval of the loan and letter were not provided until [Redacted] [Redacted] on the same day. Prior to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026 despite complete documentation being provided at application, there was no meaningful communication or updates from Loan Processor [Redacted] [Redacted] or Loan Officer [Redacted] [Redacted]. Responsiveness only began on the failed closing day in reaction to the miscommunication. The delay from [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] to [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026 caused additional financial harm to the Buyers through additional per diem interest accrued to close the loan and travel costs. [Redacted] Unfair Underwriting Conditions on [Redacted] [Redacted] ( W-2 Employee ) : [Redacted] [Redacted] provided full dissolution agreements for [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ( releasing him from all financial impact and tax liabilities ), plus two years of personal tax returns and K-1s. Per HUD Handbook 4000.1, he qualifies solely as a W-2 wage earner. Yet, Seller required and demanded full business tax filings, including all schedules, business income and/or Profit & Loss statements, and company tax transcripts at the borrowers expense even though lenders are responsible for ordering IRS transcripts via Form 4506-C. Financial Harm : Travel costs : [Redacted] Lost wages for self-employed [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ) : {$3300.00} ( 10 days at $ [Redacted] ) Groceries for 2 adults in [Redacted] for 10 days : {$200.00} ( based on 2026 averages of ~ {$560.00} $ [Redacted] for a couple, adjusted for Florida/[Redacted] costs ) Additional per diem interest charged due to the lender-caused delay Total minimum harm : Estimated {$7700.00} plus unquantified lodging/transportation costs These acts constitute unfair, deceptive, or abusive practices under UDAAP and violate responsible mortgage servicing/origination standards. What I want Pulte Mortgage to do : Refund all additional per diem interest and reimburse all documented harms ( minimum {$7700.00} ). Provide a full explanation and apology for improper underwriting conditions to qualify [Redacted] [Redacted] as a [Redacted] employee despite already-submitted documents. Provide a full timeline and explanation of the communication and condition-clearing failures, with followup of feedback and training for Processor and Loan Officer. Copies of all internal notes showing when conditions were actually reviewed and by whom. A complete explanation of why pending conditions were not reviewed or clarified until the day of closing while borrowers were at the title company.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint against Wells Fargo regarding unauthorized debit card transactions totaling {$4600.00}. On or around [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026, I discovered multiple transactions that I did not make or authorize. I reported this immediately to Wells Fargo and clearly stated that these charges were unauthorized. Since then, I have contacted the bank multiple times, including speaking with representatives, visiting a branch in person, and escalating to supervisors. At the time these transactions occurred, my wallet was missing, which included my debit card and identification. Additionally, [Redacted] of my [Redacted] devices, which had my card information saved through [Redacted] [Redacted], could not be located. I did not have access to all of my devices during this time. Despite providing this information, Wells Fargo has denied my claim twice, stating that the transactions appear authorized. I have consistently stated that I did not authorize any of these transactions, regardless of what device or location may be shown in their system. I also contacted my local police department regarding this situation and was advised to proceed directly through my bank for handling unauthorized transactions. I have followed that guidance and fully cooperated with Wells Fargos process. I have also opened a case with [Redacted] to review device and account activity related to these transactions. These charges are not consistent with my normal spending behavior, and I was not alerted to any suspicious activity. This raises serious concerns about Wells Fargos fraud detection and how my claim has been handled. This situation has now caused immediate financial hardship. I do not have access to the majority of my funds, and I have essential bills, including rent, that are due immediately. I am requesting that Wells Fargo : 1. Immediately provide provisional credit for the full disputed amount 2. Conduct a proper reinvestigation of these transactions as unauthorized under Regulation E 3. Provide a clear explanation for why my claim was denied despite my repeated statements 4. Expedite resolution due to financial hardship This matter is urgent and requires immediate attention.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing a complaint against Beyond Finance regarding their mishandling of my account and failure to properly manage their role as my alleged representative. While I previously enrolled in their debt management program, I later experienced financial hardship and ceased participation. Despite this, Beyond Finance never provided clear written notice that my account was no longer active or that they were no longer acting on my behalf. [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted], a debt collection law firm, later claimed they were communicating with Beyond Finance as my authorized representative regarding alleged debts. However, Beyond Finance never notified me of these communications, never forwarded any correspondence, and never took any action to protect my interests. As a result, I was completely unaware of collection activity and was later served with a lawsuit. Even after I contacted Beyond Finance following the lawsuit, they only then sent a power of attorney revocation to [Redacted], confirming that they had allowed themselves to be treated as my representative without actively managing or terminating that role. Their failure to communicate, act, or properly revoke authority created confusion, allowed third parties to bypass me directly, and contributed to legal action being filed against me without my knowledge. I believe Beyond Finance failed in their duty to properly manage my account, failed to notify me of critical developments, and failed to timely revoke any authority that allowed third parties to treat them as my representative. I am requesting a full investigation into their practices and appropriate corrective action.

metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], at around [Redacted] PM I had received [Redacted] notifications stating that there were [Redacted] purchases of {$150.00} at a merchant that I had never heard of before ( merchant name is " [Redacted] '' ). Someone had used by debit card information, as well as my email address to make purchases. I know they used my email address because I am the one who received the receipts from the purchase ( I was also signed up for that company 's marketing emails which I never consented to ). This was not me making these purchases. I did not authorize these purchases. I was home when those two orders went through, so I called U.S. Bank immediately via the number in the back of my debit card to inform them this was not me. By that time, I had already locked my debit card through the U.S. Bank app. As I was on the phone, I remember telling the lady that I kept getting more notifications of purchases trying to go through. They were declining as the card was already locked, but someone was out there still trying to use my debit card. The thing is, my debit card was right in front of me while the fraudster was attempting to use it, so I am not sure as to how the fraudster got my information ( perhaps a data breach? ). She told me she was going to cancel my current debit card and send me a new one. She also told me the bank was going to give me a {$300.00} credit. I thanked her for it and was going to let the bank 's fraud department handle it. I did attempt to call the merchant the later same day but was unsure how to reach a person, and I did not yet inform the bank of the two emails I had received as I was being told the bank would launch an investigation. As of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I had already received the provisional credit, and was content with how things were going. 8 days ago on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I had received another letter from the bank that based off their investigation, I " received benefit from the transactions '' by " receiving services and/or merchandise from the merchant ( s ) ''. I would like to state once again these transactions were not made by me, authorized by me, and I did not receive anything from the transactions. They state they will remove my {$300.00} provisional credit on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. I called the bank once again and told them this was still not me making those purchases. The lady on the phone told me that the merchant had verified the information used to make the purchase, and the information matched up with mine. Therefore, they suspected I was the one who made the purchase. This was still not me making those purchases or authorizing them, so I told her that someone must have stolen my information then. She told me the fraud department could not do anything else, and to contact the merchant. I told her thank you for your help and I would speak with law enforcement. I haven't spoken with law enforcement yet, but on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] at [Redacted] while I was in class, for some reason I had received the same email yet again from when the purchase went through on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ( I assume time zone is different ). This reminded me to speak with the merchant, which I did as soon as I got out of class. When I called the number and reached a person, I was explaining the situation to the dude on the phone and asking for if they had any order information on their system. I did not get the dudes name, but he had an [Redacted] accent. I told him and spelled out my email address, and the two email addressees of who supposedly got these gift cards delivered. What was crazy to me was the dude telling me on the phone that there was no record of any order going through on their system. I told him to check every email I provided and he was telling me there wasn't any order. I told him there had to be, because the emails I had received came from their email address from their website. He told me he was going to raise the issue to their IT department. I told him yes, and to their billing department too. After the call ended, I was very upset and called the bank once again. I spoke with a dude named [Redacted] and once again explained the situation. He told me I was going to get a phone call from a [Redacted] at the fraud department as only they are allowed to re-open the case. I told him my schedule ( " today after [Redacted] ends '' ; " tomorrow after [Redacted] get off work '' ) to make sure I got the phone call. Today is [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, and I have not received the phone call from the [Redacted]. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], the bank will take away the {$300.00} credit I had received, and someone is still out there with my information ( full name, email address, and my previous debit card number ) without any consequence as of yet.

metadata.full_snippet: I have been a USAA member for approximately 14 years and have maintained my account in good standing throughout that time. Over the course of my membership, I have submitted disputes only when necessary, specifically in cases where merchandise was not received or was materially different from what was ordered. In each instance, I acted in good faith by attempting to resolve the issue directly with the merchant first and by providing supporting documentation to USAA. Many of these disputes were investigated and resolved in my favor, confirming that the claims were valid. Recently, USAA restricted my account and informed me that my account is being reviewed and/or closed due to dispute activity. I was not provided with a clear explanation identifying any specific wrongdoing or misuse of the dispute process. As of now, my funds are being held, and I am unable to access my money. This includes funds necessary to meet essential financial obligations such as rent and supporting my children. I have contacted USAA to request : A clear explanation for the restriction and/or closure The specific basis for their decision A timeline for resolution Access to or release of my funds USAA has not provided sufficient or clear information in response to these requests. The issue is that USAA is now using dispute activitypreviously investigated and validated by its own processesas justification to restrict or close my account. This is inconsistent and unfair, as I relied on USAAs dispute process in good faith and with supporting documentation. Actions taken by me : Filed disputes only when warranted and with documentation Attempted to resolve issues directly with merchants prior to disputes Contacted USAA to request explanation and access to funds Actions taken by USAA : Investigated disputes and resolved many in my favor Restricted access to my account and funds Failed to provide a clear explanation or timeline for resolution This situation has caused immediate financial hardship due to lack of access to my funds. I am requesting : Immediate release of my funds A clear and detailed explanation for the account restriction/closure A review and reconsideration of the decision to close my account based on dispute activity that was previously validated I am submitting this complaint in good faith and expect a timely and thorough response.

metadata.full_snippet: Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am submitting this formal complaint to request assistance and regulatory review regarding ongoing inaccuracies on my consumer credit reports that remain unresolved despite repeated disputes. I am a victim of identity theft that I believe resulted from large-scale data breaches involving Equifax and TransUnion, during which sensitive consumer information was exposed. As a result of this compromised data, my personal identifying information has been misused without my authorization. Since discovering these issues, I have : Filed multiple disputes directly with the consumer reporting agencies Contacted the furnishers of the disputed accounts Submitted follow-up correspondence and documentation Allowed sufficient time for investigation and correction Despite these efforts, several inaccurate and unauthorized accounts, collections, and credit inquiries continue to appear on my credit reports. These items do not belong to me, were not opened or authorized by me, and are consistent with identity-theft-related fraud. The companies involved have either : Failed to conduct a reasonable investigation Verified inaccurate information without providing validation Failed to remove or correct disputed items within the timeframes required by law This ongoing failure has caused continued harm to my creditworthiness, financial opportunities, and personal security. I believe these actions constitute violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), including but not limited to : Failure to ensure maximum possible accuracy Failure to reasonably investigate disputes Failure to correct or delete unverifiable information I respectfully request that the CFPB : Review my complaint and supporting documentation Require the consumer reporting agencies and furnishers to properly investigate Ensure removal of all inaccurate, fraudulent, or unverifiable accounts and inquiries Enforce compliance with applicable federal consumer protection laws I am submitting this complaint in good faith and am prepared to provide any additional documentation needed to support my claims. Thank you for your time and assistance in this matter.

metadata.full_snippet: Issue : Fraudulent auto loan / funds disbursed to non-existent dealership Company : USAA Federal Savings Bank Complaint : On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I entered into what I believed to be a legitimate vehicle purchase through an online dealership operating as [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. After agreeing on terms, I completed a USAA auto loan application on their app platform and the dealership provided a purchase agreement. The purchase agreement listed a different entity name ( [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ). This discrepancy was not explained, and no verification or clarification was provided by USAA prior to disbursement of funds. I believed this company to be a parent company or financial arm of [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I was informed by the dealership that an [Redacted] transfer had been requested. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I was notified that USAA disbursed the loan funds via [Redacted]. I was told the vehicle would be delivered on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. The vehicle was never delivered. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, all attempts to contact the dealership, delivery driver, and representatives failed, including the delivery driver 's phone number that was " no longer in service '' when I called. I immediately contacted USAA to report suspected fraud. As of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> : - I have not received the vehicle. - The seller appears to be a fraudulent or non-existent entity. I conducted a business entity search on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> for [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] in Minnesota ( and Colorado which was a second address listed in the documents sent to me for signature with the purchase agreement ) secretary of state website returned no registered records/entities under that name. Despite reporting this as fraud, I have been informed that I remain responsible for repayment of the loan. This situation raises serious concerns about USAAs underwriting and fraud prevention controls. Specifically : - Funds were disbursed via ACH without verification of a legitimate, registered business entity. - No independent validation of the seller was performed. - A discrepancy in entity names was not flagged or resolved prior to funding. - Funds were released without confirmation of title, delivery, or asset existence. Additionally, customer service responses have been inadequate. I was advised to file a police report and research my own options. I was informed on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] that my complaint with this loan had started in internal investigation of the fraud. I was contacted yesterday by USAA, they stated that the application was done on the USAA app, they received the purchase agreement, they did recognize the company names did not match from my application and the purchase agreement but said they verified the account the ACH transfer was going to. They stated their conclusion of their investigation ( 2 day investigation ) was that I am responsible for the loan. Failure to verify the dealer was a legal entity prior to transferring funds This transaction represents a clear failure on the part of USAA to protect me from this fraud. From what I have read since I believed this dealer to be a fraud, an ACH request from a dealer should automatically increase USAA 's verification process. As such, I dispute any assertion that I am responsible for repayment of the loan as USAA failed to verify the dealer as a legal entity prior to the ACH transfer.

metadata.full_snippet: I am extremely disappointed with my experience with Onity Mortgage. After being laid off from my job, I proactively reached out for assistance before falling behind on my mortgage. I was told that because my account was still current, they could not offer any help. Trying to stay responsible, I continued to do what I couldbut after a few months, I inevitably fell behind and reached out again. At that point, I was told they could not offer forbearance or any meaningful assistance that would actually help my situation. Instead, late fees were added to an already unaffordable mortgage. At one point, I was even told they could increase my paymentsomething that made absolutely no sense given that I was already struggling. I have contacted this company more than five times seeking help, and each time Ive been met with the same responses : * The system wont allow us to waive late fees. * We can not move missed payments to the back of the loan. There has been no flexibility, no empathy, and no real effort to provide a solution. As a [Redacted] [Redacted], I never expected to be in this positionstruggling to make ends meet and asking for help just to keep my home. I am not asking for anything unreasonable, just some level of support during a difficult time. Instead, Ive been left feeling ignored and unsupported. I dont want to lose my home, but at this point, I can no longer afford to stay. Its incredibly discouraging to feel like Im doing everything I can and still getting nowhere. No homeowner should feel this helpless when asking for assistance.

My requests for documentation have not been fulfilled. I am concerned that I am being denied access to required loan documentation and information necessary to make informed financial decisions. I am also concerned that I may be paying for add-on products that I have requested to cancel but have not received confirmation or refund details. Additionally, I was previously informed that hardship assistance may be available in the event of financial difficulty. However, when I recently requested assistance, I was told no options were available beyond deferrals, which contradicts what I was told at the time of origination. This lack of transparency is preventing me from resolving my financial situation and may be contributing to ongoing financial hardship. I am requesting : 1. A full copy of my signed loan agreement and all associated documents 2. A complete breakdown of my balance, including principal, interest, and add-ons 3. Immediate review and processing of cancellation and prorated refunds for any eligible add-on products 4. Written clarification of all available hardship or repayment options 5. Confirmation that my account has been reviewed for all applicable consumer protections I would like all responses provided in writing.

metadata.full_snippet: Axos Bank Failure to Validate Deficiency, Missing Required [Redacted] Notices, Contradictory Information, and Inaccurate Credit Reporting Complaint Narrative : I am submitting this followup complaint because Axos Banks [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> response failed to address the core issues raised in my original CFPB complaint and introduced new inconsistencies. Axos Bank admitted in writing that it can not produce the legally required Notice of Sale ( UCC 9611 ) or the postsale accounting statement ( UCC 9616 ) for my repossessed vehicle. These documents are mandatory. Without them, the Bank can not legally substantiate a deficiency balance or report one to consumer reporting agencies. Axos also stated that the remaining balance after the auction and GAP refund was {$4500.00}, yet they are reporting {$8000.00} to the credit bureaus. They did not provide any documentation supporting the additional charges, interest calculations, or how the balance increased by nearly {$3500.00}. This is inaccurate and inconsistent reporting in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). Additionally, Axos claims that No WorryFree insurance was purchased, which contradicts written confirmation I received from the dealership/NALN at the time of purchase. This raises concerns about misrepresentation of ad don products and improper handling of ancillary product refunds. Axos also stated that a GAP refund was issued instead of filing a GAP claim. If GAP was included in the loan, the Bank was required to file the claim and apply the benefit to reduce the deficiency. Canceling GAP instead of applying it is improper servicing. Finally, Axos did not provide : A copy of the retail installment contract Addon product disclosures A deficiency calculation Proof of mailing of any required notices Any documentation supporting the current reported balance I am requesting that the CFPB require Axos Bank to : 1. Provide all legally required UCC notices and accounting statements, or confirm in writing that they can not. 2. Provide a complete deficiency calculation with supporting documentation. 3. Explain the discrepancy between the {$4500.00} balance and the {$8000.00} reported balance. 4. Provide documentation regarding all ancillary products, including GAP, VSC, and WorryFree coverage. 5. Correct or delete all inaccurate credit reporting if the deficiency can not be validated. Thank you for your assistance.

metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this complaint regarding inaccurate credit reporting by Sallie Mae related to a student loan account affected by a Servicemembers Civil Relief Act ( SCRA ) misapplication. From [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] through [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], my account accrued interest at approximately 10.25 %, despite being eligible for the SCRA interest rate cap of 5 %. Sallie Mae has since confirmed this error and applied the SCRA benefit retroactively, including a credit adjustment of approximately {$510.00}. During this period, I made consistent monthly payments toward interest. Based on the corrected SCRA rate, the appropriate monthly interest obligation was significantly lower than what was charged. As a result, my payments were consistent with, and in many cases exceeded, the correct obligation. Despite this correction, Sallie Mae reported my account as 60 days past due on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. These delinquencies were based on an inflated balance resulting from the incorrect interest calculation. I escalated this matter through Sallie Maes Office of Customer Advocate. While they acknowledged the SCRA correction and applied the credit, they maintained that the delinquency was valid at the time and declined to remove it. They also stated that the late payment was only temporarily suppressed from credit reporting due to California law during the review process, not permanently corrected. Additionally, I spoke with a Sallie Mae account manager on a recorded line on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], who stated that once my payment settled, I would be able to submit a request to have the late payment removed and that it would be reflected with my next billing cycle. I confirmed this understanding during the call. This call was later reviewed internally ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ), and while Sallie Mae acknowledged the statement was made, they indicated the representative was incorrect and declined to honor that guidance. My concern is that the delinquency does not accurately reflect my account status under the corrected SCRA-adjusted terms. The reported delinquency is based on a monthly obligation that has now been confirmed to be incorrect.
