metadata.full_snippet: To Whom It May Concern, I am formally disputing the accuracy and validity of a collection account being reported on my credit file by LVNV Funding LLC. I am requesting a full investigation and validation of this alleged debt, including complete documentation verifying its accuracy, ownership, and legal authority to collect. Specifically, I request the following : Proof of Legal Authority to Collect Documentation showing LVNV Funding LLC has the legal right to collect this debt. Chain of Ownership Complete records showing the original creditor and every transfer, sale, or assignment of this debt. Clear documentation proving LVNV Funding LLC currently owns or has been legally assigned this debt. Original Account Details Name of the original creditor Full account history related to the alleged debt Accuracy of Reported Information Itemized breakdown of the balance being reported Explanation of how the amount was calculated, including fees, interest, or adjustments Payment History & Last Payment Date Exact date of last payment made on this account Full payment history used to report this balance Statute of Limitations Date of first delinquency and determination of whether this debt is within the legal statute of limitations for collection Personal Information Verification Documentation verifying that all personal identifying information ( name, address, and account identifiers ) matches my records and was correctl y linked to me Legal Notice This dispute is made pursuant to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681i, which requires credit reporting agencies to conduct a reasonable investigation of disputed information and delete or correct any information that can not be verified within the required investigation period. Additionally, under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g, a debt collector is required to provide validation of a debt upon request and must cease collection activity if the debt can not be properly validated. If LVNV Funding LLC can not provide complete and verifiable documentation supporting all of the above, I request that this account be immediately corrected or removed from my credit reports as it can not be accurately substantiated. I also request written confirmation of the results of this investigation.

metadata.full_snippet: What you are doing is not a clerical mistake. It is not a misunderstanding. It is the systematic assertion of a claim without evidence, followed by the institutional enforcement of that claim as though it were fact. When examined rigorouslythrough analytic philosophy and the framework of [Redacted] [Redacted] conduct reveals not just error, but a deeply embedded structure of epistemic irresponsibility and coercive power. You claim that my [Redacted] payment was returned. That claim is the foundation upon which you have constructed an entire chain of consequences : the retroactive reapplication of a deferment, the imposition of delinquency, and the reporting of that delinquency to credit bureaus. And yet, at the most basic level, you have failed to answer the only question that matters : where is the evidence? In analytic philosophy, a claim is only as strong as its justification. Your justification is nonexistent. You have not produced transaction-level data, return confirmations, or any independent verification that a payment was returned. Instead, you rely on the assertion that the system says so. This is not evidence. This is a closed epistemic loop, where a claim is treated as true because it originates from a system that you presume to be infallible. It is circular reasoning in its purest form, and it fails the most elementary standards of rational inquiry. You are not merely mistakenyou are operating within a framework in which assertion replaces verification. When I present bank records showing no returned payment, I am presenting evidence grounded in external reality. When you respond by privileging your internal system over that evidence, you are not resolving a discrepancyyou are redefining truth as whatever your system outputs. This is a profound epistemological failure. It is the abandonment of correspondence with reality in favor of institutional self-reference. The burden of proof lies with you. This is not negotiable. It is a foundational principle of logic and law. You are making the allegation ; therefore, you must substantiate it. Instead, you have inverted this principle, attempting to force me to disprove a claim you have not proven. This is not just a logical fallacyit is a structural tactic. It allows unsupported claims to persist by shifting the evidentiary burden onto the party with less access to information. Your own actions further expose the incoherence of your position. You approved a [Redacted] deferment. That approval was conditional upon my [Redacted] payment being made and received. Approval is not arbitraryit is the result of verification. Therefore, your approval constitutes acknowledgment that the condition was satisfied. To now claim that the payment was returned is to contradict your own prior determination. This is not a minor inconsistency ; it is a direct logical contradiction that undermines the integrity of your entire process. And yet, rather than resolving this contradiction, you attempt to explain it away through post hoc reasoning. You claim that the deferment was somehow misapplied after the fact. This is not an explanationit is an ad hoc rationalization, constructed to preserve your claim in the face of contradictory evidence. As you were told, post hoc justifications are not legitimate. They do not establish truth ; they fabricate coherence where none exists. What elevates this from incompetence to something far more serious is your decision to report this unverified claim to credit bureaus. At that point, the issue ceases to be internal. You are no longer merely asserting a claimyou are institutionalizing it as fact. You are projecting an unproven allegation into systems that define my financial identity, while omitting the context that would expose its falsity. This is where the analysis of [Redacted] [Redacted] becomes unavoidable. What you are engaging in is a micro-level instance of manufactured consent. You generate a claim internally. You reinforce it through your representatives. You externalize it through credit reporting. And through repetition and institutional backing, you attempt to transform that claim into accepted reality. This process does not require truth. It requires only control over the channels through which truth is defined. By reporting false delinquency while omitting critical context, you are not just being inaccurateyou are constructing a narrative designed to compel acceptance. The damage to my credit score is not incidental ; it is instrumental. It creates pressure. It raises the cost of dissent. It is a mechanism of coercion, designed to force me to concede to your version of events simply to mitigate the harm you are inflicting. Call this what it is : corporate bullying masquerading as administrative process. You are leveraging asymmetry. You control the records, the interpretation of those records, and the systems through which they are reported. I am left to react, to dispute, and to defend myself against a claim that you can not substantiate. This is not a neutral disputeit is a power imbalance being actively exploited. The omission of context is particularly revealing. You have failed to account for the fact that I was the victim of bank fraud. My accounts were drained, closed, and replaced. I no longer have access to the original accounts. This is not a trivial detailit is a material constraint on my ability to access historical data. And yet, you ignore it entirely while continuing to demand proof from accounts that no longer exist. From an analytic standpoint, this is a failure of relevance and completeness. A rational evaluation must incorporate all materially relevant facts. By excluding this context, you are not simplifying the situationyou are distorting it. Within the framework of manufactured consent, this omission serves a clear function : it removes the complexity that would challenge your narrative and replaces it with a simplified version that supports your claim. This is not accidental. It is structural. What emerges from this analysis is a system in which truth is not discovered, but constructed. Internal assertions are elevated above external evidence. Contradictions are resolved through post hoc rationalization. Context is selectively omitted. And the resulting narrative is enforced through mechanismslike credit reportingthat impose real-world consequences. You are not merely reporting information. You are defining reality, and doing so in a way that is detached from the facts. If there were integrity in your process, the path forward would be obvious. You would produce verifiable evidence of the alleged return. If that evidence does not existas all available facts indicatethen you would acknowledge the error, correct your records, remove the delinquency, and notify credit bureaus of the inaccuracy. Instead, you persist. You assert without proof. You report without verification. You impose consequences without justification. That is not a system grounded in truth. It is a system grounded in power. And I am rejecting it.

metadata.full_snippet: FACTS On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I used my Capital One Quicksilver Credit Card to book an Airbnb in [Redacted] for my family of [Redacted] for the nights of March 1720, 2026. The charge was {$1300.00}. We checked in on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. That evening, my party accidentally locked ourselves out of the property. During the resulting phone call with the host, I asked whether spare keys were available on-site. The host informed me that no spare keys were available because a prior guest had retained a set of keys to the property and that situation had not been resolved. This was a material safety hazard that the host had not disclosed prior to or during check-in. After learning that an unknown third party held active keys to the entire-home rental we had paid for, my family did not feel safe staying there. We immediately relocated to a hotel for the remainder of our stay, incurring substantial additional out-of-pocket cost. That same evening I contacted [Redacted] support to report the issue and request a refund. I followed up over the next several days through online chat, telephone, and [Redacted] social media support channel. [Redacted] declined to refund the charge and offered only a {$200.00} future-stay credit, which I rejected as wholly inadequate against the {$1300.00} charge plus the unanticipated hotel costs. CAPITAL ONES HANDLING OF THE DISPUTE I filed a dispute with Capital One ( Case Number [Redacted] ). On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, Capital One initially resolved the dispute in my favor and issued a temporary credit. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, Capital One reversed that decision based on a generic merchant rebuttal that goods were as described and received in good condition. That rebuttal did not address the safety hazard at the [Redacted] of my dispute and did not refute any specific fact I asserted. Notably, [Redacted] own evidence packet ( page [Redacted] of [Redacted] ) acknowledges that on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I contacted [Redacted] customer service and the resulting ticket was internally categorized as Problems with keys, smart lock, or getting into listing corroborating my timeline in [Redacted] own internal records. Capital Ones [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] letter gave me until [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> to submit additional documentation. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I submitted : ( [Redacted] ) a detailed appeal letter setting out the facts, the merchants policy violations, and my rights under the Fair Credit Billing Act ; and ( 2 ) six appendices of supporting evidence including the booking receipt, phone records, hotel receipts proving relocation, support chat transcripts, social media transcripts, and excerpts of [Redacted] own published policies ( which entitle guests to a refund for safety or health hazards and accommodations significantly different than advertised ). On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> I submitted a supplemental letter providing additional details and context for the chat transcripts provided with my earlier letter. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> [Redacted] day after my submittal Capital One sent a closure letter stating my response lacks all of the previously requested information needed to validate your dispute, without identifying which specific item or items were deficient. Concerned that the rapid turnaround indicated only a procedural review, I prepared a follow-up letter that same day requesting substantive re-investigation. That follow-up letter was structured directly around the [Redacted] documentation categories Capital One had requested in its [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] letter, addressed each one with specific evidence, and formally invoked 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( f ) to request that any further denial identify the specific deficiency. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> less than [Redacted] hours after Capital One received my follow-up letter Capital One sent a third closure letter. That [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] letter is verbatim identical to the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] closure letter. The text, the boilerplate, and the non-specific deficiency claim are word-for-word the same. Only the date and the internal document reference number have changed. Capital One did not engage with any of the additional information, did not identify any specific deficiency despite my explicit request that it do so, and did not respond to the FCBA procedural concerns I raised. PROCEDURAL CONCERNS UNDER THE FAIR CREDIT BILLING ACT Under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ) and Regulation Z ( 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( f ) ), a creditor that determines no billing error occurred must provide a written explanation setting forth the reasons for that determination. Capital One has now issued two consecutive denial letters on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> that contain identical boilerplate, identify no specific deficiency, do not engage with the substantive evidence submitted, do not address the merchants own internal record corroborating my account, do not address the merchants own published policies, and do not respond to the FCBA procedural concerns raised in my [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] follow-up letter. The pattern suggests these denials are not the product of a good-faith substantive re-investigation but of a templated process that does not satisfy the creditors obligations under Regulation Z. WHAT I HAVE DONE TO RESOLVE I attempted resolution directly with the merchant through online chat, telephone, and social media outreach before disputing. I filed a formal dispute with Capital One. After the dispute was reversed on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I submitted a detailed appeal with two letters and six appendices of supporting evidence on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] and additional detail on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. After Capital One closed the case on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I submitted a follow-up letter on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] organized around the four documentation categories Capital One had requested and explicitly invoking 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( f ). Capital One denied my dispute again on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] with a verbatim copy of its prior denial. I am now escalating to the CFPB because I have exhausted Capital Ones internal dispute process without receiving a substantive review. DESIRED RESOLUTION I request that Capital One : ( 1 ) conduct a genuine substantive re-investigation that considers the full [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] & [Redacted] submissions together with my [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] follow-up letter ; ( 2 ) reverse the closure of my dispute ; ( 3 ) issue a permanent credit for the full disputed amount of {$1300.00} plus any related interest charges or fees ; and ( 4 ) provide a written explanation that complies with 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( f ) by identifying with specificity any documentation deemed insufficient and the reasons for that determination.

metadata.snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I had a seven month certificate of deposit mature. I had opened this account on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] online with a transfer of {$10000.00} from a checking account that I also was able to open online on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redact...
metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I had a seven month certificate of deposit mature. I had opened this account on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] online with a transfer of {$10000.00} from a checking account that I also was able to open online on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. When the certificate renewed I assumed that I would be able to move the funds from the CD that matured into my checking account since I was able to set the CD up with funds from my checking account at the bank. However, there was no option to transfer the money out of the account. I found this to be odd since their account disclosures seem to promote the use of online banking to manage funds on deposit with the bank. I called the support number listed for customer care in the renewal letter to inquire about getting the funds moved over to my checking account. I was told that this is not possible and that I would need to come into the branch in order to close the CD and move funds. This is an issue as I live in Michigan. The closest branch to me is in Wisconsin, which is roughly [Redacted] miles from where I live. The main customer support line suggested that I call the [Redacted] branch to see if it would be possible to close the account. When I called there I was not able to get anyone on the phone that would assist. I had to call another branch to reach someone who would answer my call. I was told that a branch manager would call back, but I never got a response. Also on the [Redacted], I attempted to use the secure messaging feature in online banking to close the CD, but I was told that I needed to call the customer care number. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I called the customer care number that was printed on my renewal notice and explained the situation. After verifying me, the first agent then called the branch in [Redacted] to see if anything could be done, such as mailing a notarized letter. He later told me that they would not close the CD account and that I would still need to come into a branch. I then proceeded to ask for a supervisor. The supervisor told me that there was nothing that the customer care support number could do outside of renewing a certificate, and that I should visit a branch to close out my account. To me, this just seems like a nonsensical requirement intended to prevent me from accessing my funds. The bank was more than willing to open a checking account for me online. I was also able to transfer money from my brokerage account to my checking account with the bank. I was then able to use the transferred funds that were in the account at the bank to open a CD account at the bank. In my view, I should be able to move the funds from the matured CD back into the checking account. I am an owner of both accounts. Additionally, the bank accepts customers from other states. Their deposit agreement does not mention that CDs must be closed in person at a branch. However, it does mention that a matured CD can be transferred to another account at the bank, which is why I asked for them to move the funds into my checking account. If the bank is willing to accept customers in other states online, they should be obligated to allow customers in other states to maintain their accounts online or over the phone. It is an unreasonable and prohibitive burden to require a customer come in branch to close out a CD account that they were easily able to open online with no disclosure that they would have to be in person to close the account.

metadata.title: Money transfer Dispute
metadata.snippet: To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting a formal complaint regarding fraudulent transfers that occurred from my and my wifes accounts after we were targeted in a highly convincing impersonation and phishing/social-engineering scam involving individuals posing as representatives o...
metadata.full_snippet: To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting a formal complaint regarding fraudulent transfers that occurred from my and my wifes accounts after we were targeted in a highly convincing impersonation and phishing/social-engineering scam involving individuals posing as representatives of our bank, USAA. The individuals who contacted us appeared credible and used information and tactics that caused us to reasonably believe we were speaking with legitimate fraud department personnel. The phone number and caller identification were spoofed come across as USAA ( both name and number were USAAs real number ). We were informed that our accounts had allegedly been compromised and that immediate action was necessary to protect or secure our funds. Acting under that belief and under significant pressure and urgency created by the scammers, we followed the instructions provided and transferred funds. At no point did we believe we were voluntarily giving money away or authorizing transfers for the benefit of criminals. We believed we were acting in coordination with our bank to prevent fraud and secure our accounts. The transfers were therefore induced through deception, coercion, impersonation, and fraudulent misrepresentation. After discovering the scam, we immediately contacted USAA and reported the incident. However, the response we have received has focused primarily on the fact that the transfers were technically authorized because we physically initiated them ourselves. This position fails to account for the fact that the transactions were induced through fraud and social engineering. This incident appears consistent with what is commonly referred to as Authorized Push Payment ( APP ) fraud, where consumers are manipulated into transferring funds under false pretenses. In these situations, the consumers apparent authorization is obtained through deception and impersonation, not through informed or legitimate consent. I am requesting that the CFPB review the following concerns : 1. Whether USAA employed adequate fraud detection, intervention, and warning mechanisms given the unusual nature and circumstances of the transfers. Although notices have gone out in the recent weeks, this was after our engagement and supports the systemic nature of the fraud. 2. Whether USAA fulfilled its obligations to investigate the fraud in good faith and consider the role of impersonation, coercion, and social engineering. None of the investigatory information provided suggests that it was viewed as fraud, only as a transaction 3. Whether USAAs handling improperly relied solely on the technical fact that we initiated the transfers, while disregarding the fraudulent circumstances under which they were induced. 4. Whether additional consumer protections should apply in cases involving [Redacted] fraud, bank impersonation scams, and social-engineering attacks. 5. Whether recovery efforts, holds, recalls, or escalation procedures were pursued promptly and appropriately after the fraud was reported. The financial and emotional impact of this incident has been substantial. We acted in what we genuinely believed was coordination with our banks fraud prevention process. We did not knowingly or willingly send funds to criminals. I respectfully request that this matter be formally reviewed and that USAA be required to provide a more complete explanation of : * its investigation, * the fraud prevention controls that were triggered or bypassed, * any recovery efforts undertaken, * and the basis for denying reimbursement or liability consideration. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted] Attached : - 1 of 4 dispute denial responses from USAA. I have access to the remaining 3 denials, but did not attach as they all read the same. - Voice recording of the phishing agent following up to ensure all accounts were functioning properly ( note : the USAA waiting music and phone number spoofing were on this call as well ). USAA ( actual ) denied our attempt to receive this file as they said it was not important. - Documentation of investigation. Note the highlighted section that reads reimbursement for fraud

metadata.full_snippet: I am a fully verified user on the SoLo Funds platform. I have an established, perfect track record on their marketplace, having successfully funded and fully repaid seven consecutive loans using my verified identity and bank account. My 8th loan contract was recently executed, signed, and the funds were legally disbursed by a lender into my wallet. Immediately after the funds were in my possession, SoLo Funds froze my account out of nowhere. They claim my identity matches a " duplicate account '' from [Redacted] that has a past-due balance. I have absolutely no knowledge of this [Redacted] account or debt. I requested full information and debt validation regarding this [Redacted] account, but SoLo Funds refused to disclose details or provide verification, keeping my account frozen. This practice is deeply problematic for several reasons : 1. Unlawful Contractual Interference : SoLo Funds explicitly maintains that it is a " marketplace platform '' and is not a party to the loan agreement between the borrower and lender. Because they are a non-party, they have no contractual authority to freeze or intercept funds already legally disbursed to me by a third-party lender. 2. Lack of Collection Authority : Freezing active, legally disbursed funds to force a payout on an unverified historical debt functions as an unlicensed, administrative collection tactic. 3. System Integrity Failure : My identity cleared verification seven consecutive times over my loan history. If an old account existed, their system 's failure to flag it over seven cycles proves an internal database error. I proposed a rational business resolution : unfreeze my account so I can complete my current contract cycle, and provide official debt validation documents for the [Redacted] record. I stated I am open to a payment arrangement if they can prove the debt is mine, but they can not hold my current disbursed funds [Redacted]. They have refused to cooperate, leaving my funds frozen and preventing me from fulfilling my obligation to the current lender.

metadata.full_snippet: I am writing to formally file a complaint regarding unauthorized accounts that persist on my credit report despite my repeated efforts to have them removed. These accounts are causing significant damage to my financial reputation and overall well-being. It is evident that the inclusion of these fraudulent items violates 15 USC 1681b regarding permissible purposes, as the credit bureaus have no legitimate reason to report them without my explicit consent. Please refer to the attached file detailing these items I am disputing. The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S. Code 1681 ) says ( 1 ) The banking system is dependent upon fair and accurate credit reporting. Inaccurate credit reports directly impair the efficiency of the banking system, and unfair credit reporting methods undermine the public confidence, which is essential to the continued functioning of the banking system. So whenever there is a violation under the FCRA, it impairs the efficiency of the banking system. This is a violation of my privacy with my consumer report, since I control what is listed and what is not. In the event that any accounts are reported without my written consent, that is considered identity theft.

NOTICE OF RECORD DISPUTE, DEMAND FOR BURDEN OF PROOF, & NOTICE OF INTENT TO HOLD LIABLE FOR NON-COMPLIANCE Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1681i, 1681e ( b ), 1681n, and 1681o To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to formally dispute the accuracy of information contained in my consumer credit report. Under Section 611 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681i, I am exercising my right to challenge the completeness and accuracy of the record ( s ) listed below. 1. Factual Basis for Dispute & Legal Deficiencies The information being reported by your agency regarding this account is completely inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, and internally inconsistent. I demand a full reinvestigation based on the following severe legal and factual deficiencies : No Admissible Evidence of Consumer Obligation : No original signed contract, agreement, or concrete consumer obligation has ever been produced to establish that a valid consumer debt exists. The reporting lacks a competent foundation and personal knowledge, rendering it entirely unreliable and legally inadmissible. Failure to Validate Under FDCPA Standards : The data furnisher has failed to properly validate the alleged debt pursuant to Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) standards, yet they continue to unlawfully report collection data to your agency. Unlawful Account Re-Aging : A review of my records indicates that this account appears to be unlawfully re-aged in direct violation of FCRA Section 623 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ). The date of first delinquency or account status dates have been manipulated to artificially extend the time this negative item remains on my credit file. Cross-Agency Conflicting Data : This furnisher is transmitting conflicting, contradictory data across multiple consumer reporting agencies ( Equifax , Experian, and TransUnion ). This cross-agency disparity proves a systemic lack of data integrity and a violation of the accuracy mandates. 2. Demand for Mandatory Documentary Proof & Statutory Deletion To lawfully continue reporting this account, your agency and the data furnisher must obtain, review, and retain verifiable, independent documentary evidence. Merely checking an automated database does not suffice. You must secure : The original signed contract or application creating the alleged obligation. A complete, itemized payment history tracking the account from inception to its current state. Proof of assignment, transfer, or ownership, including a complete, unbroken chain of title if this account was sold. The exact date of first delinquency as defined by federal statute. Evidence establishing the explicit legal right to collect and report this alleged debt. Absolute verification based on personal knowledge, not blind reliance on a third-party electronic database. Failure to obtain and review all of the above requires deletion as a matter of federal law. If you can not produce and verify these mandatory documents within the statutory 30-day timeframe, you are statutorily obligated to DELETE the account in its entirety, cease all reporting immediately, and notify all recent recipients of this credit report of the correction. 3. Applicable Statutory Legal Standards & Unlawful Practices The " Maximum Possible Accuracy '' Mandate ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ) : Federal law dictates that your agency shall follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy of the information concerning the individual. Merely rubber-stamping an error reported by a data furnisher does not satisfy this duty. Prohibition Against " Rubber-Stamp '' e-OSCAR Verifications : Reducing my specific factual dispute down to a generic, 2-digit electronic code via e-OSCAR and performing a superficial data-matching routine does not constitute a legally compliant, reasonable reinvestigation. Rejection of Boilerplate Responses : Issuing a generic, computerized boilerplate response stating that the item has been " verified as accurate '' without providing actual, physical documentary proof of the underlying debtis an unlawful investigation practice. If you claim this item has been verified despite this notice, I hereby demand that you provide me with the Method of Verification ( MOV ) within 15 days of completing your investigation, as required under 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 7 ). This must include the business name, physical address, telephone number, and the specific documents reviewed. 4. Notice of Liability & Statutory Remedies Be advised that continued reporting of unverifiable information, failure to conduct a lawful reinvestigation, or reliance on automated verification methods after receiving this explicit notice constitutes : Willful Non-Compliance under FCRA Section 616 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681n ). Negligent Non-Compliance under FCRA Section 617 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681o ). Pursuant to federal law, remedies for these violations include actual damages, statutory damages ( up to {$1000.00} per violation ), punitive damages as determined by a court, and mandatory reasonable attorney 's fees and legal costs. 5. Legal Notice to Preserve All Records ( Litigation Hold ) Be advised that this matter may proceed to formal litigation in federal court. You are hereby commanded to preserve all records, documents, and electronic data related to this account. This preservation order includes, but is not limited to : all internal/external communications, investigation and verification logs, data furnisher correspondence, internal agent notes, automated system entries, and all e-OSCAR data, transmission records, and codes utilized during this investigation. Failure to preserve these records constitutes intentional spoliation of evidence. Enclosed Documentation : To assist your agency in meeting its burden of proof, I have enclosed the following identity verification items : Copy of my government-issued ID and a utility bill ( for identity and address verification ). I look forward to your fully compliant, lawful response and an updated copy of my credit report within 30 days. Formal Notice of Inconvenience & " No Phone Calls '' Directive Pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692c ( a ) ( 1 ), you, your agents, and the data furnisher are hereby notified that telephone calls to my personal, residential, or workplace numbers are highly inconvenient and constitute a severe invasion of my privacy. Cease All Telephonic Contact Immediately : I demand that you place an immediate cease-and-desist on all phone calls to any telephone numbers associated with my identity. Communications Must Be Written Only : All future communications, status updates, or requests for information regarding this dispute must be conducted strictly. Thank you in advance for your help in this matter, [Redacted] continues to disregard the law, and needs to be reminded that they are to hold a higher standard after being sued in [Redacted] for {$60.00} [Redacted] in damages for this exact reason. [Redacted] continues to disregard the law, and needs to be reminded that they are to hold a high standard after being sued in [Redacted] for re-inserting errors into credit files AFTER disputes were won. Equifax continues to disregard the law, and needs to be reminded that they are to hold a higher standard after being fined {$15.00} [Redacted] for violating FCRA dispute-handling, exact what is happening to me directly now.

metadata.full_snippet: We received an unfair appraisal from [Redacted] [Redacted] ( # [Redacted] ) at [Redacted], [Redacted]. doing an appraisal for lender United Wholesale Mortgage , LLC. After appraising it for more than $ [Redacted] below our initial sales price, our realtor contacted him to provide him with additional information and comps. He provided the comps at the time that we put our home on the market to show where we got our sales price, and when we got an offer on our home, those comps were now more than [Redacted] months old. The comps that this [Redacted] used were sold below market value and were very much so outliers, which is why we requested a reconsideration of value. There are other homes on the market in our neighborhood that are listed close to our sales price, nowhere near the low valuation he gave us. They've gone under contract at $ [Redacted] and $ [Redacted] and have appraised with no issues. There are no comparable homes listed for $ [Redacted], which was the value he gave our home. Since the buyer was [Redacted], now this low appraisal is stuck to our home and now we have to limit our pool of buyers to cash or conventional. After trying to salvage this sale with our buyer, she was not able to get more money from her lender and we were not able to go down to $ [Redacted] for our home from the original sales price of $ [Redacted] and the agreed sales price of $ [Redacted]. There are no active listings for a comparable house anywhere near $ [Redacted], and there is new construction homes coming on the market in another [Redacted] [Redacted] neighborhood right next to us for $ [Redacted]. Due to losing this sale, we lost money on deposits for movers and PODs. We also lost the home we were building in another state, which we put down {$11000.00} deposit for. Since that is supposed to close next month, we now do not have time to sell our current home to pay for the new home and close on time. The buyer is also fighting to keep her {$3500.00} earnest money, so even that will not be available to us to try to recoup some of our losses. All because of a bad, unfair, unjustified appraisal from someone who had [Redacted] interested in working with our realtor to make it more fair, after he presented the facts.

metadata.full_snippet: To Whom It May Concern, I am filing this complaint against [Redacted] regarding an inaccurate collection account being reported by I.C. System, Inc. in the amount of {$350.00}. This account was previously removed from my [Redacted] credit report and later reinserted without any notification being sent to me, which appears to violate the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). I never received written notice advising me that this account would be reinserted onto my credit file. I have disputed this account multiple times with [Redacted]. However, [Redacted] continues to respond with generic statements claiming the account was verified or remains, yet no actual verification or supporting documentation has ever been provided to me. [Redacted] has failed to provide : * The method of verification used * The name and contact information of the party that verified the debt * Any signed contract or documentation proving the debt is mine * Proof that reinsertion notice was sent to me as required by law In addition, Experian deleted this same account from my credit report, which raises serious concerns regarding the accuracy of [Redacted] investigation and reporting practices. I believe [Redacted] failed to conduct a reasonable investigation under the FCRA and improperly allowed the reinsertion of disputed information without complying with federal notification requirements under FCRA Section 611 ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ).

metadata.full_snippet: Company : Rocket Mortgage ( Rocket Companies ) Product : Mortgage ( Conventional home mortgage ). Issue : Trouble during payment process On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, our mortgage payment of {$4600.00} was initiated via autopay from the Rocket Mortgage portal. We received a confirmation email from Rocket Mortgage on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> stating the payment had been applied. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, the payment of {$4600.00} successfully withdrew from our [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] bank account. Rocket Mortgage subsequently reversed the payment citing " insufficient funds '', a claim that is false and directly contradicted by our bank records, which show the funds were withdrawn and never returned to our account. After receiving a call from Rocket Mortgage on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] that we had an overdue balance, They requested we submit bank statements as evidence that our payment was applied, that there were sufficient funds in that account, and that the payment was never returned to our account nor was " reversed ''. We sent those statements in an email on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. We received a call on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] from Rocket Mortgage again telling us we had an overdue balance. We informed them that we had already contacted them about this issue, they claimed to have never received that email with the bank statement attachments and we forwarded it again on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, we received confirmation that this email was received and that this issue was under review and to please allow them up to 7 days for review. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, we called Rocket Mortgage to ask for an update. We were promised a resolution by [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> and that date passed with no resolution. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], we received a letter stating " We received your inquiry on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, regarding the above-referenced loan. Unfortunately, the research required for your inquiry will likely exceed the 30 business days that we anticipated we would need to resolve the request. Our analysts continue to work toward resolving your issue, and we will remain in contact with you as we work toward a resolution, which will be provided within 15 business days of the original 30 business day deadline. '' Despite this, Rocket Mortgage has treated our account as delinquent for over three months, resulting in : repeated automated and live collections calls ; a certified delinquency letter mailed to us ; a debt collector voicemail left on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ; a representative calling us and mentioning foreclosure of our account on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ; and being transferred and disconnected via phone five times in a single day ( [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ) while attempting to reach a supervisor to resolve this issue as soon as possible. We sent an email to them on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] asking for immediate resolution. They replied to our email on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] that states a response, not even a resolution, will be received no later than [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, over four months after the original error. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> Rocket Mortgage 's research team sent an email to us without a subject line ( that was subsequently marked as spam and unseen for several days ) stating that the bank statement that was sent was insufficient because it was not a " full '' statement, although it did include all of the relevant account information. Upon discovering it in the spam folder, we replied on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] with a full bank statement including all bank accounts on the statement, however we did not receive a response. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], we received another live call claiming we had an overdue balance and the representative confirmed that the case had been marked as resolved after the email without a subject line had been sent. The representative started a new case for us and told us to wait 5 to 7 business days for a response from their research team. Throughout this, we have continued to consistently pay our full monthly payment. Despite this, our account still states we are {$3000.00} overdue with accumulating late fees since the first error in [Redacted]. Additionally, since this error began, we have been unable to make extra principal-only payments, as those payments are being miscategorized by Rocket Mortgage 's system. Extra principal payments directly reduce our outstanding loan balance, which reduces the interest that accrues each month. Being blocked from making these payments means we are accruing more interest than we should be, a measurable ongoing financial loss that compounds the longer this error goes unresolved.

metadata.full_snippet: I am a confirmed successor in interest on a mortgage serviced by LoanCare. The borrower is deceased, and the associated estate has been closed for approximately two years. LoanCare has repeatedly failed to properly issue an escrow overage refund. Despite confirming my successor in interest status, LoanCare continues issuing the escrow refund check payable to the closed estate instead of to me directly. I previously notified LoanCare that the original check was incorrectly issued. LoanCare later stated that a replacement check had been processed, but the replacement was also improperly made payable to the estate. metadata.full_snippet: Dear Sir or Madam, I am submitting this complaint regarding force-placed insurance charges added to my mortgage account by Bank of America [Redacted] In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], prior to closing on my newly constructed home, I proactively purchased homeowners insurance based on the builders estimated closing timeline at that time. However, the builder repeatedly delayed the closing date, and the home did not actually close until early [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Because of the construction and closing delays, the original insurance policy was ultimately cancelled and refunded since the transaction had not yet closed and the premium was not processed through escrow/title as initially expected. Around the time of closing, I received an insurance refund and reasonably believed the refund was related to escrow/title payment reconciliation or duplicate payment adjustments associated with the delayed closing process. I was not aware that there was any lapse in homeowners insurance coverage after closing. Most importantly, Bank of America did not notify me during [Redacted] that there was any issue with insurance coverage or any alleged lapse. Had I been notified promptly at that time, I would have immediately reinstated or replaced the policy. Instead, I did not receive notice from Bank of America regarding this issue until [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], after Bank of America had already retroactively imposed force-placed insurance coverage for a prior period. Bank of America is now charging me {$3100.00} in force-placed insurance premium for coverage that was purchased retroactively for the prior year. I understand the lenders right to protect its collateral interest. However, the delayed notification deprived me of any meaningful opportunity to cure the issue in real time. This situation was not caused by intentional neglect or refusal to maintain insurance, but rather by builder delays, escrow/title timing confusion, and the absence of timely communication from the servicer. I respectfully request that Bank of America : [Redacted]. Conduct a full review of the force-placed insurance charges and coverage timeline ; [Redacted]. Provide documentation showing all notices allegedly sent regarding the insurance lapse and force-placed coverage ; [Redacted]. Reconsider and reduce or waive the {$3100.00} retroactive force-placed insurance premium based on the circumstances and delayed notification ; [Redacted] Review whether the retroactive coverage period and premium assessed were reasonable and necessary. I am seeking a fair and reasonable resolution based on the facts and timeline of this situation. Regards, [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint against MOHELA, my federal student loan servicer, for billing me an incorrect payment amount that is inconsistent with my approved Income-Driven Repayment ( PAYE ) plan, and for failing to provide any notification regarding my recertification or payment amount. BACKGROUND : I have a federal student loan balance of {$210000.00} serviced by MOHELA. I am enrolled in the Pay As You Earn ( PAYE ) Income-Driven Repayment plan. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], an automatic IDR recertification was initiated on my behalf. The recertification was reviewed and completed by MOHELA on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. My approved monthly payment under the [Redacted] plan, as confirmed by my Federal Student Aid account at [Redacted], is {$780.00} per month. THE ERROR : My billing statement for my [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] payment, following the completed recertification reflects a payment due of {$1800.00} almost {$1100.00} above my approved IDR payment of {$780.00}. MOHELA has provided no explanation for this amount and has not identified what repayment plan or calculation method was used to arrive at {$1800.00}. FAILURE TO NOTIFY : At no point did MOHELA send me any communication, by email, postal mail, or portal message, regarding my recertification, my approved payment amount, or the {$1800.00} billing amount. I only became aware of my approved {$780.00} payment by independently checking my [Redacted] account. I became aware of the {$1800.00} billing amount only upon receiving my my most recent billing statement. This failure to communicate violates federal servicing requirements. IMPACT : The difference between the incorrect billing amount and my approved payment is {$1000.00} per month. If left uncorrected, this would result in me being overbilled by {$13000.00} annually. I am a Massachusetts resident and this error places a significant and unlawful financial burden on me. ACTIONS TAKEN : On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I submitted a written dispute through MOHELA 's online portal requesting immediate correction of my payment to {$780.00}, a written explanation of the {$1800.00} figure, and a processing forbearance to protect my account during the dispute. I am simultaneously filing a formal Notice of Error by certified mail and complaints with the Massachusetts Attorney General 's Student Loan Assistance Unit and the FSA Ombudsman. RESOLUTION REQUESTED : 1. Immediate correction of my monthly payment to {$780.00} as approved under my PAYE recertification completed [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] ; 2. A written explanation from MOHELA identifying the basis for the {$1800.00} billing amount ; 3. Confirmation that no late fees, penalties, or negative credit reporting will be applied to my account as a result of this error ; 4. A processing forbearance applied to my account for the duration of this dispute.

metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted] [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, Citibank [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], via [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], initiated a wire transfer of USD [Redacted] from the deceased estates wealth management account to a beneficiary estate account at [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ( Transaction Ref : [Redacted] ). As of [Redacted] [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> ( 85 days later ), [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] confirmed in writing that the funds were never received. Citibank/[Redacted] reported : they made four trace requests ( [Redacted] [Redacted], early [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted], and [Redacted] [Redacted] ) to the receiving bank. A formal recall was also submitted on [Redacted] [Redacted] ; however, no substantive response was received from the receiving bank on either request. [Redacted] [Redacted], VP of Beneficiary Services, informed me on [Redacted] [Redacted] that the funds were " no longer at Citi '' and that she had " no transparency '' into their current status. Wealth management stated they had done everything possible. I independently contacted [Redacted] [Redacted] via their public help desk. [Redacted] [Redacted] responded that I am a third party and that only Citibank/[Redacted] may escalate directly. Despite this, Citibank/[Redacted] did not escalate beyond these routine wire trace requests. There was no escalation to [Redacted] [Redacted] compliance or investigations teams, despite my repeated requests. Most concerning, no definitive confirmation has been provided that the funds left [Redacted] [Redacted] or were routed onward. [Redacted] [Redacted] confirmed that their estate account is open and ready to receive international wires, but no proof was provided by Citibank that the funds left [Redacted] or that a resolution is underway.

metadata.full_snippet: Re : Formal Demand for Deletion of Improper Child Support Reporting, Notice of FCRA Violations, Conflicting Reporting Practices, and Preservation of Evidence This correspondence serves as a formal demand for immediate deletion of the child support tradeline currently being reported on my consumer credit file by Equifax. The reporting of this account is inaccurate, misleading, obsolete, and in violation of multiple provisions of the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., as well as related consumer protection obligations. The account at issue has remained on my Equifax consumer report for more than seven ( 7 ) years and three ( 3 ) months. Although Equifax attempted to merely mark or classify the account as closed, that action does not cure the underlying reporting violations. I do not consent to continued reporting of this tradeline in any form, including as a closed account, and I specifically demand complete deletion from my consumer file. Despite disputes submitted regarding the accuracy, completeness, and legal reporting status of this account, Equifax has continued furnishing damaging and misleading information while failing to conduct a lawful and reasonable reinvestigation. Specifically, Equifax has failed to : * Properly investigate disputed information as required under 15 U.S.C. 1681i ; * Maintain maximum possible accuracy under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ; * Correct or delete inaccurate, unverifiable, or obsolete information; * Provide complete and accurate reporting regarding payment history and account status ; * Ensure that continued reporting complies with federal consumer protection standards and fair furnishing requirements. Additionally, the reporting of this account appears materially misleading because the payment history is incomplete, inconsistent, stale, or non-updated, creating a false and damaging impression regarding the status of the alleged obligation. Reporting information in a manner that is technically incomplete or materially misleading may constitute inaccurate reporting under the FCRA. Further, any state practices, agency policies, internal procedures, or reporting customs that conflict with the protections guaranteed under the FCRA are preempted by federal law pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1681t. Federal law supersedes any inconsistent state action or furnishing practice that permits inaccurate, misleading, unverifiable, or unlawfully prolonged credit reporting. To the extent the Ohio child support enforcement authorities, contractors, or affiliated agencies are furnishing information in a manner inconsistent with the FCRA, such conduct may violate : * 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) Duty to provide accurate information; * 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Duty to conduct reasonable investigation after notice of dispute ; * 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Requirement to follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy; * 15 U.S.C. 1681i Requirement to reinvestigate disputed information; * 15 U.S.C. 1681n Civil liability for willful noncompliance; * 15 U.S.C. 1681o Civil liability for negligent noncompliance; * 15 U.S.C. 1681t Federal preemption of inconsistent state laws and practices. Additionally, any attempt to continue reporting inaccurate or obsolete information under color of state authority may implicate constitutional due process concerns under the Fourteenth Amendment where inaccurate reporting results in continuing financial harm, reputational damage, denial of credit opportunities, or improper collection activity. To the extent wage garnishment or collection activity continued improperly after [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> without accurate accounting, lawful verification, or proper adjustment, such conduct further supports the existence of inaccurate furnishing and potential statutory violations requiring judicial review. You are hereby placed on notice to preserve all records related to this account, including but not limited to : * Consumer disclosures; * Dispute records ; * [Redacted] communications ; * Furnisher verification records; * Internal notes ; * Payment histories; * Audit trails; * Methods of verification ; * Furnisher correspondence ; * Metadata associated with reinvestigations. Failure to preserve such evidence after receipt of this notice may constitute spoliation of evidence. Accordingly, I demand the following within thirty ( 30 ) days of receipt of this letter : 1. Immediate deletion of the disputed child support tradeline from my Equifax consumer report ; 2. Written confirmation of deletion ; 3. A complete description of all investigative procedures used regarding my disputes ; 4. Identification of every furnisher, employee, contractor, or third party involved in verification of the account ; 5. Copies of all records relied upon to continue reporting this information. Should Equifax fail to comply, I am prepared to pursue all available remedies, including : * Filing and supplementing complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau; * Seeking review by state and federal regulatory authorities; * Pursuing claims for statutory, actual, and punitive damages; * Seeking attorneys fees and costs where applicable; * Initiating litigation for willful and negligent noncompliance under the FCRA and other applicable laws. Nothing in this notice constitutes a waiver of any rights, claims, remedies, or causes of action, all of which are expressly reserved.

metadata.full_snippet: FDCPA 15 U.S.C. 1692g & 15 U.S.C. 1692c ( c ) Section 1 Purpose of This Notice This document serves as both : A formal request for debt verification under 15 U.S.C. 1692g, and A cease and desist demand under 15 U.S.C. 1692c ( c ). I dispute the alleged debt referenced by your company and request full verification. Section 2 Required Debt Verification ( FDCPA 1692g ) Please provide the following documentation : Original creditor information Full account number associated with the alleged debt Itemized breakdown of all amounts claimed ( principal, interest, fees, penalties ) Copy of the original signed contract or agreement Proof of your legal authority to collect ( chain of title, assignment, purchase records ) Date of alleged default Date of last payment Statement confirming whether the debt is within the statute of limitations Your state license number ( s ) and collection jurisdictions Until this information is provided, you must cease all collection activity, including credit reporting. Section 3 Cease and Desist Demand ( FDCPA 1692c ( c ) ) Effective immediately, you must stop all communication with me regarding this alleged debt. Under federal law, you may only contact me to : Confirm that collection efforts are being terminated, or Notify me of specific legal remedies you may lawfully pursue Any other communicationincluding calls, letters, emails, texts, or thirdparty contactwill constitute a violation of federal law. You are also instructed not to contact my employer, family, neighbors, or any third parties. Section 4 Notice of Intent to Report Violations If you continue collection efforts without providing verification, or if you contact me in violation of this cease and desist notice, I will file complaints with : The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) The Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) My State Attorney General I will also pursue all remedies available under the FDCPA, including statutory damages.

metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this complaint regarding the reporting and servicing of my student loan accounts serviced by MOHELA. During the period when my student loan forbearance was ending and my loans were being transferred between servicers, I experienced significant confusion and lack of access regarding who serviced my loans and how to access my accounts for payment. I did not receive adequate or timely information allowing me to properly transition my accounts and resume payments without interruption. As a result, multiple late payments, including 120+ day late reporting, were added across several student loan accounts during the same concentrated time period. I dispute the accuracy and fairness of this reporting because : * I was actively attempting to determine the correct servicer and regain account access * I experienced difficulty accessing account information during the transfer period * Notices regarding the transfer and payment obligations were inadequate and/or untimely * The late reporting occurred during a narrow transition period rather than as a long-term pattern of nonpayment * My accounts are now current and in good standing I am requesting a full investigation into : * The servicing transfer timeline * All notices allegedly sent regarding transfer of servicing and end of forbearance * Account access availability during the transfer period * Payment posting history * Whether proper servicing procedures and notification requirements were followed * The accuracy of all late payment reporting during this transition period I also request review of whether these late payments were improperly reported during a period of servicing disruption and lack of reasonable account access. If errors, servicing failures, inadequate notice, or reporting inaccuracies are identified, I request correction or removal of the associated late payment reporting from all consumer reporting agencies. These derogatory marks are significantly impacting my credit profile and ability to qualify for a mortgage despite my accounts currently being in good standing.

After reviewing my credit reports and the attached dispute letters, I identified multiple accounts reporting late payments, collections, and/or charge-offs that ...
metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting a complaint regarding inaccurate and misleading information being reported on my consumer credit file. After reviewing my credit reports and the attached dispute letters, I identified multiple accounts reporting late payments, collections, and/or charge-offs that appear inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable. Pursuant to the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), consumer reporting agencies are required to maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy of all information reported. Additionally, under 15 U.S.C. 1681i, disputed information must be properly investigated and corrected or deleted if it can not be verified with complete accuracy. These inaccuracies may be connected to compromised consumer information and recent data breach activity affecting financial institutions, furnishers, and consumer reporting systems. Because of these concerns, I am requesting a lawful reinvestigation of all disputed accounts referenced in my attached correspondence. The late payment reporting appearing on certain accounts does not accurately reflect my records and is unfairly damaging my credit standing. Additionally, the collections and charge-off accounts being reported appear inaccurate, misleading, duplicated, incomplete, and/or unverifiable. The continued reporting of this derogatory information is causing significant financial harm.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint against ( CRI ), [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], an alleged federal student loan debt previously serviced by [Redacted]. CRI has violated the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) by continuing aggressive collection activity, including credit reporting and threats of legal action, while completely ignoring [Redacted] formal written validation requests. TIMELINE OF EVENTS : [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : I sent CRI a formal written Debt Validation Request via certified mail under 15 U.S.C. 1692g, disputing the debt in its entirety and requesting full validation documentation, including proof of ownership, the original promissory note, a complete payment ledger, chain of title, and loan forgiveness records. CRI did not respond. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : Having received no response, I sent a second written validation request documenting CRI 's noncompliance and noting that continued collection while the debt was disputed violated 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ). CRI again sent no documentation. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : I called [Redacted] and spoke with a representative named [Redacted]. [Redacted] confirmed that CRI had received both of my written letters but stated they did not respond in writing because " it is better to do it by phone. '' [Redacted] claimed she was submitting my request and that I would receive the documentation. I have never received anything- not a single document, not even written confirmation of this call. [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] : Despite [Redacted] unanswered written validation requests, CRI sent me a collection letter stating my account is 180 days past due, threatening continued delinquent reporting to national consumer reporting agencies, threatening legal action including liens and garnishment of wages, and threatening referral to additional collection agencies. This letter contains no acknowledgment that the debt is disputed. VIOLATIONS : [Redacted]. Violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) : CRI has continued collection activity - including billing, credit reporting, and threats - without providing any validation of the debt after receiving [Redacted] written disputes. This is a direct and documented violation of the FDCPA. [Redacted]. Violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 8 ) : CRI 's representative misrepresented that a phone call satisfies the written validation requirement under federal law. It does not. CRI also communicated credit information while knowing the debt was disputed without disclosing the disputed status, which constitutes a false and misleading representation. [Redacted]. Violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 3 ) ( FCRA ) : CRI has reported this account to national consumer reporting agencies as delinquent. As a furnisher who has been formally notified of a consumer dispute, CRI is required to include the dispute status in all credit reporting. I have no evidence this has been done. ADDITIONAL CONTEXT : [Redacted], the prior servicer, has a documented history of inaccurate recordkeeping, misapplied payments, and improper transfer errors, including a multi-state settlement in [Redacted]. This history makes full chain-of-title and transfer documentation essential to validating any claimed balance. I have requested this documentation twice in writing. CRI has provided nothing. I have copies of both validation letters with proof of delivery, notes from my [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] call including the representative 's name, and CRI 's [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] collection letter, all of which I can provide as supporting documentation.

metadata.full_snippet: I own a roofing company, [Redacted] [Redacted], and in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> we purchased another [Redacted] truck for our Delaware office and sales team. We currently own and maintain [Redacted] other [Redacted] trucks, all financed through [Redacted] [Redacted] and all maintained in good standing with automatic payments. When purchasing this truck, the dealership arranged financing through Chase Auto. Because all of our previous vehicles were financed through [Redacted] [Redacted], I mistakenly assumed this vehicle was as well and expected the payments to be included with our existing automatic payment setup. At the same time, the registration and mailing address used for the vehicle was tied to a temporary Delaware office location that we lost access to almost immediately after purchasing the truck due to relocating offices. As a result, all physical correspondence and billing notices were being sent to an address we no longer had access to. After missing the initial payments, I eventually received a notification regarding a Chase Auto loan that I did not recognize. I genuinely believed it may have been fraudulent activity or identity theft, so I immediately contacted Chase. During that call, I learned the loan was tied to the truck purchase and was informed the account had become delinquent. As soon as I realized the situation, I immediately brought the account current, paid both missed payments, and also paid over {$1500.00} in accrued interest without dispute. The monthly payments on this vehicle are approximately {$4000.00}, and since that time every payment has been made on time. I contacted customer service immediately after resolving the account and explained the circumstances surrounding the missed payments. This was a genuine oversight and not a result of unwillingness or inability to pay. Prior to this incident, I had not missed a payment on any account in over [Redacted] years and had worked extremely hard to rebuild and maintain strong personal and business credit. Unfortunately, these [Redacted] missed payments caused my credit score to drop from approximately [Redacted] to nearly [Redacted]. While I have worked hard to recover my score to around [Redacted], the delinquency marks continue to report as serious late payments and have already resulted in multiple financing denials. I fully understand the importance of accurate credit reporting and I take responsibility for the mistake. However, given the circumstances, my immediate corrective action, my long-standing positive payment history, and the fact that the account has remained current since, I am respectfully requesting a one-time goodwill adjustment to remove these delinquency marks from my credit report. I sincerely appreciate your time, consideration, and willingness to review my situation.

metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I spoke to a customer service representative at Synchrony regarding interest that was charged on my CareCredit credit card statement. I was advised that a purchase made at my vet was not on a promo plan. Ok- my fault. No dispute of past interest charges were made. Instead, I made it very clear that I wanted to pay off the balance of that transaction. I agreed to make the payment of {$1000.00} over the phone IF and only IF it was credited to that balance so no more interest would be charged. I was VERY clear that the funds were to be directed there and I would not be paying any more interest to that balance. The representative stated that it is Synchronys policy to apply the payment as requested but that it could take 2-3 payment cycles to occur in which case interest would still be charged. No information that the payment would be retroactively applied and interest removed when the payment was applied correctly. I again made it very clear that they cant charge interest against funds paid on the balance and if they charge me Id be filing a complaint. So here we are. Despite my payment, I was charged interest on that balance just 6 days later. They can take my funds but dont want to credit the correct balance until months later in order to collect more money. Im sure they will respond that this is due to system limitations. Thats fine but not retroactively refunding interest is predatory. I wonder how many hundreds of thousands of accounts have been affected by this practice. I know how these complaints work. I want this practice brought to life for the problem that it is and I want my interest refunded with the payment applied correctly. Also - regulators- please note that synchrony has a practice of retaliation against consumers who make complaints. Im sure my cards will now be closed and/or credit limits lowered to affect my credit score despite being an A credit consumer. Synchrony- fix my account. You know its wrong. Credit my payment appropriately and refund all interest since [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Please do not grant an extension to respond. This is an easy issue to correct. Im also requesting publication as Im sure many consumers face this same predatory practice.

metadata.full_snippet: Despite multiple disputes submitted with supporting documentation, the bureau has continued to report inaccurate and unverifiable information. The bureau has shown a pattern of willful noncompliance with the FCRA, specifically 15 U.S.C. 1681n. Under 1681i, the bureau must conduct a reasonable reinvestigation and delete or correct information that can not be verified. Instead, the disputed accounts and inquiries were re-reported without competent verification. The bureaus persistence in publishing unverifiable data after repeated notice reflects reckless disregard of its statutory duties, resulting in ongoing consumer harm, including adverse credit decisions and increased costs. This pattern meets the willfulness threshold under 1681n and warrants immediate deletion of the unverifiable items, corrective disclosures, and appropriate remedial measures.

 Protect customer funds and securities

metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this complaint to request correction and resolution of inaccurate and unverified information currently appearing on my consumer credit report. Several items being reported are incorrect, incomplete, or lack proper verification, including inaccurate payment history, unauthorized inquiries, collection reporting without sufficient documentation, and incorrect personal information. These errors are negatively impacting my credit profile and do not meet the legal standards required under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). Under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), consumer reporting agencies are required to follow reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy. The continued reporting of inaccurate late payments, unverified accounts, and incorrect personal data demonstrates a failure to comply with this obligation. I previously disputed these items directly with the credit reporting agency and/or furnishers and requested proper investigation and documentation. However, the reporting remains unchanged, and I have not received adequate proof validating the accuracy of the disputed information. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681i, credit reporting agencies must conduct a reasonable reinvestigation and delete or correct any information that can not be verified. In addition, any credit inquiries reported without proof of permissible purpose violate 15 U.S.C. 1681b and must be removed. metadata.full_snippet: requested a replacement debit card from Wells Fargo due to physical damage/wear. The bank mailed the new plastic, but it never arrived at my address ; it was intercepted and stolen from the mail. Wells Fargos system automatically denied my fraud claim, arguing that the transactions are valid because the card number remained the same. However, the bank is completely ignoring the fact that the newly issued plastic required activation and featured a completely different expiration date and CVV security codedata that I never possessed or activated. This is a clear case of mail theft and identity fraud. The total unauthorized amount is {$670.00}. Wells Fargo initially provided a provisional credit of {$110.00}, but they have now notified me that they intend to reverse and debit this provisional credit back from my account, while denying the remainder of the total disputed amount. I never received this card, I did not activate it, and I did not authorize any of these transactions. I have filed a formal police report regarding this mail theft and identity fraud. Under federal law ( Regulation E / Electronic Fund Transfer Act ), I am protected against unauthorized electronic fund transfers, and the bank is failing to conduct a proper and fair investigation by relying on an automated system error. I request a permanent reversal of the {$110.00} debit and a full credit for the remaining balance, totaling {$670.00}.

The Direct Consolidation Loan program is authorized under the Higher Education Act and implementing regulations, including 20 U.S.C. 1087e ( g ) and 34 C.F.R. 685.220. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), after receiving notice of a dispute from a consumer reporting agency, a furnisher must conduct an investigation, review all relevant information provided, report the results of the investigation, and correct, delete, or permanently block information that is found to be inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable. That case is directly relevant here because the issue is not merely whether a default notation exists in isolation, but whether the continued default status accurately and fairly reflects the full circumstances, including my pending consolidation application, the lack of meaningful notice, and the servicers failure to timely process or explain the treatment of all eligible loans. Fourth, the conduct described in this complaint raises concerns under the prohibition against unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices. Under the Consumer Financial Protection Act, 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 5536, covered persons and service providers are prohibited from engaging in unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices in connection with consumer financial products or services. A practice may be unfair when it causes or is likely to cause substantial injury to the consumer, the injury is not reasonably avoidable, and the injury is not outweighed by countervailing benefits to consumers or competition. metadata.full_snippet: I dispute Consumer Adjustment Companys response because it does not address the specific validation and verification requests submitted through my CFPB complaint and attached validation letter. My complaint requested documentation necessary to validate the alleged debt under the FDCPA, including : A complete copy of the original signed contract or agreement creating the alleged obligation ; A full itemized account history, including all charges, payments, interest, fees, adjustments, and charge-offs ; Documentation establishing ownership or authority to collect the debt, including any purchase or assignment agreements ; The name and address of the original creditor ; and Copies of prior notices and communications, including the validation notice required by federal law. Additionally, I requested information necessary to verify the accuracy and completeness of the reporting under the FCRA, including : The Date of First Delinquency ( DOFD ) ; The charge-off date ; The assignment or purchase date ; The complete data set maintained and reported for the account ; and The investigation procedures used to verify the disputed information. Consumer Adjustment Companys response states that it contacted the creditor and requested validation and that the account was removed from [Redacted]. However, the response does not demonstrate that the requested validation documents were provided to me, nor does it address the specific records and verification items requested in my complaint. A statement that information was requested from the creditor is not the same as providing the documentation necessary to validate the debt. The response also does not explain what investigation procedures were used, does not provide the requested ownership documentation, and does not address the remaining FDCPA and FCRA requests outlined in my submission. Because the requested validation and verification information has not been fully provided, I continue to dispute the validity, ownership, and reporting accuracy of this account.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint because [ Central Portfolio Control ] is reporting an inaccurate, predatory, and damaging collection account on my credit report and is engaging in illegal, abusive collection practices. This account stems from my enrollment at [ [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ].
