Immediately after my cohort graduated, the company completely disbanded the program, revealing it to be a short-term scam designed solely to secure financing from students before abandoning them without career infrastructure or valid credentials. The fundamental issue is that this debt was predatory and fraudulent from its inception. I am invoking the [Redacted] [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> stipulated final judgment against [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. [Redacted] ). They are calling me nonstop in an abusive, harassing manner. They have repeatedly threatened to take me to court to intimidate me, yet they refuse to cooperate, validate the true underlying terms, or consider any reasonable settlement options to resolve the dispute. At no point did any statement indicate that additional fees had accrued on my total amo...
metadata.full_snippet: As of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, my loan reached maturity. Throughout the life of the loan, every statement I received consistently reflected the regular monthly payment amount of {$130.00}. At no point did any statement indicate that additional fees had accrued on my total amount due. On Saturday, I received a phone call informing me that my account now has a balloon payment of {$970.00} due to 37 alleged late payments. This information came as a complete surprise, as I was never notified of any late payments by phone, mail, or through my monthly statements. Furthermore, none of the statements I received ever reflected late fees being added to my monthly payment amount. After receiving this information, I submitted a formal complaint with the company on Saturday. However, I was not informed at that time that the complaint review process could take up to 30 days. It was only when I contacted the company again today for an update that I learned of this timeline. The balloon payment is due by the [Redacted] of this month, and I have been advised that failure to pay by that date could negatively impact my credit score. This effectively provides me with only 14 days to address a substantial and unexpected balance while my complaint remains under review. When I originally established this loan, I was informed that payments could only be made either by phone or through my bank. I have consistently made payments through my bank as instructed. However, I was unaware that the processing time for those payments may have resulted in them being received late by the company. Additionally, I recently learned that the company does not offer any grace period for payments, a policy that I find unreasonable given that many financial obligations and billing arrangements commonly provide some form of grace period. I was also informed for the first time on Saturday that the company has an online payment system. My understanding is that this system has only been available for about one year. Even so, the online portal appears to serve only as a payment platform and does not provide account details regarding accrued late fees or other charges that may affect the loan balance. Given these circumstances, I am extremely concerned by the lack of notification regarding the alleged late payments and the resulting balloon payment now being demanded with very limited notice. I believe this situation warrants a thorough review and a fair resolution.

metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I received a notice ( EX-01 ) stating that loan forgiveness would be processed in the coming months and providing an [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> deadline to decline forgiveness. The notice described forgiveness as a future process, stated that information would be sent to loan servicers after the opt-out deadline, and presented the deadline as an actionable decision point for borrowers. However, a subsequent forgiveness confirmation ( EX-03 ) stated that the forgiveness was effective as of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. The [Redacted] Ombudsman later confirmed that [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> was the effective date of forgiveness ( EX-05 ). A credit reporting record ( S-1 ) reflects later reporting activity associated with the same account, highlighting the existence of multiple dates in the record and contributing to questions regarding when the forgiveness became effective, when it was processed, and what actions remained available to the borrower during that period. Because the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> notice presented forgiveness as a future process with an [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> deadline, I sought clarification regarding how that notice could be reconciled with an asserted [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> effective date. Specifically, I requested clarification regarding what actions remained available to borrowers between [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> and [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, what notice was provided prior to the asserted effective date, and what authority governed the notice and opt-out process. The record also contains correspondence stating that account adjustments could result in reinstatement of the loan ( EX-02 ). However, subsequent responses from the loan servicer stated that it could not reopen the discharged consolidation loan, did not administer the one-time IDR adjustment, and did not control the underlying count or discharge process ( EX-04 ). As a result, I requested clarification regarding the circumstances under which reinstatement may occur and which office possesses authority to review, approve, deny, or otherwise address such requests. The Ombudsman response concluded that no further action could be taken regarding the discharged consolidation loan ( EX-05 ). However, the response did not directly address the specific factual questions raised by the record regarding timing, notice, available borrower actions, authority, and the reinstatement pathway. Those questions are summarized in EX-06. In addition, a Department of Education FOIA request seeking servicing correspondence and related account records remains pending ( S-2 ). According to the Department 's FOIA office, records are still being sought from the program office. Those records may help clarify the timeline of communications, notices, and servicing activity associated with this matter. I am seeking clarification regarding the timeline reflected in the record, the notice provided to borrowers, the actions that remained available after the asserted [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> effective date, the reinstatement language contained in the record, and the office responsible for these determinations.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing a complaint regarding deferred interest charges assessed on my promotional financing account with Comenity Capital Bank. I accepted a promotional financing plan that was presented to me as payments over a two-year period. My understanding was that I would make the required payments during those [Redacted] years. I enrolled in automatic payments and consistently made my payments throughout the promotional period. I often paid more than the minimum payment due and acted in good faith at all times. I was shocked to discover that approximately {$2600.00} in deferred interest charges were added to my account when there was only about {$580.00} remaining on the balance. These charges were unexpected and disproportionate to the remaining amount owed. I believe the marketing and explanation of the financing program were confusing and did not clearly communicate the consequences of having a remaining balance at the end of the promotional period. I do not recall being clearly informed that a relatively small unpaid balance could result in thousands of dollars in deferred interest charges. I was enrolled in electronic communications and automatic payments and did not receive a clear warning that [Redacted] my attention to the approaching promotional expiration date or the significant financial consequences that would result if the balance was not paid in full. I attempted to resolve this matter directly with Comenity Capital Bank. I submitted disputes and contacted customer service multiple times. However, I felt that my concerns were not properly addressed and that I was repeatedly redirected rather than provided with a meaningful review of my situation. I was ultimately told to submit additional written disputes after previous disputes had already been denied. Additionally, I am still in the process of receiving the services associated with the financing arrangement, making these unexpected charges even more concerning. I respectfully request that the CFPB review whether the promotional financing terms, disclosures, marketing, and customer service practices were fair and adequately communicated. I also request that Comenity Capital Bank reconsider the deferred interest charges and provide appropriate relief based on my payment history, good-faith efforts to repay the account, and the circumstances described above. Thank you for your time and consideration.

During this period, I contacted Aidvantage multiple times and applied for hardship assistance, including requests for forbearance, deferment, or other payment relief options. Despite my repeated efforts to obtain assistance and avoid delinquency, my requests were denied. Because I was unable to afford the payments and was not provided the relief options I requested, my account became delinquent and late payments were reported to the credit bureaus. I now have [Redacted] late payment entries on my credit report. These negative credit reporting entries have had a severe impact on my financial stability. I have been unable to obtain loans and financing needed for personal and transportation-related matters, and this situation is affecting my livelihood, employment opportunities, and mental well-being. My student loan account is now current and up to date. I am requesting that Aidvantage and the CFPB review the handling of my hardship requests and the resulting credit reporting. I believe my repeated attempts to seek assistance before falling behind should have been given appropriate consideration. I respectfully request : - A full review of my hardship assistance requests and the decisions made on those requests. - An investigation into whether the servicing of my account complied with applicable student loan servicing requirements. - Correction or removal of the late payment reporting associated with the period during which I was seeking hardship assistance, if appropriate. - A written explanation of why my requests for forbearance, deferment, or other relief were denied. I am prepared to provide supporting documentation, including records of my communications with Aidvantage, copies of hardship requests, and proof that my account is now current.

Without this information, I am unable to determine whether the closure resulted from a misunderstanding, an error in their review process, or possible unauthorized activity involving my account. I respectfully request that Cash App provide : 1. A detailed explanation of the specific Terms of Service violation they believe occurred. 2. The date ( s ) and transaction ( s ) related to the alleged violation. 3. Confirmation of whether the account closure was the result of an automated review or a manual investigation. 4. A fair review of my account and an opportunity to appeal the decision if appropriate. I have attempted to obtain clarification but have not received a meaningful explanation. I am requesting the CFPBs assistance in obtaining information regarding this account closure and ensuring that Cash App responds to my concerns. Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing this complaint regarding [Redacted] handling of a fraudulent transaction and its failure to adequately respond to my concerns. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, a payment of {$12000.00} was made toward my Citibank loan account ( # [Redacted] ). Before releasing the item that was being sold, I contacted Citibank on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, to verify that the payment had been received. Citibank confirmed the payment. I contacted Citibank a second time on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, the day the embroidery machine was delivered to the buyer, and Citibank again confirmed that the payment had been received. Based on these confirmations, I released my embroidery machine ( [Redacted] [Redacted], Serial Number [Redacted] ) to the buyer. I later learned that the payment was reversed on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. However, Citibank never notified me that the payment had been reversed. I did not receive any alert, email, letter, phone call, or other communication informing me that the payment had been canceled. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, when I contacted Citibank to pay the remaining balance on my loan, I discovered for the first time that the {$12000.00} payment had been reversed. This was [Redacted] days after the reversal occurred and [Redacted] days after I had delivered the machine based on Citibanks payment confirmations. As a result, I suffered a financial loss of {$12000.00}. Subsequently, law enforcement investigated the matter and determined that the payment was connected to identity theft. The owner of the account used for the payment was a victim of identity theft from New Mexico. Law enforcement informed me that this victim has also been connected to similar fraudulent activity affecting other states and that the suspect appears to be involved in a broader pattern of fraud. My concern is not only the fraud committed by the suspect, but also Citibanks failure to notify me when the payment was reversed. Had I been notified promptly on or shortly after [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I could have taken immediate action to attempt recovery of the machine and protect myself from further loss. I submitted a formal written complaint to Citibank by certified mail. The bank received my correspondence, but I have not received a satisfactory response regarding : * Why I was not notified when the payment was reversed. * What policies governed the handling of this transaction. * Whether Citibank reviewed the circumstances surrounding the reversal. * What steps, if any, were taken to protect me as the account holder. I respectfully request that Citibank provide a complete written explanation regarding the reversal of the payment, the lack of notification, and the banks handling of this matter. I also request that Citibank review whether its actions or omissions contributed to my financial loss. Thank you for your assistance.

metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this complaint regarding Aqua Finance , Inc. concerning a roofing loan that was originally obtained for a property owned by my late mother. The roofing work was performed by [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. Although the actual cost of the roof was approximately {$18000.00} the financing amount through Aqua Finance exceeded {$22000.00}. Over the years, despite payments being made, the balance failed to decrease appropriately, and excessive interest and additional charges continued to be added. After my mother 's death, Aqua Finance began attempting to hold me personally responsible for the remaining balance, claiming that because I was listed as a point of contact and successor in interest of the property not the borrower, I am liable for the debt. I dispute this claim. I never signed as a borrower, co-borrower, guarantor, or otherwise agreed to assume this obligation. Merely being identified as a contact person or successor in interest does not create personal liability for this account. Furthermore, I have reason to believe that the account was charged off years ago and that Aqua Finance received payment through insurance or other means. Despite this, the company continues to pursue collection activities and has repeatedly attempted to report this debt on my credit report. They have also attempted to report the debt under my deceased mother 's credit file, although such attempts have reportedly been rejected. Although I am not legally obligated on this debt and never knowingly executed or assumed responsibility for the underlying loan, I nevertheless made payments to Aqua Finance because of their persistent collection efforts, repeated harassment, and my fear that they would improperly damage my credit standing. These payments were made under duress and solely to avoid the consequences of continued collection activity and adverse credit reporting. To the extent that Aqua Finance relies upon any documents purporting to establish my liability, I dispute the authenticity and validity of such documents and do not acknowledge them as binding upon me. Any information I provided to Aqua Finance was communicated verbally over the telephone, which in [Redacted] I recognize I should not have done, and such communications should not be interpreted as an admission of liability, an assumption of the debt, or a waiver of any rights or defenses available to me. Furthermore, I understand that this account had already been written off and/or otherwise satisfied through insurance or other recoveries. Accordingly, any payments made by me were made solely in response to the coercive circumstances created by Aqua Finance 's conduct and should not be construed as evidence that I am personally responsible for this alleged obligation. In addition, I have experienced repeated harassment in the form of telephone calls and emails, including communications occurring after [Redacted] [Redacted] These collection efforts have caused significant distress and appear to violate consumer protection laws governing debt collection practices. metadata.full_snippet: In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I applied for a Citi / AAdvantage [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. Citi denied my application and stated that " the credit privileges on your existing account ( s ) are currently restricted. '' The denial is particularly confusing because I currently maintain another Citi credit card account that remains open and in good standing. In addition, I maintain a credit score exceeding [Redacted], annual income exceeding {$300000.00}, and an otherwise strong overall credit profile. While I understand that Citi may consider factors beyond credit score and income, the reason provided does not appear consistent with my current financial standing or existing relationship with Citi. Following the denial, I submitted a written request for executive review and clarification. Specifically, I asked Citi to identify the restriction being referenced, explain whether the restriction was related to prior account history from several years ago, and confirm whether any internal restriction remains in place despite my active Citi account. Rather than providing clarification, Citi responded with a generic form letter stating only that I did not meet its internal approval criteria and that it would not disclose its specific approval requirements. Citi did not answer any of the questions I asked, did not explain the meaning of the stated restriction, did not identify what account is allegedly restricted, did not explain whether any restriction remains active today, and did not identify the actual basis for the denial. This is not a meaningful response to the information requested. Citi cited a specific reason for denying my application, yet when I requested clarification regarding that reason, the company refused to provide any substantive explanation. If Citi is relying on an internal restriction, prior account history, or other relationship-based criteria, it should clearly disclose that fact rather than provide a vague explanation and then refuse to clarify it when asked. As a consumer, I should be able to understand the basis for an adverse credit decision, particularly when the reason provided appears inconsistent with my current account status and financial profile. Citi 's response has prevented me from determining whether inaccurate, outdated, or misleading information is being relied upon and has deprived me of any meaningful opportunity to address or understand the issue. In addition, Citi 's failure to provide a substantive explanation has negatively impacted my ability to manage my personal and business travel expenses. I am a long-time [Redacted] [Redacted] customer and applied for this card specifically because of its travel benefits, airport lounge access, expense management features, and integration with my ongoing travel activity. Without a clear explanation from Citi, I have no way of knowing whether I am subject to an undisclosed internal restriction or whether I will continue to be denied access to products that support my travel needs. I am not asking that Citi be forced to approve my application. I am requesting that Citi provide a complete and transparent explanation regarding the stated restriction, identify whether any internal relationship-based restriction exists, explain whether prior account history is affecting my eligibility for new credit, and provide a substantive response to the questions raised in my executive review request rather than a generic form-letter response. I respectfully request that Citi fully investigate this matter and provide a detailed explanation of the basis for its decision so that I may understand the reason for the denial and determine whether any inaccurate, outdated, or undisclosed information is being relied upon.

metadata.full_snippet: * * To : * * Experian Information Solutions , Inc . Equifax Information Services LLC TransUnion LLC * * CC : * * Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) * * RE : * * Formal Dispute of Fraudulent Accounts Demand for Immediate Deletion, Full Validation, and Compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act To Whom It May Concern : This letter serves as my formal notice of dispute regarding the following accounts that are currently reporting on my Experian , Equifax, and TransUnion consumer credit reports : [Redacted] {$0.00} [Redacted] {$400.00} [Redacted] [Redacted] {$250.00} [Redacted] [Redacted] {$61.00} [Redacted] [Redacted] {$410.00} I have never applied for, opened, authorized, possessed, used, or benefited from any account with the above-listed companies. These accounts are fraudulent, inaccurate, and do not belong to me. I dispute the accuracy, completeness, ownership, and legal reporting of each account in its entirety. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( " FCRA '' ), you are required to maintain maximum possible accuracy of the information contained in consumer reports pursuant to * * 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) * *. Furthermore, upon receipt of a dispute, you are required under * * 15 U.S.C. 1681i * * to conduct a reasonable reinvestigationnot merely rely upon automated verification or repeat information supplied by the furnisher. Additionally, pursuant to the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act ( FACTA ), including * * 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 * *, credit reporting agencies are required to block information resulting from identity theft once appropriate notice is received. I further invoke my rights under : 15 U.S.C. 1681g Full File Disclosure 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( a ) ( 3 ) ( A ) Permissible Purpose Requirements 15 U.S.C. 1681n & 1681o Civil Liability for Willful and Negligent Noncompliance 15 U.S.C. 1692e, 1692f & 1692g ( FDCPA ) regarding false representations, unfair collection practices, and validation requirements where applicable. Accordingly, I demand that each credit bureau provide competent documentary evidence establishing the legal basis for reporting these accounts, including but not limited to : The original signed application or contract bearing my signature. Complete account opening documentation. Proof of my authorization. Documentation establishing permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( a ) ( 3 ) ( A ). The complete Method of Verification ( MOV ) used during your investigation. The name, address, and telephone number of every furnisher relied upon. The date the information was furnished. Every document relied upon to verify the accuracy of these accounts. Any electronic records, audit trail, IP logs, or authentication records supporting that I opened or used these accounts. Copies of any documents demonstrating your legal authority to continue reporting these accounts. If you can not produce competent documentary evidence establishing that these accounts belong to me, then continued reporting constitutes inaccurate and unverified information in violation of federal law. Please be advised that merely responding that the creditor " verified '' the account through an electronic system does not satisfy your obligations under the FCRA. A reasonable reinvestigation requires more than simply parroting information received from a data furnisher. Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation, failure to maintain maximum possible accuracy, failure to verify the disputed information, or continued reporting of inaccurate information may constitute violations of the FCRA and subject the responsible parties to civil liability. Therefore, I demand that Experian , Equifax, and TransUnion : 1. Conduct a lawful and reasonable reinvestigation of each disputed account. 2. Provide all documentary evidence supporting your continued reporting of these accounts. 3. Permanently delete each account if you can not fully verify it with competent evidence. 4. Send me written confirmation that the deletions have been completed. 5. Ensure these fraudulent accounts are not reinserted except in full compliance with 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ). I reserve all rights and remedies available under federal and state law, including the right to file additional complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the Federal Trade Commission, my State Attorney General, and to pursue all available legal remedies for any willful or negligent violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act or other applicable consumer protection laws. I expect your complete written response within the time required by federal law. Sincerely, -- - [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: To Whom It May Concern, This correspondence concerns Loan Number [Redacted], originally held by my mother, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], deceased. I am [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], her lawful successor in interest regarding the property secured by this loan. Since I apparently have to go to great lengths to spell this out, I want this matter clearly documented. Select Portfolio Servicing has repeatedly contradicted itself, changed its story, lost or disregarded documents, and continued creating problems since my mother passed away. Shortly after my mother died, I was told that the house was going to be closed, that SPS was forcing the matter, and that SPS would not do business with me. SPS also put that position in writing. I went to great lengths to explain what was going on and to provide the documentation required by law, yet SPS still refused to properly communicate with me. Sending me threatening letters, of intent to foreclose At the same time, SPS continued sending letters and correspondence while refusing to properly recognize my rights as successor in interest. I called SPS out on that, told SPS to cease and desist from improper handling, and SPS appeared to follow that directive only after I made the issue clear. I have submitted the required legal documentation numerous times, including the death certificate and the recorded [Redacted] [Redacted] deed / enhanced life estate deed. SPS specifically stated that those documents would suffice, and under the law, those documents are sufficient to establish my successor in interest status and ownership interest. I have submitted those documents four separate times. The first two times, SPS claimed it could not locate them, did not receive them, or otherwise could not find them. I then submitted them again. SPS later claimed the documents were not sufficient because the death certificate was supposedly missing, so I submitted both the death certificate and the [Redacted] [Redacted] deed again. After that, I was informed that only the death certificate was supposedly invalid, for whatever reason. SPS has repeatedly claimed the death certificate was invalid while never properly disclosing to me that SPS considered the [Redacted] [Redacted] deed improper or invalid. In fact, at no time before SPS responded to the CFPB did SPS disclose that it was claiming the [Redacted] [Redacted] deed was invalid. I have had numerous emails, calls, and letters back and forth regarding this entire situation, and not once did SPS clearly disclose that position to me before then. SPS has consistently changed its story. SPS also provided, in writing to the CFPB, the basic legal definition of a [Redacted] [Redacted] deed : that the original owner retains control of the property during life while naming a beneficiary or remainder person to receive the property upon death if the deed is not revoked or otherwise changed. That is exactly the type of deed involved here. The contradiction is obvious. SPS acknowledged the legal function of a [Redacted] [Redacted] deed while refusing to properly accept and process the deed that establishes my interest in the property. That is unreasonable, inconsistent, and appears to be a blatant violation of federal mortgage servicing law. Under Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.30 ( d ), a confirmed successor in interest must be treated as a borrower for purposes of the applicable mortgage servicing protections. Federal mortgage servicing rules also make clear that a successor in interest does not have to formally assume the mortgage loan before being treated as a borrower for those servicing protections. SPS has repeatedly told me, in writing and on recorded lines, that I can not be helped and that I am being forced to assume the mortgage. That is not what federal law requires. SPS can not use formal assumption as an excuse to deny basic servicing rights, communication, review, or assistance once successor in interest status is established. Additionally, 12 C.F.R. 1024.38 requires mortgage servicers to maintain reasonable policies and procedures to provide accurate and timely information, investigate and respond to complaints, communicate with potential and confirmed successors in interest, determine what documents are reasonably required, and promptly make a determination. SPS has not done that here. Instead, SPS has lost documents, contradicted itself, changed its position, continued improper correspondence, and repeatedly created new excuses to delay or deny proper handling of this matter. The Garn-St. Germain Act, 12 U.S.C. 1701j-3, also protects certain transfers from due-on-sale enforcement, including transfers to a relative resulting from the death of a borrower and transfers where a borrowers child becomes an owner of the property. SPS does not get to ignore federal law, refuse to recognize a lawful recorded deed, and then force me into an assumption process as a condition of basic servicing rights. I can not believe a mortgage company is acting this predatory when dealing with a deceased borrowers family and successor in interest. SPS has sent letters and written correspondence that directly contradict prior statements. SPS has also responded to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau in a way that contradicts what I was previously told and appears to openly admit the very servicing problems I have been raising. No matter what I do, SPS finds another excuse, another reason, or another changed story to continue giving me problems. I have been dealing with this for over two years. This has become ridiculous. I have also been advised by the County Clerks office that what SPS is doing is typical of mortgage companies that attempt to bully successors or recipients into unnecessary steps. I was further advised that the Clerks office will not issue another deed simply because SPS refuses to process what is already legally recorded. Everything SPS needs is already on file. If another title document were ever issued, it would follow what is already recorded. I am tired of SPS violating my rights, changing its story, and forcing me to repeatedly resubmit documents that SPS either loses, ignores, or contradicts itself about. I have provided the documentation. I have explained the issue. I have pointed out the law. SPS needs to correct this matter immediately and stop pretending that I have not already provided what is legally required. Please see the attached document I received from Select Portfolio Servicing. Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] Successor in Interest Loan Number [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I took a carshare ride home using the service called [Redacted]. I fell asleep in the back seat during the ride. After being dropped off, I discovered that the driver had stolen my phone, my Chase debit card, and my [Redacted] [Redacted] credit card. The perpetrator then - Unlocked my phone and accessed my Chase mobile banking app. - Changed my Chase online banking password, locking me out of my own account. - Transferred all funds from my Chase savings account into my Chase checking account. - Used my stolen Chase debit card to withdraw {$4000.00} from a Chase ATM. The PIN was obtained through means I can not confirm but it was not something I gave to the person who essentially robbed me. -Used [Redacted] [Redacted] on my stolen phone to make fraudulent purchases at an [Redacted] [Redacted] using my Chase credit card. I filed a police report documenting these events. Law enforcement is actively investigating and has requested ATM surveillance footage from Chase in order to identify the carshare driver, who is the person of interest in what amounts to a robbery. After I reported the theft, Chase froze my accounts, issued new account numbers, and opened a fraud investigation into the {$4000.00} ATM withdrawal. They issued a temporary provisional credit of {$4000.00} pending investigation and told me they would contact me for additional evidence. However, before I had any opportunity to submit the official police report which Chase had said they would request but Chase closed the investigation and concluded the transactions were " authorized '' by me. That conclusion is directly contradicted by Chase 's own records, which show : - I reported my card and phone stolen. - My online banking password was changed without my authorization, locking me out of my own account. - Chase itself determined the accounts were compromised and had frozen the account for some time and issue me a verbal passcode for additional safety. - A police report exists documenting the theft, and ATM footage from Chase 's own ATM has been requested by police. Even after I subsequently submitted the official police report, Chase has refused to reopen the claim and has informed me they will reverse the {$4000.00} provisional credit meaning I will be left bearing the full loss from a theft that Chase 's own actions ( freezing accounts, reissuing account numbers ) confirm took place. The {$4000.00} ATM withdrawal was unauthorized I did not perform it, did not consent to it, and did not benefit from it. Chase has documentary evidence of the theft on file, and now has a copy of the police report. There is no reasonable factual basis for classifying this transaction as authorized, and closing the investigation before reviewing the police report does not satisfy Chase 's obligations under Regulation E.

metadata.full_snippet: * * To : * * Experian Information Solutions , Inc . Equifax Information Services LLC TransUnion LLC * * CC : * * Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) * * RE : * * Formal Dispute of Fraudulent Accounts Demand for Immediate Deletion, Full Validation, and Compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act To Whom It May Concern : This letter serves as my formal notice of dispute regarding the following accounts that are currently reporting on my Experian , Equifax, and TransUnion consumer credit reports : [Redacted] {$0.00} [Redacted] {$400.00} [Redacted] [Redacted] {$250.00} [Redacted] [Redacted] {$61.00} [Redacted] [Redacted] {$410.00} I have never applied for, opened, authorized, possessed, used, or benefited from any account with the above-listed companies. These accounts are fraudulent, inaccurate, and do not belong to me. I dispute the accuracy, completeness, ownership, and legal reporting of each account in its entirety. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( " FCRA '' ), you are required to maintain maximum possible accuracy of the information contained in consumer reports pursuant to * * 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) * *. Furthermore, upon receipt of a dispute, you are required under * * 15 U.S.C. 1681i * * to conduct a reasonable reinvestigationnot merely rely upon automated verification or repeat information supplied by the furnisher. Additionally, pursuant to the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act ( FACTA ), including * * 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 * *, credit reporting agencies are required to block information resulting from identity theft once appropriate notice is received. I further invoke my rights under : 15 U.S.C. 1681g Full File Disclosure 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( a ) ( 3 ) ( A ) Permissible Purpose Requirements 15 U.S.C. 1681n & 1681o Civil Liability for Willful and Negligent Noncompliance 15 U.S.C. 1692e, 1692f & 1692g ( FDCPA ) regarding false representations, unfair collection practices, and validation requirements where applicable. Accordingly, I demand that each credit bureau provide competent documentary evidence establishing the legal basis for reporting these accounts, including but not limited to : The original signed application or contract bearing my signature. Complete account opening documentation. Proof of my authorization. Documentation establishing permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( a ) ( 3 ) ( A ). The complete Method of Verification ( MOV ) used during your investigation. The name, address, and telephone number of every furnisher relied upon. The date the information was furnished. Every document relied upon to verify the accuracy of these accounts. Any electronic records, audit trail, IP logs, or authentication records supporting that I opened or used these accounts. Copies of any documents demonstrating your legal authority to continue reporting these accounts. If you can not produce competent documentary evidence establishing that these accounts belong to me, then continued reporting constitutes inaccurate and unverified information in violation of federal law. Please be advised that merely responding that the creditor " verified '' the account through an electronic system does not satisfy your obligations under the FCRA. A reasonable reinvestigation requires more than simply parroting information received from a data furnisher. Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation, failure to maintain maximum possible accuracy, failure to verify the disputed information, or continued reporting of inaccurate information may constitute violations of the FCRA and subject the responsible parties to civil liability. Therefore, I demand that Experian , Equifax, and TransUnion : 1. Conduct a lawful and reasonable reinvestigation of each disputed account. 2. Provide all documentary evidence supporting your continued reporting of these accounts. 3. Permanently delete each account if you can not fully verify it with competent evidence. 4. Send me written confirmation that the deletions have been completed. 5. Ensure these fraudulent accounts are not reinserted except in full compliance with 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ). I reserve all rights and remedies available under federal and state law, including the right to file additional complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the Federal Trade Commission, my State Attorney General, and to pursue all available legal remedies for any willful or negligent violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act or other applicable consumer protection laws. I expect your complete written response within the time required by federal law. Sincerely, -- - [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I attempted to deposit {$360.00} in cash at a Wells Fargo ATM located at [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted], VA ( ATM ID : [Redacted] ). I tapped my card to the reader, entered my PIN, and inserted the cash. The ATM displayed a total of {$360.00} on screen, confirming it had registered the full amount. At that point, the ATM began making an unusual noise and appeared to be cycling the cash internally. Because I was concerned something was wrong, I began recording a video on my phone and captured approximately one minute of footage showing the ATM display with the {$360.00} deposit amount clearly visible. Shortly after I stopped recording, the ATM screen went black and then reset to the " Welcome '' screen skipping the normal confirmation step where I would have been prompted to acknowledge the deposit total before the transaction completed. When I checked the Wells Fargo mobile app, the {$360.00} had not been credited to my account. I immediately called the Wells Fargo Claims Department and was assigned claim number [Redacted]. I informed the representative that I had a video recording of the incident. The representative told me not to worry about the video and that I would receive a response within 10 business days. Approximately 14 days later, Wells Fargo issued a provisional credit of {$360.00} ( reflected on my bank statement as [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> ). On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I discovered that my account had a negative balance. Wells Fargo had reversed the provisional credit and closed my claim, citing that no overbalance of cash was found in the ATM. The reversal of {$360.00} caused my account to go negative, which resulted in two overdraft fees of {$35.00} each ( {$70.00} total ) charges I would not have incurred had the deposit been properly processed or the provisional credit not been reversed without a thorough investigation. The only notification I received was a push notification through the Wells Fargo mobile app ; I did not see any mailed notice in time, as I was in the middle of relocating. Upon discovering the reversal, I visited the Wells Fargo branch at [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted] A branch employee helped me contact the claims department, and I was provided an email address to submit my video evidence. I was told to call back within 23 days if I had not received a response. When I followed up, I was told Wells Fargo could not receive video files via email and was asked to send a screenshot instead. I complied. When I followed up again, I was told only PDF files could be accepted. I converted the screenshot to a PDF and emailed it. On my next follow-up, I was told nothing had been received. With the assistance of a family member who is a long-standing Wells Fargo customer , I was connected with an employee at the Wells Fargo [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] VA, who had a direct contact in the claims department. Over several weeks through multiple back-and-forth communications between that employee, other branch staff, myself, and the claims department Wells Fargo employees made genuine efforts to find additional avenues to investigate this matter. At one point, near the end of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I was told I would receive photographs from the ATM camera in the mail to serve as the basis for their conclusion. Instead, I was subsequently informed that Wells Fargo 's legal department had intervened and stopped that correspondence from being sent. Throughout this entire process, spanning more than four months, my video evidence which shows the ATM display confirming a {$360.00} deposit at the time of the malfunction was never reviewed by anyone in the claims department. Wells Fargo 's conclusion that no overbalance existed does not account for the possibility of an ATM malfunction, which my video documents. I have been given no explanation for why the ATM reset without completing the transaction, and no one has reviewed the footage that could resolve this dispute. I am requesting that the CFPB investigate Wells Fargo 's handling of this claim, including : ( 1 ) the failure to review available video evidence before closing the claim ; ( 2 ) the repeated miscommunication about how evidence could be submitted ; and ( 3 ) the reversal of the provisional credit without a thorough investigation into the documented ATM malfunction. I am seeking the return of my {$360.00} deposit, the refund of {$70.00} in overdraft fees that resulted directly from the improper reversal, and a full review of the claim with consideration of the video evidence I possess. metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this follow-up complaint because the consumer reporting agency responded to my prior dispute by stating the information was verified as accurate, yet failed to provide any supporting documentation or competent evidence to substantiate that conclusion. This response does not establish that a reasonable reinvestigation was conducted in accordance with 15 U.S.C. 1681i. Instead, it suggests reliance on automated or summary furnisher responses, rather than a substantive and independent review of the underlying account-level data, including payment history, account status, balances, and dates of delinquency. A generalized assertion of verification does not meet the requirements of the FCRA. Verification must be supported by reliable, verifiable documentation confirming the accuracy and completeness of the reported information. The failure to produce such documentation raises serious concerns regarding both the adequacy of the reinvestigation and the continued reporting of the disputed items. This conduct also implicates 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), as the consumer reporting agency continues to report information without demonstrating that it maintains reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy. Given the nature of the response, this issue appears to extend beyond an isolated dispute and may indicate systemic deficiencies in reinvestigation practices, overreliance on automated verification systems, and insufficient internal compliance controls.

metadata.full_snippet: Company Names : Ally Financial , Inc. [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. Issue : Inaccurate Credit Reporting / Failure to Provide Account Ownership Information / Failure to Accept Payment Complaint : I am filing this complaint regarding an account that continues to be reported on my consumer reports despite conflicting information from the companies involved and my repeated good-faith efforts to resolve the matter. I contacted Ally Financial concerning an account appearing on my credit report. Ally advised me that the account had been transferred and that I needed to contact [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. I subsequently contacted [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] and entered into a hardship payment arrangement. [Redacted] accepted the arrangement and accepted my initial payment. The following day, after receiving no confirmation, I contacted [Redacted] again and was informed that the account had been closed, the payment was being returned, and that the account was allegedly no longer with [Redacted]. I then contacted Ally Financial again and was informed that Ally did not have the account. As a result, both companies have effectively disclaimed responsibility for the account. Neither company has identified the current owner of the account, the current servicer of the account, the party authorized to accept payment, or the party furnishing information to the consumer reporting agencies. Despite this, the account continues to be reported on my consumer reports and continues to negatively impact my credit profile. I have made good-faith efforts to resolve the account and tender payment, but those efforts were frustrated when the payment was accepted and subsequently returned. To date, neither company has provided : A complete accounting of the account. Documentation identifying the current owner or holder of the account. Documentation explaining the transfer history of the account. Documentation explaining why payment was accepted and then returned. Documentation establishing who currently has authority to collect, settle, or administer the account. Documentation supporting continued credit reporting. The continued reporting of an account for which no responsible party can be identified is causing ongoing harm. The reporting has negatively affected my ability to obtain housing, employment opportunities, and financial opportunities and has caused substantial emotional distress and mental anguish. Requested Resolution : Immediate investigation of the account ownership and servicing history. Identification of the entity currently authorized to collect, settle, administer, or report the account. A complete accounting and payment history. Written explanation for the acceptance and subsequent return of my payment. Suspension of all credit reporting concerning this account while the ownership, reporting, and account information are investigated. Removal or correction of any inaccurate, misleading, incomplete, unverifiable, or unsupported information being reported concerning this account. Written confirmation of the results of the investigation. I am willing to resolve any legitimate obligation upon receipt of accurate information identifying the proper party and providing a complete accounting.

metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], a Retail Installment Sale Contract was executed for a [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. Following a subsequent repossession, the lender, American Credit Acceptance, issued a " Notice of Our Plan to Sell Property '' ( Pre-Sale Notice ) dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. This notice stated that the vehicle would be sold at a private sale sometime after [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. The vehicle was subsequently sold at auction. However, the lender failed to automatically send the legally mandated post-sale accounting and explanation of the deficiency balance. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I contacted the lender directly via their online virtual customer messaging system to obtain these missing documents. I explicitly requested the complete post-sale paperwork, including : The final accounting of the sale, the exact sale date, and the final sale price, an itemized calculation of the alleged deficiency balance, and proof of mailing for any post-sale notices, a written explanation regarding a specific {$1000.00} credit that was applied to the account in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. During this chat, the customer service agent explicitly confirmed that while the initial " intent to sell '' letter had been dispatched, the mandatory " Repossession Sold Letters '' were not showing as sent in the system. The agent stated that a request for the Copy of Repossession Sold Letters and Payment History had been submitted and explicitly advised me to allow 24 to 48 business hours for completion. The lender failed to provide these legally required disclosures within the promised timeframe, meaning they have failed to provide a valid, legal accounting of the balance they are reporting. Because the lender can not or will not provide the underlying post-sale documentation required to validate the balance, the information currently being reported to the credit bureaus is legally incomplete, inaccurate, and unverified under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). I am requesting that the lender immediately stop reporting this unverified debt and completely delete the trade line from my credit file.

The reason I am unable to provide traditional supporting documentation is because the merchant failed to provide it at every stage of the t...
metadata.full_snippet: A significant part of my complaint concerns not only the merchant 's conduct, but also Apple Card 's handling of the dispute process itself. The reason I am unable to provide traditional supporting documentation is because the merchant failed to provide it at every stage of the transaction. I never received an order confirmation email, receipt, order number, or any other proof of purchase after being charged. When I returned the item in-store, I specifically requested documentation confirming the return. Store employees informed me that they could not provide a receipt because their printer was broken. Later, when I contacted customer service regarding the missing refund, I was told that the merchant had no record of the transaction at all. In other words, the entire premise of this dispute is that the merchant failed to generate, maintain, or provide basic transaction records. The absence of documentation is not evidence against my claim ; it is the very reason the claim exists. Despite this, Apple Card repeatedly treated the lack of documentation as though it were my responsibility rather than the merchant 's. Over the course of more than two months, I made repeated phone calls, submitted written explanations, responded to requests for information, and attempted to provide every piece of evidence available to me. I also made good-faith efforts to resolve the matter directly with the merchant before involving Apple Card [Redacted] Each time I contacted Apple Card, I was forced to re-explain the facts from the beginning. On multiple occasions, I was informed that the dispute had been closed or decided despite the fact that the merchant still had not produced basic proof supporting its position. I repeatedly requested that the matter be reviewed and reopened because fundamental questions remained unanswered. Why was the merchant unable to produce a receipt, order confirmation, or transaction record? Why was the merchant permitted to claim I agreed to terms and conditions when it could not even establish the existence of the underlying transaction? Why was the merchant allowed to retain both the returned merchandise and the funds without providing proof that it had fulfilled its obligations? To this day, neither Apple Card nor the merchant has provided me with documentary evidence showing that the merchant has a valid basis for retaining my funds. Instead, Apple Card appears to have accepted the merchant 's position at face value while holding me to an impossible standard : producing documents that the merchant itself failed to provide and now claims do not exist. What I find most troubling is that Apple Card repeatedly relied on the assertion that I agreed to the merchant 's terms and conditions, while simultaneously failing to provide any evidence that such an agreement occurred. If the merchant can not locate the transaction, can not produce a receipt, can not produce an order confirmation, and can not provide a record of the purchase, then it is unclear how Apple Card determined that there was sufficient evidence to deny the dispute. I have been a loyal Apple Card customer for years and have trusted that disputed transactions would be investigated fairly and impartially. Instead, I have spent months repeatedly calling, emailing, reopening disputes, and providing detailed explanations, only to receive conclusions that appear unsupported by the evidence available. Throughout this process, I have cooperated fully, responded promptly, and made every reasonable effort to resolve the issue. The merchant, by contrast, has been unable to produce basic records of either the purchase or the return. The result is that I am being held financially responsible for a transaction that the merchant can not properly document, for merchandise that I no longer possess because it was returned to the merchant, and for a refund that was promised but never issued. I believe Apple Card failed to conduct a reasonable investigation, failed to require adequate substantiation from the merchant, and unfairly placed the burden of the merchant 's recordkeeping failures on me.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing a complaint against Capital One for their continued attempts to collect an alleged debt that they have completely failed to validate. I formally dispute this debt and demand that Capital One cease all collection activities immediately, as required by the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ). Since I first became aware of an alleged debt, I have sent multiple letters, including on [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] specifically requesting validation. Capital One has admitted in writing that they do not possess the original application, contract, or account statementsdocuments that are essential for legal validation. They have provided zero documentation to substantiate their claim. They are " unable to fulfill '' my request. This would not stand in court. Capital One has ZERO documentation or proof of this alleged debt. Despite their failure to validate, a representative named [Redacted] spoke with me over the phone on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] as I called Capital One as I became frustrated with Capital One 's lack of care and urgency to validate this alleged debt. [Redacted] had offered me a settlement of {$21000.00}. I rejected this offer and reiterated that I will not discuss any payment until Capital One provides ALL the required validation. [Redacted] suggested that I send another letter to get the validation that I need, therefore the letter dated [Redacted] was sent out. And yet again, I receive another useless letter back from Capital One dated [Redacted] stating, " We are unable to fulfill your request.... '' I have a cease and desist notice in place that Capital One continues to ignore, and their continued collection efforts without validation are a direct violation of the FDCPA at {$1000.00} per communication. I have received literally 13 useless letters from them that all appear to be autogenerated. That is {$13000.00} in violations that I demand Capital One to pay up on. I say this respectfully and professionally, Capital One purposely does not provide information as a tactic to get people to pay and be pressured to not go to court when a summons is served. However, I am 100 % ready to answer a summons and press on into legal court hearings as to date I have received ZERO information validating this alleged debt. However, if this goes into court, please be advised all requested documents will be demanded upon. Capital One has significantly hurt me financially and is causing exhaustion from mental stress. Please be advised that I require ALL of the below documentation. If Capital One decides to keep playing games, all of this information will be requested in court. Frankly and admittingly, Capital One doesn't have this information available. I will not accept a ; " we believe this is your debt '', statement without providing ALL of this below documentation. 1 ) Proof of Alleged Debt Assignment a ) Complete chain of assignment documentation showing how the alleged debt was transferred from [Redacted] [Redacted] to Capital One. b ) Date of assignment and purchase price paid by Capital One for the alleged debt. c ) Forward flow agreement between [Redacted] [Redacted] and Capital One. 2 ) Original Account Documentation a ) The original signed credit card application or contract. b ) All terms and conditions that were in effect when the account was opened. c ) Complete account history from opening date to present. d ) All account statements from the date the account was opened. [Redacted] ) Proof of Amount Owed a ) Detailed calculation of the alleged debt amount. b ) Proof of authorized interest rates and fee assessments. c ) Documentation of payments made by me. 4 ) Identity Verification a ) Written statement identifying the original creditor per 15 U.S.C. 1692 ( g ). b ) Documentation proving Capital One is the responsible party for this alleged debt. c ) Proof of Capital One 's legal standing to collect on this alleged debt. 5 ) Legal Authority Documentation a ) Proof of the legal contract between [Redacted] [Redacted] and Capital One. b ) Documentation showing [Redacted] [Redacted] had the right to sell [Redacted] [Redacted] accounts. c ) Proof that Capital One has legal authority to collect. 6 ) Jurisdiction Information a ) Written statement on which state Capital One is the under jurisdiction of. b ) Statute of limitations for debt collection in the applicable jurisdiction. 7 ) Communication History a ) All communications between [Redacted] [Redacted] and Capital One regarding this alleged debt. b ) Documentation of any previous settlement offers or negotiations. c ) Record of any cease and desist notices placed on the account. 8 ) Validation of Collection Practices a ) Written statement confirming whether Capital One is acting as a creditor or a debt collector. b ) Documentation of all collection activities to date. 9 ) Account Status Documentation a ) Current status of the alleged debt in Capital One 's records. b ) Any notation of disputes or validation requests. 10 ) Discover Card Transfer Information a ) Date Discover Card transferred or sold the alleged debt to Capital One. b ) Reason for transfer or sale. c ) Documentation of [Redacted] [Redacted] 's authority to transfer the account. I request that the CFPB compel Capital One to either provide the complete validation I am legally owed or cease all collection activities and delete any negative reporting related to this unvalidated alleged debt from my credit files. Also demand {$13000.00} from Capital One for their cease and desist violations. Please note that this information will be used in court if Capital One decides to continue to pursue this alleged debt collection.

I believe this may involve : * Misapplication of client funds * Lack of transparency in fee assessment * Potential violation of debt relief service disclosure requirements * Possible unfair or deceptive practices I am requesting a full accounting, refund of improperly assessed fees, and correction of all account records. Desired Resolution * Full itemized accounting * Refund of {$2300.00} damages settlement * Refund of all deposits totaling {$11000.00} * Written explanation of non-enrolled debt settlement authorization * Correction of account records

I humbly request that your agency/ office sends me valid proof of claim that I am legally obligated to pay you. Please provide me with the below mentioned items : * The amount you claim the respondent owes you * An explanation showing me how you have computed the amount. * Copies of any documents that prove I agreed to pay the alleged amount * The identity of the original creditor * Confirmation that the account has not crossed the statute of limitation ( SOL ) period * Evidence that you are a licensed debt collector * Evidence of your license numbers and your registered agent. * Chain of Title of ownership of the debt * Error & Omissions Insurance

metadata.full_snippet: To Whom It May Concern, I am filing a complaint against Alperstein regarding what I believe were misleading representations about its debt consolidation program, inadequate disclosure of the program 's impact on my credit, and improper handling of my cancellation request. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I enrolled in Alperstein 's debt consolidation program to address my credit card debt. During the enrollment process, I explained that one of my primary goals was to improve my financial situation so that I could qualify for a mortgage and purchase a home. At no point was I adequately advised of the significant negative impact that the program could have on my credit scores. Had I been properly informed of the potential consequences, I would have made a different decision regarding enrollment. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], I contacted Alperstein to cancel my participation in the program and requested the return of the {$610.00} balance that remained in my dedicated account. I was informed that the cancellation would take between five and seven business days to process. I believe this delay was unreasonable and appears designed to allow additional payments to be collected before the cancellation became effective. As a result, I was forced to contact my bank and take the additional step of blocking future withdrawals from Alperstein. During the cancellation call, I was advised that I would receive written confirmation of the cancellation by email or mail. To date, I have not received any cancellation confirmation. Additionally, when I inquired about the funds remaining in my account, the representative appeared unaware of the balance. Based on the interaction, I am concerned that the remaining funds may not have been returned had I not specifically raised the issue and understood that the company 's negotiation fees had already been deducted. I believe I was misled regarding the nature of the program, its impact on my credit profile, and the cancellation process. I am also concerned about Alperstein 's handling of client funds and whether its business practices comply with applicable consumer protection regulations.

metadata.full_snippet: Product : Checking account Company : TD Bank, N.A. Issue : Fees, foreign ATM/debit fees, monthly maintenance fees, and lack of clear notice I am [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] and have a TD Bank checking account ending in [Redacted]. I opened and maintained this account because I understood that the account had no TD ATM fees, reimbursement or waiver of non-TD ATM fees, no foreign fee on ATM transactions and when the required balance was maintained, and no $ 25 monthly maintenance fee as long as I maintained the required {$2500.00} minimum balance. This fee structure was very important to me because I spend substantial time outside the United States, primarily in [Redacted]. Especially during the war, I have spent extended time in [Redacted] and have relied on access to my TD account while abroad. Over approximately the last year or slightly longer, TD Bank began charging substantial fees connected to foreign ATM withdrawals, foreign debit activity, international transactions, and/or monthly maintenance. These fees were unexpected and inconsistent with the reason I opened and maintained the account. I do not believe TD Bank gave me clear and effective advance notice of these changes or of any change in how foreign ATM/debit fees would be applied. I am enrolled in paperless statements/notices, but I did not see any clear notification explaining that TD would begin charging these fees or materially change the fee structure. I am elderly and rely on my daughter, [Redacted] [Redacted], to help me manage online banking communications. She also reviewed the available online/paperless communications and did not find a clear notice explaining the change before the fees began. I am requesting that TD Bank provide a full written explanation and refund any fees that were not properly disclosed or were charged incorrectly. Specifically, I request that TD Bank provide : The exact date, method, and content of any notice TD claims it sent regarding changes to foreign ATM fees, foreign debit card international fees, international transaction fees, foreign exchange fees, non-TD ATM fees, or monthly maintenance fees. The account agreement and fee schedule that applied when I opened the account, plus each later version TD claims governed the fees charged. A line-by-line explanation of each disputed fee, including the exact contractual provision TD relied on. A refund of all monthly maintenance fees charged during any statement cycle where my account met the {$2500.00} minimum daily balance requirement. A refund of foreign ATM/debit fees, international transaction fees, foreign exchange fees, non-TD ATM fees, and related fees charged after any fee change that was not clearly and effectively disclosed in advance. A clear written statement of the current fee terms going forward so I can decide whether to keep, convert, or close this account.

The reps at Rocket Mortgage submitted an application for a loan modification or forbearance plan. This p...
metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted] [Redacted] I fell behind on my mortgage payments. In the middle of [Redacted], I called Rocket Mortgage to discuss help with repaying the two months that I owed. The reps at Rocket Mortgage submitted an application for a loan modification or forbearance plan. This plan was rejected because my account was not 90 days due. The Rocket Mortgage agents then advised me to wait 90 days and reapply. They did not inform me that 90 days also meant that the foreclosure proceedings would begin for my home. I resubmitted the application at about 90 days past due not knowing this information. In early [Redacted], I received a denial for both a loan modification and forbearance. The reason that was given is that my loan with Rocket Mortgage was less than 24-48 months old so therefore I did not meet the qualifications. At this point, the demand letter had expired, and Rocket Mortgage was drawing up paperwork to foreclose on my home. Had I known that I did not meet the requirements for the loan modification and forbearance, I would have never made the application and looked for alternative means of paying what I owed before the 90 days. I strongly feel that Rocket Mortgage was deceptive and pushed me to 90 days so that they could foreclose on my home. Today, [Redacted] [Redacted] I called Rocket Mortgage to talk about a repayment plan. I was very clear on the phone that I wanted to know if I met the requirements before submitting an application. Ultimately, I declined to submit a repayment plan application. The agent then recommended a forbearance plan. I pressed them again on whether I met the requirements for the application in which they admitted I did not. The agent asked me if I wanted to submit one anyways, which of course I declined again. Rocket Mortgage is deceiving their customers so that they can foreclose on their home. They do not offer any real means of helping their customers that are struggling.

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing a complaint against GreenState Credit Union for inaccurate credit reporting, contradictory internal records, misapplied payments, failure to properly investigate my dispute, and continued collection activity after I disputed the account. Their internal logs, credit reporting, and communication all conflict with each other, and these errors have caused financial harm and credit damage. My auto loan with GreenState has been handled inconsistently for several months. I originally stopped making payments because GreenState could not explain major discrepancies in their own internal records. When I requested documentation, they provided internal logs that contained contradictory dates, balances, and payment information. Later, they sent a corrected version that did not match the original. One example is the down payment my son made at the start of the loan. GreenStates internal records show the payment in one month, but my credit report shows it in a different month. This is inaccurate reporting and raises concerns about how they are handling and transmitting my account data. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026, when I made a payment in person, GreenState told me I was [Redacted] months behind and required me to pay approximately {$780.00} in pastdue amounts, interest, and fees. However, my credit report only shows [Redacted] [Redacted] late mark in [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026, and does not show any [Redacted] or [Redacted] late marks. If I were truly [Redacted] months behind, GreenState should have reported [Redacted], [Redacted], and [Redacted] delinquencies. They did not. GreenState is also reporting a balance of {$3000.00} to the credit bureaus, but the balance they showed me in person on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2026 was {$2000.00}. These [Redacted] balances differ by nearly {$1000.00}, and GreenState has not provided any explanation for the discrepancy. Parts of my credit report related to this account are now showing as unavailable, which raises concerns that GreenState may be altering or updating data without notifying me. Attempts to Resolve the Issue : Before filing this complaint, I made multiple attempts to resolve these issues directly with GreenState. I requested documentation several times, asked for clarification about the discrepancies in their internal records, and pointed out the inconsistencies between their logs and my credit report. GreenState did not provide a clear explanation, did not correct the errors, and did not conduct a proper investigation into my dispute. Instead, they continued collection activity and sent a RighttoCure notice. I stopped making payments only after GreenState failed to explain their own accounting errors and could not provide accurate or consistent documentation. Dispute With the Credit Bureau : I also disputed this account directly with the credit bureau. However, the credit bureau did not conduct a reasonable investigation. They simply accepted GreenStates response without requiring documentation, despite the fact that GreenStates internal records and credit reporting contradict each other. The credit bureau did not address the misreported down payment, the inconsistent delinquency timeline, or the contradictory balances. I believed I had rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, but the credit bureau did not follow proper dispute procedures and did not correct or investigate the inaccurate information. What I Want : I am requesting that CFPB investigate GreenState Credit Union for inaccurate reporting, inconsistent internal accounting, improper delinquency calculations, failure to investigate disputes, and improper collection activity after a dispute. I want GreenState to correct all inaccurate credit reporting, provide a full and accurate accounting of my payment history, explain the contradictory balances, correct the misreported down payment, remove any improper fees or interest, stop sending collection notices after a dispute, and provide accurate and consistent documentation going forward. I will upload supporting documents, including screenshots of my credit report, the internal paperwork GreenState provided, the corrected logs, the RighttoCure notice, and proof of my paymentsGreenState also failed to update my contact information. I requested that they change the email address on my account and send me confirmation paperwork, but they never did. My deceased husband is still listed on the account, and they have not corrected this despite multiple requests. This raises serious concerns about their handling of account ownership, successor information, and required documentation.

metadata.full_snippet: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) Subject : Complaint Against PayPal Credit Regarding Failure to Investigate Non-Delivery and Denial of Buyer Protection Claim Complainant : [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted], [Redacted] Financial Institution : PayPal Credit / PayPal Holdings , Inc. Nature of Complaint : Failure to properly investigate a disputed transaction, denial of buyer protection claim despite non-delivery of merchandise, and refusal to provide supporting delivery documentation. Complaint Details : I am submitting this complaint regarding PayPal 's handling of a disputed transaction involving a purchase made through [Redacted] and paid through PayPal Credit. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/2025, I purchased a [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] camera through [Redacted] for a total of {$750.00}, including taxes. The seller was listed on [Redacted] as an overseas merchant. Payment was processed through PayPal Credit. The item was never delivered to my address. During the expected delivery period, I monitored the transaction and did not receive the camera. Subsequently, the seller 's account was removed or became unavailable on [Redacted]. After the delivery window expired and the item remained undelivered, I filed a dispute and requested a refund through PayPal. During the investigation, PayPal informed me that the seller had provided documentation indicating that the item was delivered. Based on that information, PayPal denied my claim and refused to issue a refund. I dispute PayPal 's conclusion for the following reasons : 1. I never received the camera. 2. The seller is no longer active on [Redacted]. 3. PayPal has not provided me with verifiable proof that the package was delivered to my address. 4. PayPal has not identified the shipping carrier allegedly used for delivery, such as USPS, [Redacted], [Redacted], [Redacted], or any other carrier. 5. I have repeatedly requested the carrier information, tracking verification, proof-of-delivery documentation, delivery signature records, GPS delivery confirmation, and evidence showing that the package was delivered to my specific address. 6. PayPal has failed to fully cooperate with these requests and has not provided sufficient evidence supporting its determination. 7. Because the seller was located outside the United States, I am concerned that the delivery information submitted may have been inaccurate, misleading, or fraudulent. I also contacted [Redacted] regarding the matter. However, [Redacted] informed me that because the dispute had already been filed through PayPal, they would not intervene further. Requested Resolution : I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate PayPal 's handling of this dispute and require PayPal to : 1. Produce all documentation relied upon in denying my claim. 2. Identify the shipping company allegedly used to deliver the item. 3. Provide complete tracking records and proof of delivery. 4. Demonstrate that the package was delivered to my specific address. 5. Reopen and independently review the dispute. 6. Refund the full transaction amount of {$750.00} if PayPal can not establish actual delivery of the purchased item. I believe I acted in good faith, promptly reported the non-delivery, and exercised my rights under PayPal 's buyer protection process. I am requesting regulatory review because PayPal has not provided adequate transparency regarding its investigation or the evidence supporting its decision. Respectfully, [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted], Texas United States

As Chimes banking services are provided through FDIC-insured partner banks, I expect full compliance with all applicable federal consumer protection laws governing electronic fund transfers and consumer disputes. Requested Resolution : I request that Chime : * Immediately reimburse the unauthorized {$4900.00} transaction. * Provide copies of all evidence and documentation relied upon in denying or handling my dispute. * Correct any errors related to this transaction and comply with the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E. * Provide written confirmation once my funds have been returned. I have attempted to resolve this issue directly with Chime in good faith, but they have failed to return my money. I am requesting the CFPBs assistance in ensuring Chime complies with federal consumer protection laws and reimburses me for my unauthorized loss.
