Ally refused to provide this information. I then submitted a written request by email asking for a detailed accounting of the payoff calculation, the application of the insurance proceeds, and whether any surplus existed. Ally did not provide the detailed accounting I requested. When I reviewed my Ally account, I found numerous unexplained accounting entries labeled only as Reallocations. These entries include transactions involving : * {$46000.00} * {$13000.00} * {$13000.00} None of these entries are explained, and Ally has never informed me what these amounts represent or how they relate to my insurance settlement. My online account now reflects : * Outstanding Balance : {$0.00} * Balance Paid : {$15000.00} However, these figures still do not explain how the insurance proceeds were applied or whether any excess funds remained after satisfying my lease obligation. As a consumer, I believed that making a substantial down payment would reduce my financial obligation and benefit me throughout the lease. I did not understand that, in the event my leased vehicle was declared a total loss, I could lose my substantial down payment, lose the benefit of the lease payments I had already made, and receive nothing from the insurance settlement while the leasing company retained the insurance proceeds. Although the lease contains legal provisions regarding total-loss settlements, I do not believe these consequences were clearly and prominently disclosed in a manner that an ordinary consumer could reasonably understand. [Redacted] leasing process is completed primarily through a digital application, and I do not believe consumers are adequately informed that a significant capitalized cost reduction may provide no financial benefit if the vehicle is declared a total loss. Had these consequences been clearly explained, I would not have made such a substantial down payment. I would have made a significantly smaller down payment or pursued another financing option. As an active-duty service member, I am particularly concerned that these lease structures may disproportionately affect military consumers. Leasing is often viewed as an attractive option because of the flexibility it offers service members. However, I believe many military families may unknowingly place substantial amounts of money down on leased vehicles without understanding the financial consequences if the vehicle is declared a total loss. This accident was not my fault, yet I still had to pay approximately {$2000.00} out of my own pocket to obtain replacement transportation. This financial burden occurred while Ally retained the insurance proceeds and refused to provide me with a complete accounting of how those proceeds were applied. I believe consumers deserve complete transparency regarding how insurance proceeds are applied following a total-loss claim and deserve clear disclosures before entering into a lease that explain the consequences of making substantial upfront payments.

I believe these provisions significantly limit consumers ability to challenge unfair or deceptive practices. I am also concerned that this loan was marketed as a financial solution despite carrying costs that far exceed what most consumers would reasonably expect or be able to repay. I respectfully request that this loan be reviewed for compliance with applicable federal and Washington consumer protection laws, including laws prohibiting unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices. I also request that Uprova Credit , LLC cancel this loan, cease all collection activity while this matter is under review, and report that no negative information be furnished to any consumer reporting agency during the investigation. I believe these lending practices warrant regulatory review to determine whether consumers are being subjected to unlawful or abusive financial products. Thank you for your attention to this matter. metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this formal complaint to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau regarding inaccurate, incomplete, and potentially unverifiable reporting of multiple late open [Redacted] student loan accounts appearing on my consumer credit reports with Experian , Equifax, and TransUnion. The disputed accounts include [Redacted] account ending [Redacted] reported with balances of {$6100.00}, {$6300.00}, {$9000.00}, and {$2500.00}, all showing a Last Reported date of [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. I dispute the accuracy and completeness of these tradelines because I have not been provided with competent evidence establishing the accuracy of the reported balances, late payment history, account status, payment application history, date of first delinquency ( if applicable ), or the records used to support the continued reporting of these accounts as late. Despite my dispute, these derogatory entries continue to adversely impact my creditworthiness without sufficient documentation demonstrating that the information has been properly verified. Under FCRA 609 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681g ), I am entitled to receive full disclosure of all information contained in my consumer file, including complete payment histories, account-level records, furnisher identification, and all documentation relied upon to verify these tradelines. Additionally, FCRA 607 ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ) requires consumer reporting agencies to maintain maximum possible accuracy, FCRA 611 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ) requires a reasonable reinvestigation of disputed information, and FCRA 623 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ) requires furnishers to report complete and accurate information and to properly investigate disputes. The continued reporting of these accounts without providing competent documentary verification raises serious concerns regarding compliance with these federal requirements.

metadata.full_snippet: On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, a payment of {$37000.00} was submitted in error to my Wells Fargo credit card account ending [ LAST 4 ]. The amount actually due was {$3800.00}. The error created a credit balance of {$33000.00}. I called Wells Fargo on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> to correct it. I was told the excess would be reversed within 10 days. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I was told something different : that the funds would be held, after which a check would be mailed, taking an additional 10 to 14 business days to arrive. That puts return of my own money four to five weeks out from the date of the error, and it does not match what I was told on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. Also on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I filed a complaint directly with Wells Fargo and was assigned case number [Redacted]. Wells Fargo subsequently opened a second case, [Redacted], on the same day for the same issue. On these calls I made a request under 12 CFR 1026.11 ( a ) ( 2 ) for refund of the credit balance. Wells Fargo declined to refund by wire or ACH. Wells Fargo stated it could take no action until a hold was released, but would not tell me whether the funding payment had cleared and settled, and would not identify the authority for the hold. I was told the matter would be escalated to the Executive Office. On the second call, Wells Fargo stated the hold would be released on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. Wells Fargo did not confirm whether the refund itself would issue on that date, or whether the 10 to 14 business day mailing period would only begin on that date. Given that I was told on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] the excess would be reversed within 10 days, and on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] that a check would be mailed 10 to 14 business days after a hold, I have received three different accounts of when and how my money will be returned and have no written commitment to any of them. Wells Fargo 's online Message Center no longer offers a compose or reply function, so I have no way to submit a written request through my account. I am therefore submitting this complaint as my written request for refund of the credit balance under 12 CFR 1026.11 ( a ) ( 2 ), which requires a card issuer to refund a credit balance within seven business days of receiving a written request from the consumer. I request : Refund of {$33000.00} by ACH or wire transfer to an account I will designate, rather than by mailed check. If Wells Fargo will only issue a paper check, that it be sent by overnight or expedited delivery at no cost to me. Written confirmation of whether the [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> payment of {$37000.00} has cleared and settled, and if so, the specific authority under which Wells Fargo has continued to hold a credit balance funded by a settled payment. Written confirmation of the exact date the refund will be issued, and the date Wells Fargo considers the seven-business-day period under 12 CFR 1026.11 ( a ) ( 2 ) to have begun. This is {$33000.00} of my money being held after a corrected clerical error. Wells Fargo has given me three different accounts of when and how it will be returned, has declined to refund by wire, and has not provided any written commitment to a date. Desired resolution : refund of {$33000.00} by ACH, wire, or expedited check, at the earliest possible date and no later than the seven business d ays required by Regulation Z.

metadata.full_snippet: My spouse and I have held a joint account at Ally Bank for several years. Earlier this year I opened a savings account with [Redacted] [Redacted] and linked it to our Ally account using Ally 's own online account-connection procedure. Ally verified that [Redacted] [Redacted] account through its portal before allowing any transfers between the two. In [Redacted], we transferred about a total of {$9000.00} from our Ally account into the verified [Redacted] [Redacted] account. Both banks allowed these transfer with no problem. In [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I initiated a transfer of {$4000.00} to move funds from the [Redacted] [Redacted] account back to our same Ally account. The money never arrived and the transaction showed as denied. Two things then went wrong at once, and together they have left roughly {$9000.00} of our savings stranded between the two banks : [Redacted] [Redacted] : When I called to ask why the transfer failed, I was told an investigation had been opened that would be resolved in three business days. I never received any call, email, or letter with a resolution. I called back repeatedly, waited on hold for more than two hours each time, and was told each time that another investigation had to be opened, with no record of my earlier calls and no written explanation. I was eventually told the account had been closed due to " fraud, '' with no explanation, no findings, and no way to recover my money. These are my own savings, and I am not aware of any fraudulent activity. The full balance of about {$9000.00} remains in the closed account, and [Redacted] [Redacted] will not release it. Ally Bank : Ally will not accept the incoming transfer from the very same [Redacted] [Redacted] account that Ally itself verified through its account-connection process and had already allowed us to send money to. Ally permitted the funds to flow out but will not let them come back in. When I asked why, I was again told an investigation had been opened that would resolve in three business days, and again I received no call, email, or letter. Repeated calls led only to more investigations, no record of prior calls, and no written explanation. I was later told it was because it was coming out of my profile ( [Redacted] [Redacted] ) but the [Redacted] account was opened under my wife 's name and information ( [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ). We didnt think this was a problem as Ally is a joint account with both of our information and all outgoing transfers where allowed with no problem. To try to resolve this, I have made numerous phone calls since [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, taken part in several three-way calls between supervisors at both banks, and submitted proof of identity, proof of address, and proof of the transactions. Nothing has produced a resolution or a written response. As a result, about {$9000.00} of our savings is now trapped : [Redacted] [Redacted] has closed the account and will not release the funds, and Ally will not accept them back.

metadata.full_snippet: To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding the handling of a business check deposit into my Wells Fargo Business Checking account, the inconsistent information I received, and the customer service I experienced while attempting to resolve the matter. I have been a Wells Fargo customer for approximately [Redacted] years, and this experience has significantly damaged my confidence in the bank. Timeline of Events On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I deposited a legitimate business check from [Redacted] of my clients into my Wells Fargo Business Checking account. Immediately after the deposit, I was notified that a hold had been placed on the check and that the funds would be available on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I checked my Wells Fargo account expecting the funds to be available. The funds were still unavailable. I also checked my Wells Fargo mobile application and my email and found no notification indicating that the hold had been extended. Because I had received no notification, I contacted Wells Fargo Customer Service to determine why the funds had not been released. Customer Service Experience The first representative was unable to provide additional information regarding the hold. I therefore requested to be transferred to the Escalations Team. I was connected with [Redacted] [Redacted]. Throughout the conversation, I attempted to understand why the hold had been extended and asked several questions regarding the status of my deposit. On multiple occasions, my questions went unanswered. At [Redacted] point I asked whether I was being ignored because there was extended silence on the call. [Redacted] [Redacted] responded by asking, " Are you done talking? '' She repeatedly stated that nothing was going to happen, that the hold would remain in place, and that she was the highest authority available. She also threatened to terminate the call. At no point was I provided with a meaningful explanation, a practical solution, or an opportunity to speak with anyone with additional authority. I ultimately ended the call because it was clear that no assistance would be provided. The interaction left me feeling dismissed and disrespected as a long-time customer. Visit to the [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] Branch Immediately after the phone call, I went in person to the Wells Fargo branch in [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]. The [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted], attempted to assist me and contacted Wells Fargo 's back-office department on my behalf. Unfortunately, despite his efforts, he was unable to obtain any assistance because the back office refused to transfer us to the [Redacted] Department or anyone with authority to discuss or review the hold. Inconsistent Explanations During my interactions with Wells Fargo, I received different explanations regarding the reason for the hold. Initially, I was told there was unusual activity or possible fraud associated with the account on which the check was drawn. My client immediately contacted [Redacted] [Redacted], where the check originated. [Redacted] confirmed that : The account was in good standing. The funds had already been debited from my client 's account. There were no issues reported with the account. After this information was relayed, I received a different explanation from Wells Fargo indicating that the bank had attempted to collect the funds but that they were unavailable. These differing explanations left me without a clear understanding of the actual reason for the extended hold. Business Impact I operate a business and rely on timely access to legitimate client payments in order to conduct normal business operations. As a result of this situation, I spent several hours attempting to obtain accurate information by : Contacting Customer Service. Requesting escalation. Visiting a Wells Fargo branch in person. Involving my client, who contacted her bank to verify the status of the check. Working with the Branch Manager in an attempt to obtain assistance. Despite these efforts, no one was able to provide a consistent explanation or connect me with the department responsible for making the decision. As of the date of this complaint, my business account has become approximately {$1900.00} overdrawn, creating additional financial stress and uncertainty. This experience has also caused me to lose confidence in depositing future business checks with Wells Fargo because I no longer know whether legitimate client payments will be made available according to the dates communicated by the bank. Requested Resolution I respectfully request that Wells Fargo : Conduct a formal review of this extended hold. Provide a written explanation identifying the specific reason for the extended hold and the policy under which it was applied. Explain why I did not receive notification that the hold had been extended before the original availability date. Review the conduct of the representatives involved in this matter, particularly my interaction with [Redacted] [Redacted]. Review why neither I nor the Branch Manager were permitted to speak with or obtain assistance from the department responsible for the decision. Reimburse any applicable account fees incurred as a result of this matter and consider providing an appropriate goodwill credit for the significant time, inconvenience, and disruption caused. Respond to this complaint in writing. I have attached screenshots and supporting documentation that corroborate the timeline described above. After approximately [Redacted] years as a Wells Fargo customer, I expected transparent communication, consistent information, and meaningful assistance when seeking help with my business account. Instead, I encountered conflicting explanations, an inability to escalate my concerns, and customer service that fell well below the standard I believe customers should expect. I appreciate your prompt attention to this matter and look forward to your written response. Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: Company : Google Pay / Google Payments Nature of Complaint : Failure to conduct a reasonable fraud investigation ; suspension of consumer payment account after valid fraud report. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, my [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] card ending in [Redacted] was compromised by a criminal. The fraudster attempted numerous unauthorized purchases. [Redacted] [Redacted] fraud detection systems blocked nearly all of them. One transaction, however, was successfully processed through Google. The fraudulent purchase was : Google Store Order ID : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] ( Unlocked ) Amount : {$1300.00} The phone was shipped to : [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] I have never lived at, visited, or had any association with this address or the recipient. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], after receiving an email from the Google Store regarding this purchase, I immediately contacted Google to report that the transaction was fraudulent. I opened Google Support Inquiry [Redacted]. [Redacted], later changed to [Redacted] [Redacted] ID [Redacted]. During my conversations with Google 's representatives, I repeatedly requested that shipment of the phone be stopped before delivery because it had clearly been purchased by a criminal using my stolen credit card information. I was told that Google 's fraud team was investigating. Despite my prompt report, Google allowed the shipment to proceed and the device was delivered to the fraudster. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], Google informed me that it was " unable to confirm fraudulent activity '' and denied my claim. [Redacted] [Redacted] independently investigated the transaction, determined that it was fraudulent, and credited my account for the full amount. As a result, I have not suffered a financial loss. However, the matter did not end there. After [Redacted] processed the fraud chargeback, Google suspended my Google Payments profile. Google informed me that my account would remain suspended unless I contacted [Redacted] and requested that [Redacted] reverse the fraud chargeback because Google had concluded that the transaction was legitimate. Google 's explanation is deeply troubling. In its written response, Google states that it found no evidence that my Google account had been compromised. It then speculates that perhaps a friend or family member made the purchase and advises me to reverse [Redacted] [Redacted] fraud determination. This conclusion ignores the objective facts : My credit card had been compromised and was used in multiple unauthorized purchase attempts. [Redacted] [Redacted] fraud detection systems identified the activity as fraudulent. The phone was shipped to a [Redacted] address completely unrelated to me. I reported the fraud before the phone was delivered and specifically requested that shipment be stopped. Google nevertheless delivered the device to the fraudster. Google subsequently concluded that the transaction was legitimate. Google then suspended my payments account because I exercised my rights by reporting the fraud to my card issuer. My complaint is not about reimbursement. [Redacted] has already protected me from the financial loss. Rather, I believe Google 's fraud investigation was unreasonable and that its subsequent actions unfairly penalized me as the victim of identity theft. I am particularly concerned that Google is conditioning restoration of my Google Payments account on my persuading my bank to reverse a fraud determination that [Redacted] made after its own investigation. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate whether Google 's practices regarding fraud investigations, consumer disputes, and payment account suspensions are fair to consumers. Specifically, I request that Google be required to : Conduct an executive review of its determination that this transaction was legitimate. Restore my Google Payments profile without requiring me to persuade my bank to reverse a legitimate fraud chargeback. Explain the basis for concluding that this transaction was not fraudulent despite the objective evidence. Review its fraud investigation and account suspension procedures to ensure that consumers who promptly report fraudulent transactions are not penalized for doing so. I am prepared to provide copies of Google 's correspondence, Google 's fraud denial, Google 's account suspension notice, and [Redacted] [Redacted] fraud determination upon request.

metadata.full_snippet: This is a follow-up complaint to my prior CFPB Complaint # [Redacted]. I am submitting a follow-up complaint regarding Citibanks unwarranted and improper handling of my Citi / AAdvantage [Redacted] [Redacted] account ending in [Redacted]. On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, I received a response letter from the Citi Executive Response Team stating that my account underwent a routine review for card reissue, did not pass, and has been permanently closed without the option to reopen, declaring the issue resolved on their end. There is absolutely no valid financial or contractual reason for this closure, and I request CFPB intervention based on the following key points : Breach of Express Assurances & Seamless Transition Promise : This account originated as a [Redacted] account, which I held with an exemplary payment record and zero issues. During the portfolio transition from [Redacted] to Citibank, I was explicitly promised a seamless transition with no account closure. Furthermore, in Citis formal response to my initial CFPB complaint, Citi explicitly reaffirmed that my account was in good standing and would not be closed. Closing it now during a routine card reissue directly violates those official representations. Outstanding Credit Profile & Lack of Justification : There is no risk-based or financial justification for closing my account. I maintain an outstanding credit report and immaculate credit history. It is completely contradictory and arbitrary to close an active, well-maintained account during a standard reissue process. Contradictory Communications Regarding Card Reissue : Prior to receiving this sudden closure letter, I was notified that my new replacement/reissued card was already processed and on its way to me in the mail. Moving immediately from mailing a card to terminating the entire account demonstrates extreme administrative dysfunction. Probable Account Mix-Up : I strongly suspect an internal administrative error or account mix-up on Citis end. I previously held an old, separate account with Citi that was closed years ago. It appears the review team may have mistakenly linked data or history from that old closed account to my current, active account ( ending in [Redacted] ). Desired Resolution Full Account Reinstatement : Reopen and fully reinstate my Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select account ( ending in [Redacted] ) with its original credit line, terms, and history intact. Issuance of Replacement Card : Expedite and send the active replacement card that was previously in transit. Credit Bureau Protection : Ensure no negative marks, adverse action notices, or " closed by grantor '' notations are placed on my credit reports as a result of Citi 's internal erro

metadata.full_snippet: To Whom It May Concern : Please accept this letter as a formal Notice of Error pursuant to Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.35.I am writing to formally dispute the recent denial of my loss mitigation application. My account is currently approximately 7 months past due with total arrears of roughly {$17000.00}. MidFirst Bank [Redacted] Incorrect Use of Automated Prior Plan Limits : MidFirsts denial letter dated [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year> states that I am non-approved because my loan 'exceeded the limit for defaulted trial plans. ' Under FHA/HUD Single Family Housing Policy guidelines , a prior trial plan issue does not permanently strip a borrower of their right to a manual underwrite. Because my income is verified and fully capable of maintaining the current monthly payment, MidFirst is required to review my file manually for a standard capitalization modification rather than relying on a generic, automated system rejection. '' Failure to Advance to the Next Tier of the Waterfall : While I have previously utilized an FHA Standalone Partial Claim and may have reached the statutory 30 % partial claim cap, FHA guidelines explicitly state that a servicer can not halt loss mitigation reviews at that stage. If the partial claim tool is exhausted, MidFirst Bank is contractually and legally required to evaluate me for the next tier of the FHA waterfall : a Standard FHA Capitalization and 40-Year Term Extension Modification.Financial Feasibility : My current household income is fully stable and completely capable of supporting my regular ongoing monthly mortgage payment. I do not require a payment reduction ; I simply require a vehicle to absorb the {$17000.00} past-due balance. A standard FHA 40-year capitalization modification accomplishes this without requiring additional HUD partial claim funds.

metadata.full_snippet: Dear CFPB, I am writing to formally request the removal of an inaccurate medical collection account from my credit report. When I reviewed my credit report, I discovered a collection account related to an emergency room visit in [Redacted] [Redacted], Texas. I immediately disputed the account because I believed it was reported in error. Unfortunately, my dispute was denied. After my dispute was denied, I contacted both my health insurance company and the collection agency to understand how this debt was created. My health insurance company informed me that they have no record of ever receiving a claim or medical bill for services allegedly provided on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>. Since my insurance was never billed, they were never given the opportunity to process or pay the claim. I then contacted the collection agency, and they informed me that the emergency room had reported my information incorrectly, including my name and my date of birth. They also told me that the medical bill was sent directly to collections on the very same day of the alleged service, instead of first being submitted to my insurance company. As a result, my insurance never received the claim. The collection agency also told me that I could pay {$370.00} for them to pursue a legal dispute on my behalf to avoid paying the full medical bill. However, I do not believe I should have to pay to correct an error that was caused by the medical provider. I also attempted to contact the emergency room directly. They told me they have no record of treating me on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, and therefore could not provide any additional information regarding this account. I have made every reasonable effort to resolve this issue by contacting my insurance company, the collection agency, and the medical provider. Unfortunately, no one has been able to correct the error or provide a valid explanation for why this account was reported. Because this account appears to have been reported using incorrect personal information and without first billing my insurance, I respectfully request that you conduct a thorough reinvestigation and remove this inaccurate collection account from my credit report in accordance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). Thank you for your time and consideration. I appreciate your prompt attention to this matter and look forward to your response. Sincerely, [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: The entire application process was a multi-faceted bait and switch. The sales people [Redacted] [Redacted] and [Redacted] [Redacted] took down a bunch of my information wrong on the application [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. But, I couldn't see what they had typed into the application until after I gave them the payment info for the {$500.00} " lock-in fee ''. I tried to have them correct it right away but they said it would be corrected in the next steps and to just proceed ; this was after doing a digital appraisal and assuring me that the {$500.00} fee was in lieu of having an appraisal done. I did submit all the requested documentation for the loan. The first major mistake they made was they said I could have a domestic partner on the title and put down that I was married on the application. I specifically said I was not married and my domestic partner was on the title. The loan processor, after submitting all the paperwork, told me the " palladium '' loan product I was signing up for would not allow a [Redacted] person on the title without being on the loan. I said we could put her on the loan or try a different loan product and she said the sales people would call me back about setting that up but they never did. The bigger mistake was the sales manager assured me I would not need an appraisal on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted], before he " finalized '' the " lock-in '' fee. [Redacted] weeks later, I had submitted all the documentation including having my home insurance reflect [Redacted] as the mortgage lender. I got a text message from a [Redacted] party appraisal company saying I needed to schedule an appraisal. This is [Redacted] weeks into the process, after the sales person assured me I wouldn't need an appraisal, and after I had submitted the required documentation. The loan processor told me that because it was a " palladium '' loan and my [Redacted] was 85 %, I would need an appraisal and the sales manager would call me to resolve it as the loan officer on the loan wasn't answering calls. A week later, the sales manager called back, saying that it was 85 % and shouldn't need an appraisal and he would figure it out, like he has a different loan product he's selling from the rest of the company. I never heard back from him again. Another week after that, [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted] I requested a refund initially- the customer service agent said she would forward the refund request to sales, but I had not heard from them so I made another refund request on [Redacted]/[Redacted]/[Redacted]. This is a bold face bait and switch. The sales people, underwriters, and loan processors all seem to be selling different products. The sales people push the application through and say whatever it takes to get the {$500.00} fee, and then all the terms change. According to the original terms of the lock-in fee, it is refundable in cases of mistakes by the sales people, which I outlined above, but I haven't been refunded yet.

Case # [Redacted] On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, at approximately [Redacted] [Redacted], I vis...
metadata.full_snippet: I am submitting this complaint because I believe Wells Fargo did not conduct a complete or reasonable investigation into my dispute involving missing cash during a deposit transaction. Case # [Redacted] On [Redacted]/[Redacted]/year>, at approximately [Redacted] [Redacted], I visited a Wells Fargo branch on[Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], [Redacted] [Redacted], CA [Redacted] Phone : ( [Redacted] ) [Redacted] to make a cash deposit. I arrived believing I had {$4000.00} in {$20.00} bills inside an envelope. After counting the cash, the teller informed me that the envelope actually contained {$8000.00}, not {$4000.00}. I instructed the teller that I only wanted to deposit {$4000.00} and asked her to return the remaining {$4000.00} to me. The teller completed the {$4000.00} deposit and handed me what was supposed to be the remaining {$4000.00} in cash inside an envelope. I did not open the envelope or handle the cash after leaving the bank. I kept the envelope closed until I arrived home. As soon as I got home, I opened the envelope and immediately counted the cash. I counted it at least 8 times to make sure I had not made a counting mistake. Each time, the total was {$3900.00}, confirming that {$40.00} ( two {$20.00} bills ) was missing. I immediately contacted the branch to report the discrepancy. Wells Fargo opened Case [Redacted] and later informed me that its investigation found no {$40.00} overage or shortage in the tellers cash drawer. I do not believe that conclusion resolves my complaint. A balanced cash drawer does not explain why I received only {$3900.00} when I should have received {$4000.00}. The investigation appears to have been limited to reconciling the tellers drawer and did not address what actually happened during my transaction. Additionally, while I was standing at the teller window, I observed the teller place some bills off to her right-hand side before handing me my cash. I do not know what those bills were, and I am not accusing anyone of theft or intentional wrongdoing. However, because I observed this, I believe the surveillance footage could clarify whether it is related to the missing {$40.00}. When I later spoke with a representative from Wells Fargos Executive Office regarding my complaint, I was told that Wells Fargo was unable to review the surveillance camera footage and that a court order would be required before the footage could be viewed. I do not know whether that explanation is accurate, but if true, I do not understand why Wells Fargo can not review its own security footage as part of an internal investigation into a customer complaint. The facts of this matter are straightforward : I entered the bank with {$8000.00} in cash. I deposited {$4000.00}. I should have left with {$4000.00} in cash. I left the bank with an envelope that I did not open until I arrived home. Upon opening the envelope and immediately counting the money, I discovered that it contained only {$3900.00}, even after counting it repeatedly to verify the amount. There is no dispute regarding the amount of cash I brought to the bank because the teller counted and confirmed that I had {$8000.00}. There is also no dispute that I deposited only {$4000.00}. The only unresolved issue is why I received only {$3900.00} instead of the remaining {$4000.00}. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau review this matter and require Wells Fargo to conduct a thorough investigation. Specifically, I ask that Wells Fargo explain why it declined or refused to review the available surveillance footage, or why it believes it lacks the authority to review footage from its own branch during an internal customer complaint investigation. If the footage still exists, I request that it be preserved and reviewed before it is destroyed pursuant to any retention policy. My goal is not to accuse anyone without evidence. My goal is simply to determine what happened to the missing {$40.00} and to ensure that my complaint receives a complete and fair investigation based on all available evidence, rather than solely on the balancing of the tellers cash drawer.

metadata.full_snippet: Subject : CFPB Complaint Aargon Agency , Inc . Formal Dispute and Demand for Deletion of Unverified Collection Account I am filing this complaint against Aargon Agency , Inc. concerning its collection and credit reporting of an alleged [Redacted] [Redacted] account in the amount of {$180.00}. I dispute this alleged debt in its entirety. Pursuant to my rights under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq., and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., I request a complete investigation and immediate correction of any inaccurate or unverifiable information. I demand that Aargon Agency , Inc. produce competent documentary evidence establishing that I am legally responsible for this alleged debt, including : * A copy of the original agreement or other evidence showing I am legally obligated for this account. * A complete itemized accounting showing how the alleged balance of {$180.00} was calculated. * Documentation establishing Aargon Agency, Inc.s authority to collect this account on behalf of [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] through a lawful assignment. * Records identifying the date of default and the complete account history. * Copies of all documents relied upon when furnishing this account to [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] Under 15 U.S.C. 1692e, a debt collector may not use any false, deceptive, or misleading representation in connection with the collection of a debt. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692f, a debt collector may not use unfair or unconscionable means to collect or attempt to collect a debt. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, furnishers of information have a duty to investigate disputes and correct or delete information that can not be verified. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), consumer reporting agencies must follow reasonable procedures to assure the maximum possible accuracy of the information reported. If Aargon Agency , Inc. can not provide competent evidence establishing my legal responsibility for this account, it must : * Immediately cease all collection activity. * Permanently delete this collection account from [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], and any other consumer reporting agency. * Notify each consumer reporting agency that the account has been deleted. * Provide written confirmation that the account has been permanently removed. Verification through automated systems such as e-OSCAR, internal database records, account summaries, or unsupported electronic records alone is insufficient to establish the legal validity of a disputed debt. A reasonable investigation requires review of competent documentary evidence. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate Aargon Agency , Inc.s compliance with the FDCPA and FCRA and require the company to correct or delete any information that can not be substantiated through a reasonable investigation. If Aargon Agency , Inc. can not verify this alleged debt with competent evidence, I request the immediate and permanent deletion of this account from all consumer reporting agencies and the termination of all collection activity. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted] [Redacted], NC [Redacted]

metadata.full_snippet: I am filing a complaint against U.S. Bank regarding multiple overdraft fees that I believe were handled unfairly. My checking account became overdrawn after several debit card purchases. At the time I continued using my debit card, I was not seeing overdraft fees posted to my account. Because the fees were not visible, I believed I only needed to cover the negative balance. If I had seen the first overdraft fee when it was assessed, I would have immediately stopped using my debit card and would not have continued making purchases. Instead, multiple overdraft-related fees were added to my account over a short period. I was ultimately charged [Redacted] overdraft-related fees totaling {$210.00} all in [Redacted] day. These fees significantly increased my negative balance. Before receiving my paycheck, I contacted U.S. Bank and explained that I would be able to pay the negative balance when I was paid on Friday. After seeing the overdraft fees, I requested a courtesy refund because I was not aware the fees had accumulated while I was making purchases. U.S. Bank denied my request for any refund. I am asking for U.S. Bank to review the circumstances surrounding these overdraft fees, explain how each fee was assessed, and reconsider refunding some or all of the - {$210.00} in overdraft fees. I believe I was not given a fair opportunity to avoid additional fees because they were not visible to me while I was continuing to use my debit card. I pay rent and [Redacted] with this card. And this is the first time this has ever happened to me. I am in college and can not afford this and I dont want to close this account.
